It will be stated later that *bhrājṛ* and *ṭubhrāśṛ* belong to the class beginning with *phaṇ* (I. 875–876); because it belongs to that class, the optional substitution of *e* for the radical vowel and the elision of the reduplication (*etvābhyāsalopau*) are its purposes: *bhreje* or *babhrāje*. Likewise, by the rule *vraścabhrasja* (VIII. 2. 36), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs so that it may apply to the form associated with *rājṛ*: *bābhrāṣṭi*, whereas for this [root *bhrāj*], it is *bābhrākti*.

By the rule *bhrājabhāsadhūṣi* (III, 2, 177), the suffix *kvip* is applied: *vibhrāṭ*. By the rule *nabhrāṇnapāt* (VI, 3, 75), the original form (*prakṛti*) is retained. By the rule *bhuvaś ca* (III, 2, 138), because of the word "and" (*ca*), the suffix *iṣṇuc* is added: *bhrājiṣṇuḥ*. Candra [also] mentions the root *rejṛ* (Ca. Dh. I, 364). (192–195) The root *īj* means "to go" and "to revile": *ījate*, *vījyate*. Durga says: *ījiti* means *īñjate*. From the root *vīj* in the sense of the worldly [root] (X, 60): *avījayat*. (196–197) These are the roots with acute [accent] that have anudātta [as their indicatory letter]. 179.

The root *śuc* means "to grieve. From this [root], there are seventy-two [derivative forms], including those ending in the *parasmaipada*. *śocati* (he grieves), *śocitā* (he will grieve). Regarding *śokaḥ* (grief) and *śocyam* (that which is to be grieved): the substitution of *k* for *c* (*kutvam*) is not desired here; rather, it is either a form of the causative (*ṇyanta*), or [the suffix] *yuc* is applied according to Pāṇini III.2.150 (*jucaṅkramya-* etc.), resulting in *śocanaḥ* (one who grieves). Alternatively, by applying the suffix *ki* to a root with *i* as its penultimate vowel (cf. Uṇādi IV.119), we have *śuciḥ* (pure/bright). By applying the suffix *is* according to Uṇādi II.109 (*arciśuci-* etc.), we have *śocis* (light/radiance). (198)

The root *kuca* is used in the sense of "to sound" (*tāra*) and "to contract" (*saṃparcana*). It will be listed among the *jvalādi* group for the sake of distinguishing its meanings. According to the rule *udupadhād bhāvādikaṛmaṇor anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini I.2.21), there is optionally the absence of the *kit* suffix: *saṃkucitam* or *saṃkocitam*. (199) The root *kruñc* means "to move. One *kruñcati*. The forms *kruṅ* and *kruñcā* [are derived from this root]; the absence of *nalopa* (elision of the *n*) occurs due to the specific grammatical rule (*nipātana*) *añcuyujikruñcām* (Pāṇini III.2.59). From the *prajñādi* group, the suffix *aṇ* is applied: *krauñcaḥ*. (201)

The root *kuñc* is used in the senses of "crookedness" (*kauṭilya*) and "diminution" (*alpa-bhāva*). It is used for the crookedness of movement and for the smallness of a substance. One says *kuñcati*. The forms *kuñcita*, *kuñcikā*, and *kuk* [are derived from it]. Regarding the suffix *ṇvul* (Pāṇini III.1.133), the elision of the nasal (*na-lopa*) is desired: thus we have *saṃkocakaḥ*. However, even so, there would be a prohibition by the rule *na dhātulopa ārdhadhātuke* (Pāṇini I.1.4). Therefore, this form [of the suffix] belongs to the root *kuc* (DhP. 199). The fact that the root is marked with an *u* in the Candra system (Ca. Dh. I.47) is not authoritative, since Kātyāyana provided the *udupadhatva* as a purpose for the *saṃnipāta-paribhāṣā* (the technical rule concerning the non-disturbance of a grammatical occasion). [Kātyāyana] did not state [this as a purpose] because of the following: [he added] "by way of irregularity" (*nipātanāt*); [and he] did not state [it as a purpose].

21. Regarding the rule *kittvasya nikucita* (Pāṇini I.1.39, vārttika 6): if this [root *luc*] were marked with the *udic* indicatory letter (*udit*), the augment *iṭ* would not be applied here [in the gerundive].

[The root] *lunc* means "to remove" (*apanayane*); it is used in the sense of discarding what has not been used (*anupayuktāpāsane*). One says *luñcati*. By the rule *vañciluñcyṛtaś ca* (Pāṇini I.2.24), the suffixes *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā* are optionally *kit*: *luñcitvā* or *lucitvā*, *luñcitaḥ* or *lucitaḥ*. (202) 1.

The root *añc* is used in the senses of "going" and "worshiping. From *añcati*, we have *ānañca*. Regarding the forms *aktvā* and *añcitvā*: by the rule *udito vā* (Pāṇini VII.2.56), the suffix *iṭ* is optional. However, by the rule *añceḥ pūjāyām* (Pāṇini VII.2.53), *iṭ* is mandatory after *añc* when followed by the suffixes *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā* (the past passive participle suffix *kta*) in the sense of worshiping: *añcitvā gurūn* ("having honored the teachers") and *añcito rājā* ("the king was honored"). In other cases, by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VII.2.15), *iṭ* is not added to the *niṣṭhā*: *samaknau śakuneḥ pādau* ("the two feet of the bird are even"). By the rule *añco 'napādāne* (Pāṇini VIII.2.48), the substitution of *n* for *c* occurs, but this applies when there is no *apādāna* (ablative case). In the presence of an *apādāna*, however:

"Drawn up from the well with water. There is no elision of the *n* [in *añc*] because of the rule "of those not having *i* or *t* as it, when a consonant follows as an upadhā, before *k* or *ṅ* suffixes" (Pāṇini VI.4.24), since there is the exception "not in the sense of honor" (VI.4.30); thus: "the teachers were honored" (*añcitā guravaḥ*). From the rule "after *ud*, after *añc*, [there is the suffix] *ku*" (Uṇādi I.18), we have *nyaṅkuḥ*; by the rule "for *vṛkṣa* and *śvan*, elsewhere [than these], for *nyañc*, [there is] *kutva*" (VII.3.53), there is the substitution of *k*. In a sense other than "tree" or "dog," *nyañcuḥ* means a drop of sweat. "The word *udaṅka* is correct when not meaning water" (III.3.123); but when meaning water, the suffix *lyuṭ* (III.3.117) applies: *udañcanī* means a water-drawing vessel.

By the rule *ṛtvigdadhṛk* (Pāṇini III.2.59), the suffix *kvin* is applied; by the rule *ugidacām* (VII.1.70), the augment *num* is added: *prāṅ*. With the suffix *ghañ*, [the forms] *paryaṅkaḥ* and *palyaṅkaḥ* are formed (VIII.2.22). The word *udakam* is established as an irregular form (*nipātita*) by Uṇādi-sūtra II.39. (203)

The roots *vañcu*, *cañcu*, *tañcu*, *tvancu*, *mruñcu*, *mluñcu*, *mruçu*, and *mlucu* have the meaning of "motion. In the case of *vañcati*: when the suffix *yaṅ* is applied, although lengthening of the reduplicated syllable would normally occur, the augment *nīg* is inserted by the rule *nīg vañcusraṃsudhvaṃsv* (Pāṇini VII.4.84), resulting in *vanīvacyate*. By the rule *udito vā* (Pāṇini VII.2.56), the suffix *iṭ* is optional: thus we have *vaktvā*, *vacitvā*, or *vañcitvā*. Furthermore, by the rule *vañciluñcyṛtaś ca* (Pāṇini I.2.24), there is optionally the status of being *kit*; because *iṭ* is optional, the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VII.2.15) applies, so that the suffix *niṣṭhā* does not take the augment *iṭ*.

The agent [of the action] is *vañcitaḥ*, derived from the root *vañcu* in the *curādi* group, meaning "to deceive" (*pralambhana*; X, 163). Regarding the rule *ghṛdhivañcyoḥ pralambhane* (I, 3, 69), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *bālaṃ vañcayate* ("he deceives the child"), but not here: *ahiṃ vañcayati* ("he avoids the snake"). By the rule *sphāyi* (Uṇ. II, 13), the suffix *rak* is added to form *vakra* ("crooked"), which belongs to the *nyaṅkvādi* class (VII, 3, 53). When the suffix *ghañ* is used, there is no *kutva* substitution (as per VII, 3, 63) because *vañc* means "going": *vañcaṃ vañcanti vaṇijaḥ* ("the merchants move along the path"; cf. VII, 3, 63 Kāśikā). [The root also forms] *cañcati*.

*Cañcā* is a straw figure (*tṛṇapuruṣa*); *cañcu* means the beak (*troṭi*). *Cañcala* means fickle (*capala*); *cācala*, however, is a form meaning "moving" (*cale*). *Taṅca* is buttermilk (*takra*). [The root] *mruca-*: *mrocati*. *Mlocati* means "to fade" (*malina*); *malimluca* means a thief (*caura*). By the rule *jṝ-stambhu-mrucu-mlucu-grucu-glucu-glucu-śvi-bhyaś ca* (Pāṇini III.1.58), the suffix *aṅ* is optionally applied: *amrucat* or *amrocīt*; *amlucat* or *amlocīt* (204–211).

The roots *gruc* and *gluc* are used in the sense of stealing (*steyakaraṇe*). [Aorist forms: *agrucat*, *agrocīt*; *aglucat*, *aglocīt* (Pāṇini III.1.58). [With the suffix] *ghañ* (Pāṇini I.3.18): *glocaḥ*. Due to the rule *na kvādeḥ* (Pāṇini VII.3.59), there is an absence of *kutva* (the change of *c* to *k*) [in these cases]. (212–215) 1 201 vor 200 2 P omits I 22.

*gluncu* and *ṣasja* mean "to move. [Examples: *nyaglucat*, *nyagluñcīt* (III, 1, 58). From *sajj*: *sajjati*, *sisajjiṣati*, *siṣajjayiṣati*; *sajjaḥ*, *sajjito hastī*. In some instances, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) and *āna* (desiderative suffix) occur: "Those deluded by the qualities of nature cling to the actions of the qualities" (*Bhagavadgītā* III, 29); "clinging to improper acts" (*Kāmandakīyanītisāra* IV, 41 or 45). Śiva says this root ends in *c*: *saścati* (216, 217). *guji* means "inarticulate sound": *guñjati*. [Derivatives: *guñjari*, *guñjitam*, *guñjā*. Some say it is *anidit* (having an *it*-augment): *gojati*, *jugoja* (218).

The root *arc* is used in the sense of worship (*pūjā*). [Forms: *arcati*, *ānarca*; *arcitaḥ*, *arcā*. By the rule *yaja-yāca-ruca-pravaca-arc-aś ca* (Pāṇini VII.3.66), there is an absence of *kutva* (the change of *c* to *k*): *arcyah*. According to those who hold that the root *ṛc* is included here by the rule *yeṣāṃ mate ’tra ṛceḥ* (Vārttika VI.19), in their view the form is *arkyaḥ*. From the rule *arci-śuci-husṛpi-* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.109), the suffix *is* is applied: *arciḥ*. That which is worshipped (*arcyate*) is called *arkaḥ* (by rule III.1.134). In the *curādi* class, one finds *arcayati* (X.266). (219)

*Mleccha* [is used] in the sense of indistinct speech. One *mlecchati*. *Mlecchanam*, *mlecchaḥ*; for indeed, that which is an incorrect word (*apaśabda*) is a barbarian (*mleccha*). "One should not speak barbarously, one should not speak incorrectly" (*Paspaśā* p. 2). According to *kṣubdha-svānta-dhvānta* (Pāṇini VII.2.18), when indistinct, *mliṣṭam* is correct; anything else is *mlecchitam*. *Lacha*, *lāchi*, and *lakṣa* [are used] in the sense of marking. A mark (*lakṣaṇa*) is a sign (*cihna*). One *lachati*, *lāñchati*; *lāñchanam*. *Vāch* [is used] in the sense of desire. One *vāñchati*. *Vāñchitam*, *vāñchā*.

The root *āñch* means "to stretch. It is conjugated as *āñchati*, *āñchyate*. [In the phrase] *dordaṇḍāñchitacandraśekharadhanurdaṇḍāvabhaṅgodyataḥ* ("ready to snap the staff-like bow of Śiva, which was being stretched by his staff-like arms"), the forms *āñcha*, *āñchatuḥ*, and *āñchuḥ* occur; due to the inclusion of this root in the *grahādigaṇa* (Pāṇini VI.4.71), there is an absence of the augment *nuṭ*.
(224) The root *hrīcch* means "to feel shame. It is conjugated as *hrīcchati*, *jihrīccha*. (225)

The root *hurch* is used in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*). It forms *hurchati*. By the rule *rvor upadhāyāḥ* (Pāṇini VIII.2.76), there is lengthening of the vowel. In the case of the *niṣṭhā* suffix, by the rule *āditaś ca* (Pāṇini VII.2.16), the augment *iṭ* is not present: *hurṇaḥ*. By the rule *rāl lopaḥ* (Pāṇini VI.4.21), there is elision of the *ra*, and by *radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ* (Pāṇini VIII.2.42), the dental *ta* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix is replaced by *na*. By the rule *vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini VII.2.17), the augment *iṭ* is optional: *hūrṇam* (with *iṭ*) or *hurṇam* (without *iṭ*). Examples include: *anena hurchitam* ("he has acted crookedly"), *hūrṇam*, *prahūrchitaḥ*, *prahūrṇaḥ*. With the *kvip* suffix (Pāṇini III.2.178), one gets *hūḥ* and *hurau*. (226)

The root *murch* is used in the senses of fainting (*moha*) and increase (*samucchrāya*). It takes the form *mūrchati*. Regarding the word *mūrchā*, there is no substitution of *ṇatva* (the change of *ch* to *ṇ*) in the past participle suffix (*niṣṭhā*), according to Pāṇini VIII.2.57: "In the case of roots ending in *dhyā*, *khyā*, *pṝ*, *mūrch*, and *mad*, [there is no ṇatva]. Thus we have *mūrtaḥ*. According to Kāśikā III.3.94, the suffix *ktin* is treated like *niṣṭhā*: thus *mūrtiḥ*. From this [root], we derive *mūrchitam* and *mūrtam* (by this person); likewise *pramūrchitaḥ* and *pramūrtaḥ*; and *saṃmūrchitaḥ* by virtue of belonging to the *tārakādi* group (Pāṇini V.2.36), which takes the suffix *itac* (227). The root *smurch* is used in the sense of forgetting (*vismṛti*). It takes the form *smūrchati*; the noun is *smūrchā*. Durga states that *sphurch* is also used in the sense of forgetting: *sphūrchati*, *sphūrṇaḥ* (228). [Note: In manuscript C, the meaning is given as "expanded" (*vistṛta*).]

23. *yuccha* means to be negligent (*pramāda*). *yucchati*. (229) *uch* is *uñch*. *Uñcha* means gathering (*uccayana*). *Uñchati*, *uñchāṃcakāra*. *Uñchitaḥ*, *śiloñchanam*; the meaning is "gathering gleanings" (*śiloccayana*). (230) *uchī* means to fade away (*vivāsa*). *Vivāsa* means destruction; the meaning is "completion. *Ucchliti*. *Uṣṭaḥ*; when the night has faded at dawn (*uṣasi*), he begot a son. These two [roots] need not be recited here, because the desired forms are established precisely by their belonging to the *tudādi* class (VI.1.7). (231) *vṛja*, *dhraji*, *dhraja*, *dhvaji*—these mean "to go. *Varjati*, *varīvṛjyate*.

By the rule *rīg ṛdupadhasya* (Pāṇini VII.4.90), there is the substitution *rīk*; some say that this [root] has *i* and *u* as its penultimate vowels: *veñjati*. [From the roots] *dhrañj*, *dhraj*, and *dhvañj*: *dhrañjati*, *dhrajati*, *dhvañjati*. Some say *dhvaj* [is the root]: *dhvajati*, *dhvajaḥ*. By the rule *ato halādeḥ* (Pāṇini VII.2.7), there is no *vṛddhi* in the case of *sica*: *adhvajīt*.

*adhvājīt* (236. 233. 232. 239. 238). *kūj* means "to make an indistinct sound": *kūjati*; *kūjitam* (240). *arj* and *sarj* mean "to acquire. [From *arj*: *arjati*, *ānarja*, *arjijiṣati*. By the rule *arjidṛśikamyami* (Uṇ. I, 28), the suffix *u* is applied: *ṛjuḥ*. By the rule *arjer ṇiluk ca* (Uṇ. III, 58), the suffix *unan* is applied with the elision of *ṇi*: *arjunaḥ*. By the rule *arjer ṛja ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 28), the suffix *iṣan* is applied with the change of the root to *ṛj*: *ṛjīṣam*, meaning "the vessel for baking flour. *Sarjati*; *sarjikā*. [The suffix *ikan* is applied] after the roots *kṛṣ*, *cam*, *tan*, *dhani*, *sarj*, and *kharj*.

*Ūḥ* (Uṇ. I, 82): *sarjūḥ*. *garj* in the sense of sound (*śabda*). He roars (*garjati*). That which is roared is thunder (*garjitam*, stanitam). *tarj* in the sense of threatening (*bhartsana*). He threatens (*tarjati*). In the *curādi* group (X, 142), he causes to threaten (*tarjayate*). *karj* and *kharj* in the sense of pain (*vyathana*). He suffers pain (*karjati*, *kharjati*). From the rule *kṛṣicami* (Uṇ. I, 82), the suffix *u* is applied: *kharjūḥ*. *kharj* also in the sense of cleaning (*mārjana*). From the rule *kharjapiñjādibhya ūrolacau* (Uṇ. IV, 90), [the suffixes] *ūra* and *ulac* are applied: *kharjūraḥ*. (246, 247)

The root *aja* means "to go" and "to cast. In the context of the *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes, by the rule *ajer vy aghañapoḥ* (Pāṇini II.4.56), the substitution of *vi* for *aja* occurs: *saṃvivāya*, *saṃvīya*. The fact that the acute accent (*udāttatva*) applies before *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes beginning with *val* is a sign (*liṅga*) that the substitution of *vī* is not obligatory; for *vī* itself is unaccented (*anudātta*), as seen in *prājitā rathasya* and *pravetā* (cf. II.4.56 Bh.). Why specify "before *val*"? Consider *samajyate*. By the rule *vā yau* (II.4.57), *vī* [is optionally substituted].

The suffix *khaś* is applied after the roots √aj, √dheṭ, √tud, and √hā when preceded by *pra*, *ava*, *vi*, and *ā* respectively, as well as after √aj, √dhā, √tud, and √hā when preceded by *vāta*, *śunī*, *tila*, and *śardha*. (Pāṇini III.2.28). Examples: *vātamajā* (deer), from √aj (*to go*) with the sense "going"; *aja* (goat), from √aj (*to drive/impel*) with the sense "driving"; *ajā* (she-goat); *vyajana* (fan). Regarding the root √aj, the suffix *ap* is applied after *sam* and *ud* when referring to animals (Pāṇini III.3.69): *samajaḥ* (a herd of animals), *udajaḥ* (the driving forth of animals). In other senses, the suffix *ghañ* is used: *samājaḥ* (an assembly), *udājaḥ* (driving out). In these cases, there is an absence of *kutva* (the substitution of *k* for *j*) due to the rule *ajivrajyoś ca* (Pāṇini VII.3.60).

In the case of *samajyā* and *sabhā*, the suffix *kyap* is applied by Pāṇini III.3.99 (*samajaniṣada...*), and because they are technical names (*saṃjñā*), there is no substitution of *v* for *ū*. The form *gocara* is correct by Pāṇini III.3.119 (*gocarasaṃcara...*) with the suffix *vyac*. By Uṇādi-sūtra II.48 (*ajer aja ca*), the form *ajina* is derived; and by Uṇādi-sūtra IV.130 (*ajyatibhyām*), [the forms *ajya* and *ajana* are derived].
(Note 1: K and C read *vraji* and *vraja*; in the Śāradā script, *dh* and *v* are often confused. Note 2: C reads *prājaṇam*. I.24.

From the root *iṇ*: *ājir* means "battle. From *pāde* and *ca* (Uṇ. IV, 131): *padājiḥ*. From *ajira-śiśira-* (Uṇ. I, 54), we have *ajiram*; because [the rule] applies extensively (*bahulam*) in names (*saṃjñā*) and Vedic meters (*chandas*), there is no substitution of *v* for *i* according to *annavadhakagātravicakṣaṇājirādyartham* (Pāṇini II, 4, 54, 11–12). From *aji-vṛ-rībhyo nic ca* (Uṇ. III, 38), we have the suffix *ṇu*: *veṇuḥ*. From *rāsnāsāsnā-* (Uṇ. III, 15), we have *vīṇā*. (248) From *kaja* in the sense of intoxication (*made*): *kajati*. (251)

*Khaja* means "to churn. *Mantha* means "stirring. It churns (*khajati*). From the root *khaj*, the suffix *ākan* is applied (cf. *Uṇādi-sūtra* IV, 13): *khajāka* is a churning-stick; *khajākā* is a ladle; *khaja* is the churning-staff of those who cook various substances. (250) [Root] *khañj* means "lameness of movement. It limps (*khañjati*). *Khañja* is one who is lame; *khañjana-udaka* is mustard; *khañjana* is the *khañjarīṭa* bird. (252) [Root] *ejṛ* means "to tremble. It trembles (*ejati*). By the rule *ejeḥ khaś* (Pāṇini III, 2, 28), [one forms] *aṅgamejayaḥ* ("one who causes the limbs to tremble").

The root *ejṛ* (I, 192), meaning "to shine" or "to move," takes the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffixes; thus, *ejate* (253). The root *sphūrjā* with the prefix *ut-* (*ṭuosphūrjā*) means "the crashing of a thunderbolt. The "crashing of a thunderbolt" (*vajraniṣpeṣaḥ*) refers to the roar of a lightning bolt (*aśaninirghoṣaḥ*).

*sphūrjati*; *sphūrjaḥ*. The long vowel in the root is for the sake of making [the rule] *dīrghoccāraṇaṃ dīrghasya* (Pāṇini VIII. 2. 78) non-obligatory. By *oditaś ca* (VIII. 2. 45), there is the substitution of *n* for the final consonant in the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*): *sphūrṇaḥ*. By *coḥ kuḥ* (VIII. 2. 30), the palatal *c* is replaced by the guttural *k*, and by *āditaś ca* (VII. 2. 16), the augment *iṭ* is not added. By *vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ* (VII. 2. 17), the augment is optional in the sense of the action itself (*bhāva*) or the beginning of an action (*ādikarman*): *sphūrjitena* or *sphūrṇena*; *prasphūrjitaḥ* or *prasphūrṇaḥ*. By *ṭvito 'thuc* (III. 3. 89), the suffix *athuc* is added: *sphūrjathuḥ*. (254)

The root *kṣi* means "to perish. [From it derive] *kṣayati* (he perishes) and *kṣetā* (he will perish). Due to the requirements of the grammatical system (*lakṣya*), the augment *iṭ* does not occur here. And [the author] will state: "In the list of roots, among those that are anudātta, an udātta vowel is sometimes inserted before the suffix *kta*."

Even though it is unaccented (*anudātta*), it becomes long by virtue of the preceding accented vowels, according to *kṣiyaḥ, niṣṭhāyām aṇyadarthe* (Pāṇini VI.4.59–60); and by *kṣiyo dīrghāt* (VIII.2.46), the *niṣṭhā* suffix receives the cerebral nasal (*ṇ*): *kṣīṇaḥ*. By *vākrośadainyayoḥ* (VI.4.61), [the same form] is *kṣitaḥ* or *kṣīṇaḥ*. In the *tudādi* class, *kṣi* means "dwelling" and "going" (VI.114): *kṣiyati*. In the *kryādi* class, *kṣiṣ* means "injury" (IX.35): *kṣiṇāti*. In the *svādi* class, among *ṛ*, *kṣi*, *ciri*, *jiri*, *dāśa*, *dṝ* meaning "injury" (V.29–34): *kṣiṇoti*. (255)

*kṣīj* [is used] in the sense of an indistinct sound: *kṣījati*, *cikṣīja*. (256) *laja* and *laji* are used in the sense of reviling: *lajati*, *lañjati*. The root meaning "to speak" belongs to the *curādi* group (X, 244): *lañjayati*. (257, 258) *lāja* and *lāji* are used in the sense of parching: *lājati*, *lāñjati*, *lājyate*, *lāñjyate*. Regarding the word *lājāḥ*, by the rule *ajivrajyoś ca* (Pāṇini VII, 3, 60), there is an absence of *kutva* (the substitution of *k* for *j*) because of the particle *ca*. According to Candra (Ca. Dh. I, 77), these four [roots] signify reviling. (259, 260)
1. All manuscripts read *pade*; cf. VI.3.52. 2. 251 s.v. 250. 3. All manuscripts read *taṅānau*. 4. So all manuscripts. 25.
*jaja* and *jaji* mean "in battle. [The forms] *jajati*, *jañjati* (26L 262).

The root *tuji* is used in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*): *tojati*, *tuñjati*. It is also used in the sense of protection (*pālana*). [That which is] "pushed up" (*tuñjyate*) is called *tuṅga*; this is formed with the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.19). Thus, the earth is "pushed up" (*tuñjitā bhūḥ*). In the *curādi* group, it has the meaning of shining (*bhāsārtha*) (X.215); likewise, *tuji*, *piji*, and *luji* are used in the senses of injury, taking strength, and dwelling (*niketana*) (X.30–31): *tuñjayati*. *Tuñja* means a dwelling (*niketana*) (263, 264).

The roots *gaja*, *gaji*, *gṛja*, *gṛji*, *maja*, *muja* have the meaning "to sound. *gajati*; having sounded (*gajitvā*). *gañjati*; having scorned (*gañjitvā*). *Gañjā* is a tavern; *gañjaḥ* is a treasury. *garjati*; *garjitam*; *garjita*. *gṛñjati*; *gṛñjanam* is a specific kind of root. *majati*. *muñjati*; *muñjaḥ* is a type of grass. They also say *muj* and *mṛj*: *mojati*, *mṛñjati*. *gaja* also means "in intoxication" (*madane*). Intoxication is the arising of passion. *Gajati*; with the suffix *ac* (Pāṇini III.1.134), *gajaḥ* is an elephant. In the *curādi* class, according to *gaja inarca mārja* (X.106, 107), one forms *gājayati* (265–270).

The root *vaj* (or *vraj*) means "to go. It forms *vajati*; *vāja-* means "speed" or "wing. From *vrajati*, the perfect form *vavrāja* is derived; by the rule *vadavraja* (Pāṇini VI.1.15), there is *vṛddhi*: *avrājīt*. By the rule *vrajayajor bhāve kyap* (III.3.98), the suffix *kyap* is applied to form *vrajyā* ("going") and *pavrajyā* ("renunciation"). In the sense of "pasture" and so forth, *vraja-* is correct by III.3.119. With the suffix *ṇyat* (III.1.124), we have *vrājyam*. By the rule *ajivrajyoś ca* (VII.3.60), there is an absence of *kutva* (the substitution of *g* for *j*). By the rule *kvib vaci* (Uṇādi II.57), the suffix *kvip* is added and the vowel is lengthened.

By [Pāṇini 8.2.36], *pauvraṭ* and *vraśca*, there is the substitution of *ṣ*; thus, *parivrājakaḥ*. In the *curādi* group, *vaja* is used in the sense of "not preparing a path" and "going" (X.75): *vājayati*. (271, 272). These are the roots with udātta vowels that are marked with an indicatory letter *ṅ* (udāttetaḥ). 251.

The root *aṭṭ* is used in the senses of "transgressing" and "injuring. From here on, thirty-five roots ending in *ṣaḍ* are *seṭ* (having the augment *iṭ*) and *ātmanepadī* (taking the middle voice). *Atikrama* means "transgression" or "overstepping. This root is read with a dental *t* as its penultimate letter (*topadha*) for the sake of hearing the sound *t* when the suffix *kvip* is applied; the substitution of *ṣṭu* (the retroflex *ṭ*) was not made because it is intended to manifest the specific form of the root. Thus: *aṭṭate*, *atiṭṭiṣate*. The forms *aṭṭaḥ*, *aṭṭanam*, and *at* (with *kvip*) follow Pāṇini III.3.108.9. According to the view that it has a dental *t* as its penultimate letter, the rule *na ndrāḥ* (Pāṇini VI.1.3) applies so that the *n* and *d* are not reduplicated: *aṭṭiṭiṣate*. Others, however, have stated it as *aḍḍ*: *aḍḍate*, *aḍḍiḍiṣate* (273).

*veṣṭ* means "to wrap" (*veṣṭane*). Wrapping (*veṣṭanam*) is binding (*granthanam*), rolling (*loṭanam*), and shrinking away (*parihāṇiḥ*). [Examples: *veṣṭate*, *aveṣṭata*. A "folded arm" (*praveṣṭaḥ bāhuḥ*) is one that is wrapped (*veṣṭitaḥ*). Regarding the rule *vibhāṣā veṣṭiceṣṭyoḥ* (Pāṇini VII.4.96), there is optionally the substitution of *ā* for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) when the causative suffix *ṇic* followed by *caṅ* is applied: *avaveṣṭat* or *aviveṣṭat*. *ceṣṭ* means "to strive" (*ceṣṭāyām*). Striving (*ceṣṭā*) is effort (*īhā*). [Examples: *ceṣṭate*, *aceṣṭata*, *aceṣṭata*. *goṣṭ* and *loṣṭ* mean "to heap together" (*saṃghāte*). [Examples: *goṣṭate*, *loṣṭate*, *aluloṣṭat*. According to the *Uṇādi* list (III.92), *loṣṭaḥ* refers to a clod of earth (*mṛtpiṇḍaḥ*). (276, 277)

To move, to rub against. From the roots *ghaṭṭi*, *vand*, and *vidi*, [the suffix] *yuc* is applied (Pāṇini III.3.107): *ghaṭṭanā*; *araghaṭṭaḥ* (a water-wheel), *udghaṭṭanam* (striking). In the *cur*-class (X.87), one causes to rub (*ghaṭṭayati*). (278) 1 *soalle* in the manuscripts; also Hemacandra Dhātupāṭha I.170. 2 See also Uṇādi-sūtra II.59. 3 Pāṇini I.26: *pariṇāhaḥ*.

*Aṭhi* means "to go. *Aṇṭhate*. (280a) *Vaṭhi* means "solitary wandering" (*ekacaryā*). It refers to the understanding of one's own conduct as being without a companion; [thus] *vaṇṭhate*. A *vaṇṭha* is a warrior who has been given wealth. (281) *Maṭhi* and *kaṭhi* mean "sorrow" (*śoka*). Here, sorrow means "meditative brooding" (*adhyāna*). [Thus] *maṇṭhate*. *Utkaṇṭhate*, *utkaṇṭhā*. In the *curādi* class (X, 303), [one finds] *utkaṇṭhayati*. (282, 283) 2.

*muṭhi* means to flee. *muṇṭhate* (284). *heṭha* in the sense of affliction: *heṭhate*, *jiheṭhe*; by the rule *ṇau caṅy upadhāyā hrasvaḥ* (VII. 4. 1), [the form] is *ajīhiṭhat*; with the causative suffix (*ṇau*), it is *heṭhayati*. *Heṭhanā* means deceit (*śāṭhyam*) (285). Also, *eṭha*: *eṭhate* (286).

*hiḍi* in the sense of movement and disregard: *hiṇḍate*. With the suffix *yuc* (Pāṇini III.2.149): *hiṇḍanaḥ* (287). *huḍi* in the sense of massing together: *huṇḍate*. *Huṇḍikā* is a seal (288). *kuḍi* in the sense of burning: *kuṇḍate*. *Kuṇḍam*, *kuṇḍī* (feminine) are vessels; *kuṇḍaḥ* is one born of adultery; in the *uṇādi* list (I.106), *kuṇḍalam* [is derived]. In the *curādi* class, *kuḍi* is used in the sense of protecting (cf. X.45): *kuṇḍayati* (289).

*Vaṭi* means "to divide. Dividing (*vibhājana*) is the act of making into portions (*bhāgīkaraṇa*), as well as the absence of a covering (*carmābhāva*). From the root *vaṇṭ*, we have *vaṇṭate*; from *vaṇṭ* comes *vaṇṭana* (the act of dividing) and *vaṇṭa* (a portion). In the *cur*-class (X, 48), it is *vaṇḍayati*. Some say that *vaṭi* is a parasmaipada root: *vaṇṭati*, *vaṇṭyate*; *vaṇṭa* refers to an elephant. However, Nandin reads it in a different manner: *vaṭi* (3) in the sense of "dividing," and *vaḍi* (3) in the sense of "encircling" (*veṣṭana*). (290)

And *maḍi*. Because of the word "and" (*ca*), [the suffixes apply] also in the sense of dividing, as well as in other meanings distinct from the separate sūtra. [It forms: *maṇḍate* (he adorns). *Maṇḍaḥ* is the best of flavors; *maṇḍakaḥ*; *maṇḍalam*; *maṇḍūraḥ* is rust or iron-dross; *maṇḍapaḥ*. By the rule *ṇer itnuc* (Uṇ. III.29): *maṇḍayitnuḥ*. By the rule *śalimaṇḍibhyām ūkan* (cf. Uṇ. IV.42): *maṇḍūkaḥ*. The root *maḍi* in the sense of adornment (I.344) is parasmaipada: *maṇḍati* (291). *bhaḍi* in the sense of reviling. [It forms: *bhaṇḍate*. *Bhaṇḍaḥ*; *bhāṇḍam*. In the curādigaṇa, *bhaḍi* in the sense of auspiciousness (X.50): *bhaṇḍayati*; *bhaṇḍanā* (292).

*Piḍi* means "to press together. [In the *ātmanepada*: *piṇḍate*, *piṇḍyate*. A *piṇḍa* is a globule (*gola*) or a ball (*piṇḍī*). In the *curādi* group (X, 131), it is *piṇḍayati* (293). *Muḍi* means "immersion" (*majjana*). Immersion implies purification (*śuddhi*) and subordination (*nyagbhāva*). [In the *ātmanepada*: *muṇḍate*; [the past passive participle: *muṇḍaḥ*. In the sense of "cutting" (*khaṇḍana*), *muḍi* is conjugated in the *parasmaipada*: *muṇḍati*. By rule III, 1, 21 (*muṇḍamiśra*), the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied:

*muṇḍayati* (294). *Tudi* means "breaking" (*toḍana*). Breaking is indeed violence (*hiṃsā*). [In the *ātmanepada*: *tuṇḍate*, *tuṇḍyate*. [The noun: *tuṇḍam*. In the *uṇādi* group (IV, 117), there is *tuṇḍiḥ* (295).

1. 280 b.s. after 356. 2. KC omits. 3. All manuscripts read thus; cf. 322 and 351. 4. K: *maṇḍūkaṃ*. 27. I: *huḍi varaṇe*. *Varaṇam* means acceptance (*svīkāraḥ*). [The root] *huṇḍate*. *Huṇḍaḥ* means a ram (*meṣaḥ*). (296) 1.

*Sphuḍi* means to blossom; it forms *sphuṇḍate*. *Caḍi* means anger; it forms *caṇḍate*. From *caṇḍa* and *caṇḍī*, the suffix *āl* is added by Uṇādi-sūtra I.116: *caṇḍālaḥ*. In the curādigaṇa (X.48a), there is *caṇḍayati*. *Śaḍi* means sickness and massing; it begins with a palatal (*tālavyādi*). It forms *śaṇḍate*. *Śaṇḍaḥ* refers to the root-stock of lotuses and the like. From the root *sanoti* (VIII.2), by the rule of diversity (*bāhulakāt*) [III.3.1], there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*, and the suffix *ḍa* (Uṇādi I.113): *ṣaṇḍaḥ* means a bull set at liberty. (299)

The root *taḍ* means "to strike. From it comes *taṇḍate*. *Vitaṇḍā* [is derived from this]. *Tāṇḍava* is that which was proclaimed by *Taṇḍu*. *Taṇḍula* [is formed] by the rule *vṛṅ-luṭi-tanitāḍibhya ulac taṇḍa ca* (Uṇādi V.9); this is merely clinging to the straw of the *kuśa* and *kāśa* grasses (referring to a weak argument). The root *paḍ* means "to go. From it comes *paṇḍate*. *Paṇḍitaḥ* [is derived from this]. *Pāṇḍu* refers to jaundice and a pale complexion. By the rule *naga-pāṃsu-pāṇḍubhyo raḥ* (V.2.107, Kāśikā): *pāṇḍuraḥ*. However, *Pāṇḍu* is derived by the Uṇādi rule (I.38). *Paṇḍaḥ* means a eunuch (Uṇādi I.113). (300–301)

*kaḍi* means to rub. *kaṇḍate*. *kaṇḍuḥ*, *kāṇḍaḥ*, *kaṇḍurā*—these denote a collection of sinews; *kaṇḍolaḥ* denotes a basket. (302) *Khaḍi* means to churn. *khaṇḍate*. *khaṇḍitaḥ*, *khaṇḍaḥ*. In the *curādi* class (*X*, 44), *khaḍa* and *khaḍi* mean to break: *khaṇḍayati*. (303a) *Khuḍi* means impairment of movement. *khuṇḍate*. *khoḍaḥ* is derived according to the *pṛṣodarādi* group (*VI*, 3, 109). In the *curādi* class (*X*, 47), *khuḍi* means to break: *khuṇḍayati*. (303b) *Heḍṛ* means to disregard. *heḍate*. *heḍaḥ* means contempt; [it is formed] with the suffix *asun* (*Uṇ.*, IV, ...).

188) *sāntaḥ* [ending in -s], by *aci* (III, 1, 134); *heḍo dantaḥ* [the root *heḍ* ends in -t]; and by *guroś ca halaḥ* (III, 3, 103), we have *helā*; [from *heḍ*] *ajiheḍat*. In the *ghaṭādi* group, *heḍa* means "to surround" (*veṣṭane*) (I, 815): *heḍati*, or *hiḍayati* (304). *vāḍṛ* [means] "in the sense of flooding" (*āplāvye*). Flooding (*āplāvyam*) is the act of flooding (*āplāvanam*). [From *vāḍ*] *vāḍate*. *Vāḍaḥ* is a horse (*aśvaḥ*), [and] *vālaḥ*; in the *uṇādi* [section], *vaḍavā* (305). Some say [it is derived] from *vali* (I, 520). *drāḍṛ* and *dhrāḍṛ* mean "to fall apart" (*viśaraṇe*). [From these] *drāḍate*, *dhrāḍate* (307, 308).

The root *śāḍṛ* is used in the sense of praise (*ślāghā*). [Present tense: *śāḍate*, *śālate*. [Derivatives: *śālā* (a hall), *śāliḥ* (rice), *guṇaśālī* (possessing virtues); *śālūkam* (the bulbous root of a lotus, etc.), or from *śal-* (DhP I, 519). From *śali* and *maṇḍi*, the suffix *-ūkañ* is added. These [roots] ending in an unaccented vowel (*anudātteta*) are 286 in number. The root *śauṭṛ* is used in the sense of pride (*garva*). From here until the end of the *gaḍ*-group (DhP I, 384), seventy roots are *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment). 1. *bhuḍi* (in the sense of choosing/acceptance): *varaṇaṃ* means acceptance (*svīkāraḥ*). [Present tense: *bhuṇḍate*. *Bhuṇḍaḥ* means audacious (*dhṛṣṭaḥ*); *bhuṇḍam* means the hip (*kaṭiḥ*). 2. *Taṇḍu*: That which was taught by him is called *Tāṇḍavam* (a type of dance). See Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 515.
And [the roots] ending in *smā* take the *ātmanepada* endings.
*Śauṭati*, *aśuśauṭat* (VII.4.2). From the roots *kṛ*, *śṛ*, *pṛ*, *kaṭi*, *paṭi*, and *śauṭi*, the suffix *īran* is added (Uṇ. IV.30): *śauṭīraḥ* (310).
*Yauṭṛ* means connection; connection is *śleṣa*. *Yauṭati*, *ayuyauṭat* (311).

The roots *mreṭṛ* and *mleṭṛ* are used in the sense of "madness. One says *mreḍati*. Some read this as *mreḍṛ*; [the term] *āmreḍitam* is defined in Pāṇini Sūtra VIII.1.2. [One says] *mleṭati*. The followers of Durga (*Daurgāḥ*) include *meṭṛ* as well; [an example is] *amiṣeṇeṭat* (Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.1.313 and 3.1.312).

The root *kaṭ* is used in the senses of "raining" and "covering. In the sense of raining and covering, it forms *kaṭati*. From this comes *kaṭaḥ* ("mat" or "cover"). According to Pāṇini VI.1.58 (*hmyantakṣaṇ-*), there is no vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) in the *sic* augment: thus, *akaṭīt*. Furthermore, from this root we derive *kaṭiḥ*, *kaṭīraḥ*, and *kaṭuḥ*. By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.82 (*kṛkadikaḍikaṭibhyo 'mbac*), we have *kaṭambaḥ*. By Uṇādi-sūtra III.1 (*varaṭ*), we have *kaṭvaraḥ*; *kaṭvarī* refers to a condiment made with buttermilk. Also, *kaṭakam*. The form *kāṭaḥ* is derived by adding the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.19). (315)

The roots *aṭ* and *paṭ* mean "to move. From *aṭ*, one has *aṭati* ("he moves"); from *aṭanaḥ* and *aṭyartyaśūrṇotīnām upasaṃkhyānāt* (Pāṇini I.1.22, Kāśikā), the intensive suffix *yaṅ* is applied: *aṭāṭyate vṛthādya lokaḥ* ("the world wanders aimlessly today"), *aṭāṭyā*; in the *uṇādi* group, *aṭaviḥ* (Uṇ. IV.133) and *aṭaniḥ*. From *paṭ*: *paṭati*; *paṭaḥ*, *paṭī*, *paṭīraḥ*, *paṭuḥ*; with the suffix *tanaṭ* (cf. Uṇ. III.150): *paṭṭanam*, *paṭalaḥ*; with the suffix *olaḥ* (cf. Uṇ. I.67) after *kapi*, *kaṇḍi*, *kaṭi*, and *paṭi*: [various derivatives].

*Paṭola*: as for *paṭaha*, it is derived with the suffix *ḍa* [by Pāṇini III.2.101] in the sense that "it is struck upon a cloth" (*paṭe hanyate*). In the *curādi* class, *paṭa* and *vaṭa* mean "to tie" (X.311) and are without a final nasal (*adanta*): *paṭayati*. Likewise, *paṭa* means "to shine" (X.212): *pāṭayati* (317, 318). *Raṭa* means "to speak. *Raṭati*; future *raṭitā* (319). *Laṭa* means "childhood" (*bālya*). Childhood is the play of a child. *Laṭati*; *lalāṭa*. *Laṭakaḥ*, *Lāṭaḥ*, *Lāṭakaḥ*. By the rule *aśū-pruṣi-laṭi* (Uṇ. I.151), *laṭvā* means "a small bee" (*bhramaraka*) (320).

The root *śaṭ* [is used] in the four senses of breaking, splitting, going, and causing dejection. It forms *śaṭati*, *śāṭī*, and *śāṭaka*. It begins with the palatal *tālavya*. *Vaṭ* means "to surround" (*veṣṭane*). One surrounds a rope (*rajjuṃ vaṭati*). [Derivatives include]: *vaṭaḥ*, *vaṭiḥ*, *vaṭakam*, *vāṭaḥ*, *vāṭī*—meaning an enclosure or fence (*vṛtiḥ*), *vaṭuḥ*, and *vaṭākaraḥ* meaning a rope. *Vaṭ* and *bhaṭ* are used in the sense of speaking (*bhāṣaṇe*) [according to Dhātupāṭha I. 816]. With the suffix *mit*: *vaṭayati*. *Paṭ* and *vaṭ* are used in the sense of weaving or stringing (*granthē*) [according to Dhātupāṭha X. 311]; they end in the vowel *a* (*adantaḥ*). [322]

*Khiṭ* means "to terrify. Terrifying is the arising of fear. One *kheṭati*. *Ākheṭaḥ* (hunting), *kheṭaḥ* (a village, and a low person). In the *curādi* group (X, 328), *kheṭayati*; *khaḍga-kheṭakau* (sword and shield) are weapons (324). *Śiṭ* and *ṣiṭ* mean "disrespect. These two have palatal and retroflex initials respectively. [One] *śeṭati*, *seṭati*, *siṣeṭa* (325, 326). 1P *varac*, 2P *aṭavī*, 3 cf. Hem. Uṇ. 680.

29. *Jaṭ* and *jhaṭ* mean "to entangle. *Jaṭati*; [noun] *jaṭā*. *Jhaṭati*, *ujjhaṭati*; by [Pāṇini III, 1, 134] *aci* and by [Pāṇini III, 3, 18–19] *ghañ*, *jhāṭaḥ* means a thicket (*ṣaṇḍaḥ*). *Bhaṭ* means "to hire" (*bhṛtiḥ*); *bhṛtiḥ* means wages (*vetanam*). [From this root: *bhaṭati*; [nouns] *bhaṭaḥ*, *bhāṭiḥ*, *bhāṭakam*, *bhaṭitram* (329).

From the root *taṭ* [in the sense of] height: *taṭaṭi*, *taṭam*, *taṭākam*, *tāṭakaḥ*. (330) From *khaṭa* [in the sense of] desiring (*kāṅkṣā*): one who desires is *kāṅkṣaḥ*; [it occurs] when the meaning of the verbal root is qualified by desire. *khaṭati*. *khaṭas* [means] grass; *khaṭakāmukhaḥ* [means] a type of hand-gesture; *kliṭikā*. By [the rule] *aśū-pruṣi-laṭi* (Uṇ. I. 151), the suffix *kvan* is applied: *khaṭvā*. (331) From *naṭa* and *nṛt* [in the sense of] dancing: *naṭati*; *naṭaḥ*. Some say [it means] "bending" (*natā*). Because it belongs to the *ghaṭādi* group (Pāṇ. I. 818), [the causative forms are] *naṭayati*, *anīnaṭat*. In the *curādi* group, *naṭa* [is used] in the sense of trickling out (*avasyandana*) (X. 12): *unnāṭayati*, *nāṭakam*. (332)

The root *piṭ* is used in the senses of a basket and a collection. *Peṭati*. *Peṭakaḥ*, *peṭā*, and *mañjūṣā* [mean] a chest; *piṭaḥ*, *piṭakaḥ*, and *kaṇḍolaḥ* [mean] a basket; *piṭakaṃ* [also means] a pustule. (333) *Haṭ* is used in the sense of shining. *Haṭati*; *hāṭakam* [means] gold. (334) *Ṣaṭ* is used in the sense of a limb or part. *Saṭati*; *siṣāṭayiṣati*. *Saṭā* [means] a mane. (335) *Luṭ* is used in the sense of rolling about. Durga says it means "agitating. *Loṭati*. Because it belongs to the *divādi* class (DhP IV. 113), one forms *luṭyati*. *Luṭ* is also used in the sense of shining (X. 214): *loṭayati*. The Draviḍas say *luḍeti*: *āloḍitaḥ*, *vyālolaḥ*. (336)

*ciṭa* means "to be sent as a servant. *Praiṣya* is the state of being a servant (*dāsatva*). [The root] *ceṭati*. [From it derive] *ceṭakaḥ*, *ceṭaḥ*, *ceṭiḥ*, *ceṭī* (337). *piṭa* means "sound. It is listed twice because of the difference in meaning (cf. sūtra 333). [The root] *peṭati*. Some say *piḍa*: [from it] *peḍati*; *peḍaḥ*, *peḍā* means a chest (*mañjūṣā*) (338). *viṭa* means "to revile. [The root] *veṭati*. [From it derive] *viṭaḥ*, *veṭakaḥ*. Nandī says that this [root] ends in *ḍ*: *viḍālaḥ* (cat), derived by *tamiviśiviḍi* (Uṇādi-sūtra I.117) with the suffix *kālan*. For this very reason, Malla says *viṭa* means "sound" and *piṭa* means "reviling," explaining it with a detailed analysis in another section of his *Paryaṭṭaka* (339).
The root *heṭh* is used in the sense of harming (*vibādhā*). One says *heṭhati*. However, Kauśika does not mention these [roots];

rather, he states: *iṭ*, *kiṭ*, and *kaṭī* mean "to go. Thus: *eṭati*, *keṭati*, and *kaṭati*. Because it is marked with the *īt* indicatory letter (*īdit*), by rule VII.2.14, we have *kaṭṭaḥ* and *kaṭṭavān*; and the word *kaṭaka*. The root *kaṭe* in the sense of "raining" (DhP 3.15) is for the sake of distinguishing its meaning. Others say that this root is marked with the *it* indicatory letter and has the vowel *ī* joined to it: *kaṇṭati*. From this come *kaṇṭāphalaṃ* (the jackfruit tree), *panasaḥ*, and *kaṇṭakaḥ* (a thorn). "The Lord of Day rises, while the Moon goes to its setting. Likewise: 'While the rope of rays, stretched upward, is rising...'"
When the sun has gone to its setting and the moon has set (*Śiśupālavadha* IV.20).
(340–342) 1. *saḥ* (with dental *n*) in all manuscripts; in C it is corrected from *ṇ*. P reverses [the order]. 3. K and C omit. 4. P reads *vibhañjyāha*. 1. 30.

The root *maḍi* is used in the sense of adorning (*bhūṣā*). It forms *maṇḍati*. By the rule *krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaś ca* (Pāṇini III.2.151), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *maṇḍanaḥ*. In the *cur*-class (X.49), it forms *maṇḍayati* and *maṇḍanā*. By the rule *śalimaṇḍibhyām ūkañ* (Uṇādi IV.42), *maṇḍūkaḥ* ("frog") is formed. The root *kuḍi* is used in the sense of deficiency (*vaikalye*). It forms *kuṇḍati*; hence *kuṇḍaḥ*. According to Kauśika and Durga, [the root] is *kuṭi*: it forms *kuṇṭati*; hence *kuṇṭaḥ*.

*Muḍi* means "to crush" (*pramardane*). [One] shaves (*muṇḍati*); *muṇḍalī*. Durga says it is *muṭeti*: [one] squeezes (*moṭati*); having squeezed (*muṭitvā*, *moṭitvā*), squeezed (*muṭitaḥ*, *moṭitaḥ*), squeezed (*muṭitam*, *moṭitam*), thoroughly squeezed (*pramuṭitaḥ*, *pramoṭitaḥ*); *āmoṭanam*. In the *curādi* class (cf. X, 72), [one] causes to squeeze (*moṭayati*). Some say it is *puḍī*: [one] marks (*puṇḍati*); *puṇḍarīka*, *puṇḍrekṣu*, *tripuṇḍraka*, *puṇḍra* (the sectarian mark on the forehead), the *Puṇḍra* country (346). *Cuḍi* means "to become small" (*alpībhāve*); [one] diminishes (*cuṇḍati*). Some say it is *cuṭī*: [one] cuts off (*cuṇṭati*). Durga says it is *cuṭeti*: [one] pierces (*coṭati*); piercing upwards (*uccoṭanam*) (347).

*Muḍi* means "to break. It is listed again because of a difference in meaning (sūtra 346); for this very reason, Kaṇṭha states: *muḍi* [is used] in the senses of breaking and crushing. *Muṭī* is found in the works of Kauśika and Durga: *muṇṭati*. *Vaṭi* means "to divide": *vaṇṭati*, *vaṇṭaḥ*. In the *curādi* group (cf. X, 48), it is *vaṇṭayati* (351). *Ruṭi* and *luṭi* mean "theft": *ruṇṭati*; *luṇṭati*, *luṇṭyate*. By the rule *jalpabhikṣa* (Pāṇini III, 2, 155), the suffix *ṣākan* is applied: *luṇṭākaḥ* (a robber). Some read *ruṭhi* and *luṭhī*: *luṇṭhiḥ*. In the *curādi* group (X, 27), it is *luṇṭhayati* (349, 350).

The roots *sphaṭi* and *sphuṭi* mean "to burst apart. *Sphaṇṭati*. According to Nandisvāmin, [it is used in the sense of] "the garment bursts apart" (*vastraṃ sphaṭati*); [past participle] *sphaṭitam*; [derivatives] *karpūrasphaṭaḥ* (camphor-powder), *sphaṭikam* (crystal). [From *sphuṭ*] *sphoṭati*; [aorist] *asphuṭat*, *asphoṭīt*; [nouns] *sphoṭaḥ*, *āsphoṭaḥ*, *visphoṭaḥ*. In the *kuṭādi* group, *sphuṭ* means "to blossom": *sphuṭati*, *sphuṭaḥ*, *asphuṭīt*. And in the *curādi* group, *caṭa-sphuṭa* means "to split" (*bhede*) [X.182]: *sphoṭayati*. [The form] *sphuṭayati* is used in the sense of "making something burst" (*sphuṭaṃ karoti*) [X.368]. (352) 7

The root *paṭh* is used in the sense of "distinct speech. One *paṭhati*. By the rule *nau gadanada* (Pāṇini III.3.64), the suffix *ap* is optionally applied: *nipaṭhaḥ*, *nipāthaḥ*; and *nipaṭhitih*. Although the prohibition [of *iṭ*] by the rule *titutra* (VII.2.9) would apply, the augment *iṭ* is added by the rule *agrahādīnām* (VII.2.9, Vārttika 1).
The root *vaṭh* means "thickness" (*sthaulye*). One *vaṭhati*. *Vaṭharaḥ* means one whose intellect is not sharp (*atīkṣṇadhīḥ*). (353–354)

The root *maṭh* is used in the sense of "dwelling" and "a monastery. One *maṭhati*. From the root *maṭh*, the words *maṭhaḥ* ("monastery") and *maṭharaḥ* ("base person") are formed; the suffix *-ara-* occurs by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulakāt*, Pāṇini III.3.1). Regarding the suffix *-ara-* [in *janara-*], the suffix *-ṭha-* is added after *jan*. As for the forms *vanima-* and *manima-*, the suffix *-ic-* is added (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra V.38–39); however, since these are not observed in this [Uṇādi] list [at 355], [the derivation is as follows].

[Notes: 1. All manuscripts read this. 2. 343 appears before 340. 3. P reads *puṇḍrakam aśvatilakaḥ*. 4. K, C, and N read *Nandisvāmī*. 5. P reads *sphāṭayati*. 6. All manuscripts read this. 7. 351 appears before 349. 31 I.

The root *kaṭh* means "to live with difficulty. It forms *kaṭhati*. From the rule *Kaṭhicakibhyām oraḥ* (Uṇ. I, 65), we have *kaṭhoraḥ*. From the rule *bahulam anyatrāpi* (Uṇ. II, 49), we have *iṇac*: *kaṭhinaḥ*. (356) The root *aṭh* means "to go"; it forms *aṭhati*. (280b) The root *raṭh* means "to speak"; it forms *raṭhati*. (357) The root *haṭh* means "leaping" (*pluti*) and "binding with a stake" (*śaṅkubandhana*); that is, in the senses of leaping and binding with a stake. However, according to the Cāndras (Ca. Dh. I, 117), *haṭha* means "force" (*balātkāra*). It forms *haṭhati*; [the noun] *haṭhaḥ*. (358)

*Uṭha* means "to strike" (*upaghāta*): *uṭhati*, *uvoṭha*, *ūṭhuḥ*. According to the followers of Durga, there are also *ruṭha* and *luṭha*: *roṭhati*, *loṭhati* (DhP 361, 359, 360). *Piṭha* means "injury" (*hiṃsā*) and "affliction" (*saṃkleśa*): *peṭhati*. From this comes *piṭhara* ("pot") and *piṭhira*; also *pīṭha* ("seat"). [The suffix] *ṭhak* or *a* is applied after the root *pīṅ* (DhP IV, 33). *Śaṭha* means "deceit" (*kaitava*): *śaṭhati*; *śaṭhaḥ* ("deceitful"). In the *curādi* class, *śaṭha* and *śvaṭha* mean "lack of refinement" (*asaṃskāra*) and "motion" (*gati*): *śāṭhayati* (DhP X, 28, 29). (363)
The root *śuṭhi* means "obstruction of movement. One says *śuṇṭhati*. According to Durga, it is *śoṭhati*.

(364) *kuṭhi* and *ca* [are also roots]. One says *kuṇṭhati*. *Kuṇṭhaḥ* [is derived from this]. From *kuṇṭhi*, there is also the elision of *na*: *kuṭhāraḥ*. (365) *ruṭhi* (4) means "laziness" and "obstruction of movement. One says *ruṇṭhati*. (366)
*Śuṭh* means to dry up. *Śuṇṭhati*; *śuṇṭhī*. Kauśika did not study this [root]. In the *curādi* class (*X*, 104), *śuṇṭhayati* (367).

*Ruṭhi* and *luṭhi* mean to go: *ruṇṭhati*; *luṇṭhati*. In the *curādi* class, it means to steal (*X*, 27): *luṇṭhayati* (368, 369). *Cudḍa* means making a gesture (*hāva*). A *hāva* is the indication of an internal state (*bhāva*). *Cuḍḍati*; *cuḍḍam* is the vulva, and *culliḥ* (370) is a hearth.

Regarding the root *aḍḍ* in the sense of "to play": *aḍḍati*. According to [Aṣṭādhyāyī] VI.1.3, the *n* and *r* are not doubled: *aḍḍiḍiṣati*. Since it does not have a stop as its penultimate (*upadhā*), it becomes *aḍiḍḍiṣati*. There is also a distinction in the case of the *kvip* suffix (III.2.108, 9): *aḍḍanam* becomes *aṭ*; however, when there is a stop as the penultimate, it becomes *at*. The *Pañcikā* states that the same applies to *cuḍḍ* (370): *cuṭ*, *cut* (371).

*krīḍ* (to play): *krīḍati*, *acikrīḍat*. By the rule *anusaṃparibhyaś ca* (Pāṇini I.3.21), the Ātmanepada is used: *anukrīḍate*, *parikrīḍate*. Regarding *samo 'kūjane* (a Vārttika on I.3.21), it is stated that this [Ātmanepada] does not apply here: *saṃkrīḍanti śakaṭāni* ("the carts play together"). (Note: The manuscript variants and commentary notes provided in the source text—such as "KC upasaṃghāte," "P om. vā," references to Hemacandra's *Uṇādi-sūtra*, and the mention of the *Pañjikākāra*—are philological annotations regarding the specific recensions of the grammatical treatise and its commentaries.)
*tūḍṛ* means "to split. Splitting (*toḍana*) is rending. *tūḍati*. Durga says the root is *tuḍṛ*: *toḍati*.

(374) *hūḍṛ*, *huḍṛ*, *hauḍṛ* mean "to go. *hūḍati*; *hūḍa* is a goat. *hoḍati*; *hoḍa* [is a donkey]. *hauḍati*. (375, 376) *rauḍṛ* means "to disregard. *rauḍati*. (377) *lauḍṛ* means "to be intoxicated. *lauḍati*. (379) *aḍa* means "exertion. *vyaḍati*. *Vyaḍa*; his descendant is *Vyāḍi*.

*Vyāḍaḥ*, *vyālaḥ* (380). The root *laḍ* means "to sport. One sports (*laḍati*). Even while biting, even while not biting, one sports; thus *lalanā*, *pramadā* [mean] a woman. From *lāḍayati*; because *laḍ* and *lāḍ* are identical, one fondles a child (*lālayati*). Or, from *lala* in the sense of "desire" (X, 148); [thus] *lalitaḥ*. In the sense of "sporting about," *parilalalalane lalitam*. With the suffix *mit* according to the rule "in the sense of 'tongue' and 'churning'" (I, 852): *laḍayati*. In the *curādi* group, *laḍ* means "service" (X, 7): *upalāḍayati* (381).

In the sense of scratching (*kaṇḍimade*): *kaṇḍati*; *kaṇḍūḥ*. The first [root] is anudātta: *kaṇḍate*. Durga says *kaḍa*: *kaḍati*; *kaḍitram* is a writing-skin (*lekhanacarma*), derived by *itra* and *otra* suffixes from *aśitrādi* (Uṇ. IV, 172). By *kṛkadikaṭikaḍibhyo 'mbac* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 82): *kaḍambaḥ* is a vegetable, *kaḍaṅgaraḥ* is chaff. *Kaḍāraḥ* is from *gaḍi* (I, 814) with the addition of *kaḍa* (cf. Uṇ. III, 135); *kalatram* is from *gaḍi* with the substitution of *ka-* (Uṇ. III, 106). *Kaḍḍa* in the sense of harshness (*kārkaśye*): *kaḍḍati*. *Kallolaḥ* (wave). Some say *kaḍḍa*. (372)

*Gaḍi* [is used] in the sense of "one part of the face"; that is to say, in the action of joining together what is located on the cheek (*gaṇḍa*). It forms *gaṇḍati*, *gaṇḍaḥ*. With the suffix *iñ*: *gāṇḍiḥ*, *gāṇḍī*. That which possesses this is *gāṇḍivaṃ* or *gāṇḍīvaṃ*; [the form is derived] by the rule *gāṇḍyajagāt saṃjñāyāṃ vaḥ* (Pāṇini V.2.110). [Other derivatives include] *gaṇḍikā*, *gaṇḍiḥ*, and the earthworm (*gaṇḍūpadaḥ krimiḥ*). These [roots] are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*) and take the suffix *udāttet*. (356) (384)

The roots *tipṛ*, *tepṛ*, *ṣṭipṛ*, and *ṣṭepṛ* have the meaning "to flow. From this point until the end of the *stubh* group (421), there are thirty-six roots that take the augment *iṭ* (*seṭ*) and are *ātmanepada*. Examples: *te-pate*, *ste-pate*; *ati-tepat*, *ati-ṣṭepat*. There is a distinction regarding *kit* suffixes: *tip-itvā*, *tep-itvā*, *stip-itvā*, *step-itvā*. The future form is *tepitā*; however, because the rule concerning the *gaṇa*-based suffixation is not universal (cf. *Paribhāṣā* 93.3), the form *teptā* also occurs. Furthermore, *tepṛ* also means "to tremble" (385–389). *Glepṛ* means "to be dejected": *gle-pate*, *aji-glepat* (390).

The root *ṭuvepṛ* means "to tremble. [Derivatives include: *vepate*, *vepitā*, *avivepat*. By [Pāṇini III.3.89], *athuc* is added: *vepathuḥ*. By [Pāṇini VIII.4.34], *na bhābhūpūkamigami*, there is no substitution of *ṇa* for the vowel in *kṛtya* suffixes: *pravepanam*. By [Uṇādi II.52], *vepituhyor hrasvaś ca*, [the form] *vipinam* is derived;
some say it is *kaḍa*. 2 See Hemacandra, Uṇādi 619. 33.

*keṣṛ*, *geṣṛ*, and *glepṛ*. Because of the word "and" (*ca*), [these roots] signify trembling as well as motion, due to the division of the rules. *kepate*, *gepate*, *glepate* (392–394). *mepṛ*, *repṛ*, *lepṛ* signify motion. *mepate*, *repate*, *lepate*; *alilepat*. In the *tudādi* class, *lip* signifies smearing (*upadeha*): *limpate*, *limpati*, *alīlipat*. Kauśika says there is also *hrepṛ*. *repṛ* also signifies sound (395–398).

The root *trap* is used in the sense of "modesty. From the rule *svaratisūtisūyati* (VII.2.44), the suffix *iṭ* is optionally applied: *trapitā*, *traptā*. From the rule *tṝphalabhajatrapaś ca* (VI.4.122), the substitution of *e* for *a* and the elision of the reduplication occur: *trepe*. From the rule *ṣidbhidādibhyo ’ṅ* (III.3.104), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *trapā*. From the rule *āsuyuvapi* (III.1.126), the suffix *ṇyat* is applied: *apatrāpyam*. From the rule *alaṃkṛñnirākṛñ uḥ* (III.3.164), the suffix *u* is applied: *trapu* (399).

The root *kapi* means "to move. From it: *kampate*: by [Pāṇini III.2.148], the suffix *yuc* is applied to roots meaning movement, yielding *kampanaḥ*. By [Pāṇini III.2.167], the suffix *ra* is applied, yielding *kampraḥ*. By [Pāṇini I.3.87], the *parasmaipada* ending is used with the causative (*ṇi*) after roots meaning swallowing or moving: *kampayati*. There is the rule for the suffix *śa* after the roots *mṛg* and *kamp*: *kampayā*. The past passive participle is *kampitaḥ*. [The root] *laṅg*...

Regarding *kampya* as "affliction" and "bodily transformation" (VI.4.24.1), there is the elision of *n*: *vikapitaḥ*. From *kuṇṭhi* and *kampi*, there is the elision of *n* (cf. Uṇ. IV.143): *kapiḥ*. From *kapi*, *kaṇḍi*, *kaṭi*, and *paṭi*, there is the suffix *ola* (cf. Uṇ. I.67): *kapolaḥ* (400).

*Rabi*, *labi*, and *abi* [are roots] in the sense of sound (*śabda*). *Rambate*; what *rambates*? *Karambaḥ*—gold inlaid with jewels. It is derived from the root *kṛñ* with the suffix *ambac* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra IV.82). Or, it means "it hangs" (*lambate*). It is also *ambate*. From the roots *amb*, *mū*, *śaki*, and *ambi*, the suffix *kla* is applied (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra IV.108): thus *amlam* (sourness). *Labi* also means "to hang down" (*avasraṃsana*). Thus: *ullambate*, *vilambate*, *avalambate*, *ālambate*. The multiplicity of meanings is indicated by the prefixes (*upasarga*); other examples may likewise be cited.

*Prālambikā* is a golden garland (*svarṇamālā*); *prālamba* is a garland hanging straight from the neck. *Lambikā* is the uvula (*trikaṭā*). *Vilambikā* is that which hangs down repeatedly. Regarding the suffix *ū* in the sense of "hanging" with the negative particle *nañ*, as stated in *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.89: *alābūḥ* (the bottle gourd), a vegetable named *alambusā*. The root *kabṛ* means "to color. *Varṇa* is the act of coloring, and it refers to colors such as white and so forth. From the root *kab* (to speak/to shine), one forms *acakābat*. With the suffix *ṇyat* (Pāṇini III.1.124), one gets *kābyam*. With the suffix *iḥ* (Uṇādi IV.138), one gets *kabiḥ* (a poet). *Kabaraḥ* means black. *Kabarī* (IV.1.42) refers to a style of hair arrangement.
*klībṛ* [meaning] lack of courage: *klībate*, *aciklībat*. *klībaḥ*, *klībitaḥ* (406).

*kṣībṛ* [meaning] intoxication: *kṣībate*, *acikṣībat*. By the rule *anupasargāt phullakṣība* (Pāṇini VIII.2.55), the form *kṣībaḥ* is correct when used with the suffix *niṣṭhā*; however, when preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*), it becomes *prakṣība-*. 1. cf. III.3.101 Bh. and Hem. Dh. I.757; 2. P. sourness; 3. P. a mass of hair; 4. all manuscripts read thus.
1.34 *kṣivu* is used in the sense of spitting at the beginning of the *divādi* class (cf. Candra-Dh I V, 4 and Hem. Dh. I V, 24): *kṣībyati* (407).

*Śībhṛ* is used in the sense of boasting: *śībhate*; *śībharaḥ* means one who boasts (408). *Cībhṛ* also [is used] in the sense of boasting due to the inclusion of *ca*: *cībhate* (409). *Rebhṛ* is used in the sense of sound: *rebhate*. [The forms *kṣubdha*, *svānta*, and *dhvānta* are formed according to Pāṇini VII, 2, 18.]

Thus, *viribdha* means "skilled in voice," while *virebhita* has another meaning. Regarding the root *rabh* in the sense of "sound," Durga says: it *ambhate*, hence *ambhaḥ*; it *rambhate*, hence *rambhā*; and *karambhaḥ* refers to curd-mixed barley meal (*dadhisaktavaḥ*). (410–412)

The root *ṣṭ̣abh* / *skabh* is used in the sense of "obstructing. Obstruction (*pratibandha*) is the cessation of action. One obstructs (*stambhate*). The forms are *stambhaḥ*, *viṣṭ̣ambhaḥ*, and *avaṣṭ̣ambhaḥ*. The substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs according to the rule: "In the case of *ava*, [the *s* of] *aurjitya*, *ālambana*, and *avidūrya* becomes *ṣ*" (*avaṣṭ̣ambhate śūraḥ*; he obstructs; *daṇḍam avaṣṭ̣ambhate*; he leans on the staff; *avaṣṭ̣abdhe sene*; the two armies are held back). By the rule "After *udaḥ*, the *s* of *sthā* and *stambh* is replaced by *t*" (*udaḥ sthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya*), the substitution of *t* occurs: *uttambhate*. Then, by the rule "A *jh* consonant is optionally elided before a following *jh* consonant of the same class" (*jharo jhari savarṇe*), there is optionally an elision [of the *t*].

*tiṣṭambhiṣate*, *tiṣṭambhayiṣati* (VIII, 3, 61); some maintain that this *ṣakāra* is followed by *ṭ* (*ṭaparaḥ*): *ṣṭambhate*, *ṭiṣṭambhiṣate*, *ṭiṣṭambhayiṣati*; *viṣṭambhyate*. However, *viṣṭabhyate* is from the root *stabhnāti* (III, 1, 82). From *skambhate* [we have] *skambhyate*; *viṣkabhyate* is from *skabhnāti*. Both *stanbhu* and *skanbhu* are Vedic roots (*sautrau*): *stabhnāti*, *stabhnoti*; *skabhnāti*, *skabhnoti* (III, 1, 82). By rule VIII, 3, 77, there is obligatory *ṣatva* for *skabhnāti* after the prefix *vi-*: *viṣkambhaḥ* (413, 414).

The roots *jabh* and *jṛbh* mean "to yawn" or "to stretch the limbs. They form *jabhate*, *jṛmbhate*; *jabhitaḥ*, *jṛmbhitaḥ*; and *jṛmbhaḥ*. By the rule *radhijabhor aci* (Pāṇini VI.1.61), the augment *num* is added: *jambhakaḥ*, *jambhanam*, *jambhaḥ*. By the rule *lupasadacara* (III.1.24), the suffix *yaṅ* is applied in the sense of censuring the action (*bhāvagarhā*), and by *japajabhadahadaśa* (VII.4.86), the augment *nuk* is added: *jañjabhyate* (415, 416). *Śalbha* means "to boast" or "to praise falsely": *śalbhate* (417). *Valbha* means "to eat": *valbhate*; *valbhaḥ* (418). *Galbha* means "boldness": *pragalbhate*; *pragalbhaḥ*; *galbha-*...

The suffix *kvip* is applied after the roots *klība* and *hoḍa* (cf. Pāṇini III.1.11); and the suffix *ām* is applied after the root *kas* and after a suffix marked with *k*, except in the case of the *liṭ* tense when used in a mantra (III.1.35): *pragalbhāñcakre*, *prajagalbhe*. The root *sranbhu* means "to be negligent"; negligence (*pramāda*) here signifies arrogance (*avalepa*). [Examples: *visrambhate*, *visrabhyate*. Some authorities read the root as *sransu*. (419–420)

The root *ṣṭ̣ubh* means "to paralyze" (*stambhe*). Paralysis (*stambhaḥ*) is the cessation of activity; Durga states that paralysis (*stobhaḥ*) signifies the increase of defects. From it come the forms *stobhate*. Regarding the form *abhiṣṭ̣obhate*, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs according to [Pāṇini] VIII.3.65: "After a prefix, [the *s* of] *sunoti* [becomes *ṣ*]. The gerund forms are *stubdhvā*, *stobhitvā*, and *stubhitvā*; the past passive participle is *stubdhaḥ*. There are also the names *anuṣṭ̣up* and *triṣṭ̣up*. The root *stunbhu* exists as a Vedic (sautra) root [according to Pāṇini III.1.82]: *stubhnāti* and *stubhnoti*. 1. Cf. VIII.3.68 and Candra-Sūtra VI.4.53. 2. *P* with an initial *ś*. 35.1.

392. Those beginning with *gup* and ending with *śumbh* are *anudātta-it* roots; thirty-four of them take the augment *iṭ* (*seṭ*) and are *parasmaipada*. By the rule *gupū-dhūpa-vichi-* (III.1.28), the suffix *āya* is applied: *gopāyati*. By the rule *āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā* (III.1.31), [the forms] *goptā*, *gopitā*, and *gopāyitā* are formed. By the rule *rājasūya-sūrya-* (III.1.114), *kupya* is correctly formed. However, *gup* in the sense of "concealing" (*gopane*) (I.1019) is intended here as a root for the derivation of the desiderative: *jugupsate*, by the rule *guptijkidbhyaḥ san* (III.1.5).

In the *curādi* class, *gup* (X.231) has the sense of "shining": *gopayati*, *gopanā*. (422) *dhūp* [means] "to heat": *dhūpāyati*, *dhūpayāṃcakāra*, *dudhūpa*. In the *curādi* class, [it is also used] with the sense of "shining" (X.232): *dhūpayati*. (423) 2.

The root *jalp* means "to speak clearly. One *jalpati*. Because of the supplementary rule regarding prohibitions such as laughter (*hasādīnām upasaṃkhyānāt*), [the form] *vyatijalpanti* occurs. With the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.18), we have *jalpaḥ*; with the suffix *ākan* by the rule *jalpabhikṣa-* (III.2.155), we have *jalpākaḥ*. The root *jap* means "to mutter" and refers to speech produced mentally: one *japati*. By the rule *lupasada-* (III.1.24), the suffix *yaṅ* is applied: *jañjapyate*. By the rule *japajabhadaha-* (VII.4.86), the augment *nuK* is added. By the rule *por adupadhāt* (III.1.98), the suffix *yat* is applied.

Regarding *japya*: by Pāṇini III.2.13, *ramijapoḥ* [the suffix *kyap* is applied after the roots *ram* and *jap*]; thus, *karṇejapaḥ*. By III.3.61, *vyadhajapor anupasarge* [the suffix *ap* is applied after the roots *vyadh* and *jap* when no prefix is present]; thus, *japaḥ*. Regarding *japitaḥ* and *japtaḥ*, they say that this is because the word "and" (*ca*) in VII.2.16, *āditaś ca*, has the sense of including what was not explicitly mentioned.

(425, 424) Regarding *capa* in the sense of "to soothe": *capati*. By IV.3.134, *tasya vikāraḥ* [the suffix *aṇ* is applied to denote a modification of that]; thus, *cāpaḥ*. *Capeṭaḥ* and *capaṭaḥ* mean "broad" (Uṇādi IV.81). (426)

The root *sap* is used in the sense of association (*samavāya*). From it: *sapati*, *siṣāpayiṣati*. *sapta*, *saptiḥ* (horse); according to Candra, *saceti* (Ca. Dh. I, 140): *sacati*, *sacivaḥ* (minister). The roots *rap* and *lap* are used in the sense of distinct speech. *rapati*, *lapati*. By the rule *āsuyuvapi* (Pāṇini III, 1, 126), the suffix *ṇyat* is applied: *apalāpyam*, *lapitam*, *lapanam* (mouth); *ālāpaḥ*, *apalāpaḥ*, *pralāpaḥ*.

The root *cup* means "to move slowly. One *copati*, meaning one moves slightly. *Copana* is derived from the *uṇādi* suffixes as *cuppaṃ*, meaning "lack of movement"; this is because of the rule *cuper aś copadhāyāḥ* (Uṇādi I.110), resulting in *capalaḥ*. Thus, since a contrary meaning is understood here, we do not know this intended sense [of yours]. If you argue that the etymological derivation of names must be performed by some means or another, then let it be accomplished with even less effort using the root *cap* (DhP 426).

*tupa*, *tumpa*, *trupha*, *trunpha* have the meaning of "to injure. [The roots] *topati* and *tumpati* are used. Regarding the prefix *pra-* before *tumpati* in the sense of "motion," *suṭ* is added (cf. VI, 1, 157 Kāś.): *prastumpati gāṃ vatsaḥ* ("the calf kicks the cow"). *Candra* (Ca. Dh. I, 142) reads *trupha* and *trunpha* as additional [roots] (431–438).

1. *gup* (Pāṇini); 2. *K* and *C* omit this, but cf. X, 232; 3. *P* states it is "intransitive" (*niṣkarmatvam*); cf. Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 01; 4. cf. *Nirukta* II, 1; 5. all manuscripts read thus. 1. 36.

*varpha*, *rapha*, *raphi*, *arbha*, *barba*, *karba*, *kharba*, *garba*, *gharba*, *śarba*, *ṣarba*, *sarba*, *carba*, *bharba*, *narba*—these fifteen [roots] have the sense of "motion" (*gati*). Kaṇṭha reads the first three, beginning with *varpha*, in the sense of "injury" (*hiṃsā*). *Garba* is not of Vedic origin (*anārṣa*); here the *va* is labial because of the context of the *pa*-class (labials). Kauśika considers that in *arbha* and the others, there is a *na* in place of the *ra*. One *śarba* begins with a palatal (*tālavya*), another is a root taught with a *ṣa* (*ṣopadeśa*), and another begins with a dental. *Arba* means "horse."

*Barbaraḥ*, *barbarī*: curly hair. *Karbaṭaḥ*: a town situated among four hundred villages. *Karburaḥ*: a variegated color. *Kharbaḥ*, *garbaḥ*, *śarbaḥ*, *sarbaḥ*. *Carbaṇam* (439–442, 445, 447–449, 449a, 450–452, 452a, 452b): from the root *cubi*, meaning "to touch the mouth"; used figuratively as in *namas tuṇgaśiraścumbi* (*Harṣacarita* V.2, ed. BoSS 66), "the salutation kissing the lofty head. *Cumbati*, *cumbitam*, *cumbanam* (456).

*sr̥bh* and *sr̥nbh* have the meaning of "to injure. One says *sarbhati*, *sr̥mbhati*. These two are also not taught with an initial *ṣ* (*aṣopadeśa*), because by the rule "excepting *sr̥*" (Pāṇini VI.1.64), even that which is meaningless is included. (457, 458) *śunbha* means "speaking" and "injuring. Durga [interprets] it as "shining" (*bhāsana*). One says *śumbhati*. Regarding *śubha* and *śunbha* having the meaning of "beauty" (cf. VI.33), this form *śumbhate* belongs to that root. Gupta [maintains] that this is a root taught with an initial *ṣ* (*ṣopadeśa*), because of the observation of forms such as *sāvaṣṭambhaniṣumbhasumbhananamadbhūgola* (see *Mālatīmādhava* V.22). One says *sumbhati*; [the word] *kuṣumbha* (460).

Those beginning with *udātta* vowels [are] *udātta-ita*. 426. *ghiṇi*, *ghuṇi*, *ghṛṇi* mean "to seize. Ten roots ending in *kam* (470) take the augment *iṭ* and are *ātmanepada*. *Ghiṇṇate*, *ghiṇṇitaḥ*. *Ghuṇṇate*. *Ghṛṇṇate* (461–463). *Ghuṇa*, *ghūrṇa* mean "to whirl. *Ghoṇate*; *ghoṇā* ("snout"), *ghuṇākṣara* ("worm-eaten letter"), *ghuṇāvarta* ("water-wheel"). *Ghūrṇate*. In the *tudādi* class (VI, 48–49), they are *parasmaipada*: *ghuṇati*, *ghūrṇati* (464, 465).

The root *paṇ* is used in the senses of "transaction" (*vyavahāra*) and "praise" (*stuti*). In the example *cakrapāṇiṃ paṇāyati*, the substitution of *taṅ* (the *ātmanepada* endings) does not occur because of the intervention of the prefix *ā*. According to the rule *gupū-dhūpa-vicha-paṇi-panibhya āya* (Pāṇini III.1.28), the suffix *āya* is added to the root *paṇ* in the sense of praise; due to its association with *pan* (which takes *āya*), the *āya* is not applied to the root *paṇ* in the sense of transaction. Consequently, the genitive case is used by the rule *vyavahṛ-paṇoḥ* (Pāṇini II.3.57): *śatasya paṇate*; and as in the verse: *na copalebhe vaṇijāṃ paṇāyām* (Bhaṭṭikāvya III.27).

1. *varpa* (P), *vapha* (K and Cv) 2. *tarba* (P) 3. *grāmacatuḥśatīmukhyapuram* (P) 4. The commentary on the *Piṅgala-chandaḥsūtra* by Halāyudha also begins with these same words. 5. Thus all manuscripts. 6. P adds *ghuṇṇaḥ*; K reads *paṇāyayā*, C reads *paṇāyatām*, P reads *paṇāyate*. 37. I.

But Bhaṭṭi is mistaken. According to *avadyapaṇya* (Pāṇini III.1.101), the word *paṇya* is correct when referring to that which is to be sold (*paṇitavya*). By *nityaṃ paṇaḥ parimāṇe* (III.3.66), the form *paṇaḥ* is established; by *gocarasaṃcara* (III.3.119), *āpaṇaḥ* is correct; by *āṅi paṇipani* (Uṇādi II.45), *āpaṇikaḥ* is formed with the suffix *ikan*; by *paṇer ijy ādeś ca va* (Uṇādi II.70), *vaṇik* is formed; and by *aśipaṇāyyor* (Uṇādi IV.132), *pāṇiḥ* is formed. (466)

Furthermore, by the inclusion of *ca* [in the rule], [the root] is used in the sense of praise (*stuti*). One praises Hari (*panāyate Hariṃ*). Here, even though the grammatical marker (*liṅga*) is applied to a single part [of the root], it serves as a qualifier for the whole; thus, despite the intervention of *āya*, the *ātmanepada* ending occurs. From the rule *atyavicami* (Uṇ. III. 117), the suffix *asac* is added: *panasaḥ* (467).

*Bhāma* means "anger" (*krodha*). One is angry (*bhāmate*); *bhāminī* (468). *Kṣamūṣ* means "to endure" (*sahana*). One endures (*kṣamate*); the future forms are *kṣantā* and *kṣamitā*. The past passive participle is *kṣāntaḥ*; the abstract noun is *kṣamā*. In the *divādi* class (IV. 97), one endures (*kṣāmyati*); the abstract noun is *kṣāntiḥ* (469).

*Kāntau*. *Kāntiḥ* means desire (*abhilāṣaḥ*). This [form] is caused by the root *kam-* with the suffix *ṇiṅ* (Pāṇini III.1.30): *kāmayate*; and by the rule *āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā* (III.1.31), we have *cakame* and *kāmayāñcakre*. [The nouns] *kamanam*, *kāmanam*; *kāntiḥ*, *kāmanā*; [the gerunds] *kamitvā*, *kāntvā*, *kāmayitvā*; [the past participles] *kāntaḥ*, *kāmitaḥ*. [In the case of the aorist] *acīkamata*, because of the supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyāna*) for the root *kam-* in the *caṅ* formation (Kāśikā on III.1.48), we have *acakamata*.

By the rule *tuṃ kāmamanasor api* (Pāṇini VI.1.144, Kāśikā), [the suffix tumun is used] when one wishes to act; by *śīlikāmibhakṣācaribhyo ṇaḥ* (III.2.1.7), [the suffix ṇa is used]: "a woman who desires meat" (*māṃsakāmā*). By *laṣapatapada* (III.2.154), [the suffix ukañ is used]: "one who lusts after a maidservant" (*dāsyāḥ kāmukaḥ*). Although the prohibition [of the genitive case] by *na lokāvyaya* (II.3.69) would have applied, the genitive is maintained by the rule *kamer bhāṣāyām* (II.3.69.3). Although the prohibition [of vṛddhi] by *nodāttopadeśasya* (VII.3.34) would have applied...

By the rule *vamikamicamīnām* (Pāṇini VI.1.34 Bh.), there is *vṛddhi*: *kāmī*. By *namikampi* (III.2.167), there is *ra*: *kamraḥ*. It is also desired [that *ra* follows] *yuj*: *kamanaḥ*. By *kamimanijanibhyas tuḥ* (Uṇādi I.73), there is *kantuḥ*. By *kamer aṭhaḥ* (Uṇādi I.102), there is *kamaṭhaḥ*. By *kalas tṛpaś ca* (Uṇādi I.106), there is *kamalam*. By *vṝtṝvadi* (Uṇādi III.62), there is *sa*: *kaṃsaḥ*. In the *uṇādi* [section], there are *kambalaḥ* and *komalaḥ*.

From the root *kam* (Uṇ. I, 108), [we derive] *kamala*; from *kam* with the suffix *la* (Uṇ. I, 106), *kāmalā*. From *arti-kami-bhrami* (Uṇ. III, 132), by means of the suffix *ara*, [we derive] *kamara*. From *kam* with the substitution of *u* for the penultimate vowel (cf. Uṇ. III, 138), [we derive] *kumāra*. Because of the rule *ataḥ kṛkami-kaṃsa-* (VIII, 3, 46), there is the change to *s*: *payaskāmaḥ*. Because of the rule *na bhābhūpūkami-gami-* (VIII, 4, 34), there is no change to *ṇ* after a vowel following these roots: *prakamanam*, *prakāmanam*. (470) These are the roots ending in anudātta vowels that take the suffix *an*. 436.

*Aṇ*, *raṇ*, *vaṇ*, *maṇ*, *kaṇ*, *kvaṇ*, *vraṇ*, *bhraṇ*, *dhvaṇ* have the meaning of "sound. These are roots whose meanings consist of the act of sounding. From here follow those ending in *kram*: 1) in the sense of "anger"; 2) cf. Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 499; I 38.

(502) Thirty-three roots ending in *ṣet* are *parasmaipada*. From the root *aṇ*: by *kvun* [is formed] *aṇakaḥ*, meaning a barber (*nāpitaḥ*), according to *Uṇ.* I, 32; by *iñ* [is formed] *āṇiḥ*, meaning the pin at the front of an axle (*akṣāgrakīlakaḥ*), according to *Uṇ.* IV, 124; *aṇiḥ* is given by Amarasiṃha (II, 8, 57). From *aṇḍam*: by *aṇaś ca* (*Uṇ.* I, 8), *u* is added: *aṇuḥ*; by *aṇo ḍa ca* (cf. *Uṇ.* I, 88), because of the *ṇit*-suffix, *āḍū-* is added: *ālukā*. From *raṇati*: [the following forms are derived].

Regarding the rule *vaśiraṇyoś ca* (Pāṇini III.3.58), the suffix *ap* should be stated [after the root *raṇ*]. It is called *raṇa* because "they delight in this" (*raṇanti asmin*). It is recorded in tradition that the roots *raṇ*, *maṇ*, and *kvaṇ* take the designation *mit* when meaning "motion": thus *raṇayati* (in the sense of motion), but otherwise *rāṇayati*. From *vaṇ* we have *vaṇati*; *udvaṇaḥ* and *ulvaṇaḥ*—the substitution of *l* for *v* occurs here either by analogy with *udūkhalolūkhalam* (Pāṇini VI.3.109) or because they belong to the *pṛṣodarādi* group. *Vāṇaḥ* is so called because the bowstring (*jyā*) "resounds" (*vaṇati*) in it; or, it is "resounded" (*vaṇyate*) by means of it: from the suffix *iñ*, we have *vāṇiḥ* and *vāṇī*.

The term *maṇita* is conventionally established for the cooing of sexual pleasure; likewise, *kaṇita* refers to crying out from distress (*ārta*); *kvaṇita* to the sound of a lute (*vīṇā*) and the like; *raṇita* to that of anklets (*nūpura*) and the like; *kūjita* to the warbling of birds and the like; *bṛṃhita* to the trumpeting of an elephant; *hreṣita* (cf. 653) to the neighing of a horse; *vāśita* (IV, 54) to the barking of animals; *garjita* (244) to the thundering of clouds and the like; *guñjita* (218) to the humming of bees and the like; and *gṛñjita* (268) to the roaring of lions and the like—these and others are situated according to their respective roots.

How much can we explain? That which is beyond the reach of scholars must be understood from common usage (*loka*); for a grammatical definition (*lakṣaṇa*) is rooted in the linguistic reality it defines (*lakṣya*). Thus: *maṇiḥ*, *maṇikaḥ* (a large water-jar), *mahākumbhaḥ*; *kaṇati*; *kaṇaḥ*, *kaṇikā*, *kaṅkaṇaḥ*, *kaṇūkaḥ*, *kaṇṭhaḥ*.

From the root *kvaṇ* with the suffix *kvan* [according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.151], we have *kaṇva*, meaning "evil" or "a section. From *kvaṇ* with the suffix *ap* [according to *Pāṇini* III.3.65], we have *nikvaṇa* and *nikvāṇa*; *kvaṇa* and *kvāṇa*; *prakvaṇa* and *prakvāṇa*; *upakvaṇa* and *upakvāṇa*. From the roots *pīyū* and *kvaṇ* with the suffix *kālaḍ*, there is shortening and vocalization (*prasāraṇa*) [according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* III.76]: *kuṇāla*. From *kvaṇ* with vocalization [according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* III.143]: *kuṇapa*. From *vraṇ*: *vraṇati*, *vraṇa*.

In the *cur*-class, the root *vraṇ* (meaning "to wound" or "to powder the body") is not dental: *vraṇayati*. The palatal-final root *dhvaṇ* does not exist in common usage. (471–473, 475–480) 2. The root *oṇṛ* (meaning "to remove"): *oṇati*; [in the prohibitive form] *mā bhavān oṇiṇat*. This very fact that it is marked with *ṛt* serves as an indicator (*jñāpaka*) that reduplication—which is both permanent and internal—is superseded by the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasvatva*). Otherwise, once reduplication has occurred, the penultimate vowel would no longer exist, and thus the shortening would not apply; what then would be accomplished by marking it with *ṛt*? Therefore, in forms such as *mā bhavān aṭiṭat*, the shortening is established. (482) 3.
The root *śoṇṛ* is used in the senses of coloring and going. *Śoṇati*. *Śoṇaḥ* means red; *śoṇitam* means blood. In the sense of going, *śoṇaḥ* refers to a river.
(483) The roots *śroṇṛ* and *śloṇṛ* are used in the sense of gathering together (*saṃghāta*). *Śroṇiḥ* [the hip]; *śroṇaḥ* means a cripple.
(484, 485) The root *paiṇṛ* is used in the senses of going, impelling, and joining. *Paiṇati*; *apipaiṇat*. (486)
1. *ūhyaṃ* 2. 474 after 486 3. 481 after 490 4. *Ppeṇṛ*, *peṇati*, *apipeṇat* 39.

*I* for the roots *vana*, *bhaṇa*, and *dhaṇa* in the sense of "sound. *vanati*; *vanaṃ*, *saṃvananaṃ* (subduing), *vaśīkaraṇam* (the act of bringing under control). *bhaṇati*; *bhāṇaḥ*, well-known in the sense of "ornament. *dhaṇati*. Kauśika, however, says that [the root] ends in a dental (*dantya*). From *us* (Uṇ. IV, 118): *dhanuḥ* (bow). From *vanip* (cf. Uṇ. I, 156): *dhanvā* (archer/desert). From *kṛṣicami* (Uṇ. I, 82) with the suffix *ū*: *dhanūḥ* (a heap, 490. 474. 481). 1. *rāśiḥ* (heap).

The root *kan* is used in the senses of radiance, beauty, and motion. Radiance (*dīpti*) means light; beauty (*kānti*) means splendor. It forms *kanati*. From it are derived *kanīnikā* (the pupil), *kanaka* (gold)—as found in the list beginning with *aghnya* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.111)—*kanyā* (maiden), and *kāntaḥ* (lovely). (488)

Regarding the word *stana* meaning "sound": [the root] *stan* forms *stanitam*, *stanaḥ*, and *stānayati*; it is an *adanta* (ending in -a) in the *curādi* class (X, 313–314): *meghaḥ stanayati* ("the cloud thunders"). By the rule *abhiniḥḥstanaḥ śabdasaṃjñāyām* (VIII, 3, 86), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*: *abhiniḥṣṭānaḥ* refers to the *visarga*. Regarding *dhvan*: [the root] *dhvan* forms *dhvānaḥ* and *dhvaniḥ*. By the rule *kṣubdhasvāntadhvānta...* (VII, 2, 18), if *dhvāntam* means "darkness," it is so formed; otherwise, it is *dhvanitam*. It is also an *adanta* in the *curādi* class (X, 343): *dhvanayati*. (See 489, 487.)

The root *van* is used in the sense of devotion (*bhakti*). Devotion means worshiping. [From this root we derive: *vanati*, *vanam* (wood), *vanitā* (woman); and by the rule *ṛtanyañji* (Uṇādi IV, 2), *vaniṣṭhu* (the small intestine), *vānaraḥ* (monkey) according to the Uṇādisūtras, and *vānīraḥ* (the reed). In the *tanādi* group, *vanu* is used in the sense of requesting (*yācana*): *vanute*, *vanoti*. [Regarding the root *san*: ] *sanati*. By the rule *sano ye vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VI, 4, 43), there is optionally the substitution of *ā* for *i*: *sāyate*, *sanyate*. How is *sanyāt* formed? Because the rule applies when *ya* follows an *ad*-class root. By the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini VII, 2, 49), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: [thus we have *sisaniṣati* or *sisaniti*].

In *sisaniṣati*, there is no *ṣatva* (the substitution of *s* with *ṣ*) because of the restriction: "The *ṣatva* occurs only after the reduplicated syllable of the roots *stu* and *ṣaṇ*" (Pāṇini VIII.3.61); thus it is *siṣāsati*. In *sānuḥ*, the suffix *ñuṇ* is applied by the rule *dṝsanijani-* (Uṇādi I.3). In *saniḥ*, the suffix *sani* is applied by the rule *khanikaṣyañjyasi-* (Uṇādi IV.139). In *sātiḥ*, the rule *na ktici dīrghaś ca* (VI.4.39) applies. In *satiḥ* and *santiḥ*, the rule *lopaś cāsyānyatarasyām* (VI.4.45) applies. In the *tan*-class, the root *ṣaṇu* meaning "to give" (VIII.2) forms *sanute* and *sanoti* (491, 492).

The root *am* is used in the sense of "going" (*gati*) and so forth; *kanī* is used in the sense of "shining," "beauty," and "going"—this is "going"; *stan* is used in the sense of "sound"—this is "sound"; *van* and *ṣaṇ* are used in the sense of "devotion" (*bhakti*)—this is "devotion. These are the meanings beginning with "going. In the case of *āmayati*, [the rule] "na kamyamicamām" (Pāṇini I.869) prevents the designation of *mit*: thus it is *āmayati*. Regarding the suffix *niṣṭhā* (the past passive participle suffix -ta/-na), [the rule] "ruṣyamatvarasaṃghuṣāsvanām" (Pāṇini VII.2.28) allows for the optional insertion of *iṭ*: thus we have *abhyamitaḥ* and *abhyāntaḥ*. From *ambhaḥ* [we derive the word]; from *am* with the suffix *san* (Uṇādi V.21) we get *aṃsaḥ*; and from *am* with the suffix *gur* we get *raśmiḥ* (with the substitution of *l* for *r*).

*vā* 1: *aṅguriḥ* and *aṅguliḥ* [are derived from] *aṅg* [with the suffix] *uri*. *Andhuḥ* means "well"; it is properly formed by *arjidṛśi* (Uṇ. I, 28). *Āmraḥ* [is derived from] *am* and *tam* with lengthening (Uṇ. II, 16). By *hasimṛgriṇ* (Uṇ. III, 86), the suffix *tan* is added, resulting in *antaḥ*. By *amicimidiśasibhyaḥ ktraḥ* (Uṇ. IV, 163), *antram* [is formed]; by *aminakṣikaliyajivadhipatibhyo 'tran* (cf. Uṇ. III, 104), *amatram* means "vessel. By *amer itran* (cf. Uṇ.
IV, 173), *amitraḥ* means "enemy. By *ṣṭran* (Uṇ. IV, 158), *antram* [is formed again]. (493)

The root *dram* (in the sense of "to move") is *hamma mīmṛ gatau*. From *dramati*, by the rule *hmyantakṣaṇa* (VH 2.5), there is no *vṛddhi* in the *sic* suffix: *adramīt*; [the intensive] *dandramyate*. From the intensive (*yaṅ*) form, by the rule *jucaṅkramyadandramya* (III.2.150), the suffix *yuc* is added: *dandramaṇaḥ*. By the rule *dramimasyor uc ca*, [the suffix *lac* is added with the substitution of *u* for the final vowel]: *drumalam*, meaning "a vessel for measuring. According to the *Bhāṣya* on the *Paspaśā* (p. 9), "the root *hammat* is used among the Surāṣṭras," the *m* is doubled. The root *mīmṛ* is also used in the sense of "sound": *mīmati*, *amimīmat* (494–496).

*Cam*, *cham*, *jam*, and *jham* are used in the sense of eating. Because of the rule *camati, vicamati, ṣṭhivuklamvācamāṃ śiti* (Pāṇini VII.3.75, Kāśikā), there is lengthening [of the vowel]: *ācāmati*. Because of the rule *na kamyamicamām* (Dhātupāṭha I.869), the designation *mit* does not apply: *ācāmayati*. By the rule *āsuyuvapi* (Pāṇini III.1.126), the suffix *ṇyat* is applied: *ācāmyam*. Due to the prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *nodāttopadeśasya māntasyānācamer* (Pāṇini VII.3.34), there is no *vṛddhi*: *ācāmakaḥ*. By the rule *kṛṣicami* (Uṇādi-sūtra I.82), the suffix *ū* is applied: *camūḥ*. [And] by *atyavicami* (Uṇādi-sūtra...).

117) Thus, from the root *cam*, we have *camasaḥ* [a ladle]; and by the rule *camasaḥ, kṛdarādayaś ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra V.41), we have *camaraḥ* [a yak]. By the rule *udito vā* (Pāṇini VII.2.56), the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied: *cāntvā* or *camitvā*. From this, we derive *ācāntaḥ* [one who has sipped water] and *ācāmaḥ* [water for rinsing the mouth]. From the root *cham*: *ācchamati*, *ācchāmaḥ*. From the root *jam*: *jamati*. Some maintain that this root has *i* and *u* as its penultimate vowels (*idupadha*): *jemanam*, *jemaḥ*. From the root *jham*: *jhamati* (497–501).

*Kram* means "stepping" (*padavikṣepa*) or "placing the foot" (*padanyāsa*). In the sense of [motion], there is lengthening by the rule *kramaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (VII. 3. 76): *krāmati*. In the senses of "continuous flow," "emission," and "stretching," there is the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) by the rule *vṛttisargatāyaneṣu krama* (I. 3. 38): *ṛkṣv asya kramate buddhiḥ*, meaning "his intellect does not stumble over the Vedic verses"; *yuddhāya kramate*, meaning "he exerts himself for battle"; *prājñe śāstrāṇi kramante*, meaning "the scriptures flourish in the presence of a wise man. With the prefix *āṅ*, it means "rising up" (*udgamana*) by the rule *āṅa udgamane* (I. 3. 40).

The sun ascends the sky; this should be expressed as *jyotir udgacchati* (the light rises), not as *ākramate*. Regarding *veḥ pādaviharaṇe* (Pāṇini I.3.41): "The horse strides well," but not here: "the joint of the skin moves. Regarding *propābhyāṃ samarthābhyām* (Pāṇini I.3.42): "He begins to eat" (*prakramate bhoktum*), "he undertakes" (*upakramate*). Regarding *anupasargād vā* (Pāṇini I.3.43): "He steps" (*kramate*) or "he steps" (*krāmati*).

The augment *iṭ* is applied [to the roots] *snuk* and *kram* when they do not have a cause for the middle voice (*anātmanepada*): *prakramitum*, *cikramiṣati*, *cikramiṣā*, *cikramiṣuḥ*. It is not applied here: *praci-* [etc.]¹. ¹ See Uṇ. IV.2 and Hem. Uṇ. 699.
