By [Uṇādi-sūtra] II, 13, the suffix *rak*: *Vṛtraḥ*; *vārtākaḥ*. *Vartakaḥ*; and *vartakā* in the sense of a bird according to the Easterners (Pāṇini VII, 3, 45, Kāśikā); for the Northerners, it is *vartikā*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV, 118, *hṛpiśi* etc., the suffix *in*: *vartili*.

According to some, *vṛt* meaning "to choose" belongs to the *divādi* class (*I*, *vṛtu varaṇe*, 52): *vṛtyate*. In the *curādi* class (*X*, 241), it has the sense of "shining": *vartayati* (795). The root *vṛdh* means "to grow. It takes the form *vardhate*. From the causative (*ṇyanta*) stem, the suffix *lyu* (*III*, 1, 134) is applied: *sukhavardhanaḥ* ("one who increases happiness"). *Vṛddhvā* (having grown) and *vardhitvā* (having increased); *vṛddhaḥ* ("grown") and *vṛddhiḥ* ("increase"); with the suffix *iṣṇuc* (*III*, 2, 136): *vardhiṣṇuḥ* ("inclined to grow"). From the rule *vṛdhivapibhyāṃ ran* (*Uṇ.*, II, 27): *vardhraḥ* ("leather"). In the *curādi* class, *vṛdh* has the sense of "shining" (*X*, 242): *vardhayati*. In that same class, *vardha* is listed for the senses of "cutting" and "filling" (*X*, 112) (796): *vardhayati*.
The root *śṛdh* is used in the sense of contemptuous sound. Contemptuous sound arises from the making of a noise with the anus. [Examples: *śardhate*, *aśṛdhat*, *aśardhiṣṭa*. (797)

The root *syandū* means "to flow. It forms: *syandate* (present), *asyadat* (imperfect), *asyandiṣṭa* (aorist), *syantsyati* (periphrastic future), *syandiṣyate* (periphrastic future), *syanttum* (infinitive), and *syanditum* (infinitive). Regarding the suffixing of *ṣ*, Pāṇini VIII.3.72 states that *ṣ* is optionally substituted for *s* after the prefixes *anu*, *vi*, *pari*, *abhi*, and *ni* when used with *syandati* in the sense of non-living beings: *anuṣyandate* or *anusyandate tailam* ("the oil flows along"). In the sense of speed, *syadaḥ* is formed according to VI.4.28. According to VI.4.31, the augment *iṭ* is not added after the roots *skand* and *syand* when the suffix *ktvā* follows: *syanttvā*. By adding the suffix *yuc* (Uṇ. II.78), one gets *syandanaḥ* ("a vehicle" or "flow"). Furthermore, by the rule "there is vocalization (*prasāraṇa*) and *dha* is substituted [for *ya*]" (cf. Uṇ. I.12), one derives *sindhuḥ* ("river") from *syand*. (798)

The root *kṛp* has the meaning "to be capable" (*sāmarthya*). According to Pāṇini VIII.2.18, *kṛpe ro laḥ*: [the substitution of] *l* for *r* occurs in *kṛp*. Thus: *kalpate*, *akḷpat*, *akalpiṣṭa*, *kalpsyati*, *kalpiṣyate*, *cikḷpsati*, *cikalpiṣate*. By the rule *luṭi ca kḷpaḥ* (I.3.93), the *parasmaipada* ending may optionally occur; by the rule *tāsi ca kḷpaḥ* (VII.2.60), the augment *iṭ* is not applied: *kalptāsi*, *kalpitāse*. [Gerundives: *kalptum*, *kalpitum*; [past participle: *kḷptam*. By the prohibition in *ṛdupadhāc cākḷpicṛteḥ* (III.1.110), the suffix *ṇyat* is not applied [to form *kalpya*]; however, by the rule *kṝtṝkṛpibhyaḥ kīṭan* (Uṇ. IV.184), [the suffix *kīṭan* is applied].
*kṛpīṭam* is the root *kṛp-* in the sense of "to cut" (*chur-ādau kṛpeḥ*) according to [Pāṇini] X.208; it belongs to the group beginning with *ā-garva* (X.350–359): *kalpayate* (799). 1. Turning; 2.
the word *pāyu*; 3. in the sense of flowing forth; 4. all manuscripts read this; 5. the *ā-garvīya* roots are X.350–359. I.62.

*vṛt*: *vartanam* (the act of turning) is *vṛt*. The two internal groups (*gaṇas*), beginning with *dyuti* and *vṛt*, have turned [i.e., concluded]; the meaning is that they have come to an end. According to some, from the root *vṛdh* with the suffix *kvip*, *vardhitau* means "filled" or "complete."

The root *ghaṭ* is used in the sense of "exertion" (*ceṣṭā*), where exertion means effort (*īhā*). One says *ghaṭate* and *ghaṭitam*. Because of the rule "roots beginning with *ghaṭ* are marked with the indicator *m*" (*ghaṭādayo mitaḥ*, Pāṇini I.3.5), it is a *mit* root; thus, by the rule "the short vowel is substituted for [the penultimate vowel] of *mit* roots" (*mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*, VI.4.92), one forms *ghaṭayati* and *ghaṭanaḥ*. In this context, the designation *mit* applies only to those roots that are listed in that specific section and whose meaning is restricted to what is stated there. However, for those roots that are listed here [in the *dhātupāṭha*], they possess multiple meanings in general. Therefore, in the case of *vighaṭayati*, even though there is no exertion, the shortening of the vowel occurs. How so?

Those who perform the opening of the lotus groves—who, like the sun rising, opens the beds of lotuses? Regarding the roots *caṭa*, *sphuṭa*, and *ghaṭa* in the *curādi* group, they have the sense of "to kill" (*han*). According to the rule *ghaṭir nānye mito 'hetau ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.15), *ghaṭi* is not *mit*. The meaning is that those [roots] such as *jñap* which were studied in [the section on] *mit* roots (Pāṇini 6.1.139–144) are *mit* when followed by the causative suffix *ṇic* in their own sense (*svārtha*), but others are not *mit*. Therefore, regarding *śama* and *lakṣa* in the sense of "perceiving" (*ālocane*) [as listed in Pāṇini 6.1.156–157]: 1. *kamalavanodghāṭanaṃ kurvate ye* 2. *pravighāṭayitā samutpatan haridaśvaḥ kamalākarān iva* 3. *curādau caṭa sphuṭa ghaṭa ca hantyarthāś ca* (cf. X, 181–184) 3. *iti ghaṭir nānye mito 'hetau ca* (X, 87) — thus it is not *mit*. The meaning is that those [roots] such as *jñap* which were studied [in the section on] *mit* roots (X, 81–86) are *mit* when followed by the causative suffix *ṇic* in their own sense, but others are not *mit*. Thus, [the same applies to] *śama* and *lakṣa* in the sense of "perceiving" (X, 156. 157).

*niśāmayate*, *āmayati*, etc., are established [from the roots] *ama* in the sense of "sickness" (*roga*) [Dhātupāṭha X, 180]. According to the view that the three roots beginning with *caṭ*—which function in the sense of "killing" (*han*)—induce the causative suffix (*ṇic*), there is a causative suffix after these [roots] when they end in *ghañ*; and thus: "of him whose neck [supports] all the mountains have been raised up... (*unnāmitākhilamahīdharakandharasya*).

And thus, forms such as *caurasyotkrāthayati* (I.1.3.56) are established. As for *saṃkrāmayati*, however, it is derived from *saṃkrāmantam karoti* (X.369) with the suffix *ṇic*. Having exhausted the abundance of clouds, the drying up of the water was brought about by the sun; likewise, because of the consensus in the rule *bheṣajakṣapitāṅgānām ca* (X.392), it should be inferred that the root *kṣapi* in the *curādi* group ends in a short vowel (*adanta*). [The rule] *ciṇṇamulor dīrgho 'nyatarasyām* (VI.4.93) applies.

(4.93): *aghāṭi*, *aghaṭi*; *ghāṭaṃ ghāṭam*, *ghaṭaṃ ghaṭam*. Because [the formation] is characterized by verbal expression (*abhidhāna-lakṣaṇatvāt*), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the causative form (*kṛta-ṇyantāt*). Since roots beginning with *ghaṭ* are marked with the *ṣit* designation (as per the rule following Pāṇini 8.3.12), the suffix *aṅ* is applied according to Pāṇini III.3.104: *ghaṭā*. According to Pāṇini III.4.65, *śaka-dhṛṣa*, the suffix *tumun* is applied: *ghaṭate bhoktum* ("he strives to eat"); *ghaṭaḥ* ("a jar"). Regarding these roots beginning with *ghaṭ*, some are recited right here as having appropriate *vikaraṇa*s for the scope of the root-base (*prakṛti*) and so forth; others, however, undergo the operations prescribed in their own respective places and are merely restated (*anūdyante*) for the sake of the *ṣit* and *mit* designations—this should be inferred accordingly (800).

The root *vyath* is used in the senses of fear and trembling; according to Durga, it is used in the senses of suffering and trembling. It forms: *vyathate*, *vyathayati*, *avyāthi*, *avyathi*, *vyāthaṃ vyātham*, *vyathaṃ vyatham*, *vyathām*. Regarding the form *vivyathe*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the reduplication by rule VI.4.68: "In the case of *vyatho* in the *liṭ* [perfect tense]. By rule III.1.114, "rājasūya-sūrya-...", the word *avyathyaḥ* is correctly formed in the sense of the agent (*kartari*). In the list beginning with *grah-* (cf. III.1.134), *vyathavat*... [the following is a fragmentary commentary on grammatical rules].

1. *Sūryaśataka* 2 2. *Kirātārjunīya* II.46 3. "Those having the meaning of 'to kill' (*pantyarthāḥ*)" 4. "Those having the meaning of 'proper modification' (*nyāyyavikaraṇārthāḥ*)" 63. I. [End of section]

Regarding those [words] prohibited [from taking the suffix *yuc*]: *avyāthī*; [the form] *avyathī* is derived from the root *vyath* by [Pāṇini III 2, 175] *jidṛkṣiviśri*, and [the form] *vyathanaḥ* is derived from the same root by [Pāṇini III 2, 149] *anañpūrvād yuc*. Furthermore, [the form] *vithuraḥ* is derived from *vyathi-* with vowel lengthening (*prasāraṇa*) and the addition of the suffix *ki*, as stated in [Uṇādi-sūtra I 40]: "The *rākṣasa* is called *vithuraḥ*. (801)

Next, regarding *prath* in the sense of becoming manifest (*prakhyāne*). Manifestation means becoming well-known (*prasiddhi*). From the roots *prath*, *smṛ*, *dṝ*, *tvar*, and *prath*, [the rule] *VII.4.95* prescribes *ātvam* for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*): *apaprathat*. From *prath*, *mrad*, and *bhrasj*, there is vocalization (*prasāraṇa*) and the elision of the *s* (cf. *Uṇ.* I.29): *pṛthuḥ*. From *prath*, with the suffix *ṣivan* and vocalization (cf. *Uṇ.* I.150): *pṛthivī*. In the group beginning with *alīka* (cf. *Uṇ.* IV.25 and Hem. Dh. 1003): *pṛthvīkā*. The feminine form *prattiḥ*. From *prath* with the suffix *amac* (*Uṇ.* V.68): *prathamaḥ*. (802)

*Pṛthu* [is derived from] *pṛ*, meaning "to spread. From the root *prath* (with *saṃprasāraṇa*), they consider this [form] to be non-Vedic (*anārṣa*). Thus, when there is the root *mṛd* (in the sense of softening), we have *mradim* (Uṇ. I, 804). *Pras* means "procreation" (*prasava*); Durga says *pras* means "expansion" (*vistāra*). *Mṛda* means "crushing" (*mardana*). One crushes (*mradate*), one causes to crush (*mradayati*), one crushed (*amamradat*). From the rule *prathimradi* (Uṇ. I, 29), we have *mṛduḥ* (soft) and *mṛdvīkā* (grape). In the *kryādi* class, *mṛd* means "to grind" (*kṣoda*): *mṛdnāti*, *amīmṛdat*, *amamardat* (Pāṇini VII, 4, 7). (Uṇ. I, 804)

*Skhada* means to tear apart; *khadana* is tearing apart. *Skhadayati* (805). *Kṣaji* [is used] in the senses of moving and giving. Its inclusion [in the root list] is for the sake of lengthening [the vowel] even when it is not a penultimate syllable, in the case of the affixes *ciṇ* and *ṇamul* (Pāṇini VI.4.93). It is precisely for this purpose that a rule for lengthening is prescribed there, even though an option for shortening ought to have been applied. The same should be understood for *dakṣi*, *kandi*, *krandi*, and *klandi* (807, 809–811). Kauśika says it is *kṣaji*. In the *curādi* group, *kṣaji* is listed in the sense of "living with difficulty" (X.79): *kṣañjayati* (806).

The root *dakṣ* is used in the senses of "to go" and "to injure. It is also used in the sense of "to increase" (*vṛddhi*) and "to be swift" (*śīghra*)—as stated in [Dhātupāṭha] I, 639—and because of these distinct meanings, it is recited again for the sake of derivatives such as *dakṣa*.

The root *krap* is used in the sense of "pity" (*kṛpā*). From it, one forms *krapate* and *krapayati*. According to the rule "there is vocalization (*prasāraṇa*) of *krap*" (Kāśikā on Pāṇini III, 3, 104), the word *kṛpā* is derived; furthermore, according to the Uṇādi-sūtras (II, 79), the word *kṛpaṇa* is formed. (807–808)

The roots *kadi*, *kradi*, and *kladi* signify agitation (*vaiklavya*). One who is agitated (*viklava*) is timid (*kātara*). According to Candra (see Ca. Dh. I, 520), the term is *vaikalya*. [From these roots] one forms *krandate* and *krandā*. Nandī states: *kada*, *krada*, and *klada*; thus, *kradā*. According to the rule "kadi, kradi, kladi in the sense of calling out and weeping" (I, 70–72), these are parasmaipada roots: *krandati* (809–811).

1 A gloss: *vrajavadavasām* is the reading in the *Gaṇapāṭha*; however, this [author], considering *vyathi* to be in place of *vraji*, has cited it. [In P] "jehlend" (wandering), which in K and C was subsequently inserted into the text. 2 PC *pṛthīkā*. 3 Cf. Hem. *Uṇ.* 647. 4 Cf. Candra-Dh. I 515, 516; I 64.

*Ñitvarā* means agitation (*saṃbhrama*). Here, agitation refers to acting with haste. [The forms are: *tvarate*, *tvarayati*, *tvarā*; [the aorist] *atatvarat*. [The gerund] *tvaritvā*. With the suffix *kvip* (Pāṇini III, 2, 178; VI, 4, 20), [we get] *tūḥ*. By the rule *ñītaḥ ktaḥ* (III, 2, 187), the suffix *kta* is applied; by the rule *niṣṭhāyāṃ ruṣyamatvarasaṃghuṣāsvanām* (VII, 2, 28), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: thus *tūrṇaḥ* and *tvaritaḥ*. In this way, the fact that the root begins with *ad* is for the sake of detailed exposition. [The noun] *tūrtiḥ*. By the rule *vahiśriyuśruglāhātvaribhyo nit* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV, 51), [we get] *tūrṇiḥ* (812).

The roots beginning with *ghaṭ* are marked with the *ṣi*-sign (*ṣit*). The result of being marked with the *ṣi*-sign has already been shown. Here, the first ten have been recited; however, some say that the four beginning with *dakṣ*, *kaṇḍū*, and so on, were recited in other locations and are restated here for the sake of their specific grammatical operations.
These are acute-accented (*udātta*) and belong to the class of those ending in an unaccented vowel (*anudāttet*). (768)

In the sense of "fever" (*jvara*): from here until the end of the section [of *phaṇ*], thirty-six roots are *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment) and are *parasmaipada*. *jvarati*, *jvarayati*; *ajvāri*, *ajvari*. *jvāraṃ-jvāram*, *jvaraṃ-jvaram*; *jvaritaḥ*; *jūḥ*; *jūrtiḥ*. By the rule *vījyājvaribhyo niḥ* (Uṇ. IV, 48): *jūrṇiḥ*. Because of the prohibition regarding *ajvarati* (Pāṇini II, 3, 54), the genitive case prescribed by *rujārthānām* (II, 3, 54) does not apply; thus: *cauraṃ jvarayati jvaraḥ* ("the fever causes the thief to suffer").

The root *gaḍ* means "to sprinkle. [It forms] *gaḍati*, *gaḍayati*. [The noun] *gaḍuḥ* [is formed by] *gaḍo ’ci* (Pāṇini III.1.134). [In the phrase] "the ox sleeps comfortably, being *gaḍī*," [it is derived from] *gaḍer ādeś ca kaḥ* (Uṇādi III.106): *kaḍatram*. [From] *gaḍeḥ kaḍa ca* (cf. Uṇādi III.135), [we get] *kaḍāraḥ*, meaning "tawny" (814). The root *heḍ* means "to surround" or "to cover. [It forms] *heḍati*, *hiḍayati*; the short vowel [of the root] occurs due to the authority of the specific recitation [in the Dhātupāṭha]. [Examples: *ahiḍi*, *aheḍi*; *heḍaṃ heḍam*, *hiḍaṃ hiḍam*. Others, having made the vowel short, state that there is optionally a lengthening in the *ciṇ* and *ṇamul* suffixes: *ahīḍi*, *ahiḍi*; *hīḍaṃ hīḍam*, *hiḍaṃ hiḍam* (815).

*vaṭ* and *bhaṭ* are used in the sense of commanding (*paribhāṣaṇa*). From *vaṭ* (in the sense of surrounding, *veṣṭana*) and *bhaṭ* (in the sense of hiring, *bhṛti*), as per [Dhātupāṭha] I.322 and 329, one forms *vāṭayati* and *bhāṭayati* (816, 817). *Naṭ* is used in the sense of bending (*nati*). One says *naṭati* and *naṭayati* in reference to a branch (*śākhā*); however, in the sense of dancing (*nṛti*), one says *nāṭayati*. In the *curādi* group, *naṭ* occurs in the sense of trickling down (*avasyandana*) [as X.12]; from this root, one forms *caurasyonāṭayati* according to [Pāṇini] II.3.56 (818).

The root *caka* means "to satisfy" and "to strike. From it, one forms *cakati* and *cakayati*. From the rule *kaṭhicakibhyām oraḥ* (Uṇādi-sūtra I.65), *cakoraḥ* is derived. Regarding the root *caka* in the sense of "satisfaction" (I.93), one has *cakate* (820). The roots *ṣṭaka* and *staka* mean "to strike. From them, one forms *ṣṭakati*, *tiṣṭakayiṣati*, and *tistakayiṣati* (819). The root *kakha* means "to laugh. One forms *kakhati* and *kakhayati*. Because it contains the vowel *e* (as indicated by the *edittva* rule), the form *akakhīt* is derived according to Pāṇini VII.2.5. In the Uṇādi-sūtras, from the root *kikh* one derives *lomaśaḥ* (821). 4.
¹ Thus all manuscripts. ² Kg *taḥ*. ³ Vgl. Hem. Uṇ. 626. ⁴ 820s before 819. ⁵ 65 *rage* in the sense of doubt (*śaṅkāyām*). *ragati*, *aragīt*. *ragaḍas* is a cymbal (*tālaḥ*) [822].

*lagi* means "to adhere. [It forms] *lagati*, *lagayati*, and *alagīt*. In the rule *kṣubdhasvāntadhvāntalagna* (Pāṇini VI.4.18), *lagna* is correct in the sense of "attached" (*sakta*); *lagita* is another form. *hrage*, *hlage*, *ṣṭhage*, and *sthage* mean "concealing" (*saṃvaraṇa*). Concealing is covering. [From these roots one forms] *sthagati*, *sthagayati*, *tiṣṭhagayiṣati*, and *tisthagayiṣati*. Durga reads *ṣage* and *sthage* (in the respective order). *Kage* is not mentioned. It is not stated what its meaning is because it has multiple meanings. Regarding that which is "not stated," some say that in that sense the root is *kagi*.

The roots *aka* and *aga* mean "to go crookedly. They form *akati* and *agati*. According to the rule for words beginning with *pṛṣodara* (Pāṇini VI.3.109), the vowel of *ana-* becomes *ā* [in the compound *anoka-*, where the *na* is elided]. Thus, *anokahaḥ* ("one who destroys the movement [of others]") refers to a tree. *Agati* means "the top" (*agram*; cf. Uṇādi-sūtra II.28). The roots *kaṇa* and *raṇa* mean "to go. These two, having the sense of motion, possess the property of being *mittva* (causing the substitution of *vṛddhi* by *eC* when followed by the suffix *nic*). However, when they mean "to sound," they take the form *kāṇayati*. (831, 832)

The roots *caṇ* and *śraṇ* have the meanings "to give" (*dāna*). One says *caṇati*, *caṇayati*, and *caṇakaḥ*; and because it also has the meanings of "motion" and "injury," one says *cāṇayati*. One says *śraṇati*, *śraṇayati*; and in the *cur*-class (X, 42), one says *viśrāṇayati*. Regarding the root *bhaj* in the sense of "giving away" (*viśrāṇana*)—as in [the verse] "by giving away other milch-cows" (Raghuvamśa II, 54)—Durga also cites *śaṇ*: *śaṇaḥ*, *śāṇaḥ* (Aṣṭādhyāyī 833, 835, 834).

Now, *kratha* and *klatha* have the meaning of "to injure. One says *krathati* and *krathayati*; and in the *curādi* class (X, 282, cf. 13), one says *caurasyotkrāthayati*. According to Candra and Durga, this is because the suffix *ṇic* follows a word ending in *ghañ*, and also because of the indicative mark (*liṅga*) in Pāṇini’s rule *nāṭakrāthapiṣām* (I. 3. 56). [The root] *can* also has the meaning of injury.
From the particle *ca* ("and"), it follows that it means "to injure. One says *canati* and *canayati* (840).

And *vanu* is not mentioned [in the list]. Likewise, the particle *ca* (*and*) serves the purpose of inclusion. Alternatively: not only *kage*, but *vanu* also is not mentioned, because it expresses general action (*kriyāsāmānya*). [Examples: *vanati*, *vanayati*; [gerunds] *vatvā*, *vanitvā*; [nouns] *vataḥ*, *saṃvananam*. Or, regarding the root *vana* and *ṣaṇa* in the sense of "eating" (*bhakti*) [DhP I 491–492], one says *vānayati*. *jvala* in the sense of "shining" (*dīpti*): *jvalati*, *jvalayati*. Its recitation here [at this point] is for the sake of the grammatical operations (*kārya*) beginning with *jvalā* [as taught in Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.150]. *hvala* and *hmala* in the sense of "moving" (*calana*): *hvalati*, *hvalayati*; *vihvalaḥ*.

*Smṛ* [is used] in the sense of *ādhyāna*. *Ādhyāna* means longing. [In this sense: *smarati*, *smarayati*. In the sense of reflection (*cintā*): *smārayati*, *vismārayati*. This recitation here is for the purpose of [indicating] the *mittva* [quality] regarding specific meanings not mentioned elsewhere. (845) 1 *okaṃ*; for *anokaha* ‘tree’, cf. Hem. I, 1020 and Uṇ. 595; all manuscripts read thus. 3 KC add *ślatha*. 1 66.

The root *dṝ* is used in the sense of fear (*bhaya*). It forms *darati*. *Daraḥ* refers to the Darad region, which is the land of the Romakas; [it also means] "he causes the hair to fall out" (*bālaṃ darayati*). In the *kryādi* class (IX, 23), *dṝ* is used in the sense of splitting (*vidāraṇe*): *dṛṇāti*, *dārayati kāṣṭham* ("he splits the wood"). Some say that its inclusion here is for the purpose of marking it as having the *mit* designation. In the *divādi* class, the *Pañcikā* states *dīryati*; some say that in the case of a reflexive object-agent (*karmakartṛ*), it is *dīryate*. The root *nṝ* in the sense of leading (*naye*) belongs to the *kryādi* class (IX, 25); its inclusion here is rare, being for the purpose of the *mit* designation. When one employs someone who is performing the action of leading, one says *narayati*.

The root *śrā* is used in the sense of "cooking. Its reading here after *adādi* (Pāṇini I.1.44) as *śrai* (I.966) is for the purpose of making it marked with the *mit* designation. Thus, one says *śrāti* or *śrāyati*; or when someone employs another to do so: *śrapayati caruṃ caitreṇa* ("he causes Caitra to cook the sacrificial porridge"). In another sense: *śrāpayati gharmaḥ*, meaning "it causes distress" (*khedayati*). (848)

Regarding the senses of killing (*māraṇa*), satisfying (*toṣaṇa*), and sharpening (*niśāna*): *niśāna* means sharpening or whetting; some read it as *niśamana*. The root *jñā* in the sense of "understanding" (*avabodhana*) belongs to the *kryādi* class (IX), but when used with the prefix *ni-* in the senses of killing and so forth, it is treated as a *mit* root: *saṃjñapayati paśum* ("he causes the animal to be killed"), *viṣṇuṃ vijñapayāmy aham* ("I inform Viṣṇu"), *prajñapayati śastram* ("he sharpens the weapon"). In other cases: *rājānaṃ vijñāpayati* ("he informs the king"); in the sense of understanding: *jñāpayati*; in the sense of making known: *prajñāpayati prāptim* ("he makes known the attainment"). Regarding satisfying: *evam ājñapto 'smi sāmājikaiḥ* ("Thus have I been commanded by the members of the assembly"). How? [The following:]...

Is *pradhvaṃsābhāva* intended [here] in the sense of "desiring to cause to know," according to the rule *pracha jñīpsāyām* (Pāṇini VI.1.20)? The short vowel here is due to an indicatory mark (*jñāpaka*), because of the rule *āpjñapyṛdhām īt* (Pāṇini VII.4.55), which applies the substitution of *īt* after the short vowel has been substituted. In the *curādi* group, *jñapi* (X.81) also serves the purpose of the *ṇic* affix when there is no external cause; some say its meaning is "desiring to cause to know. In the *curādi* group, *jñā* is used in the sense of "commanding" (X.193); from this [root], one says *ājñāpaya* [in the verse]: "O you who have known the distinctions of men, command them! (849).

The *ca-li* suffix [is applied] after *kam*. Although this root is already listed under the group beginning with *jval* (885), its repetition here is for the sake of making it *mit*; the vowel *i* is for the purpose of pronunciation. *Pracalayati latām* ("he shakes the creeper"). Elsewhere: *cālayati śīlam*, meaning "he removes" (*harati*) it. (850) *chadi* in the sense of strengthening (*ūrjana*). This root *chad* (meaning "covering," X.41), belonging to the *cur*-class, is *mit* when used in the sense of strengthening or giving life. *Chadayaty agniḥ* ("the fire strengthens"); [here] the causative suffix *ṇic* is used in the sense of the root itself (*svārthe*), or [it is used] in the sense of motive (*hetau*), meaning "he causes that which covers to act. Elsewhere: *chādayati gṛham* ("he covers the house"). (851)

The root *laḍ* occurs in the senses of "licking" (*jihvonmanthana*) and "churning" (*unmanthana*). This root *laḍ*, meaning "to sport" (*vilāsa*), belongs to the *bhvādi* class; it is marked as *mit* when denoting an action pertaining to the tongue or the act of churning. Examples: *lāḍayati jihvām* ("he licks the tongue"); *lalayati dadhi* ("he sports with the curd"). In other senses: *lāḍayati citram* ("he fondles the picture"); *lālayati bālam* ("he caresses the child"). Derivatives: *lālitaḥ*, *lālitakaḥ*, *lālikā*, *lālā*. According to Gupta, the sense is "licking the tongue": *abhīkṣṇaṃ jihvāśatāny ullalayati* ("he repeatedly lolls out hundreds of tongues"). In the *curādi* class, *laḍ* is used in the sense of "service" (*upasevā*): *lāḍayati* (Dhp. X. 7).

The root *mad* is used in the senses of "rejoicing" and "intoxication. Regarding *madī harṣe* (Dhātupāṭha IV.99), this root belonging to the *divādi* class is marked with the *mit* designation in this sense: *madayati surā Caitram* ("The wine gladdens Caitra"), *vimadayati śatrum* ("He intoxicates the enemy"). In other senses, because it has multiple meanings, it is used as follows: *unmādayati puruṣam* ("It drives a man mad"), *pramādayati* ("It causes negligence").
[Note: All manuscripts read this; KC reads *jñaḥ*.]

"And by the shame caused by the sounds of bursting, splitting, falling, and clashing"—thus says the *Śrī-Bhoja-sūtra* 1. It causes to burst; it resounded, making the quarters of space resound. Pots and other vessels were measured out. This has been illustrated.

The roots *jan*, *jṝṣ*, *knasu*, and *rañj*, as well as those ending in *-am*, are designated as *mit*. These are: *jan* in the sense of "manifesting" (IV, 41); *jṝṣ* in the sense of "decay of age" (I, 22); *knasu* in the sense of "bending and shining" (I, 6); and *rañj* in the sense of "coloring" (I, 1048). [Thus] *janayati*. The root *jan* in the sense of "procreation" (III, 24) is also included here because it belongs to the *juhoty-ādi* class; otherwise, since there is no difference between the meaning and form, he would have stated that they optionally do not take the *mit* designation. Or rather, this [root] is Vedic: *janayati*. *jṝṣ* in the sense of "decay of age" belongs to the *div-ādi* class.

From the root *jṛ* (I, 924), [the suffix *ṇic*] forms *jārayati*; however, from *jṛṇāti* (IX, 24), it forms *jārayati* as in *patim jārayati* ("he causes his husband to age") and *abhrakam jārayati* ("it dissolves mica"). From the root *rañj* (I, 1048), when used with the causative suffix (*ṇic*) in the sense of "pleasing deer," there is the elision of the nasal (*nalopaḥ*) according to Pāṇini VI, 4, 24, 3: *rajayati mṛgān* ("he pleases the deer"). [The following roots form their causatives with the suffix *ṇic*: *ramayati*, *bhramayati*, *saṃkramayati*, *viśramayati*. (862–866) Regarding *jvala*, *hvala*, *hmala*, *cala*, and *nama*: for these, the status of having the marker *m* (*mittva*) is established as compulsory; however, when they are not preceded by a prefix (*anupasargāt*), it is made optional. Thus: *jvālayati* or *jvalayati*, *hvālayati* or *hvalayati*, *hmālayati* or *hmalayati*.

It causes to move, it moves; it inclines, it inclines. However, with prefixes, it is always [mittvanta]: *prajvalayati*, *vihvalayati*, *prahlādayati*, *pracalayati*, *praṇamayati*. And for *glā*, *snā*, *van*, and *vam*: there is an option (*vikalpa*) regarding the first two because they do not otherwise apply; for the other two, it applies because they already do. For these, when without prefixes, the status of being *mit* is optional: *glapayati* / *glāpayati*; *snapayati* / *snāpayati*; *vanayati* / *vānayati*; *vamayati* / *vāmayati*. Only when without a prefix: *praglāpayati*, *prasnāpayati*; *upavanayati*, *udvamayati*.
The designation *mit* is prohibited for these because they end in *m*. [Examples: *kāmayate*, *āmayati*, *ācāmayati*. Regarding *śamo ’darśane*:

the designation *mit* applies to the root *śamu* (meaning "to calm," Pāṇini IV.1.92) in senses other than "seeing. Since this is already established by its ending in *m*, the statement is for the sake of restriction (*niyamārtham*). [Examples: *śamayati rogam* ("he calms the disease"), *niśamayati ślokam* ("he causes the verse to be heard"). But in the sense of "seeing," [it is not *mit*]: *niśāmayati rūpam* ("he observes the form"); *niḥśarkaram idaṃ tīrthaṃ Bharadvāja niśāmaya* (Rāmāyaṇa I.2.6, Gorresio edition), meaning "look! (870).

The root *yama* [is marked with the technical term] *mit* when it does not mean "to serve food. For the root *yama* in the sense of "ceasing" (*uparama*)—as listed at I, 1033—the designation *mit* applies only to meanings other than "serving food. Examples: *yamayati*, *niyamayati*, *saṃyamayati*. However, in the sense of "serving food," [it is used thus]: *yāmayati śrāddhe 'nnam* ("he serves food at a funeral feast"). [Notes: 1 Śrī Bhoja did not include this rule. 2 See 861. 3 P reads *vinamayati*. 4 P reads *prāptau*. 5 The editions of Schlegel and Bombay read *akardamam* and *niḥśarkaram*. 6 P omits this. 68.
[The root] *mayati* [is used in the sense of] "shining like the moon. Regarding this very point, Durga states that *svana* means "to adorn": "he adorns the garment" (*svanayati vastram*).

From the prefixes *apa-* and *pari-*, the root *skhadir* [takes the suffix *ṇic*]. From these two prefixes alone, *skhadir* is [conjugated as] *mit*. Thus: *apaskhadayati*, *pariskhadayati*. Śrī Bhoja says that it occurs with the prefix *ava-*: *avaskhadayati*. It does not occur with other prefixes: *praskhādayati*.

The root *phaṇ* means "to move. From it, one forms *phaṇati* and *phaṇayati*. By the rule *phaṇāṃ ca saptānām* (Pāṇini VI.4.125), there is optionally the substitution of *et* for the vowel and the elision of the reduplication: *paphaṇuḥ* or *pheṇuḥ*. When meaning something other than movement, one uses *phāṇayati*, which means "to make a pot free from moisture. By the rule *kṣubdhasvāntadhvānta* (Pāṇini VII.2.18), the form *phāṇṭam* is correct when it does not mean "effort" (*anāyāsa*). Some say that the roots beginning with *ghaṭ* precede *phaṇ*; these [roots] are udātta and have an udātta indicatory letter (*udāttet*). (804) [Note: 873 refers to the serial number of the preceding section.]

The root *rāj* means "to shine" and is udātta. With the suffix *svariteta*, it forms *rājate* and *rajati*; the future participle is *rājitā*. From the separate mention of the suffixes *ana* and *kan* in the rule *śīṅ-bhi-ya* (Uṇ. III.82, cf. Hem. Uṇ. 71), we derive *rājānakaḥ*. With the suffix *kanin* (Uṇ. I.156), we have *rājā*. With the suffix *anya* (Uṇ. III.100) applied to *rāj*, we have *rājanyaḥ*. (874)

The roots *bhrājṛ*, *ṭubhrāśṛ*, *ṭubhlāśṛ*, and *āśṛ* signify "to shine. They are udātta and anudāttet. From them are derived: *bhrājate*, *babhrāje*, *bhreje*; according to some, because of the suffix *ṭu*, there is also *bhrāje*. By *ṭvito 'thuc* (Pāṇini III.3.89), we have *bhrājathuḥ*. Some do not accept the *ṛt* designation for *bhrāj* and *bhrāś*, and in that alternative view, the *iṣṭha* rule applies to the short vowel: *ababhrājat* or *abibhrajat*. By *naptṛ-neṣṭṛ* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.96), we derive *bhrātṛ* ("brother"). By *vā bhrāśa-bhlāśa* (Pāṇini III.1.70), the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied: *bhrāśate* or *bhrāśyate*, *bhlāśate* or *bhlāśyate*; and *bhrāśathuḥ*, *bhlāśathuḥ*. (875–877)

The roots *syam*, *svan*, *stan*, and *dhvan* [are listed here]. From this point until the end of the section on *kṣal*, twenty-eight roots are *seṭ* and take the *parasmaipada* endings. *Syam*: *syamati*, *syemuḥ*, *sasyamuḥ*; by the *uṇādi* rule (III. 46), *syamīkā* means "a worm. *Svan*: *svanati*, *svenuḥ*, *sasvanuḥ*; by Pāṇini VIII. 3. 69 (*veś ca svano bhojane*), there is the substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*]: *viṣvaṇati*, *avaṣvaṇati*; *svanayati*. The root ending in *svan* belongs to the *phaṇādi* group. *Stan*: *stanati*, *stanayati*. *Dhvan*: *dhvanati*, *dhvanayati*. Candra (Dhātupāṭha II. 1. 153) lists *ṣṭan*: *tiṣṭanayiṣati*. (878–881)

*ṣama* (to calm), *ṣṭama* (to grow weary), *avaikI* (to go), *avye3* (to protect)—these end in *i*. *samati*; *samaḥ*, *viṣamaḥ*, *samayati*. *stamati*, *stamayati* (882, 883). [The class] *vṛt* (to turn). The learned hold that the roots beginning with *ghaṭ* end with these [roots]. *jvaIa* (to blaze); *jvalati*, *jvalitā*. According to Pāṇini III.1.140 (*jvalitikasantebhyo ṇo vā*), there is optionally the suffix *ṇa*: *jvālaḥ*, *jvālā*, *jvalaḥ* (884).

1. *a* and *duṇt* should be stated [as suffixes]. 2. *pū* is added. 3. All manuscripts read *so*. 69. The root *cal* means "to shake. [Derivatives: *calati*, *calitaḥ*, *calanaḥ*; *cālaḥ*, *calaḥ*; *caracalavat* (cf. VI.1.12.6) thus forms *calācalaḥ*; even when there is elision (*yaṅluk*), there is an option: *cācalaḥ*, *cañcalaḥ*. *Caliḥ* in the sense of shaking (850); with the causative suffix (*ṇau*), it is *calayati*. In the *curādi* group, *cala* means "to support" (X.68): *cālayati* (885).

*Jala* means "to strike. "Striking" (*ghātya*) refers to the state of being dull (*jaḍatva*), meaning a lack of sharpness. It is *jalati*. *Jāla* and *jala* are two forms derived from the same root; due to the established optionality of the suffix, they have distinct meanings. In the *curādi* group, there is *jala* in the sense of "obstructing" (*apavāraṇe*, X, 10): *jālayati*. Because *la* and *ḍa* are identical, [the derivative] is *jaḍaḥ* (886). *Ṭala* and *ṭvala* mean "overflowing" (*vaiplavye*). Overflowing itself is "overflow-ness" (*vaiplavyam*). *Ṭalati* (387, 888). *Sthala* means "in a place" (*sthāne*). Candra reads *ṣṭhala* (Ca. Dh. I, 565). *Sthalati*. *Sthālam*, *sthālī*, *sthalam*, *sthalī* (889).

The root *hal* means "to scratch" (*vilekhane*). Scratching (*vilekhana*) is pulling (*karṣaṇa*). It forms *halati*. From the *Uṇādi-sūtra* IV.117: *hālā* (wine), *hālam*, *halam*; and from *haliḥ*, *haḍiḥ*. The root *ṇal* (with prefix *pra-*) means "to crush" (*gandhe*), where "crushing" (*gandha*) means "destroying" (*ardana*). It forms *praṇalati*. [Derivatives: *nālam* (stalk); *nālā* (the stalk of lotuses and the like); *nālī*, *nāḍī* (tube/vein); *praṇālaḥ*, *praṇālī*, *praṇāḍikā* (water-channel); *nalaḥ*, *naḍaḥ* (reed). The root *pal* (with prefix *pa-*) means "to go" (*gatau*). It forms *pālaḥ* (protector); *palam* (flesh); *palalam* (sesame paste). One who protects cows (*gāḥ pālayati*) is a *gopālaḥ* (cowherd). In the *Cura-di* group (X.69), *pal* means "to protect": it forms *pālayati*. (892)

The root *bal* means "to breathe" (*prāṇana*). Breathing is life. It breathes; thus, *bāla*, *bālā*. Before suffixes such as *ac* (Pāṇini III.1.134), it forms *bala*, *balam*. In the *curādi* class (X.85), with the *mit* designation, it forms *balayati*. And [it is used] in the sense of enclosing grain (*dhānyāvarodha*). That wherein grain is enclosed—[this refers to] the meaning of a granary (*kusūla*); thus, *balataḥ*. However, *val* in the sense of covering (*saṃvaraṇa*) is *ātmanepada*: *valate* (893).

The root *pul* has the meaning "greatness. *Polati*. *Polaḥ*, *vipulaḥ*, *pulaḥ*, *pulaḥ*; "that which has *pula* [as its characteristic]" is *pulinaṃ* (cf. *Uṇ.* I.53); from *kuṇi* and *pula* with the suffix *kindac* (cf. *Uṇ.* IV.85): *Pulindaḥ*; in the *pināka*-group (cf. *Uṇ.* IV.15): *pulākaḥ* means "chaff"; with the suffix *ik* (cf. *Uṇ.* IV.142): *puliḥ*, *pulakaḥ*. In the *tudādi* group (III.144): *pulati*; in the *curādi* group (X.61): *polayati* (894).

The root *kula* is used in the senses of "gathering" (*saṃstyāna*) and "relatives" (*bandhu*). "Gathering" means a collection. From this [root] are derived: *kola* (the jujube fruit), *kakkola*, *kaṅkola*, *kula*, *nakula* (mongoose)—[all formed] by the suffix *kālan* according to Uṇādi-sūtra I.117—and *kulāla* (potter). The roots *śala*, *hula*, and *paṭḷ* mean "to go. *Śalati*. [From this: *śālā* (hall), *śala* (a kind of bird), *śalala* (the bristle of a porcupine), *śalyaka* (scorpion), *śalya* (dart), *śalmali* (silk-cotton tree), *śalabha* (locust), *śalka* (scale), *śalākā* (pin), and *śālūka* (the bulbous root of a lotus, etc.). Regarding the root *śala* in the sense of "moving" and "covering" (Dhātupāṭha I.519), its recitation here is for the purpose of applying the operations belonging to the *jvalādi* group. *Holati*. *Patati*. Because it is marked with the indicator *ḷ*, in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense... [it takes the augment *iṭ*].
1. Regarding *ḍa* and *la*: 2. All manuscripts read *sa*. ^ ? See Hem. Dh. I, 980; I, 70; *aṅ* (III, 1, 55);

*pataḥ pum* (VII, 4, 19): *apaptat*; *utpātaḥ*, *nipātaḥ*, *pāto rāhuḥ*, *pataḥ*; by *ner gadanada* (VIII, 4, 17), there is *ṇatva*: *praṇipatati*; by *sanīvantardhabhrasja* (VII, 2, 49), there is *veṭ*; by *sani mīmāghv* (VII, 4, 54), there is *iṭ* and the elision of the reduplication (58): *pitsati*, *pipatiṣati*.

*Patitaḥ*: because there is no prohibition of the augment *iṭ* by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* (VII. 2. 15), as indicated by the evidence of the rule *dvitīyā śritātītapatita* (II. 1. 24); *utpatiṣṇuḥ*: with the suffix *iṣṇuc* by the rule *alaṃkṛñ* (III. 2. 136); *patanaḥ*: with the suffix *yuc* by the rule *jucaṅkramya* (III. 2. 150); *prapātukaḥ*: with the suffix *ukañ* by the rule *laṣapatapada* (III. 2. 154); *gehānuprapātam āste*: with the suffix *ṇamul* by the rule *viśipatipadiskandām* (III. 4. 56); [and] *pātakaḥ*: with the suffix *ṣṭran* by the rule *dāmnī* (III. 2. 182).

From the roots *pat* and *caṇḍi*, the suffix *āl-añ* [is applied] (Uṇ. I.116): *pātāla*; from *pat*, the suffix *aṅgac* in the sense of a bird (Uṇ. I.118): *pataṅga*; from *pat*, *ra* and *la* [are added] (Uṇ. III.74): *patsala*; by the rule *aminakṣi* (Uṇ. III.105), the suffix *atran* [is applied]: *patatra*; from *vi* and *pat*, the suffix *tanan* (Uṇ. III.150): *pattana*; from *pat*, the suffix *tha*...

The suffix *ini* [is applied] by [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.12: *panthāḥ* (“path”); the suffix *ni* [is applied] after the roots *śali*, *pati*, and *padi* (cf. Uṇādi IV.14): *patākā* (“banner”); from the rule *spṛhigṛhi* (Pāṇini III.2.158), [we derive] *patayāluḥ*. From the roots *hula* in the senses of “injury” and “concealing”: *holaḥ*, *hulaḥ*, *huḍaḥ*; *huliḥ*, *huḍiḥ*; in the *uṇādi* section, *Huluḥ* means “a region” (896–898). In the sense of “boiling” or “cooking”: *kvathati*, *akvathīt*; *kvāthaḥ*, *kvathaḥ*; in the sense of possession (Pāṇini V.2.115), *kvāthikā* means “barley-gruel. (899) In the sense of “going on a path”: *pathati*, *apathīt*; *pāthaḥ*, *pathaḥ*. (900)

The root *math* means "to churn" (*viloḍana*). From it: *mathati*, *amathīt*. [The nouns] *māthaḥ* and *mathaḥ* are formed with the suffix *urac* according to Uṇādi-sūtra I.39: *mandivāśi* etc.; thus, *Mathurā*. Regarding *manth* in the sense of "churning": *manthati*; in the *kryādi* class (IX.40), *mathnāti*. (901) 3

The root *ṭuvam* means "to vomit. Vomiting is the upward movement of what has been eaten. [Derivatives include: *vamati*, *vāmaḥ*, *vamaḥ*, *vamathuḥ*, *vamitaḥ*. According to some, there is the augment *ud*: *vāntvā* or *vamitvā*; "one who eats what has been vomited is indeed shameless" (*aghṛṇaḥ khalu vāntāśī*). By the rule *na śasadada* (VI.4.126), we have *vavamatuḥ*. By the rule *glāsnāvanuvamāṃ ca* (868), there is optionally the designation *mit*: *vāmayati* or *vamayati*. By the rule *jidṛkṣi* (III.2.157), the suffix *ini* is applied.

Regarding *vāmī*: although the prohibition [of *vṛddhi*] by rule VII.3.34, *nodāttopadeśasya*, would apply, the *vṛddhi* is established by the Vārttika on VII.3.34, *avamika-micamīnām*. From the root *vāmi* with the suffix *ṇvul* (III.1.133), we have *vāmakaḥ*. From the root *vāmayati* with the suffix *lyuṭ* (III.3.115), we have *yogavāmanam*. "One who does not vomit" (*na vamati*) is *avamaḥ* (with the suffix *ghañ*, III.3.18–19). In the sense of possession (*astyarthe*), by rule V.2.100, we have *vāmanaḥ*. *Vāmī* (IV.1.41) refers to a female horse (*aśvā*). (902)

The root *bhram* means "to wander. By the rule *vā bhrāśabhlāśa* (Pāṇini III.1.70), the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied: *bhramati*, *bhramyati*. By the rule *vā jṝbhramutrasām* (Pāṇini VI.4.124), the substitution of *e* for the vowel and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*) occur: *bhemuḥ*, *babhramuḥ*. [The gerunds] *bhrāntvā*, *bhramitvā*. 1. *phuḍūr* 2. *soalleHss.* (an orthographic error for *meṣaḥ*? 3. Omitted. 71. I.

The suffix *ṇa* [is applied] after the root *bhram* (to wander); according to Durga, [the forms] are *bhrāmaḥ* and *bhramaḥ*. From the root *bhram*, the suffix *u* is added: *abhramuḥ*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV, 117: *bhramiḥ*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV, 120, "from *bhram*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the suffix *ki*": thus *bhṛmiḥ* means wind. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] III, 132, "after *arti*, *kami*, and *bhrami*, the suffix *aran*": thus *bhramaraḥ*. In the *divādi* class (IV, 96), it is listed for the meaning of the *śamādi* group: *bhrāmyati* (903). The root *kṣar* (to flow/move): *kṣarati*, *kṣariṣyati*. *Kṣāraḥ*, *kṣārī*; although the suffix *ṇa* is used, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* (IV, 1, 15, Kāśikā) is applied here because "in some cases, even when *aṇ* is prescribed, [it occurs]. *Kṣaraḥ*, *akṣaram* (904).

The root *kṣal* is used in the sense of accumulation (*saṃcaya*) and movement (*saṃcalana*). It forms *kṣalati*. In the *cur*-class (*curādi*), *kṣal* means purification (*śauca*); see [X, 57]: *kṣālayati*. [These roots] are accented on the first syllable and have an indicatory vowel *ṭ* (*udāttā udāttetaḥ*). 836. (904a)

The root *saha* is used in the sense of enduring (*marṣaṇe*). Enduring is patience (*kṣamā*). This [root] is udātta and anudāttet; it takes the augment *iṭ* and is conjugated in the ātmanepada. It forms *sahate*; *sisahiṣate*. By the rule *stanbhusivusahāṃ caṅi* (Pāṇini VI.1.116), there is the substitution of *ṣ*: *paryasīṣahat*. By the rule *saḥ svidisvadisahīnāṃ ca* (VI.1.62), there is the substitution of *s*: *sisāhayiṣati*. By the rule *parinivibhyaḥ* (VIII.3.70), there is the substitution of *ṣ*: *viṣahate*. By the rule *sivādīnāṃ vāḍvyavāye ’pi* (VIII.3.71), the substitution of *ṣ* is optional: [either *viṣahate* or *visahate*].

*paryasahata* and *paryaṣahata*: because of the explicit recitation [of the root] *sah* in the rule *kṛtya-eti-sākṣāt-prabhṛtiṣu karmasu* (Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.4.74), there is no [application of the suffix *ṇamul*]; by the rule *tīṣasa-ha-līḷa-vām-ava-tām* (VII.2.48), there is optionally *iṭ*: *sahitā*, *soḍhā*, *visoḍhā*. By the rule *sahivahor ot* (VI.3.112), there is *oṭ*: *soḍhaḥ*. Because of the mention of the phoneme (*varṇagrahaṇa*), this applies to *sāhi* as well, resulting in *soḍhā*; when the *ṇi*-affix is elided, by the rule *pūrvatrāsiddhena* (VIII.2.1) and the principle that "an operation is as if it had not taken place" (*sthānivadbhāva*), the substitution of *ḍha* and so forth occurs.

In the word *dāśvān*, [the suffix] *kvasu* is applied according to [Pāṇini] VI.1.12; *sāhvān* is formed by [the rule] *śakisahoś ca* (III.1.99); *sahyam* is formed by [the suffix] *yat*; *sahanaḥ* is formed by [the suffix] *lyuḥ* (III.1.134); *pṛtanāṣāṭ* is formed by [the suffix] *ṇviḥ* according to *saheḥ pṛtanartābhyāṃ ca* (VIII.3.109); and *turāṣāṭ* is formed by [the same rule] (III.2.63). Regarding the substitution of *s* for *ṣ* in *sāḍ* [from the root] *sah*, [the rule] *saheḥ sāḍaḥ sa* (VIII.3.56) applies; however, this substitution does not occur when the form lacks the quality of *sāḍ*, as in the expression *turāsāhaṃ purodhāya* (Kumārasambhava).

In *sahiṣṇuḥ*, the vowel is lengthened by Pāṇini VI.3.116 (*nahivṛtivṛṣi...*), and the suffix *iṣṇuc* is added by III.2.136 (*alaṃkṛñ...*); thus, *sahiṣṇuḥ*. In *sāhayaḥ*, the suffix *śa* is added to the causative form (*ṇyantāt*) by III.1.138 (*anupasargāl limpavinda...*); thus, *sāhayaḥ*. In *sarvaṃsahaḥ*, the suffix *khac* is added by III.2.46 (*saṃjñāyāṃ bhṛtr...*); thus, *sarvaṃsahaḥ*. By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.188 (*asun*), we have *sahas*. By III.4.65 (*śakadhṛṣajñā...*), the suffix *tumun* is used: *sahate bhoktum* ("he is able to eat"). By the rule *saheḥ ṣaṣ kvip ca* (Vārttika 905), the root *sah* becomes *ṣaṣ* with the suffix *kvip*; thus, *ṣaṭ* ("six").
According to the *curādigaṇa* (X.267), the suffix *ṇic* is optionally applied up to the root *dhṛṣ*: *sahati* or *sāhayati*.
1. Cf. Hem. Uṇ. 800. 2. All manuscripts read *siṣahiṣate*, but cf. VIII.3.61; the Kāśikā reads *vihasane* for *visahane*. 4. Cf. I.767. 5. Cf. Hem. Uṇ. 951; I.72.

The root *ram* is used in the sense of "playing" (*krīḍā*). It is marked with an anudātta accent, is anudāttet, lacks the augment *iṭ*, and is ātmanepada. [Examples: *ramate*. By Pāṇini I.3.83–84, the parasmaipada is used after the prefixes *vi-*, *ā-*, and *pari-* with *ram*: *viramati*, *uparamati*. Here, the root is transitive because it contains an implied causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*). By Pāṇini I.3.85, the parasmaipada is optionally used when the root is intransitive: *yāvadbhuktam uparamate* or *uparamati*. By Pāṇini VII.2.73, the suffix *sak* is added to the roots *yam*, *ram*, *nam*, and *mā*: [Aorist] *vyaraṃsīt*; [Future] *rantā*.

*ramaṇaḥ*, *ramaṇī*, *ramaḥ*, *ramā*, *Rāmaḥ*, *rāmā*, *ramyaḥ*; by [Pāṇini] III.2.13, *stambakarṇayo ramijapoḥ*, the suffix *ac* is applied: *stamberamaḥ* (an elephant); by [Uṇādi-sūtra] II.2, *hanikuṣi*, the suffix *kthan* is applied: *rathaḥ* (a chariot); by [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.14, *ramas ta ca*, *ratnam* (a jewel); by [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.214, *ramer deśe haś ca*: *rahas* (a secret place); *raṇḍā* (by Uṇādi I.113); by [Uṇādi-sūtra] V.14, *sau rameḥ ktaḥ pūrvasya ca dīrghaḥ*: *sūrato budhaḥ* (a wise man who is self-restrained); by [Uṇādi-sūtra] II.14, *cakiramyor uc copadhāyāḥ*: *rumram* (906).

The root *ṣadl* is used in the senses of falling apart (*viśaraṇa*), going (*gati*), and despondency (*avasādana*). "Falling apart" means crumbling; "despondency" means lack of enthusiasm. From here up to the end of [the section on] *ruh*, there are five roots that are *aniṭ* (taking no *iṭ*) and are *parasmaipada* (active voice). By the rule *pāghrādhmādheṭdrśaḥ śaḥ* (Pāṇini VII.3.78), the root *sad* becomes *sīd*: *sīdati*, *siṣatsati*. Regarding the form *asadat*, the substitution of *s* for *ṣ* occurs by the rule *sader aprateḥ* (VIII.3.66): *pariṣīdati*, *pratisīdati*. Furthermore, by the rule *sadi-svañjyoḥ parasya liṭi* (VIII.3.118): [the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs after these roots when followed by the suffixes of the *liṭ* tense].

He sat down (*niṣasāda*). From the rule *lupasadaścara* (Pāṇini III.1.24), the intensive suffix *yaṅ* is applied in the sense of censuring the action, resulting in *sāsadyate*. From the rule *satsūdviṣa* (Pāṇini III.2.61), the suffix *kvip* is applied; by the rule *pūrvapadāt* (Pāṇini VIII.3.106), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs: *śuciṣat*, *pariṣat*, *upaniṣat*, and *niṣaṇṇaḥ*. From the root *sad-* with the suffix *iñ* (Uṇādi IV.124), we have *sādī*; with *ni-* prefixed, *niṣādī*. From the root *sad-* with the suffix *ṇaḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.140), we have *niṣādaḥ*. With the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.18), we have *viṣādaḥ*. By the rule *sado 'ci* (Pāṇini III.1.134) [we have *sadman*]; and by the rule *nau sader* (Uṇādi IV.95)... [the suffix *man* is applied].

From the rule *svarac* [Uṇādi IV, 124], we have *niṣadvaraḥ* meaning "mud"; from *asun* [Uṇādi IV, 188], *sadaḥ* meaning "an assembly hall"; from *gudhṛvīpacivaci* [Uṇādi IV, 166], *sattram*; from *saṃjñāyāṃ samaja* [Pāṇini III, 3, 99], *kyap*: *niṣadyā* meaning "marketplace"; by the rule *sādakārayoḥ kṛtrime* [VI, 3, 122, 1], there is lengthening: *prāsādaḥ*; from *dādheṭsi* [III, 2, 159], *ruḥ*: *sadruḥ*. (907)

The root *śad* is used in the sense of "cutting" (*śātana*), which means making thin. According to Pāṇini VI.1.78 (*pāghrādhmā...*), the root *śad* undergoes the substitution *śīy*. Furthermore, by I.3.60 (*śadeḥ śita*), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) terminations and the suffix *āna* are applied: *śīyate*, *śatsyati*, *aśadat*. By VII.3.42 (*śader agatau taḥ*), the suffix *ta* is added: *śātayati*. From this, we derive *śātanaḥ* (masculine) and *śātanī* (feminine, belonging to the *gaurādi* group). *Śādaḥ* refers to a patch of grass; *śadaḥ* refers to an outcaste among Kṣatriyas (*kṣatriyāpaśadaḥ*). From *vi-śad-* comes *viśadaḥ*. By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.65 (*adi-śadi-bhyāṃ krin*), the suffix *krin* is added: *śadriḥ*. [Also] from *ruś* and *śāti*, the suffix *krun* is added (Uṇādi...).

(IV, 103): *śatruḥ* [is derived from] *śad*, with *ūc* as the suffix and *rak* added; thus *śūdraḥ*. Regarding *dādheṭsiśadasado ruḥ* (III, 2, 159): *śadruḥ*. (908) 1 See I, 767. 2 According to the manuscripts, this is also the correct reading of the Kāśikā. 3 All manuscripts read thus. 4 See Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 394. 73 I.

The root *kruś* is used in the sense of calling out and weeping. From it come: *krośati* (he cries out), *kroṣṭṛ* (one who cries out), *ākroṣṭṛ* (one who reviles). Also *krośaḥ*, *kruśaḥ*, and *utkrośaḥ* (the osprey). By the rule *sitanigamimasi* (Uṇādi I.70), the suffix *tun* is applied: *kroṣṭṛn*. (909)

The root *budh* is used in the sense of "understanding" (*avagamana*). Understanding is making known (*jñāpana*). 2. *bodhati*, *abodhīt*. By the rule *gatibuddhipratyavasānārtha* (Pāṇini I.4.52), the agent (*kartṛ*) receives the designation of object (*karman*): *bodhayati śiṣyaṃ dharmam* ("he causes the student to understand the Dharma"), [and thus] *boddhā* ("one who understands"). By the rule *igupadha* (Pāṇini III.1.135), the suffix *ka* is applied: *budhaḥ* ("wise one"). By the rule *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.18): *bodhaḥ* ("awakening"). By the rule *matibuddhi* (Pāṇini III.2.188), the suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the present tense: *rājñāṃ buddhaḥ* ("known by kings"). In the *divādi* class (Pāṇini IV.63), it is *budhyate*; in the *hikkādi* class (Pāṇini I.924), it is *bodhate* and *bodhati*. The future participle is *bodhitā* (911).

*ruha* [is used] in the sense of the birth of a seed. The birth of a seed is the production of a sprout. From *ruhati*, [we derive] *ruhaḥ*; by the rule *po 'nyatarasyām* (VH 3.43), we have *ropayati* and *rohayati*. By the application of the suffix *ka* in the sense of the suffix *ghañ* (III.3.58.4), we have *bījaruhākaroti* (cf. I.4.74). *Chinnaruhāḥ* refers to hair; *ke ruhaḥ* (III.1.135) refers to a deer; *praruhaḥ*, *prarohaḥ*, *ārohaḥ*, *ruḍhaḥ*, *rūḍhiḥ*; and from *ruha* there is also *vṛddhi* (Uṇ.).

I. 48) Thus, *rauhiṣa* refers to a type of grass and also to a deer. [The suffix] *in* is applied according to *hṛpiśiruhi* (Uṇ. IV. 118): *rohin* means "deer. [The suffix] *iti* is applied according to *hṛsṛruhiyuṣibhya itiḥ* (Uṇ. I. 99): *rohit*. [The suffix] *a* is applied according to *ruhc raś ca lo vā* (Uṇ. III. 94): *lohitaḥ*, *rohitaḥ*, *rohiṇī*. [The suffix] *inan* is applied according to *anyatrāpi ca* (Uṇ. II. 55): *rohiṇaḥ*. (912) Those with a low-pitched initial vowel that have a high-pitched penultimate vowel [are listed here]. 843.

The root *kuca* is used in the senses of mixing (*saṃparcana*), crookedness (*kauṭilya*), obstructing (*pratiṣṭambha*), and scraping (*vilekhana*). Mixing is being blended; obstructing is blocking; scraping is drawing away. It forms *saṃkocati* and *saṃkucitaḥ*. By Pāṇini III.1.135, the suffix *ghañ* is applied to form *kucaḥ*; there is no substitution of *kutva* [of *c* to *k*] here. (910)

The root *kasa* means "to go. From it derive: *kasati* (he goes), *utkasati* (he goes upward), and *kāsayati* (he causes to go). *Vikasitaḥ* (blossomed), *kasaḥ*, and *kāsaḥ* (cough). According to the rule *nīg vañcu-sraṃsu-dhvaṃsu-bhraṃsu-kasa-* (Pāṇini VI.4.24), one says *canīkasyate*. By the rule *stheśabhāsa-* (Pāṇini III.2.175), the suffix *varac* is added: *vikasvaraḥ* (radiant). By the rule *ṇit kasipadyarteḥ* (Uṇādi I.87), the suffix *ūḥ* is added: *kāsūḥ* (a spear). By the rule *sami kasa ukan* (Uṇādi II.29), one has *saṃkasukaḥ* (unsteady). (913)

The two roots *udāt* and *udātt* are *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*) and *parasmaipadin* (active voice). [The section] *vṛt* ends with the *jvalādi* group. *Hikka*, meaning "an indistinct sound," begins here; thirty-six roots up to *guhū* (numbered 944) are *seṭ* and *ubhayatobhāṣā* (used in both voices). Examples: *hikkate*, *hikkati*. *hikkā*, *hikkitam*.
(914) 1. cf. VII.1.95; 2. *saṃjñāpanam*; 3. all manuscripts read *abhotsīt*; 4. after 912; 5. S reads *trayastriṃśat*, KC reads *trayoviṃśatiḥ*.

I 74 *aci* in the sense of "going. *añcate*, *añcati*, *añcyate*; *añcitaḥ*. *añcu* in the sense of "going" (cf. I, 203): *añcati*, *acyate*, *aktaḥ*. Some say *acu*: *acati*, *acitvā* / *aktvā*, *aktaḥ* (915). *ḍuyācṛ* in the sense of "begging": *yācate*, *yācati*, *ayayāca*. *yācitaḥ*. By the rule *yajayāca* (VII, 3, 66), there is an absence of *kutva*: *yācyam*. From roots ending in *ḍvit*, the suffix *ktri* is applied (III, 3, 88; cf. IV, 4, 20): *yācitrimam*. Durga says that because it ends in *ṭvit*, [the suffix] *thu* is applied: *yācathuḥ* (III, 3, 89). By the rule *yajayācayata* (III, 3, 90), the suffix *naṅ* is applied: *yācñā* (916).

*Reṭ* in the sense of reviling: *reṭate*, *reṭati*, *arireṭat*. (917) *Cat* and *cad* in the sense of begging. The letter *ca* [in the root] is for the purpose of expressing speech (*bhāṣārtha*), while the meaning of *reṭ* is for the purpose of speech (*reṭrartha*). From the rule *mandivāśi* (Uṇ. I, 39), the suffix *urac* is applied: *caturaḥ*. From the rule *cater uran* (Uṇ. V, 58): *catvāraḥ*. From the rule *cater varac* (cf. Uṇ. II, 123): *catvaram*.

(918) *Prothṛ* in the sense of sufficiency (*paryāpti*). Sufficiency means fullness (*pūrṇatā*). [Conjugations: *prothate*, *prothati*, *apuprothat*. *Prothaḥ* is the horse's nostril; "one should follow the horse as it snorts" (I, 4, 56 Bh. v. l.). (919)

The roots *mithṛ* and *methṛ* signify "injuring" (*aliṃsana*). They take the forms *methate* and *methati*. There are two [roots] for the purpose of allowing an option regarding the *guṇa* [vowel strengthening] before a *kit* suffix: *mithyate* and *methyate*; the imperfect form is *amimethat*. By the rule *metho 'ci* (Pāṇini III.1.134), the word *methī* belongs to the *gaurādi* group (IV.1.41). Indeed, even a cow tied to a *methī* wanders about while eating mouthfuls of fodder (Subhāṣitāvalī 2958, where *vīthī* is corrected to *methī*). However, Amarasiṃha says: "In the masculine, *methi* is the wooden post (*khaledāru*) set up for tethering cattle" (Amarakośa II.9.15). Durga reads the roots as *midṛ* and *medṛ*. (920)

The root *medh* [is used] in the sense of meeting (*saṃgama*). By the use of the word "and" (*ca*), [it is also used] in the senses of intelligence (*medhā*) and injury (*hiṃsana*). [Examples: *medhate*, *medhati*, *amimedhat*; *medhā*, *medhyam*, *gṛhamedhī*, *aśvamedhaḥ*, *medhiḥ*. The roots *ṇidr* and *ṇedṛ* [are used] in the senses of censure (*kutsā*) and proximity (*saṃnikarṣa*). [Examples: *praṇedati*, *nidyate*, *nedya-te*, *aninedat*. According to the Easterners (*prāñcaḥ*), those who are clever (*hevākinaḥ*), there are also *ṇivr* and *ṇevṛ*. The roots *śṛdhu* and *mṛdhu* [mean] to moisten (*unda*). Moistening (*undaḥ*) is the act of wetting. [Examples: *śardhate*, *śardhati*; [gerunds] *śṛddhvā*, *śardhitvā*; [past participle] *śṛddhaḥ*. [The root] *śṛdhu* [is also used] in the sense of contemptuous sound (*śabdakutsā*) [as listed at I.797]: *śardhate*. [The roots] *mardhate*, *mardhati*; [the noun] *mṛdhaṃ* means battle (*samaraḥ*). (922, 923)

*Budh* in the sense of awakening: *bodhate*, *bodhati*. According to Nandī, the root is *budhi*; [the aorist forms are] *abudhat*, *abodhīt*. The future participle is *bodhitā*; the agent of the former [root] is *boddhā*. (Note: Regarding the entry for *reṭṛg*—meaning "speaking" and "begging"—see Hemacandra’s *Dhātupāṭha* I.897. Note 3: C reads *methīruddho*. Note 4: Kṣīrasvāmī, in his commentary on the *Amarakośa*, identifies this as a compound, referring to *Pāṇini* VI.3.5. Note 75: P omits from *ṇivṛ* up to *hevākinaḥ*.)

*Ubundi* is used in the sense of "observing" (*niśāmana*). Observing means perceiving (*ālocana*). [It forms] *bundate*, *bundati*, *abudat*, *abundīt*, *buttvā*, *bunditvā*, and *bunnaḥ*. Nandī says that this root ends in *dh*; others say it is *ubedi* (925).

The root *veṇ* is used in the senses of moving, knowing, thinking, observing, and taking up musical instruments. A "musical instrument" (*vāditra*) is a musical device; its "taking up" (*grahaṇa*) is for the purpose of playing it. From this root, one forms *veṇate*, *veṇati*, and *aveviṇat*. By the rule *rāsnāsāsnā* (Uṇ. III.15), the suffix *in* is applied to form *veṇī*; by the rule *in* (Uṇ. IV.117), we have *veṇiḥ*, *veṇikā*, and *veṇī*. Alternatively, by the rule *veniḥ tu vījyājvaribhyo niḥ* (Uṇ. IV.48), the suffix *ni* is applied to form *veṇiḥ*. By the suffix *ṇa*, we have the river named *Veṇṇā*. (926)

The root *khan* is used in the sense of digging (*avadāraṇe*). It forms *khanate* and *khanati*. After the suffixes *ktvā* and *lyap*, by the rule *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ* (Pāṇini VI.4.42), there is substitution of *ā*: *khātaḥ*. By the rule *ye vibhāṣā* (VI.4.43): *khāyate* or *khanyate*. By the rule *gamahanajanakhanaghasaḥ* (VI.4.98), there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*): *cakhnuḥ*. By the rule *ī ca khanaḥ* (III.1.111): *kheyaḥ*. With the suffix *ṣvun* in the sense of an artisan (*śilpin*), according to Pāṇini III.1.145 and the Bhāṣya, [the form is *khānukaḥ*].

*Khanaka* [is derived from] *janasanakhanakram* (Pāṇini III.2.67), which forms the suffix *viṭ*; *bisakhā*. [In the sense of "digging,"] *parikhā* [is formed with] the suffix *ḍa*, as it is seen in other cases as well (Pāṇini III.2.101); it is that which is dug (*khanyate*), hence *kham*.

*ḍit khaner muṭ codāttaḥ* (Uṇ. V.20): *mukham*. From *artiludhūsūkhanaḥ* (III.2.184), *itran*: *khanitram*. From *uṣikhanibhyāṃ kit* (Uṇ. IV.161): *khātram*. From *āṅparayoḥ khaniśṝbhyāṃ ḍic ca* (Uṇ. I.34): *ākhuḥ*. From *khanikaṣyañjyasi* (Uṇ. IV.139), *in*: *khanir* means a mine (*ākaraḥ*). From *āṅi paṇipanipatikhanibhya ikan* (cf. Uṇ. II.45): *ākhānikaḥ*. From *khano gha ca* (III.3.125): *ākhanaḥ*. (927)

Regarding the roots *cīv* in the senses of taking up (*ādāna*) and covering (*saṃvaraṇa*): [the forms] *cīvate*, *cīvati*. Durga states that the root is *civṛ*: [the form] *acicīvat*. In the *chitvara* group (Uṇādi-sūtra I.1), there is *cīvara*, the garment of a sage (928). The root *cāyṛ* is used in the senses of honoring (*pūjā*) and perceiving (*niśamana*). [It forms] *cāyate*, *cāyati*, *acacāyat*. By Pāṇini VI.1.35, there is *kī* for *cāya* in the *liṭ* tense: *cikyuḥ*. By Pāṇini VI.1.19 and 21, there is *kī* for *cāya* in the *yaṅ* [intensive] after *svapi*, *śyani*, and *vyeñ*: *cekīyate*. By Pāṇini VII.2.30, there is *apacita*; optionally, *apacāyita*. From the Vārttika on VII.2.30, there is *apacitiḥ*. By the rule "there is *kī* for *cāya*" (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra I.74), there is *tu*: *ketuḥ* (929).

In the sense of "going out" (*vyaya-gatau*): *vyayate*, *vyayati*; *vyāyayati* (with *avyayīt* by rule VI.1.25); in the *curādi* group, ending in *-a* (X.386): *vyayayati* (930). [Note 1: The *Kaumudī* adds "visual cognition" (*cākṣuṣajñānam*); these words are absent in K and P, and thus appear to have entered the text later as original manuscript glosses. [Note 2: P adds "river" (*nadī*). [Note 3: See Hem. *Uṇ.* 182. [Note 4: All manuscripts read this. [Note 5: K and C read *ādhāna°*. [Note 6: All manuscripts read *acicāyat*. [Note 7: All manuscripts read *apacitaḥ*. [Note 8: End of section 16.]

The root *dāśṛ* means "to give. It forms *dāśate*, *dāśati*, and *adadāśat*. With the suffix *kvasu*, the form *dāśvān* is correct according to Pāṇini VI.1.12; and by I.4.73, the terms *dāśa* and *goghna* are used when [the recipient] is the beneficiary (*saṃpradāna*). In the word *puroḍāśaḥ* ("sacrificial cake"), it is said "it is offered before" (*puro dāśyate*); the substitution of *ḍa* for *da* occurs because it belongs to the *pṛṣodarādi* group (VI.3.109). Similarly, "it is offered with difficulty" (*duḥkhena dāśyate*) results in *dūḍāśaḥ*. According to Kauśika (931), *dāyṛ* means "to give. The root *aya* (935) means "to go"; it forms *ayate*. "The Lord of Day rises" (*udayati dinanāthaḥ*)—see I.342.

*bheṣṛ* and *bhreṣṛ* mean "to fear" and also "to move. [From these roots: *bheṣate*, *bheṣati*; *abibheṣat*; *bheṣayati*. Regarding *bibheti*: "A shaven-headed man terrifies (*bhīṣayate*)" (Pāṇini III.1.2 and VII.3.40). *Bhreṣate*, *bhreṣati*; *bhreṣaḥ* (Dhātupāṭha 932, 933). *As* in the sense of "going, shining, taking": *asate*, *asati*. Regarding the verse from the *Kumārasambhava* (I.35): "An effort was made, as if producing loveliness" (*lāvaṇyam utpādya ivāsa yatnaḥ*), Vāmana (in his *Kāvyālaṃkāra-vṛtti*, ed. Cappeller V.2.29) states that here *āsa* is from the root *as* ("to sit"). Some say it is from *as* ("to be"). In the *ad-ādi* class, *as* means "to exist" (II.56): *asti* (934).

The root *spaś* is used in the senses of "afflicting" (*bādhanā*) and "binding" (*pāśana*). Binding (*spāśana*) means tying together (*granthana*). One uses the forms *spaśate* and *spaśati*. This is the rope that binds from both ends (cf. VI, 1, 68, 2 Bh); *spaśaḥ* means a spy (*caraḥ*); *paspaśaḥ* means an introduction (*upodghātaḥ*). In the *curādi* group, *spaś* is used in the sense of afflicting (cf. X, 141), and *paś* in the sense of binding (X, 179): one uses *spāśayate* and *pāśayati*. Some say it is *paṣ*: *pāṣaḥ*, *pāṣāṇaḥ* (936).

The root *laṣ* means "to desire" (*kānti*). Desire is longing. By the rule *vā bhrāśabhlāśa* (Pāṇini III.1.70), the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied: *abhilaṣyate* / *abhilaṣate*, *abhilaṣyati* / *abhilaṣati*. By the rule *jucaṅkramya* (Pāṇini III.2.150), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *abhilaṣaṇaḥ*. By the rule *laṣapatapada* (Pāṇini III.2.154), the suffix *ukañ* is applied: *abhilāṣukaḥ*. By the rule *laṣeḥ śa ca* (cf. Uṇādi III.57), the suffix *unan* is applied: *laśunam* (garlic). The root *caṣ* means "to eat. [It forms] *caṣate* and *caṣati*. [From it derive] *cāṣaḥ* (the blue jay) and *caṣakaḥ* (a drinking cup). By the rule *sānasivarṇasi* (Uṇādi IV.107), [the suffix *āl* is added to form] *caṣālaḥ*, which is the ring at the top of a sacrificial post (*yūpakaṭakaḥ*).

*Chaṣ* in the sense of injury (939); *jhaṣa* in the senses of seizing and covering. *Jhaṣate*, *jhaṣati*. *Jhaṣaḥ*. *Jhaṣ* has the meaning of injury (I, 720): *jhaṣati* (940). *Bhlakṣa* in the sense of eating. *Plakṣa*—so says Durga (941). *Dāsṛ* in the sense of giving. *Dāsate*, *dāsati*. *Dāsaḥ*. The first [root] is *dāyṛ*; some say this is *dāśṛ* (942). *Māhṛ* in the sense of measuring. Measuring is the act of turning around. *Māhā gauḥ* (the cow measures). (943) *Guhū* in the sense of covering. By the rule "of *guh* with a penultimate *ū*, [the substitute is *ū*]" (VI, 4, 89): *gū-* [hita].

In the *laṅ* [aorist], *gūhati*; in the *luṅ* [aorist], *aghukṣat*. However, in the *taṅ* [ātmanepada], by the rule *lug vā duhadihalihaguhaḥ* (Pāṇini VII.3.73), there is optionally elision [of the penultimate vowel]: *agūḍha* or *aghukṣata*. By the rule *sani grahaguhoś ca* (Pāṇini VII.2.12), there is no *iṭ* augment: *jughukṣati*. In the *caṅ* [periphrastic aorist], a short vowel is not desired: *ajugūhat*. The forms are *gūḍhā* (past participle) and *gūhitā* (future participle). The word *guhā* occurs in the *bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III.3.104) in the sense of "mountain" or "herb. [The suffix] *ke* (Pāṇini III.1.135) [is applied]. (Note 1: cf. also 942; Note 2: all manuscripts read thus; Note 3: see 935 before 932; 771).

From the roots *guh* (to hide), *śaṃs* (to praise), *duhi* (to milk), and *guh*, the suffix *kyap* may optionally be applied (Pāṇini III.1.109, Kāśikā): *guhyam* or *gūhyam*. In the *uṇādi* group (Uṇ. III.1), from *guh* we have *gahvaraḥ*; and from *guh* we have *gahaḥ*: *gahanam* (944).
These [roots] are udātta and marked with the svarita accent. 881.

The root *śri* (ś ri ñ), meaning "to serve" or "to resort to," is udātta. It forms the following: *śrayate*, *śrayati*, *śrayitā*. By the rule *ṇi-śri-dru-srubhyaḥ kartari caṅ* (Pāṇini III.1.48), the *caṅ* suffix is applied in the *parokṣā* (perfect) for the agent: *aśiśriyat*. By the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini VII.2.49), there is optionally the *iṭ* augment: *śiśrīṣati* or *śiśrayiṣati*. By the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VII.2.15), the *iṭ* augment is not applied: *śritaḥ*. By the rule *śryukaḥ kiti* (Pāṇini VII.2.11), the *iṭ* augment is not applied before a *kit* suffix: *śritvā*. By the rule *śriṇībhuvo ’nupasarge* (Pāṇini III.3.24), the suffix *ghañ* is optionally applied when no prefix (*upasarga*) is present: *śrayaḥ*.

The suffix *ghañ* is applied [to the root] *śri* according to Pāṇini III.3.49 (*udi śrayatiyauti*), resulting in *ucchrāyaḥ* ("height"); by virtue of the rule regarding "abundance" (*bāhulaka*)—as stated in the Kāśikā (X.392, 49)—"all elevations end in falling. The suffix *ni* is applied [to *vahi* and] *śri* according to Uṇādi-sūtra IV.51, resulting in *śreṇiḥ* ("row"). The suffix *kvip* with lengthening of the vowel is applied to *vac*, *pracch*, etc., according to Uṇādi-sūtra I.57, resulting in *śrīḥ* ("glory"). The suffix *ḍun* is applied to the root *śri* before the word *śman* according to Uṇādi-sūtra V.28, resulting in *śmaśru* ("beard"). The suffix *asun* with the augment *śir* and the marker *kit* is applied to the root *śri* when referring to a limb of the body according to Uṇādi-sūtra IV.193, resulting in *śiraḥ* ("head").
The suffix *in* with the marker *ḍit* and a short vowel is applied to the roots *śri* and *han* after the prefix *āṅ* according to Uṇādi-sūtra IV.137, resulting in *aśriḥ* ("edge").

The root *hṛ* (hṛ ñ haraṇe, "to take")—ending with *tra* (i.e., *trai*)—is one of the sixty-eight roots that are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*) and are *parasmaipada* (active voice), excluding those marked with *ñ* or *ṅ*. Examples: *harate* and *harati*. By the rule *harater gatatācchīlye* (Pāṇini I.3.21), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used when the sense is habitual movement: *paitṛkam aśvā anuharante* ("the horses follow the father's [example]"). By the rule *vyavahṛpaṇoḥ samarthayoḥ* (II.3.57), the genitive case is used: *śatasya vyavaharati* ("he deals with a hundred"). The future participle is *hartā*. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sya* (VII.2.70), the augment *iṭ* is added: *hariṣyati*. By the rule *hṛkror anyatarasyām* (I.4.53), the object (*karman*) may optionally be designated as the agent (*kartṛ*) when the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied.

He causes the burden to be carried by Caitra, or he causes Caitra to carry it. By the rule *śyādvyadha* (Pāṇini III.1.141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied: *avahāraḥ* means "a crocodile. By the rule *harater anudyamane ac* (III.2.9), [the suffix *ac* is applied]: *riktaharaḥ*. By the rule *vayasi ca* (III.2.10): *kavacaharaḥ*. By the rule *āṅi tācchīlye* (III.2.11): *puṣpāharaḥ*. [And] *hara-*...

In the sense of "one who brings," the suffix *in* is applied by [Pāṇini III.2.25] *dṛtināthayoḥ paśau*, resulting in *dṛtihariḥ* ("one who brings a skin") and *nāthahariḥ* ("one who brings a protector"). In the sense of the instrument (*karaṇa*), the suffix *ghañ* is applied by [Pāṇini III.3.122] *adhyāyanyāyodyāvasaṃhāra*, resulting in *adhyāhāraḥ* ("the act of supplying/elaborating"). The word *hari* ("the color yellow" and "the direction East") is derived from the roots *hṛ*, *sṛ*, *ruh*, and *yuṣ* with the suffix *it* according to [Uṇādi-sūtra I.99]. The word *hariṇaḥ* ("deer") is derived from the roots *śyai*, *styai*, and *hṛ* with the suffix *inan* according to [Uṇādi-sūtra II.46]. The word *haritaḥ* ("green") is derived from the roots *hṛ* and *śyai* with the suffix *itan* according to [Uṇādi-sūtra III.93]. The word *harikaḥ* is derived from the roots *vṛ* and *hṛ* with the suffix *kayan* and the substitution of *su* and *du* respectively, according to [Uṇādi-sūtra IV.100].

*Hṛdayam*: by *paddannādau* (Pāṇini VI.1.63), [the form] *hṛt* is derived; there is also another base (*prakṛti*), for by *hṛpiśi* (Uṇādi IV.118), the suffix *in* is applied: *hariḥ*. By *janihṛbhyām imanin* (Uṇādi IV.148), *harimāṇam* is formed; and [the text says] "destroy it. By *hṛdhṛbhṛsr* (Uṇādi IV.147), the suffix *īmanin* is applied: *harīmā*. By *veño ḍit* [and] *praharateḥ kūpe* (Uṇādi IV.133–134), *prahiḥ* is formed. By *kṛhṛbhyām enuḥ* (Uṇādi II.1), *hareṇuḥ* is formed, which is both a fragrant substance and a type of grain (947). 1 See Hemacandra’s Uṇādisūtra 275. 2 All manuscripts read thus. 1 78.

*bhṛñ* in the sense of "supporting" (*bharaṇe*). *bharate*, *bharati*—belonging to the *hvādi* class (III, 5)—is *ḍubhṛñ*: *bibharti*, *bhāraḥ*, *bhṛtaḥ*. In the *kryādi* class, *bhṝ* in the sense of "supporting" (IX, 21): *bhṛṇāti*, *bharaḥ*; by the rule *ṝdor ap* (III, 3, 57), [the suffix] *ap* is applied: *bharitaḥ*. For the formation of a name, by the rule *saṃjñāyāṃ bhṛtṝ* (III, 2, 46), the suffix *khac* is applied: *viśvaṃbharā*. By the rule *ave bhṛñaḥ* (Uṇ. II, 3), the suffix *kthan* is applied: *avabhṛthaḥ*, meaning the conclusion of a sacrifice. By the rule *aṇḍan kṛsṛbhṛvṛñaḥ* (Uṇ. I, 128), [the suffix] *aṇḍan* is applied.

*bharaṇḍaḥ*, *bhṛśam*, *bhṛṅgaḥ*, *bhurik* meter, and *ku-bhraś-*, from which *babhruḥ*, *Bharataḥ*, and *Bharur* (the name of a region) [are derived] (cf. Uṇādisūtra I, 23). The root *kṛ* means "to do" (*karaṇe*). [In the *bhvādi* class: *karate*, *karati*. In the *svādi* class, *kṛñ* means "to injure" (*hiṃsāyām*): *kṛṇute*, *kṛṇoti*. In the *tanādi* class (VIII, 10), *ḍukṛñ* means "to do": *kurute*, *karoti*. In the *uṇādi* group: *kāruḥ* (artisan), *kāriḥ* (maker), *karaṇiḥ* (similar), *kareṇuḥ* (elephant), *kratuḥ* (sacrifice), *karakaḥ* (a water-jar and so forth), *kṛkaḥ*, *karkaḥ* (white), *cakram* (wheel), *karaṇḍaḥ* (basket), *karma* (action), *karambhaḥ* (gruel), *kṛsaraḥ* (rice mixed with peas). (949)

The roots *ṇī* and *ñi* have the meaning of "causing to reach" (*prāpaṇe*). "Causing to reach" means bringing near (*āsādana*). [Examples: *nayate*, *nayati*, *praṇetā*. By the rule *saṃmānana* (Pāṇini I.3.36), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used: *nayate cārvī lokāyate* ("the Cārvāka leads the world toward his own doctrine"). By the rule *kartṛsthe cāśarīre karmaṇi* (Pāṇini I.3.37), [the middle voice is used] when the object is something non-corporeal residing in the agent: *krodhaṃ vinayate* ("he subdues his anger"). By the prohibition in *adikhādinīvahīnām pratiṣedhāt* (Vārttika on Pāṇini I.4.52, 5): *nāyayati bhāraṃ grāmaṃ Caitreṇa* ("he causes Caitra to carry the load to the village").

Regarding *vipūyavinīya* (Pāṇini III.1.117), the term *vinīya* means "suitable for a medicinal paste" (*kalke sādhuḥ*). Regarding *ānāyyo 'nitye* (III.1.127): *ānāyya* refers to the *dakṣiṇāgni* fire, and *ānāyya* refers to one who milks a cow. Regarding *praṇāyyo 'saṃmate* (III.1.128): "One should speak the Veda to a *praṇāyya* student"; the meaning is "to one who is not in favor of *saṃsāra*" (cf. *Chāndogya Upaniṣad* III.11.5).

In the rule *pāyyasāṃnāyya* (Pāṇini III.1.129), *sāṃnāyya* refers to the sacrificial oblation (*havis*). In the rule *dunyor anupasarge* (III.1.142), the suffix *ṇa* occurs in the sense of the agent (*kartari*), yielding *nāyaḥ*. In the rule *śriṇībhuvo ’nupasarge* (III.3.24), the suffix *ghañ* occurs, also yielding *nāyaḥ*. By virtue of the "diversity" (*bāhulaka*) [of Vedic usage] (X.392), we have *nayaḥ*. According to *avodor niyaḥ* (III.3.26), we have *avanāyaḥ* and *unnāyaḥ*. According to *parinyor nīṇor dyutābhreṣayoḥ* (III.3.37), [we have *pariṇāyaḥ* and *niṇāyaḥ*].

*pariṇāyaḥ* [is derived from] *śārīṇām*, *jālam* [is derived from] *ānāyaḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.124); by the rule *satsūdviṣa-* (III.2.61), the suffix *kvip* is applied: *grāmaṇīḥ*; by the rule *dāmnīśasa-* (III.2.182), the suffix *ṣṭran* is applied: *netram*; by the rule *rak* (Uṇādi II.13): *nīram*; by the rule *naptṛneṣṭṛ-* (Uṇādi II.96), *neṣṭṛ* is the name of a priest (*ṛtvij*); by the rule *hanikuṣi-* (Uṇādi II.2), the suffix *kthan* is applied: *sunīthaḥ*. By the rule *nayater ḍic ca* (Uṇādi II.101), the suffix *ṛ* is applied: *nā*, *narau*, *naraḥ*; by the rule *pānīviṣibhyaḥ paḥ* (Uṇādi III.23): *nīpaḥ*; by the rule *niyo miḥ* (Uṇādi IV.43): *nemiḥ* (950).

The root *dheṭ* means "to drink. The letter *ṭ* is for the purpose of applying the suffix *ṅīp* in forms such as *stanandhayī* (Pāṇini IV.1.15). It takes the form *dhayati*. Regarding the rule *vibhāṣā dheṭśvyoś caṅ* (III.1.49), the *caṅ* affix is applied: *adadhat*; the *luṅ* affix with *sici* gives *adhāsīt*. According to *vibhāṣā ghrādheṭśā* (II.4.78), there is elision (*luk*) of the *sic* affix: *adhāt*. By the rule *pāghrā* (III.1.137), the suffix *śa* is applied: *uddhayaḥ*. By the rule *nāsikāstanayor dhmādheṭoḥ* (III.2.29), the suffix *khaś* is applied [to form *nāsikandhama*, *stanandhaya*, etc.]. 1 P adds *saṃbharate*; 2 P *bharaṇḍa* means "a sowing vessel"; 3 all manuscripts read this; 4 C reads *cārvākaḥ*; 5 P reads *pratiṣedhe*; 6 P reads *asaṃmate*; 79 I.

*stanandhayaḥ*, and *nāḍīmuṣṭyoś ca* (Pāṇini III.2.30): *muṣṭindhayaḥ*; *dādheṭsisadaśado ruḥ* (III.2.159): *dhāruḥ* [one who milks] cows; *dhaḥ karmaṇi ṣṭran* (III.2.181): *dhātrī*; *dheṭa ic ca* (Uṇādi III.34): *dhenuḥ*; from *dhyai* (Dhātupāṭha I.957), however, *dhīḥ*; with the suffix *kta* (VI.4.66), *dhītaḥ*. (951)

*Glai* [is used] in the sense of the destruction of joy (*harṣakṣaye*). Here, the "destruction of joy" refers to the depletion of the bodily constituents (*dhātvapacaya*). One becomes weary (*glāyati*). Regarding the forms *gleyāt* and *glāyāt*, the substitution of *e* for *ā* occurs by rule VI.4.68 (*vānyasya saṃyogādeḥ*) when the suffix *liṅ* follows. By rule I.868 (*glāsnāvanuvamāṃ ca*), there is optionally the designation of the root as having the marker *m* (*mittva*); thus, one causes to weaken: *glapayati* or *glāpayati*. By rule VIII.2.43 (*saṃyogāder āto dhātor yaṇvataḥ*), there is the substitution of *na* for the final letter of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*); thus, *glānaḥ*. By rule III.2.139 (*glājisthaś ca ksnūḥ*), the suffix *ksnu* is added; thus, *glāsnuḥ*. By rule Uṇ. II.64 (*glānudibhyāṃ ḍauḥ*), the suffix *ḍau* is added.

*Glau* means the moon; from *glā* and *jyā* with the suffix *niḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.95.4), we have *glāniḥ*. From *śakadhṛṣajñāglā* (Pāṇini III.4.65), the suffix *tumun* is applied: *glāyati bhoktum* (he is weary of eating). The root *mlai* means the bending of limbs (*gātravināma*). Bending (*vināma*) is the loss of luster. [Conjugations: *mlāyati*, *mleyāt*, *mlāyāt*. [Past participle: *mlānaḥ*; by virtue of the rule for multiplicity (*bāhulaka*), *mlāniḥ* is also formed. The root *dyai* means the formation of a defective limb (*nyaṅgavidhāna*). A defective limb (*nyaṅga*) is a contemptible limb. [Conjugation: *dyāyati*. (952–954)

There are three [roots] meaning "to sleep. From *drā*, by the rule *spṛhigṛhi* (III.2.158), the suffix *āluc* is applied: *nidrāluḥ*. By the rule *kte* (VIII.2.43), [the form] is *nidrāṇaḥ*; by the rule *tārakādi-* (V.2.36), [the form] is *nidritaḥ*; and by the rule *ātaś copasarge* (III.3.106), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *nidrā*. From *drā* in the sense of "wicked motion" (II.45): *drāti*; [the past participle] is *vidrāṇaḥ* (955).
From *dhrai* in the sense of "satisfaction": *dhrāyati*; [the past participle] is *dhrāṇaḥ*. In the *Bhāṣya*, the substitution of *na* is not desired: [the form] is *dhrātaḥ* (956).

The root *dhyai* means "to think. According to Pāṇini II.3.52 (*adhīgarthadayeśāṃ karmaṇi*), the genitive case is used: *mātuḥ dhyāyati* ("he thinks of his mother"). Regarding *dhyāpayati svayam eva* ("he causes [someone] to think by himself"), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffix does not apply because of the prohibition in the context of *ādhyāna* (intense meditation), as per Pāṇini I.3.67 (*ṇer aṇau*). *Dūḍhyaḥ* ("evil-minded") is derived from *duṣṭaṃ dhyāyati*. By Pāṇini III.2.3 (*āto ’nupasarge kaḥ*), the suffix *ka* is applied. Then, by Pāṇini VI.3.109 (*duro dāśanāśadabhadhyeṣu*), the substitution of *ḍha* for *da* and *ū* for *a* occurs. Furthermore, by Pāṇini III.1.136 (*ātaś copasarge kaḥ*), the suffix *ka* is applied: *ādhyāyanti enam* ("they think highly of him"), resulting in *āḍhyaḥ* ("wealthy/respected").

By the rule *na dhyākhyāpṛmūrchimadām* (Pāṇini VIII.2.57), the substitution of *ṇatva* for the *niṣṭhā* suffix does not apply: *dhyātaḥ*. From the *uṇādi* list: *dhīḥ* (IV.114); from *dhyāpyoḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca* (Uṇ. IV.114), with the suffix *kvanip*: *dhīvā*; from *chitvarachatvara* (Uṇ. III.1): *dhīvaraḥ*. He meditates upon me: *madhyaḥ*, by *āto ’nupasarge kaḥ* (III.2.3). That in which they meditate together is *saṃdhyā* (957).

1. Regarding the accusative, cf. II, 3, 69. 2. *P* [gives] *dhītam*. 3. *P* [gives] *j.* and *h.* in the sense of "diminution of enmity, etc."; here *dh.* [is used]. 4. *P* [gives] *nyaṅge*. 5. Where? 6. ? Cf. III, 2, 178, 4. 6. Cf. Hem. Dh. I, 30, and Ujjval. on Uṇ. IV, 111: "He meditates upon me (*mām dhyāyati*), thus *maddhyam*"—this is from the *Dhātupārāyaṇīya* 1.

80. *rai* in the sense of "sound. *rāyati*. By the rule *kṛdādhārā* (Uṇ. III, 40), the suffix *ka* is applied: *rākā*. By the rule *rāśadibhyāṃ trip* (Uṇ. IV, 67): *rātriḥ*. By the rule *rāter ḍaiḥ* (Uṇ. II, 66): *rā* meaning "wealth. In the *ad-ādi* class, *rā* in the sense of "giving" (II, 48): *rāti*. (958)

The roots *ṣṭyai* and *styai* mean "to sound" and "to collect. One says *ṣṭyāyati* or *styāyati*; because both are taught [in the root lists], the change of *ṣ* at the beginning of the root to *s* (Pāṇini VI.1.64) does not apply. By the rule *styaḥ prapūrvasya* (VI.1.23), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*); and by *prastyo 'nyatarasyām* (VIII.2.54), the *niṣṭhā* suffixes may optionally take the form *m*: *prastītaḥ* or *prastīmaḥ*. From the rule *śyāstyā...* (Uṇādi II.46), the suffix *inan* is added: *styenaḥ*. From the root *stenayati* (X.349), we have *stenaḥ*. From *styāyateḥ*, the suffix *ḍraṭ* is added (Uṇādi IV.165): *strī* (959).

The root *khā* means "to eat. It forms *khāyati*. With the suffix *lyuṭ*, by rule III.3.115, it forms *khānam*. [Note 2] *Āhuḥ* [Note 2]. (960) The roots *kṣai*, *jai*, and *sai* mean "to waste away" (*kṣaye*). They form *kṣāyati*; with the *niṣṭhā* suffix, by rule VIII.2.53, *kṣāya-* becomes *kṣāma-*: *kṣāmaḥ*. *Jāyati*, [past participle] *jātaḥ*. *Sāyati*, [past participle] *sātaḥ*, [optative] *sāyāt*. Because of the inclusion of the root *si* [in the rule], there is no change to *e* [by VI.4.67]; thus, [the aorist] *asāsīt*. Because of the inclusion of *si*, by rule II.4.78, the optional elision of *sic* (*vibhāṣā ghrādheḍ*) does not apply here. (961–963)

The roots *kai* and *gai* mean "to sound. They are used in the specific sense of singing: *kāyati* and *gāyati*. From the rule *iṇ-bhī-kā-pā-...* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.43), the suffix *kan* is added to form *kākaḥ* ("crow"). In the case of *agāsīt*, because there is a substitute for the root *iṇ* (by Pāṇini II.4.45), the suffix *sic* is elided by the rule *gāti-sthā-* (Pāṇini II.4.77), resulting in *agāt*. In the word *geyaḥ*, derived from the rule *bhavya-geya-* (Pāṇini III.4.68), it is correct [to derive] the agent (*kartṛ*). From the root *gas* with the suffix *thakan* (Pāṇini III.1.146), we have *gāthakaḥ*; and with the suffix *ṇyuṭ* (Pāṇini III.1.147), we have [the same].

A singer (*gāyanaḥ*); by *gāpoṣ ṭak* (Pāṇini III.2.8), a singer of the *sāman* is an *udgātṛ*. By *kamimanijanibhyaḥ tun* (Uṇādi I.73), *gātuḥ*. By *uṣikuṣigābhyas than* (Uṇādi II.4), *gāthā*. By *gaś codi* (Uṇādi II.10), *thak* [is added], resulting in *udgītha*, which is the syllable *oṃ*. By *ghumāsthāgāpā...* (Pāṇini VI.4.66), there is the substitution of *ī*: *gītam*, *gānam*. By *sthāgāpāpaco bhāve* (Pāṇini III.3.95), *gītiḥ*. From the root *gāṅ* in the sense of singing (Dhātupāṭha I.998), one sings (*gāte*) [as per rules 964 and 965].
