*Śrai* and *śrai* [mean] cooking. *Srāyati*. *Śrāyati*; *śrā* [is used] in the sense of cooking (I, 848). [In the causative: *śrapayati*. Regarding *śrāti*, [the rule] "after *śrā* and *śrap*, *śṛtaṃ* is correct in the sense of cooking" (VI, 1, 27) applies (967, 966). *Pai* and *ovai* [mean] drying. *Pāyati*; the substitution of *piba-* (VII, 3, 78) is not desired here.

Here, *pā* in the sense of drinking (*pāne*, I 972): *pibati*; and *pā* in the sense of protecting (*rakṣaṇe*, II 47), belonging to the *adādi* class: *pāti*. *Vāyati*; by the rule *oditaś ca* (VIII 2.45), there is the substitution of *ṇatva* for the final consonant in the past participle: *vānaṃ* (dried); by *kṛvāpājimi...* (Uṇ. I 1), [the word] *vāyuḥ* (wind). In the *adādi* class, *vā* in the sense of motion and scenting (*gati-gandhanayoḥ*, II 41): *vāti*; in the *curādi* class, *vā* in the sense of motion, pleasure, and service (*gati-sukha-sevanayoḥ*, X 336): *vāpayati* (968, 969). *Ṣṇai* in the sense of enveloping (*veṣṭane*): *snāyati*, *snāyuḥ* (sinew). In the *adādi* class, *ṣṇā* in the sense of cleansing (*śauce*, II 43): *snāti* (970).

The root *daip* means "to purify. The letter *p* is for the purpose of distinction, according to the rule *dādhā ghv adāp* (Pāṇini I.1.20). Thus, *dāyati*; "the face is bright (*avadātam*). Here, the root *dāṇ* meaning "to give" (Dhātupāṭha I.977) is [treated as] 1P;
[addition: "he added wealth"; 2P omits [this]; 3 so all the manuscripts. 81 I.

*Yacchati* [is derived from] *yama* in the sense of "restraining" (I 101); *dayate* [is derived from] *dāp* in the sense of "giving" (II 50), belonging to the *adādi* class; *datte*, *dadāti*, and *dyati* [are derived from] *ḍudāñ* in the sense of "giving" (III 9), belonging to the *hvādi* class; and *do* in the sense of "cutting" (IV 40), belonging to the *divādi* class. (971)

The root *pā* means "to drink. By the rule *pāghrādhmā* (Pāṇini VI.1.78), the form *piba* is used: *pibati*. Because the root ends in a short vowel (*adanta*), there is no *guṇa* strengthening. By the rule *ghumāsthāgāpā* (VI.4.66), the substitution of *ī* occurs: *pīyate*. By the rule *er liṅi* (VI.4.67): *peyāt*. By the rule *gātisthāghupā* (II.4.77), the suffix *sij* is elided: *apāt*. By the rule *śāchāsāhvā* (VII.3.37), the augment *yuk* is added: *pāyayate*. According to the rule *na pādamyāṅyamāṅyasa* (I.3.89), the *parasmaipada* voice does not apply here. [In the case of the intensive], there is the elision of the *ī* of *pibati* and of the reduplicated syllable (*lopaḥ pibater ī cābhyāsasya*). (See reference).

(III, 1, 129) [is applied] in the sense of "suitable for measuring," as in *pāyya* (from √pā), with the suffix *śa* by rule III, 1, 137: *utpibaḥ*. Since the suffix *ṇa* applies only after prefixes (III, 1, 141), we have *pāyaḥ*. By rule III, 2, 8 and its Vārttika 1, *ṭak* is added to *pibati* when referring to *surā* and *śīdhu*: *surāpaḥ*. *Pānīyam* is formed by the application of the suffix *ka* in the sense of the suffix *ghan* (III, 3, 58, 4).
By [Pāṇini III.3.95], *prapā* is formed in the sense of an action; by [Uṇādi-sūtra I.1], *pītiḥ*; and by [Uṇādi-sūtra II.7], *pāyuḥ*.

*thak*: *pīthaḥ*; *ṣṭran* (Uṇ. IV, 158): *pātram*; *manin* (Uṇ. IV, 144): *pāmā*; from the root *pibati* with the suffix *asun* and the change of the vowel to *ī* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 189): *payaḥ*; from *pibati* with the suffix *thasun* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 203): *pāthaḥ* meaning water; from *pā*, *nī*, and *viṣi* with the suffix *paḥ* (Uṇ. III, 23): *pāpam*; by the rule *sānasivarṇasi* (Uṇ. IV, 107): *palvalam*; *pākaḥ* means a child (Uṇ. V, 53); *Kalāpakaḥ*; *Pampā* is a lake (972).

The root *ghrā* is used in the sense of smelling. By the rule *pāghrā-dhmā-sthā-nā-dāṇ-dṛśy-arti-sarti-śada-sado ’liṭo dīrgho ’ṅi ca* (Pāṇini VI.1.15), *ghrā* becomes *jighra*: *jighrati*. Alternatively, by the rule *vānyasya saṃyogādeḥ* (Pāṇini VI.4.68), there is optionally the substitution of *e* for the vowel: *ghreyāt* or *ghrāyāt*. By the rule *vibhāṣā ghrā* (Pāṇini II.4.78), the *sij* suffix is optionally elided: *aghrāt* or *aghrāsīt*. By the rule *ī ghrā-dhmoḥ* (Pāṇini VII.4.31), the form *jeghrīyate* is derived. By the rule *jighrateḥ vā* (Pāṇini VII.4.6), there is optionally the substitution of *i*: *ajighripat* or *ajighrapat*. By the rule *pāghrā-dhmā-sthā-nā-dāṇ-dṛśy-arti-sarti-śada-sado ’ṅi ca* (Pāṇini III.1.137), the suffix *śa* is applied.

In the word *ujjighraḥ*, there is optionally the substitution of *ṇatva* for the *t* of the suffix *niṣṭhā* according to Pāṇini VIII.2.56 (*nudavidondatrā*): *ghrātaḥ* and *ghrāṇaḥ*. [The word] *ghrāṇam* means "that by which one smells. [The word] *vyāghraḥ* is derived from the root *ghrā* with the prefix *vi-ā-* and the suffix *ka* according to Uṇādi-sūtra V.63 (*vyāṅi ghrāteś ca jātau*). (973)

The root *dhmā* is used in the senses of "sound" and "contact with fire. Regarding sound, such as [blowing] with the mouth and so forth, and regarding contact with fire, the form *dhama-* is derived by Pāṇini VI.1.78 (*pā-ghrā-dhmā-* etc.): *dhamati*. By Pāṇini III.1.137 (*śa*), we have *vidhamaḥ*, and *ādhmātaḥ śaṅkhaḥ* ("the conch is blown"). By Pāṇini III.2.29 (*nāsikā-stanayor dhmādheṭoḥ*), the suffix *khaś* is applied: *nāsikandhamaḥ* ("one who blows through the nose"). By Pāṇini III.2.30 (*nāḍī-muṣṭyoś ca*), we have *nāḍindhamaḥ* ("one who blows through a tube"). And by Pāṇini III.2.37 (*ugraṃ-paśye-rammadapāṇindhamāś ca*), and by the rule *dhmo dhamaś ca* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra II.35), the suffix *kvun* is applied.
From the root *dham* (to blow), by [Uṇādi-sūtra] II.103, *artisṛdhṛdhami*, the suffix *ani* is applied: *dhamaniḥ* means "a vessel" (*nāḍī*); this is due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulakāt*).
All manuscripts read thus at I.82.

(HI, 3, 1) There is the substitution of *dham*. Some say that *dham* is a separate verbal root (*prakṛtyantara*), as in: "The root ending in *dh* is like a mass of fire" (974). The root *sthā* means "cessation of motion. For *sthā*, there is the substitution of *tiṣṭhā* (VII, 3, 78): *tiṣṭhati*. By the rule *samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ* (I, 3, 22), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is applied: *saṃtiṣṭhate*, *avatiṣṭhate*, *pratiṣṭhate*, *vitiṣṭhate*. By the rule *sthāghvor ic ca* (I, 2, 17), [the augment *iṭ* is added]: *samasthita*, *samasthiṣātām*. An addition (*upasaṃkhyāna*) is made to the rule *āṅaḥ sthaḥ pratijñāne* (I, 3, 22, 1): [the middle voice is used when expressing a promise].

He maintains the letter *sakāra*; he maintains the word as eternal; the meaning is that he recognizes it as being eternal. And regarding [the rule] *prakāśanastheyākhyayoś ca* (Pāṇini I.3.23): "The maiden stands for the students" (*tiṣṭhate kanyā chāttrebhyaḥ*). By the rule *ślāghahnuṅsthā* (Pāṇini I.4.34), there is the designation of the recipient (*saṃpradāna*); as in: "He who, having doubted, stands by Karṇa and others" (*Kirātārjunīya* III.14). Regarding *udo 'nūrdhvakarmaṇi* and *uda īhāyām* (Pāṇini I.3.24 and Vārttika 1): [he stands up].

[The suffix *ātmanepada*] occurs after [the verb *ut-thā*] when used with *geha* and *mukti*: *gehād uttiṣṭhate*, *mukter uttiṣṭhate*; but not here: *pīṭhād uttiṣṭhati*, *grāmāc chatam uttiṣṭhati*. [The suffix *ātmanepada* occurs] after [the verb *upa-sthā*] when a mantra is the instrument (Pāṇini I.3.25): *aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhate*, *āgneyyāgnīdhram upatiṣṭhate*; but not here: *bhartāram upatiṣṭhati yauvanena*, *upatasthuḥ prakṛtayaḥ*. [The suffix *ātmanepada* occurs] also after [the verb *upa-sthā*] when it is intransitive (Pāṇini I.3.26).

The verb *upatiṣṭhate* is used in the sense of "offering food," as well as in the senses of "worshipping a deity," "associating with," and "making friends" on a path; thus it is stated [in Pāṇini I.3.25.1]: *ādityam upatiṣṭhate*, "he worships the sun"; *Gaṅgā Yamunām upatiṣṭhate*, "the Ganges joins the Yamunā"—the meaning here is "it flows into" (*upaśliṣyati*); *rathikān upatiṣṭhate*, "he makes friends with the charioteers"—the meaning is "he befriends"; *ayaṃ panthāḥ Srughnam upatiṣṭhate*, "this path leads to Srughna"—the meaning is "it reaches. Furthermore, it is used in the sense of "desire to obtain" (*lipsā*) [Pāṇini I.3.25.2].

"A monk attends upon (*upatiṣṭhate*) or attends to (*upatiṣṭhati*) donors. Regarding the object of the roots *adhi-śī*, *adhi-sthā*, and *ās*: "he presides over (*adhitiṣṭhati*) the house. By [Pāṇini 6.4.66] *ghumāsthā*, there is the substitution of *i* [for the root vowel]: *sthīyate*. By [Pāṇini 8.3.65] *upasargāt sunoti*, [the *s* is changed to *ṣ*].

The substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*]: *adhiṣṭhāsyati*, *adhiṣṭhānam*; by *sthādiṣv abhyāsena cābhyāsasya* (Pāṇini VIII.3.64), [the form] *adhitaṣṭhau*; by *udaḥ sthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya* (VIII.4.61), *s* is replaced by *th*, and by *jharo jhari savarṇe* (VIII.4.65), there is the elision of that [th]; thus, *utthitaḥ*. By *gātisthā* (II.4.77), there is the elision of *sij*; by *prāk sitād aḍvyavāye ’pi* (VIII.3.63), there is the substitution of *ṣ*; [this applies] in the case of the mention of Vedic schools (*caraṇānām*) and in the aorist (*adyatanyām*) of the roots *sthā* and *iṇ* (according to Pāṇini II.4.3 and the Kāśikā).

Thus, regarding the singular form of a *dvandva* compound: *Kaṭhakauthumam*. [In the case of the root *sthā*,] by *sthā-ghvor ic ca* (Pāṇini I.2.17), we have *upāsthita*; by *tiṣṭhater it* (VII.4.5), *atiṣṭhipat*. By *bhavya-geya-pravacanīya* (III.4.68), the suffix *anīyar* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*), as in *upasthānīyaś Caitro guroḥ* ("Caitra is one who attends upon his teacher"). In the group beginning with *grah-* (III.1.134), we have *sthāyī*. By *ātaś copasarge* (III.3.106), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *āsthā*, *vyavasthā*. [The word] *praṣṭhaḥ* is used in the sense of "one who goes at the front" (VIII.3.92).
1 P °saṃgati° 2 P omits Gaṅgā — meaning 3 P adds "he attends upon the high officials" 4 P "the path to Dvārakā" 5 P adds "raised up" 83 I

The word *sādhuḥ* [is formed as follows]: by the rule *supi sthaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.4), the suffix *ka* is applied, resulting in *samasthaḥ*. Due to a separation of the rules (*yogavibhāga*), this suffix is also desired in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*): *ākhūtthaḥ* occurs, *agnyutthaḥ* occurs. By the rule *ambāmbagobhūmi-* (Pāṇini VIII.3.97), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs: *ambaṣṭhaḥ*, *ambaṣṭhaḥ*, *goṣṭhaḥ*, *bhūmiṣṭhaḥ*. By the rule *dyatisyati-* (Pāṇini VII.4.40), the substitution of *i* occurs: *sthitaḥ*. By the rule *gatyarthākarmaka-* (Pāṇini III.4.72), the suffix *kta* is applied.

Caitra attends upon his teacher. From the rule *glājisthaś ca ksnuḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.139): *sthāsnuḥ*. From *laṣapatapada* (III.2.154) with the suffix *ukañ*: *sthāyukaḥ*. From *stheśabhāsa* (III.2.175) with the suffix *varac*: *sthāvaraḥ*. Regarding the addition of the suffix *ka* in the sense of *ghañ*: "The prescription of *ka* for the sake of *sthā*, *snā*, *pā*, *vyadh*, *han*, and *yudh*" (Vārttika on III.3.58, 4): *prasthaḥ*. From *sthāgāpāpaco bhāve* (III.3.95) with the suffix *ktin*: *sthitiḥ*. [From] *ajiraśiśira* (Uṇādi).
In the [sūtra] "I, 54)," *sthira* and *sthavira* are derived; *sthālī* is formed by [the rule] *sthācatimṛjer* (Uṇ. I, 115); and *stha* is formed by *savye sthaś chandasi* (Uṇ. II, 102).

Thus ends the section on *ṛn*. [The following forms derive from the root] *sthā*: *savyeṣṭhā* means "charioteer"; the substitution of *ṣ* occurs by Pāṇini VIII.3.97 (*sthāsthinsthṝṇām*). By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.10 (*parame sthaḥ kic ca*), the suffix *in* is applied: *Parameṣṭhī* is Brahmā. By Uṇādi-sūtra III.37 (*stho ṇuḥ*): *sthāṇuḥ* ("post" or "pillar"). By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.96 (*sthaḥ sto 'mbajabakau ca*): *stambaḥ* ("bush"), *stabakaḥ* ("cluster of blossoms"), and *sthāyī* ("one who stands"). By Pāṇini III.3.3 (*bhaviṣyati gamyādayaḥ*): *prasthāyī* ("one who is about to depart"). *sthūṇā* ("pillar"); *sthūrā* refers to the shank or a block of iron. (975)

The root *mnā* means "repeated practice. Practice is a function occurring through tradition (*pāramparyeṇa*). By [Pāṇini] Sūtra VI.4.97, *mnaḥ* becomes *manaḥ*: thus, *āmanati*. From this comes *āmnāyaḥ*. Furthermore, by Uṇādi-sūtra IV.150, *nāmansīman*, the word *nāma* is formed [by adding the suffix *man*]. (976)

The root *dāṇ* means "giving. The letter *ṇ* [in *dāṇ*] serves as an indicator (*it*), according to the rule *dāṇaś ca sā ced* (Pāṇini I.3.55). Regarding the rule *dāṇo yacchaḥ* (VII.3.78): *viprāya yacchati* ("he gives to the Brahmin"). Because of the rule *dāṇaś ca sā cec caturthyarthe* (I.3.55), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *dāsyā saṃprayacchate* ("he gives to the female slave"). Regarding the grammatical operation of *ghu* (VI.4.66): *dīyate* ("it is given"). Regarding the elision of *sij* (II.4.77): *adāt* ("he gave"). The word *dāyādaḥ* ("heir") is formed by the rule *mūlavibhujāditvāt* (III.2.5, Vārttika 2); the suffix *ka* (III.2.3) does not apply here because the root is accompanied by a prefix (*sopasargatvāt*).

*Pre dājñaḥ* (III, 2, 6): *annapradaḥ* (“giver of food”). *Godaḥ*. By *do dad ghoḥ* (VII, 4, 46): *dattaḥ*. By *aca upasargāt taḥ* (VII, 4, 47): *prattam*. By *das ti* (VI, 3, 124), there is lengthening: *vīttam*. *Dādheṭsiśadasado ruḥ* (III, 2, 159): one whose nature is giving (*dānaśīla*) is *dāruḥ* (977). *Hvṛ* in the sense of crookedness (*kauṭilye*). It bends (*hvarati*). In the group beginning with *chitvara-* (cf. *Uṇ.* III, 1): *upahvaraḥ* (978).

The root *svṛ* is used in the senses of "sound" and "afflicting. From *svarati*, by Pāṇini I.3.29 (*samo gamyṛchi*), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffix is applied: *saṃsvarate*. By Pāṇini VII.2.44 (*svaratisūti...*), there is optional *iṭ*: the forms are *svaritā* or *svartā*. By Pāṇini VII.2.49 (*sanīvantardha...*), the forms are *sisvariṣati* or *susvūrṣati*. *Svaraḥ* ("sound") is derived from the rule Uṇādi I.13 (*śṝsvṛsnihi...*), where *u* is the suffix; thus *svaruḥ* means "thunderbolt. In the *curādi* class, *svārayati* is formed from *svara* in the sense of "casting aside" (X.317), with the vowel *a* added as a penultimate (*adanta*). (979) 1. *gsnuḥ* 2. All manuscripts read this. I.84.

The root *smṛ* is used in the sense of "thinking" (*cintā*). From the rule *jñā-śru-smṛ-dṛśāṃ sanaḥ* (Pāṇini I.3.57), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is applied: *susmūrṣate*. With the meaning "to remember with longing" (*ādhyāna*), it is marked as *mit*: *smarayati*. From the rule *asmṛdṛtvar-* (Pāṇini VII.4.95), we have *asasmarat*. *Smaraḥ* (love) and *smṛtiḥ* (memory).

The root *dṛ* is used in the sense of "covering" (*varaṇa*). Covering means concealing. *Dvarati*. With the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.19), we get *dvāram* (door). From the root *dvārayati*, by adding the *uṇādi* suffix *kv-in* (Uṇ. IV.54; cf. Uṇ. II.57), we derive *dvār* and *dvāraḥ*. (980–981)

The root *sṛ* means "to go. It is used in the sense of moving or spreading forth (*sarati*, *prasarati*). According to Pāṇini VII.3.78 and the Kāśikā on *pāghrādhmādheṭdrśaḥ śaḥ*, the substitute *dhāv* is applied for rapid motion: *dhāvati*. By Pāṇini VII.2.13 (*kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi*), the augment *iṭ* is not added: *sasṛvaḥ*. By Pāṇini III.1.56 (*sartiśāstyartibhyaś ca*), the suffix *luṅ* takes the *aṅ* substitute: *asarat*. According to Pāṇini III.1.104 (*upasaryā kālyā prajane*), the word *upasaryā* is formed; by Pāṇini III.1.114 (*rājasūyasūrya...*), the word *sūryaḥ* is derived; and by Pāṇini III.1.149 (*prusṛlvaḥ samabhihāre vun*), the word *sarakah* is formed.

From the root *sṛ* ("to go"): *sarvaḥ* (cf. Uṇ. I, 153); with the suffix *ṇvul* (Pāṇ. III, 1, 133): *abhisārikā*; with the suffix *ṭa* after *puras*, *agratas*, and *agre* (Pāṇ. III, 2, 18): *puraḥsaraḥ*, *agrataḥsaraḥ*, *agresaraḥ*; [and] *pūrve* in the sense of the agent (Pāṇ. III, 2, 19).

*pūrvasaraḥ* [is formed] from *sṛ* with the suffix *ap*; *parisārī* from *saṃpṛca* (Pāṇ. III.2.142); *visārī* by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*) (X.392); *prasārī* from *pra* with *lapasṛ* (III.2.145); *udāsārī* and *pratyāsārī* from *ut*, *prati*, and *āṅ* with *sṛ* (Kāśikā on III.2.78). From *jucaṅkramya* (III.2.150), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *saraṇaḥ*. From *sṛghasyadaḥ kmarac* (III.2.160): *sṛmaraḥ*. With *sṛ* used in the sense of "firm," as well as "disease," "fish," and "strength" (Pāṇ. III.3.17 and cf. Bhāṣya), the suffix *ghañ* is applied.

*candanasāraḥ* (the essence of sandalwood), *atīsāraḥ* (diarrhea), *visāraḥ* (spreading), *sāram* (essence). From the root *sṛ* with the prefix *pra-* and the suffix *jan* (Pāṇini III.3.71), there is the form *upasaraḥ* (the breeding season of cows); with the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini I.3.18–19), *āsāraḥ* (a shower) and *saṃsāraḥ* (transmigration). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), we have *visaraḥ* and *prasaraḥ*. With the suffix *vun* (Pāṇini III.1.149), *sarakaḥ* (a kind of drink). From *sṛ* with the suffix *than* (which is *ṇit*; cf. Uṇādi II.5), *sārthaḥ* (a caravan). From *sṛ* with the suffix *asun* (cf. Uṇādi IV.236): those who move in the waters are *apsarasaḥ* (Apsarases). From the roots *hṛ*, *sṛ*, *ruh*, and *yus* with the suffix *iti* (Uṇādi I.99), *sarit* (a river). With the suffix *asun* (Uṇādi...)*.

(IV, 188): *saraḥ*. From the rule *artisṛdhṛdhami* (Uṇ. II, 103), *saraṇiḥ* [is derived]. From *sarteḥ aṭiḥ* (Uṇ. I, 133), *saraṭ*; from *śakādibhyo ’ṭan* (Uṇ. IV, 81), *saraṭaḥ* means a chameleon (*kṛkalāsaḥ*). From *sarter ayuḥ* (Uṇ. III, 22), *Sarayuḥ*, i.e., the river Sarayū; from *sarter apaḥ ṣuk ca* (Uṇ. III, ...).

141): *sarṣapaḥ* ("mustard seed"); from the root *kṛs* with the suffix *aṇḍan*, [we have] *saraṇḍaḥ*; from the root *sṛ* with the suffix *ikak* and the augment *nuk*, [we have] *sṛṇīkā*, meaning saliva; from the roots *jan*, *dā*, and *cyus* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 104), with the suffix *nik*, [we have] *sṛṇiḥ*, meaning a goad; from the root *sṛ* with the suffix *ṇit* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 89), [we have] *sārathiḥ*. In the *hvādi* class (*ṛ sṛ gatau*, III, 16–17): *sisarti*; in the *curādi* class (cf. X, 322): *sārayati*; with the suffix *yuc* (III, 3, 107): *sāraṇā*, meaning the joining of strings; with the suffix *lyuṭ* (III, 3, 117): *sāraṇī*, meaning an irrigation canal. (982) 1 P adds *saṃjñāyām* before *pūrve*; 2 P reads *aḍiḥ*.

85. The root *ṛ* (meaning "to go" and "to reach") undergoes the substitution of *ṛccha* (Pāṇini VII.3.78): *ṛcchari*. By the rule *samo gamyṛchiprachisvaratyarti* (I.3.29), the Ātmanepada voice is applied: *samṛcchate*. By the rule *guṇo 'rtisaṃyogādyoḥ* (VII.4.29), there is *guṇa* [substitution]: *aryate*. By the rule *sūcisūtrimūtryaṭyartyaśūrṇotīnāṃ* (III.1.22, Kāśikā), the *yaṅ* suffix is applied: *arāryate*. By the rule *upasargād ṛti dhātau* (VI.1.91), there is *vṛddhi* [substitution]: *upārchati*. By the rule *thalīḍ attyartivyayatīnām* (VII.2.66), [the substitution of *iḍ* occurs].

From the roots *ṛ*, *sṛti*, *śās*, and *ṛti*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied by Pāṇini III.1.56; thus, *ārat*. By VII.2.74, the augment *iṭ* is added in the desiderative (*san*); thus, *aririṣati*. By VII.3.36, the suffix *puk* is added; thus, *arpayati* and *arpitaḥ*. By III.1.103, the word *aryaḥ* denotes a master or a Vaiśya; any other [meaning] is *āryaḥ*. By III.1.134, the feminine form is *ārā*; in the *bhidādi* group (III.3.104), *ārā* means a knife. *Ṛṇam* [is used] in the sense of debt (VIII.2.60).

(2.60), by the rule *ṛt-ṛt-lū-dhū-sū-khana* (III.2.184), the suffix *itra* is applied: *aritram* (oar; *Amarakośa* I.10.13). From the root *ṛ*, by *arteś ca tuḥ* (Uṇ. I.72), with the augment *kic*: *ṛtuḥ*. By *arter kid ic ca* (Uṇ. II.51), the suffix *inan* is applied: *iriṇam* (a barren, grassless place). By *artisṛdhr* (Uṇ. II.103), *araṇiḥ* (fire-drill wood). By *artipṝvapi* (Uṇ. II.118), the suffix *us* is applied: *aruḥ* (a vital spot, a wound). And by *arteś ca* (Uṇ. III.60), the suffix *unan* is applied: *aruṇaḥ* (reddish). [And] from the root *ṛ*, the suffix *nid* (cf. Uṇ.).

III, 102) Furthermore: *araṇya* ("forest"), from the rule *artikami-bhrami* (Uṇ. III, 132), the suffix *aran* is applied: *araram* means "a door-panel"; [the suffix] *ac* is applied in the *uṇādi* section.

By [the rule] *ir* (Uṇ. IV, 138): *ariḥ*. By *artigṛbhyāṃ bhac* (cf. Uṇ. III, 151): *arbhaḥ*, *arbhakaḥ*. By *arteś ca* (Uṇ. V, 7): *aratiḥ*, *aratniḥ* (Uṇ. IV, 2). By *arter bhukṣiṇak* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 12): *ṛbhukṣā* [is] Indra. By *arteḥ kyuj uc ca* (Uṇ. V, 17): *uraṇaḥ* [is] a ram. By *arter ū ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 44): *miḥ*: *ūrmiḥ*. By *snāmadipadyartipṝśakibhyo vanip* (Uṇ. IV, 112): [the suffix *vanip* is applied].

*Arvāñc*: from the roots *uṣ*, *kuṣ*, and *gār* with the suffix *than* (cf. Uṇ. II, 4). *Artha*: from the root *ṛ* with the suffix *asun* and the substitution of *u* for *ṛ* (Uṇ. IV, 194). *Uras* (*vakṣas*): from the root *ṛ* with the suffix *asun* in the sense of "disease" and the addition of *śuṭ* (Uṇ. IV, 195). *Arśas*: from the root *ṛ* with the suffix *asun* in the sense of "water" and the addition of *nuṭ* (Uṇ. IV, 196). *Arma*: from the root *ṛ* with the suffix *man* (cf. Uṇ. I, 139); *arma* is a disease of the eye. *Āru*: "tawny"; *Aryaman*; *Nirṛtiḥ*; *araruḥ* is a monkey. In the group beginning with *hve*, the roots *ṛ* and *sṛ* mean "to go": *iyarti* (983).

The root *ghṛ* is used in the sense of "to sprinkle" (*secane*). One says *garati* or *gharati*; they say its scope is not restricted. From the rule *añjighṛsibhyaḥ ktaḥ* (Uṇ. III, 89), we have *ghṛtam* (clarified butter) and *ghṛṇā* (heat/passion). In the *curādi* group, *ghṛ* is used in the sense of "flowing" (*srāvaṇe*) [X, 108], with the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings: *abhighārayate*. In the *hvādi* group, *ghṛ* is used in the senses of "flowing" and "shining" (*kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ*) [III, 14]: *jigharti*, *gharmaḥ* (heat), *ghṛṇiḥ* (sun/beam) [984, 985]. The root *dhvṛ* is used in the sense of "crookedness" (*hūrchane*). Crookedness (*hūrchana*) means curvature (*kauṭilya*). By the rule *chandasi niṣṭ̣arkyadevahūya* (Pāṇini III, 1, 123), we have *dhvaryaḥ*. That which is not crooked (*na dhvaraḥ*) is *adhvaraḥ*, meaning sacrifice (*yajñaḥ*) [986].
[Note: 1. KC reads *arariḥ*, P reads *ārariḥ*. From the rule *aca ir* (Uṇ. I, 2), we have *ariḥ* (enemy).

I 86. The roots *śu* and *śru* mean "to go. 1. *Śavati*; *śuṅgā* means "a sprout. By the rule *śruvaḥ śṛ ca* (Pāṇini III.1.74), the suffix *śnu* is applied: *āśṛṇoti caitrāya*. By the rule *pratyāṅbhyāṃ śruvaḥ pūrvasya kartā* (I.4.40), the agent of the preceding action becomes the recipient (*saṃpradāna*). By the rule *samo gamyṛchi* (I.3.29), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *saṃśṛṇute*. By the rule *kṛsṛbhṛ...* (VII.2.13), the augment *iṭ* is not added: *śuśrotha*. In the vernacular (*bhāṣā*), by the rule *sadavasaśruvaḥ* (III.2.108), the suffix *kvasu* is applied: *śuśruvān*. By the rule *jñāśrusmṛdṛśāṃ sanaḥ* (I.3.57), the ātmanepada is used for the desiderative (*san*) of these roots.

The suffix *san* is not applied after the root *śru* when preceded by *prati* or *ā*: *pratiśuśrūṣati*, *āśuśrūṣati*. With the prefix *vi*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied to *śru*: *viśrāvaḥ*. According to the rule *sravati-śṛṇoti-dravati* (VH 4.81), the vowel *o* optionally becomes *i*: *śiśrāvayiṣati* or *śuśrāvayiṣati*; *aśiśravat* or *aśuśravat*. In the list beginning with *grah* (HI 1.134), the form is *śrāvī*; some say *śravī*. By the rule *huyāmāśrubhasibhyas tran* (Uṇ. IV.137), [the suffix *tran* is added].

*Śrotra*: by the *uṇādi* suffix (*uṇādau*, I 1.78), *śravaṇaḥ* refers to the *aśvattha* tree; by the suffix *lyuṭ* (III 3.117), *śravaṇam* means the ear; by the suffix *asun* (Uṇ. IV 188), *śravaḥ*. By the rule "from *vah*, *śrī*, *yud*, *rud*, *śrug*, *glā*, *hā*, *āt*, and *ari*, the suffix *niṅ*" (cf. Uṇ. IV 51), we have *śroṇiḥ* (987, 989). The root *ṣū* (in the sense of procreation and sovereignty) is used as follows: *savati*, *sotā*, [in the passive/objective sense] *suṣuve*. From it derive *sutaḥ*, *savanaḥ*, and *savaḥ*. In the *ad-ādi* class (I 32), one says *sauti*; in the *sv-ādi* class, the root is *ṣuñ*.

The root *sru* means "to flow. According to Pāṇini VI.4.81 (*sravati-śṛṇoti-dravati*), the vowel *u* optionally becomes *i*: *sisrāvayiṣati* or *susrāvayiṣati*; *asisravat* or *asusravat*. By Pāṇini III.1.48 (*ṇi-śri-dru-srubhyaḥ kartari caṅ*), the *aṅ* suffix is applied: *asusruvat*. By Uṇādi-sūtra II.57 (*kvib vaci-praci*), the suffix *kvip* is added to form *srūḥ*, meaning "one who assumes any form at will" (Kāmarūpī). From the same root, *sruvaḥ* (the sacrificial ladle) is formed. With the addition of the suffix *cik* in the sense of the ablative (*apādāna*), one gets *sruk* (the sacrificial spoon). Furthermore, by Uṇādi-sūtra IV.201 (*srurībhyāṃ tuṭ ca*), the suffix *asun* with the augment *tuṭ* is added to form *srotaḥ* (stream). From the root *as* (to throw), *asru* (tear) is formed according to Uṇādi-sūtra IV.102. [The word] *sruya-*...

The suffix *ktin* is applied after the root *jṛ* in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*) [Pāṇini III.3.95, 3]: *srutiḥ*. After the prefix *pra*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the roots *du*, *sru*, and *stu* [III.3.27]: *prasrāvaḥ*. The root *dhru* means "to be firm. It forms *dhravati*; by virtue of the rule regarding diversity (*bāhulaka*) [III.3.1], the suffix *ka* is added [Uṇādi-sūtra II.61]: *dhruvaḥ*. In the *tudadi* class [VI.107], it forms *dhruvati* [990].

The root *du* means "to run. From it we have *davati*. By Pāṇini III.1.142, *ṇa*: *dāvaḥ*, meaning a forest fire. By III.3.57, *ṝdor ap*: *davaḥ*. By III.3.23, *sam-i-yu-dru-duvo ghañ*: *saṃdāvaḥ*. By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.90, *dutanibhyāṃ dīrghaś ca*: *dūtaḥ*. From *dravati* we have *dravaḥ* and *drutaḥ*. By Pāṇini I.3.86, *budha-yudha-...-drusrubhyo ṇeḥ*, there is the *parasmaipada* ending after the causative suffix (*ṇi*): *drāvayati*. By VII.2.13, *kṛ-sṛ-bhṛ-vṛ-...*, there is no *iṭ* augment.

*dudrotha*, *ṇi-śri-dru-srubhyaḥ kartari ca aṅ* (Pāṇini III.1.48): *adudruvat*. By *sravati-śṛṇoti* (Pāṇini VII.4.81), there is the substitution of *i* for the *o* of the reduplicated syllable: *didrāvayiṣati*, *dudrāvayiṣati*; *adidravat*, *adudravat*. 1. All manuscripts read this. 2. P adds: *snānakālāyataś ca savaḥ (?)*. 3. P reads *kāmarūpaḥ*. 4. P adds *sruvakaḥ*. 87. I.

*Pradrāvaḥ* [is derived] from *pra* with the root *dru* (I H‚ 3, 27); *saṃdrāvaḥ* from *sam* with *dru* (I H‚ 3, 23); *uddrāvaḥ* from *ut* with *śri* (III‚ 3‚ 49); *pradrāvī* from *pra* with *lap*, *sṛ*, *dru*, and *matha* (I I I ‚ 2‚ 145); *mitadruḥ* is formed in the section on *ḍu* (I I I ‚ 2‚ 180, 1). *Dru* means a tree: *taruḥ*, *drumaḥ*; and by *harimitayor druvaḥ* (Uṇ.).

I.35): From the roots *hṛ* and *dru*, by [Uṇādi-sūtra] I.50, *inan* is added: *draviṇam*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.10, *kṝ-vṝ-jṝ-si*, the suffix *na* is added: *droṇaḥ*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.51, *vahi-śri*, the suffix *ni* is added: *droṇiḥ*. By [Kāśikā on Pāṇini IV.1.45], *kṛdikārād...*, with the addition of the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*, it becomes *droṇī* (991, 992).

The root *ji* is used in the sense of "to overcome. By the rule *viparābhyāṃ jer* (Pāṇini I.3.19), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is employed: *vijayate śatrum* ("he conquers the enemy"). By the rule *parājer asoḍha* (Pāṇini I.4.26), the status of the ablative case (*apādānatva*) is applied: *adhyayanāt parājayate* ("he fails in his studies"), meaning he is weary of studying. By the rule *sanliṭor jeḥ* (Pāṇini VII.3.57), the substitution of *k* for *j* occurs: *jigīṣati* ("he desires to conquer") and *jigāya* ("he conquered"). By the rule *krīṅjīnāṃ ṇau* (Pāṇini VI.1.48), the substitution of *ā* for *i* occurs before the causative suffix (*ṇic*): *jāpayati* ("he causes to win").

By the rule *kṣayyajayyau śakyārthe* (VI.1.81), [the suffix *kyap* is applied]; by *vipūyavinīya* (III.1.117), *jityaḥ* is formed when followed by a consonant; *Dhanañjayaḥ* is formed in the sense of a name (cf. III.2.46); *abhijit*; by *glājisthaś ca ksnuḥ* (III.2.139), *jiṣṇuḥ*; by *iṇnaśajisartibhyaḥ kvarap* (III.2.163), *jitvaraḥ*; by *kṛvāpājimisvadisisu yuḥ* (Uṇ. I.1), *jāyuḥ* as a medicinal herb; by *tṝbhūvahivasi* (Uṇ. III.128), *jhac*: *Jayantaḥ*; [and] *lyuṭ* (III.3.117).
*Ujjayanī*, where the *mūḍha* suffix is *codāttaḥ* (Uṇ. III.91): *jīmūtaḥ*. Regarding *jarati* and *jrīti*, Durga says: *jrayati* (993, 994).
Some say [the root] *kṣi* means "sovereignty" (*aiśvarya*); [from this] *kṣayati*, *bhuj kṣayati*, "he rules": *bhukṣāḥ* (cf. I.983) (995).

The root *smi* is used in the sense of slight laughter (*īṣaddhasana*). [Examples: *smayate*, *vismayate*, *visiṣmiye*. By the rule *smipūṅrañjv* (VII. 2. 74), the augment *iṭ* is applied: *vismayiṣate*. Due to the restriction *stautiṇyor eva ṣaṇi* (VIII. 3. 61), there is an absence of *ṣatva* [substitution]. By the rule *bhīsmyor hetubhaye* (I. 3. 68), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used. By the rule *nityaṃ smayater* (VI. 1. 57), there is *ātvam* [substitution of *ā*] for the root vowel when followed by a causative suffix (*ṇic*): *muṇḍo vismāpayate* ("the bald man causes astonishment"). By the rule *namikampi* (III. 2. 167), the suffix *ra* is applied: *smeraṃ hāsyam* ("a smiling laugh"). (996)

The root *gu* is used in the sense of an indistinct sound: *gavate*, *gotā*, *gotram*. Some say that *gū* means "to void excrement": *gavati*, *gavitā*. In the *tudādi* class (VI.1.7), there is *guvati*, *guvitā* (997). The root *gāṅ* is used in the sense of motion: in the singular, dual, and plural, one says *gāte*, *gāte*, *gāte*; by the rule *iṇo gā luṅi* (II.4.45), we have *agāt*. Here (*iha*) [in the Dhātupāṭha], *gai* is used in the sense of sound: *gāyati* (998).

The roots *ghuṅ*, *kuṅ*, and *uṅ* mean "to sound. From *ghavate*: [the form] *kokūyate* is derived; however, there is no *cutva* (substitution of *k*) in the *yaṅ* [intensive] because of the rule *na kavater yaṅi* (Pāṇini VII.4.63). In the absence of the *yaṅ* suffix (*yaṅluk*), it is not so, according to *na lumatāṅgasya* (Pāṇini I.1.63): thus, *cokoti*. [The suffix] *gsnu* [is added] after *ku*, *su*, and *yu*, and there is lengthening [of the vowel] (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra III.27). [The suffix] *smay* does not occur after a means of action (*karaṇa*): "he causes him to be amazed by means of a key" (*kuñcikayainaṃ vismāpayati*). I 88.

Thus: from the root *pā* [we derive] *paḥ*; from *ku* with the suffix *rava*, as in Uṇādi-sūtra III.133, we have *kuraraḥ*; from *ku* with the suffix *caṭ* and lengthening of the vowel, as in Uṇādi-sūtra IV.91, we have *kūcaḥ* and *kūcī*; from *ac* with the suffix *i*, as in Uṇādi-sūtra IV.138, we have *kaviḥ*; in the *adādi* class (*ku* meaning "sound," II.33), we have *kauti*; in the *tudādi* class (cf. VI.108), we have *kuvati*. From *av* [we derive] *auṣṭa* in the *luṅ* tense; with the suffix *i*, as in Uṇādi-sūtra IV.138, we have *aviḥ*. And Durga [states] that there is also *ṅuṅ*: *ṅavate*, *ñuṅuve*. Some say there is also *khuṅ* (sūtras 1000, 999, 1001–1003).

The roots *cyuṅ*, *chyuṅ*, *jyuṅ*, *pruṅ*, and *pluṅ* mean "to go. According to Pāṇini VI.1.48 (*cyavate, sravati, śṛṇoti*), the vowel of the reduplicated syllable is optionally replaced by *i*: *cicyāvayiṣati* or *cucyāvayiṣati*; *acicyavat* or *acucyavat*. From these, we derive *cyutaḥ* and *cyavanaḥ*. *Chyavate* and *jyavate* are also forms. According to Nandī, *juṅ* means "to move" (*javate*). By Pāṇini III.2.150 (*ju-caṅkramya-*), the suffix *yuc* is applied to form *javanaḥ*. However, the author of the *Vṛtti* states that *juṃ* is a Vedic (sautra) root; from it we derive *javaḥ* and *prajavī*. Furthermore, according to Uṇādi-sūtra II.23 (*joḥ ī ca*), [the suffix *ap* is added to *ju* with the replacement of its vowel by *ī*].

From the root *jṝ*, [the forms] *jīra* and *jūtiḥ* occur by Pāṇini III.3.97; and *jūḥ* meaning "a Piśāca" occurs by Uṇādi-sūtra II.57 (*kvib vaci*). From *pru* ("to flow"): *kaṭaprūḥ* means "one who crosses a river"; *piprāvayiṣati* and *puprāvayiṣati*; *apipravat* and *apupravat*. By Pāṇini I.3.86 (*budhayudhanaśa*), the *parasmaipada* ending is used after the causative (*ṇic*): *prāvayati*. *Pravaṇaḥ* [is formed from the same root]. By Pāṇini III.1.149 (*prusṛlvaḥ samabhihāre vun*), *pravakaḥ* is formed. *Prothaḥ* means "the tip of a horse's nose" (Uṇādi-sūtra II.12).

The same applies to *pluṅ*. According to Pāṇini III.4.68 (*bhavyageya*), [the suffix *ṇyat*] is applied: *āplāvyaś Caitro nadyāḥ* ("Caitra is to be made to wade across the river"). According to III.1.134 (*pacādi*), [the suffix *ac*] is applied: *plavaṭ*. According to III.3.50 (*vibhāṣāṅi rupluvoḥ*), [the suffix] *ghañ* is applied: *āplāvaḥ* or *āplavaḥ*. (1004–1007)

The root *ru* is used in the senses of "going" (*gati*) and "making a sound" (*reṣaṇa*). *Reṣaṇa* means injury or noise. [From it we derive: *ravate*. [With the suffix *ghañ*,] *ārāvaḥ* and *āravaḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.50). [With the suffix *yuc*,] *ravaṇaḥ* (Uṇādi II.74). [With the suffix *krun*,] *ruruḥ* (cf. Uṇādi IV.103). [With the suffix *i*,] *raviḥ* (Uṇādi IV.138). In the *adādi* class, *ru* is used in the sense of "sound" (II.24): *rauti* (1008).

The root *dhṛṅ* means "to support" (*avadhvaṃsane*). It is conjugated as *dharate*. In the *tudādi* class, *dhṛṅ* is used in the sense of "supporting" (cf. VI, 119): *dhriyate*. In the *curādi* class, *dhṛ* is used in the sense of "holding" (?): *dhārayati*. With the suffix *śa* according to III, 1, 138 (*anupasargāl limpavinda*), we have *dhārayaḥ*. In the sense of a name (*saṃjñāyām*) according to III, 2, 46, we have *vasundharā*. With the suffix *śatṛ* according to III, 2, 130 (*iṅdhāryoḥ śatr akṛcchriṇi*), we have *dhārayan*. With the suffix *man* according to Uṇ. I, 139 (*artistusv*), we have *dharmaḥ*. With the suffix *ani* according to Uṇ. II, 103 (*artisṛdhṛdhami*), [we have *dharmāṇi*].

*Dharaṇiḥ*, *dharaṇī* [are formed with the suffix *ini*]; by Pāṇini III.1.134, *dharaḥ* means "a mountain"; *dharā* means "the earth"; in the *bhidādi* group (III.3.104), *dhārā*; and by III.3.122, *ādhāraḥ* [is formed]. (1009)

1. P adds *kūrcaḥ*; *kurcikā* is indeed not different from it. 2. All manuscripts [read thus]. 3. Thus KC; P reads *nadībhāraḥ* (according to Hemacandra I.597, *nadītīraḥ*). 4. P reads *'śvamukhāgram*. 5. That is, *plava* with the feminine suffix *ī*, forming *plavī* (see IV.1.15). 6. Cf. Mādhavīyadhātuvṛtti I.884: "The root *dhṛ* in the sense of holding belongs to the *curādi* group," as stated by Kṣīrasvāmin; this is not accepted by the author of the Mahābhāṣya, as he says... 89 1.

In the section on *praṇi* and *dāna*: 1. *praṇidāna* means "to return" (*pratyarpaṇa*). [From the root *mā* with *praṇi*: one says *apamayate*, *praṇimayate*. With the suffix *san*, by Pāṇini VI.1.54 (*mīmāghv*), it becomes *mīmāṃsate*. By Pāṇini III.2.2 (*hvāvāmaś ca*), the suffix *aṇ* is applied: *dhānyamāyaḥ* ("one who exchanges grain"). Regarding the suffix *ktvā*, by Pāṇini III.4.19 (*udīcāṃ māṅo vyatihāre*), one says *apamitya yācate* ("having exchanged, he begs") or *yācitvāpamayate* ("having begged, he exchanges"). By Pāṇini VI.4.70 (*mayater id anyatarasyām*), the *it* augment is optionally applied, resulting in *apamāya* in the alternative case. Furthermore, by Pāṇini VII.4.30 (*māpor ur ī ca*; cf. Uṇādi-sūtra IV.101), the *u* is substituted for the vowel and *ī* is added.

*Meruḥ* and *Sumeruḥ* [are derived from the root *mṛ*] by *Uṇ.* IV, 109: "After *mā*, *chā*, *sā*, and *sū*, [the suffix *uṇ* is applied]. *Māyā* [is derived from the root *mā*] by *Uṇ.* IV, 227: "In place of *m* [of the root *mā*], *ṅ* is substituted when [the suffix] *asun* follows": *candramāḥ*. In the *adādi* class, [the root] *mā* in the sense of "measuring" (*māne*) [is used]: *māti*; in the *hvādi* class, *māṅ* in the sense of "measuring" (*māne*) [is used]: *mimīte* (DhP. III, 6). (1010)

The root *dā* is used in the sense of protecting (*rakṣaṇe*). According to Pāṇini VI.4.92, *dayate* becomes *avadigye* in the perfect tense (*liṭ*) due to the substitution of *dig* for *day*. By the *uṇādi* suffix *manin* (IV.144), we derive *dāma*. From *dāṇ* in the sense of giving (*dāne*, I.977): *yacchati*; from *daip* in the sense of purification (*śodhane*, I.971): *dāyati mukham*; from *dāp* in the sense of cutting (*lāvane*, II.50): *dāti vrīhīn*; from *ḍudāñ* in the sense of giving (*dāne*, III.9): *datte* and *dadāti*; and from *do* in the sense of cutting (*avakhaṇḍane*, IV.40) in the *divādi* class: *dyati*. (1011)

The root *śyaiṅ* means "to congeal" (*gatau*). It forms *śyāyate*. By the rule *śyādvyadha* (Pāṇini III.1.141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied; the inclusion of the term *śyā* [in that rule] is for the sake of [the root with] prefixes: *pratiśyāyaḥ* ("catarrh"), *avaśyāyaḥ* ("dew"). By the rule *dravamūrtisparśayoḥ śyaḥ* (VI.1.24), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *śīnaṃ ghṛtam* ("congealed ghee"). By the rule *śyo 'sparśe* (VIII.2.47), there is the substitution of *n* [for *y*]: this does not apply here in *śīto vāyuḥ* ("cold wind"). By the rule *prateś ca* (VI.1.25): *Sphaiyakṛtasya pitā pratiśīnaḥ* (Mahābhāṣya I.1.1.2, p. 38). By the rule *vibhāṣābhyavapūrvasya* (VI.1.26): [there is optionally vocalization after the prefix *abhi*].

From the roots *śyaiṅ* (to congeal) and *śyā* (to become dark), the suffix *mak* is applied by *iṣiyudhi* (Uṇ. I, 144), yielding *śyāmaḥ*, *śyāmā*, and *śyāmākaḥ*. From *śyaiṅ* and *styā* (to coagulate), the suffix *inan* is applied by *śyāstyāhṛñ* (Uṇ. II, 46), yielding *śyenaḥ*. From *hṛ* and *śyaiṅ*, the suffix *itan* is applied by *hṛśyābhyām itan* (Uṇ. III, 93), yielding *śyetaḥ*. The root *pyaiṅ* (to increase) takes the form *āpyāyate*. From this root, the suffix *vara* is applied in the *chitvara* group (Uṇ. III, 1), yielding *pīvaraḥ*. Furthermore, by the rule *dhyāpyoḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca* (Uṇ. IV, 114), the suffix *kvanip* is applied, resulting in *pīvā*.

The root *trai* means "to protect. [In the example] *caurāt trāyate* ("he protects from the thief"), there is optionally the substitution of *n* by rule *nudavidondatrā* (Pāṇini VIII, 2, 56): *trāṇaḥ* or *trātaḥ*. [However,] this substitution is obligatory in the case of *devatrātaḥ* and when used with the words *gala* and *grāha*; furthermore, these rules do not apply mutually to one another. [Examples include] *gavākṣaḥ* and *saṃśitavrataḥ* (according to the Vārttika on Pāṇini VII, 4, 41). (1014)

anudāttāḥ 950 pūṅ pavane. *Pavana* means the act of purifying. From here, four roots are *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*). [The forms] *pavate*, *pavitā* take *iṭ* by the rule *smipūṅrañjaśāṃ sani* (Pāṇini VII. 2. 74). By the rule *oḥ puyaṇjyapara* (Pāṇini VII. 4. 80), the *u* of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) is changed to *i*: *pipaviṣate*. By the rule *vipūyavinīya* (Pāṇini III. 1. 117), *vipūya* means "good for *muñja* grass. [The root *pū* is used] in the sense of directing (*praṇidhāna*), as in *praṇidhāna*. *Praṇidhāna* is... [text ends]

In accordance with this rule (*kṛti* [suffixes], there is no substitution of *ṇ* for *n*: *prapavanīyam*. Regarding the root *pūṅ*, by the rule *pūṅaḥ ktvā ca* (Pāṇini I.2.22), the augment *iṭ* is optional before the suffixes *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā*: *pūtaḥ* or *pavitaḥ*; *pūtvā* or *pavitvā*. By the rule *pūṅyajoḥ śānan* (Pāṇini III.2.128): *pavamānaḥ*. By the rule *lyuḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.134): *pavanaḥ*. By the rule *nirabhyoḥ pūlvor ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.28): *niṣpāvaḥ*. By the rule *halasūkarayoḥ puvas tran* (Pāṇini III.2.183): *potram*. By the rule *kartari carṣidevatayor itran* (Pāṇini III.2.186): [the suffix *itran* is applied].

*Pavitram*: by [Uṇādi-sūtra] II.96, *naptṛ-neṣṭṛ-tvaṣṭṛ*, the word *potṛ* denotes the officiating priest; by [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.86, *hasi-mṛg-riṇ-vāmi*, the suffix *tan* is applied, so *potaḥ* means a young animal, a cub, and a type of boat; by [Uṇādi-sūtra] I.123, *chā-pūṅ-khaḍi-bhyo gak*, the suffix *gak* is applied: *pūgaḥ* means the betel nut tree and a multitude; by [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.164, *puvo hrasvaś ca*, the suffix *ktra* is applied: *putraḥ*; by [Uṇādi-sūtra] V.15, *pūṅo yaṇ ṇuḍ hrasvaś ca*, the suffix *yaṇ* with the augment *ṇuṭ* and shortening of the vowel is applied: *puṇyam*; by [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.138, the suffix *iḥ* is applied: *paviḥ*. In the *kryādi* class [Dhātupāṭha IX.12], the root is *pūñ*: *punīte*, *punāti* (1015).

The root *mūṅ* means "to bind. According to Pāṇini’s rule *oḥ puyaṇjyapare* (VII. 4. 80), [the substitution of vṛddhi occurs]: *mūṅāvayiṣati*. By the rule *mūṅyor lopaś ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 206), the suffix *uṣan* is applied: *taijasāvartanī mūṣā* (a crucible for melting metal). By the rule *tanimūṅbhyāṃ kic ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 207), the suffix *k* is added: *mūtaḥ* means "a bundle" (*puṭabandhaḥ*); *jīvanasya mūtaḥ* is *jīmūtaḥ* (a cloud), which belongs to the class beginning with *pṛṣodara-* (VI. 3. 109). The root *ḍīṅ* means "motion through the air. It forms *ḍayate*. With the suffix *niṣṭhā* (the past participle suffix *kta*), it becomes *ḍayitaḥ*;

however, the *kittva* (the property of having *k* as an indicatory letter) is not desired here. In the *divādi* group, *ḍīṅ* means "motion" (IV. 27): *ḍīyate*, *ḍīnaḥ*. The root *tṝ* means "floating and crossing over. Floating (*plavana*) is sinking; crossing over (*taraṇa*) is...

*Laṅghanam*. Regarding the root *tṛ*: by the rule *tarati-tārakaḥ, vṛto vā* (VII. 2. 38), there is optionally a long vowel for the augment *iṭ* before an affix beginning with *liṭ*: [the forms] *tatāra* and *tarītā*; [the form] *teritha*. By the rule *na liṅi* (VII. 2. 39), there is no lengthening in the *liṅ*: *tariṣīṣṭa* (may you cross); [and] by the rule *sici parasmaipadeṣu* (VII. 2. 40), there is no lengthening in the *sic* after a root ending in *ṛ* in the *parasmaipada*: *atāriṣṭām*. By the rule *iṭ sani vā* (VII. 2. 41), the augment *iṭ* is optional in the desiderative (*san*): *titīrṣati*, *titariṣati*, *titarīṣati*. By the rule *tṝ-phala-bhaja* (VI. 4. 122), there is *etva* (substitution of *e*) and elision of the reduplication: *teruḥ*.

From the root *bhṛ* with the prefix *saṃ*, the suffix *khac* is applied by Pāṇini III.2.46: *rathantaram* (the Sāman). From the roots *ava* and *tṛ*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied by Pāṇini III.3.120: *avatāraḥ* (descent). In the *Bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III.3.104), the word is *tārā*. From the causative form (*ṇyantāt*), the suffix *ac* is applied by Pāṇini III.1.134: *tāraḥ* (the quality of brightness). By Pāṇini VIII.2.42, "the substitute *na* takes the place of the final letter of a *niṣṭhā* [past participle] after roots ending in *r* or *d*": *tīrṇaḥ* (crossed over). By Pāṇini III.3.94 and the Kāśikā, the suffix *ktin* is treated like *niṣṭhā* after roots ending in *ṛ* or those beginning with *l*: *tīrṇiḥ*. From the root *tṛ* with the suffix *thak* according to Uṇādi-sūtra II.7 (*pātṛ-tudivaci*), we have *tīrtham* (ford). From the roots *ṛ*, *sṛ*, *dhṛ*, etc., [the suffix *thak* is applied] according to Uṇādi-sūtra... [text truncated].

II, 103) *taraṇiḥ* [is derived from] *vṝkṝtr* (cf. Uṇ. III, 54), hence *taruṇaḥ*. From *tṝ*, *raś* and *ca* [are added], with *aḥ* (Uṇ. I, 5): *tāru*. From *vṝtṝvadi* (cf. Uṇ. III, 62), *saḥ*: *tarṣaḥ*. From *kṝtṝkṛpibhyaḥ kīṭan* (Uṇ. IV, 184): *tirīṭam*, an ornament for the head. From *avitṝstr* (Uṇ. III, 158), *iḥ*: *tarīḥ*. From *asun* (Uṇ. IV, 188): *taras*. From *bhṛmṛśītr* (Uṇ. I, 7), *uḥ*: *taruḥ*. By *aṇḍan* (Uṇ. I, 128), [the suffix is applied] prior to the primary suffix (*prāk pratyayāt*).

1. All manuscripts read this. 2. Cf. Hemacandra, *Uṇādisūtra* 542; for the conceptual representation, cf. *Amarakośa* I.1.10, 33. 3. Cf. Hemacandra, *Uṇādisūtra* 201. 4. Here, all manuscripts follow with: *dīṅ kṣaye*. [From] *dayate*; [with] the suffix *niṣṭhā*: *dayitaḥ*. 5. KC reads *vihāyasi*. 6. Cf. I, 767; Pāṇini: *taro balam* 91.

*Taraṇḍaḥ* is a specific type of float; by the rule *trādibhyaś ca* (cf. *Uṇādi* I.119), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *taraṅgaḥ* means a wave. From the roots *pāra* and *tīra* (X.363, 364), [the form] *tīram* [is derived] (1018).

The *udātta*-accented roots beginning with 954 *gup* "to hide" are eight in number, ending in *h*, being *aniṭ* (not taking the augment *iṭ*) and *ātmanepada* (middle-voice). By the rule *guptijkidbhyaḥ san* (Pāṇini III.1.5), the desiderative suffix *san* is added: *jugupsate pāpāt* ("he feels aversion toward sin"), meaning "desiring to produce censure"; otherwise, it is *gopate*. From *gupū* "to protect" (Dhātupāṭha I.422), *gopāyati* is formed by adding the *āya* suffix (Pāṇini III.1.28). In the *curādi* group, it has the sense of "shining" (X.231): *gopayati* (1019).

The root *tij* is used in the senses of sharpening (*niśāna*) and patience (*kṣamā*). Sharpening means making something sharp. One "endures anger" (*titikṣate kopaṃ*). Regarding the sense of patience, according to the rule for the *saN* suffix in the sense of the verbal root's own occurrence (Pāṇini III.1.5, Kāśikā), another suffix is taught for the sense of sharpening: *tejate*. From this, we derive *tejas*, *tejanam*, and *tejanī*. By the rule *yujirucitijāṃ kuś ca* (Uṇādi I.145), the suffix *mak* is applied, yielding *tigma*. By the rule *tijer dīrghaś ca* (Uṇādi II.18), the suffix *sna* is applied, yielding *tīkṣṇa*. In the *curādi* group (X.110), it appears as *uttejayati* (1020).

The root *mān* is used in the sense of honoring (*pūjā*). From the rule *mānbadhadānśānbhyaḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.6), when the suffix *san* is applied in the sense of deliberation (*vicāra*), one forms *mīmāṃsate*; thus, *mīmāṃsā* means deliberation. In the *curādi* group (X.299), according to the rule *ā dhṛṣād vā*, one has *mānayati* or *mānati*; hence *mānaḥ* and *mānanam*. By the rule *naptṛneṣṭṛ* (Uṇādi II.96), [we have] *mātā* (1021). The root *badh* is used in the sense of binding (*bandhana*). From the rule *mānbadha* (III.1.6), when *san* is applied in the sense of loathing (*jugupsā*), one forms *bībhatsate*; otherwise, one has *badhate* and *badhakaḥ*. In the *curādi* group (X.14), *badh* is used in the sense of restraining (*saṃyamana*); hence *bādhayati* (1022).

The root *rabh* is used in the sense of impetuosity (*rābhasya*). Impetuosity is the undertaking of an action. [Examples: *saṃrabhate*, *ārabhate*; with the desiderative suffix (*san*), by Pāṇini VI.1.54, *is*: *āripsate*. By Pāṇini III.1.98, the suffix *yat*: *ārabhyam*. By Pāṇini VII.1.63, the augment *num* is added to *rabh* except before *śap* and *liṭ*: *ārambhaḥ*, *ārambhaṇam*. By Pāṇini III.1.134, the suffix *ac*: *rambhaḥ*, *rambhā*. By Pāṇini III.4.65, the suffix *tumun*: *ārabhate bhoktum* ("he begins to eat"). By Uṇādi-sūtra III.117, the suffix *asac*: *rabhasaḥ*, which means an impulsive activity devoid of deliberation. (1023)

The root *labh* means "to obtain. [From it we derive: *labdhiman* (by Pāṇini III.2.88), *upalabhā* (III.3.104), and by virtue of the rule for diversity (*bāhulaka*, V.3.92), *labdhiḥ* (III.3.94, Kāśikā). By the rule *labheś ca* (VII.1.64), the augment *num* is added: *ālambhaḥ*, *vilambhanam*. Regarding the forms *alābhi* and *alambhi*, the rule *vibhāṣā ciṇṇamuloḥ* (VII.1.69) applies. According to the Kāśikā on VII.1.69, they say that when the root is preceded by a prefix (*sopasarga*), the *num* augment is obligatory.

*vyalambhi* [is derived from *vi-alam-bh*]. Regarding the rule *upasargāt khalghañoḥ* (Pāṇini VI.1.90–67): *īṣallambhaḥ* (easy to obtain), *supralambhaḥ* (very easy to obtain). Regarding the rule *na sudurbhyāṃ kevalābhyām* (VI.1.90–68): *sulabham* (easily obtained), *durlabham* (difficult to obtain). Regarding the rule *āṅo yi* (VI.1.90–65): *ālambhyam* (to be seized or touched). Regarding the rule *upāt praśaṃsāyām* (VI.1.90–66):
[the *ya*-affix is applied after *upa* when expressing praise]. All manuscripts read this. 192.
When there is something to be obtained, one desires it by [the rule] *sani mīmāghv* (Pāṇini VI.1.45–54); one obtains it in order to eat, according to *labhate bhoktum* (Pāṇini III.4.65). (1024)

The root *ṣvanj* is used in the sense of embracing. By the rule *daṃśasañjasvañjāṃ śapi* (Pāṇini VI.4.25), there is the elision of *n*; by *upasargāt sunoti* (VIII.3.65), there is the substitution of *ṣ*: *pariṣvajate*. By the rule *sadisvañjoḥ parasya liṭi* (VIII.3.118), the substitution of *ṣ* does not occur [in the periphrastic perfect]; however, by *śranthigranthidambhisvañjīnāṃ ca* (Kāśikā on I.2.6), there is *kittva* [of the suffix], and thus: *pariṣasvaje*. By the rule *prāk sitād aḍvyavāye ’pi* (VIII.3.63), there is the substitution of *ṣ*.

He embraced (*paryaṣvajata*). According to the rule *sivādīnāṃ vāḍvyavāye ’pi* (Pāṇini VIII.3.71), there is optionally the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*: *paryasvajata*. [In the perfect tense: *asvaṅkthāḥ*; [in the aorist: *iḍ apīṣṭ̣aḥ*: *asvañjiṣṭ̣hāḥ*. By the rule *jāntanaśāṃ vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VI.4.32), there is optionally the elision of the *n* before the suffix *ktvā*: *svaṅktvā*, *svaktvā*. The root *had* means "to void excrement. [Examples: *hadate*, *hannam*. Regarding the statement "one should not drink cow-dung," it is due to an error [of the author]. [The roots listed] from here on are *anudātta* and *anudāttet*. 962.

The root *ñi-kṣvidā* is used in the sense of an indistinct sound. It is marked with the *udātta* accent and is therefore *udātta-it*. *kṣvedati*, *kṣveditā*. By the rule *āditaś ca* (Pāṇini VII.2.16), the augment *iṭ* is not added: *kṣviṇṇaḥ*. By the rule *vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini VII.2.17), [the augment *iṭ* is optional]: *kṣviṇṇam* / *kṣveditam*; *prakṣviṇṇaḥ* / *prakṣveditaḥ*. According to the rule *niṣṭhā śīṅ-svidi-midi-kṣvidi-dhṛṣaḥ* (Pāṇini I.2.19), the *niṣṭhā* suffixes do not take the *kit* designation when they have the augment *iṭ*. In the *divādi* class, there is the root *ñi-kṣvidā* (IV.134): *kṣvidyati*, *akṣvidat* (1027).

The root *skand* means "to dry up. From this point up to the end of [the section on] *kit* suffixes (1042), fifteen roots are *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and take the *parasmaipada* endings. Examples: *skandati*, *skadyate*. Regarding the form *pariṣkaṇṇaḥ* or *pauṣkaṇṇaḥ*, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs optionally by Pāṇini VIII.3.75: *pariskandaḥ prācyabharateṣu*. Regarding the forms *viṣkandati* or *viskandati*, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs optionally by Pāṇini VIII.3.73: *veḥ skander aniṣṭhāyām*. However, it does not occur here: *viskannaḥ*. Furthermore, by Pāṇini VIII.3.74: *pareś ca*... [the same rule applies].

*pariṣkandati*, *pariskandati*; *prāskadat*, *prāskandīt*; by the rule *nīg vañcu* (Pāṇini VI.4.84), *canīskadyate*; by the rule *skandeḥ salopaś ca* (Uṇādi I.15), the suffix *u*: *kanduḥ* (a steaming vessel); with the suffix *ac* (III.1.134), *skandaḥ*; by the rule *skandeś ca svāṅge* (Uṇādi IV.206), the suffix *dha*: *skandhaḥ*; in the case of the suffix *ktvā*, there is no elision of *na* by the rule *skandisyandor* (VI.4.31): *skanttvā*; with the suffix *ṇamul* by the rule *viśipatipadiskandām* (III.4.56): *gehāvaskandam āste* (he sits jumping into the house). (1028)

*Yabh* in the sense of inverted sexual intercourse: *yabhati*, *yabdha*, *yabhyam* (Pāṇini III.1.98). According to Durga, [the root] *jabh* [is used]: *jambhati* (Pāṇini VII.1.61). *Ṇam* in the sense of bowing (*prahvatva*). Bowing is the state of being humble (*namratva*). *praṇamati*. Regarding the agent as the object (*karmakartṛ*), [the suffixes] *yak* and *ciṇ* are not applied after *duh*, *snus*, and *nam* (Pāṇini III.1.89): *namate daṇḍaḥ svayam eva* (the staff bows by itself); *anaṃsta*. Regarding *yam*, *ram*, *nam*, and *mā*, [the suffix] *suk* is added [before the *liṭ* affix] (Pāṇini VII.2.73). [The text reads] *hanye* (it is struck), which seems to be a corruption. In Pāṇini’s version, the sentence reads: *hanyamānaḥ gāyati pramādāt* ("Being struck, he sings out of negligence"). All manuscripts read thus.

(93 I 2, 73): *anaṃsīt*. By the rule *jvala-hvala-hmala-calanam āṅ* (I, 867), it optionally takes the *mit* designation: *nāmayati*, *namayati*; with a prefix, it always takes it: *praṇamayati*. By the rule *namikampi* (III, 2, 167), the suffix *ra* is applied: *namraḥ*. By the rule *phalipāṭi* (Uṇ. I, 19), the suffix *nāk* is applied: *valmīkam* (1030).

The roots *gam* and *sṛp* mean "to go. By the rule *iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ* (Pāṇini VI.1.77), [the *k* of the suffix] *cha* is substituted [for the final consonant]: *gacchati*. By the rule *samo gamyṛcchi* (I.3.29), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *saṃgacchate*. [In the past tense: *agamat* (by III.1.55). By the rule *gamahanajana* (VI.4.98), there is elision of the penultimate vowel: *jagmuḥ*. By the rule *vibhāṣā gamahana* (VII.2.68), the augment *iṭ* is optionally inserted before the suffix *kvasu*: *jagmivān*, *jaganvān*. By the rule *gamer iṭ parasmaipadeṣu* (VII.2.58), [the augment *iṭ* is inserted] after the root *gam* when followed by parasmaipada suffixes.

By the rule *gamiṣyati, jigamiṣati, vā gama* (I, 2, 13), there is the *kittva* (the property of being treated as *kit*) for the *liṅ* and *sic* suffixes: *saṃgasīṣṭa*, *saṃgaṃsīṣṭa*; *samagata*, *samagaṃsta*. By the rule *ajjhanagamāṃ sani* (VI, 4, 16), which prescribes lengthening for the substitute *iṅ* of the root *gam*, this [lengthening] does not apply here: *saṃjigaṃsate*. By the rule *gamaś ca* (III, 2, 47), the suffix *khac* is applied: *pravaṃgamaḥ*. And by the rule *khac ca ḍit* (cf. III, 2, 38, 3): *pravaṃgaḥ*. By the rule *ḍaḥ* (cf. III, 2, 48 Bh.): [the suffix *ḍa* is applied].

*Pravagaḥ* (from *pra-vag-*, III, 2, 38, 2); *vihāyaso viha ca* (III, 2, 38, 2): *vihaṃgamaḥ*; *ḍe ca* (III, 2, 38, 4): *vihagaḥ*, *vihaṃgaḥ* (III, 2, 38, 3); *uraso lopaś ca* (III, 2, 38, 2): *uragaḥ*, and some say *uraṅgamaḥ* as well; for *tvara*, there is the substitution of *tur*: *turagaḥ*, *turaṅgamaḥ*; by *laṣapat-* (III, 2, 154), the suffix *ukañ*: *āgāmukaḥ*; and by *gatvaraś ca* (III, 2, 164), and *sitanigami-* (Uṇ. I, 70), the suffix *tun*: [the word *gatvaraḥ*].

*Āgantuḥ*: from the root *gam* with the suffix *gan* (cf. Uṇ. I, 122): *gaṅgā*; from *gam* with the suffix *ḍoḥ* (Uṇ. II, 67): *gauḥ*; in the sense of the present tense, *jagat* by [the rule] *pṛṣad* (Uṇ. II, 84); *nīlaṅguḥ* (Uṇ. I, 37) means a worm; with the suffix *kyun* (Uṇ. II, 77) after *gam*, there is also the substitution of *ga*: *gaganam*; in the sense of the future, "gamyādayaḥ" (Pāṇini III, 3, 3); with the suffix *iniḥ* (Uṇ. IV, 6) after *gam*: *gamī grāmam* ("one who will go to the village"); with the suffix *ṇit* after *āṅ* (Uṇ. IV, 7): *āgāmī*; with the suffix *tran* after *gam* and the substitution of *ā* (Uṇ. IV, 168): [e.g., *āgantā*].

From the rule *gātra, graha-vṛd-dhṛ-niścigamaś ca* (Pāṇini III.3.58), the suffix *ap* is applied, resulting in *gamaḥ*. From *gocarasaṃcara* (Pāṇini III.3.119), *nigamaḥ* refers to the Vedas and so forth. *Sarpati*, *asṛpat*: from the root *sṛp*, by *sarpo ’ci* (Pāṇini III.1.134) and *ke* (Pāṇini III.1.135), we have *sarpaḥ*. By *sphāyi* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.13), the suffix *rak* is applied: *sṛpraḥ* means the moon; *sṛprā* means a river. By *arciśuci* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.109), the suffix *is* is applied: *sarpiḥ* (1031, 1032).

The root *yama* means "to cease. Cessation (*uparama*) is withdrawal (*nivṛtti*). According to Pāṇini VII.3.77, *iṣu-gami-yama-ām chaḥ*, the suffix *cha* is applied; thus, *yacchati*. By Pāṇini I.3.56, *upād yamaḥ svakaraṇe*, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used when it means "marrying" (*svakaraṇa*), which is the taking in marriage (*pariṇaya*); for example, *upayacchate kanyām* ("he marries a girl"). By Pāṇini I.3.28, *āṅo yamahanaḥ*, [the *taṅ* endings are used]; for example, *āyacchate*. By Pāṇini I.3.75, *samudāṅbhyo yamo 'granthe*, [the *taṅ* endings are used]; for example, *saṃyacchate*. By Pāṇini I.2.15, *yamo gandhane*, there is the *kittva* (causing the *guṇa* to be replaced by *vṛddhi*); for example, *udāyata*. By Pāṇini I.2.16, *vibhāṣopayamane*, [the *kittva* is optional]; for example, *upāyata* or *upāyaṃsta*. [This applies to] the roots *yama*, *rama*, *nama*, and *mā*.
1 P adds: *nāma* (cf. Hem. Uṇ. 916); 2 P *plavaṃgamaḥ* and *plavaṃgaḥ*; 3 thus all Hśs. I 94.

And *sak* (VH 2, 73): *ayaṃsīt*; *yaṃyamyate* (VH 4, 85, 1). With the suffix *mit*, as in *yamo ’pariveṣaṇe* (I 871): *niyamayati*. With the suffix *khac* [after the root *yam*] when meaning "vow" (*vrata*), according to *vāci yamo vrata* (III 2, 40): *vācaṃyama-purandarau* (VI 3, 69). With the suffix *ac* (III 1, 134): *Yamaḥ*, *niyataḥ*, *yatiḥ*, *niyatiḥ*. According to *na pādam* (I 3, 89), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used: *āyāmayate*. And with the suffix *ghañ* [after the root *yam*] when preceded by *sam*, *upa*, *ni*, or *viṣu*, according to *yamaḥ samupaniviṣu ca* (III 3, 63).

*saṃyamaḥ*, *saṃyāmaḥ*; *upayamaḥ*, *upayāmaḥ*; *niyamaḥ*, *niyāmaḥ*; *viyamaḥ*, *viyāmaḥ*. By the rule *ṣṭran* (Uṇ. IV.158, cf. 166): *yantram*. According to Śrī Bhoja, because [the root] ends in *u*: having restrained (*yatvā*), having restrained (*yamitvā*). (1033)

The root *tap* means "to heat. By the rule *nisas tapatāv anāsevane* (VIII. 3. 102), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*: *niṣṭapati*. By the rule *udvibhyāṃ tapas* (I. 3. 27), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *uttapate*, *vitapate*. Also by the rule *svāṅgakarmakāc ca* (I. 3. 27, vārttika): *pṛṣṭham uttapate* ("he heats his back"). By the rule *tapas tapaḥkarmakasyaiva* (III. 1. 88), the agent of the action whose object is "penance" (*tapas*) is treated as if it were the object: *tapyate tapas tāpasaḥ* ("the ascetic performs penance"); the meaning is that he acquires penance. By the rule *tapo 'nutāpe ca* (III. 1. 65), the suffixes *yak* and *ciṇ* do not apply.

A *tāpasa* is one who has not performed austerity (*atapta-tapas*). He was tormented by sinful karma in [the hell] Nandīpāla and others; *tapana* refers to the sun. By the rule *asūryalalāṭayor dṛśitapoḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.36), the suffix *khaś* is applied: *lalāṭantapaḥ* ("one who scorches the forehead"). By the rule *dviṣatparayos tāpeḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.39): *dviṣantapaḥ* ("one who torments the enemy"). In the sense of a proper name (also cf. III.2.46): *parantapaḥ*. [The word] *tapas* is formed by the *uṇādi* suffix *asun* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.188). [Root] *tyaj* (meaning "in abandonment," *hānau*). Abandonment (*hāni*) is relinquishment (*tyāga*). One abandons (*tyajati*). [The gerundive] *tyājyam*. Regarding the rule *tyajiyajyoḥ kutvaṃ neṣṭam* (1035): the substitution of *k* for *c* or *j* is not desired in these cases.

The root *ṣañj* means "to attach. By the rule *daṃśasañjasvañjāṃ śapi* (Pāṇini VI.4.25), there is the elision of the nasal (*n*), and by *upasargāt sunoti* (VIII.3.65), the change to *ṣ* occurs: *vyatiṣajati*. By *sthādiṣv abhyāsena cābhyāsasya* (VIII.3.64), [the change occurs] in the reduplicated form: *abhiṣaṣañja*. By *jāntanaśāṃ vibhāṣā* (VI.4.32), there is optionally the elision of the nasal before the suffix *ktvā*: *saktvā* or *saṅktvā*. *Utsaṅga* means "lap" or "bosom"; *prāsaṅga* [means "attachment"]; *niṣaṅga* means "quiver. By *asisañjibhyāṃ kthin* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.154), [the word] *sakthi* (1036) is formed.

The root *dṛś* is used in the sense of "seeing. By the rule *pāghrādhmā* (Pāṇini VII.3.78), there is the substitution of *paśya*: *paśyati*. In the context of the rule *samo gamyṛchi* (I.3.29), by the addition *dṛśeś ca* (Kāśikā on I.3.29), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *saṃpaśyate*. By the rule *vibhāṣā sṛjidṛśos* (VII.2.65), the augment *iṭ* is optionally added before the suffix *thal*: *dadarśitha* or *dadraṣṭha*. By the rule *sṛjidṛśor jhaly am akiti* (VI.1.58), the augment *am* is added: *draṣṭā*. By the rule *syasicsīyuṭtāsiṣu* (VI.4.62), the *ciṇvat* treatment applies and the augment *iṭ* is added:
*darśiṣyate* (by you). By the rule *irito vā* (III.1.57), the suffix *aṅ* is optionally applied; when *aṅ* follows, there is *guṇa* substitution for the vowel of *ṛ* and *dṛś*.

1 KC *suk* 2 KC *yantvā*; cf. VI, 4, 37. 3 cf. I, 767. 4 KP *tyajiyujyoḥ*. The preservation of the *j* in *yaj* results from VII, 3, 66; that of *tyaj* from VII, 3, 66, 3; and that of *yuj* from VII, 3, 68. Śākaṭāyana has the rule (IV, 1, 179) *tyajyajaḥ*. 5 All manuscripts read thus. 6 KC *kthan*. 7 P *vartamāne j*. 8 *atra* 95 I.

(VII, 4, 16): *adarśat* means "he saw"; because of the rule *na dṛśaḥ* (III, 1, 47), the suffix *kso* does not occur. By the rule *jñā-śru-smṛ-dṛśāṃ sanas taṅ* (I, 3, 57), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *didṛkṣate*. By the rule *caṅy ur ṛt* (VII, 4, 7), there is optionally [the substitution of *u* for *ṛ*]: *adadarśat* or *adīdṛśat*. According to the rule *abhivādi-dṛśor ātmanepade vā* (I, 4, 53, 1), the agent (*kartṛ*) may optionally be designated as the object (*karman*): *rājā darśayate bhṛtyān* or *bhṛtyaiḥ*. By the rule *pā-ghrā-dhmā-dheṭ-dṛśaḥ śaḥ* (cf. III, 1, 137), the suffix *śa* is applied.

The suffix *khaś* is applied after the root *dṛś* when preceded by *asūrya* and *lalāṭa*, provided that the resulting meaning is "seeing" (*dṛśi-tapoḥ*): *asūryampaśyā rājadārāḥ* ("the king's wives do not look at the sun"). Furthermore, *khaś* is applied after *dṛś* when preceded by *ugra*, *īraṃmada*, and *pāṇindhama*: *ugrampaśyaḥ*, *īraṃmadapaśyaḥ*, and *pāṇindhamāḥ*. [The suffix *khaś* is also applied] after *dṛś* when preceded by words such as *tyad* (pronouns).

Regarding the rule *nālocane kañ ca* (Pāṇini III.2.60): [the suffixes] *ka*, *kan*, and *kha* are applied after the root *dṛś* when it does not mean "to look" (*ālocana*). Examples include *tādṛk*, *tādṛśaḥ*, and *tādṛkṣaḥ* (as noted in the Kāśikā on III.2.60). According to the supplementary rule *samānānyayoś ca* (III.2.60, vārttika 1), we have *sadṛśaḥ* ("similar") and *anyādṛśaḥ* ("different"). From the rule *dṛśeḥ kvanip* (III.2.94), we derive *pāradṛśvā* ("one who has seen across/to the end"), *darśaḥ* ("sight"), and *ādarśaḥ* ("mirror"). From the Uṇādi-sūtra *arjidṛśikamyami* (Uṇ. I.28), we get *paśuḥ* ("beast"). In common usage (*bhāṣā*), according to the rule *śāsiyudhidṛśidhṛṣimṛṣibhyo yuc* (Pāṇini III.3.130, as cited in the Kāśikā), we have *sudarśanaḥ*.

When used in the sense of an object (*karman*) with the meaning of totality (*sākalya*), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied to the roots *dṛś* and *vid*. Example: *kanyādarśaṃ varayati* ("he chooses a bride, having looked at her all over"). (1037)

The root *daṃś* means "to bite. Biting (*daśanam*) is the action of the teeth. By the rule *daṃśasañjasvañjāṃ śapi* (VI.4.25), there is elision of the nasal (*na*): *daśati*. By the rule *lupasada* (III.1.24), the suffix *yaṅ* is applied in the sense of censuring the action, and by *japajabhadahadaśa* (VII.4.86), there is the augment *anusvāra*: *dandaśyate*. By the rule *yajajapadaśāṃ yaṅaḥ* (III.2.166), the suffix *ūka* is added: *dandaśūkaḥ*. With the suffix *aṇ* in the sense of the object (III.2.1): *vṛṣadaṃśaḥ* ("mouse-eater") refers to a cat; this is because of the specific mention of the form *daśana*.

(above) *nalopaḥ* [Pāṇini II.4.72]; from *upadaṃśas tṛtīyāyām* (III.4.47), the suffix *ṇamul*: *mūlakopadaṃśaṃ bhuṅkte* (“he eats with a radish as a side-dish”); from *dāmnī* (III.2.182), the suffix *ṣṭran*: *daṃṣṭrā* (“fang”); from *nudaṃśo guṇaś ca* (cf. Uṇādi I.156): *daśa* (“ten”); from *ṣidbhidādibhyo ’ṅ* (III.3.104): *daśā*, meaning a wick, a state, or the hem of a garment (1038).

The root *kṛṣ* means "to scratch" (*vilekhane*). Scratching here refers to the plowing with a plow. It forms *karṣati* in the *tudādi* class (DhP VI.6). According to Pāṇini III.1.44 (Kāśikā), the suffix *sic* is optionally used after *spṛś*, *mṛś*, *kṛṣ*, *tṛp*, and *dṛp*: thus *akrākṣīt* or *akārṣīt*. In the alternative case, the suffix *ksa* is used (III.1.45): *akṛkṣat*. Furthermore, by Pāṇini VII.4.7, the substitution of *u* for *ṛ* is optional: thus *acakarṣat* or *acīkṛṣat*.

In *nandy-ādi* (DhP III.1.134), *saṃkarṣaṇaḥ*; in *aci* (DhP III.1.134), *karṣaḥ*; *ākarṣaḥ* means a gaming board; and by *saptamyāṃ copapīḍarudhakarṣaḥ* (Aṣṭādhyāyī III.4.49): *bhrāṣṭropakarṣaṃ dhānāḥ khādati* ("he eats the grains, drawing them out from the frying pan"). By *kṛṣicamitani* (Uṇādi I.82), [the suffix] *ūḥ*: *karṣūḥ* ("furrow"); by *ik kṛṣyādibhyaḥ* (Aṣṭādhyāyī III.3.108.8): *kṛṣiḥ* ("agriculture"); by *kṛṣer vṛddhiś codīcām* (Uṇādi II.38): *karṣakaḥ*, *kārṣakaḥ* ("farmer"); by *vraścikṛṣoḥ kikan* (cf. Uṇādi...).

(1 I 40): *kṛṣikaḥ*; by [the rule] *kṛṣer ādeś ca caḥ* (cf. Uṇ. II 105), *carṣaṇiḥ* means "a Vaiśya"; by [the rule] *kṛṣer varṇe* (Uṇ. III 4), with the suffix *nak*, *kṛṣṇaḥ*. (1039) *daha* in the sense of "reducing to ashes. *dahati*; by [the rule] *lupasadacara* (III 1 24), there is *yaṅ*: *dandahyate*; by [the rule] *dāder ghaḥ* (cf. VIII 2 32), *dagdhā*. 1 P omits *ṣidbhidādibhyo* etc. 2 All manuscripts read thus.

He will burn (dhakṣyati). In the group beginning with *nyaṅku* (Pāṇini VII.3.53), there is *dāgh*: *nidāghaḥ*, *avadāgho bhakṣye* (‘heat in food’); otherwise, it is *avadāhaḥ*. (1040) *Miha* means ‘to sprinkle’: *mehati*. *Mehanam*. In the *kvasu* suffix, *mīḍhvān* (VI.1.12). By the rule *dāmnī-* (III.2.182), the suffix *ṣṭran* is applied: *meḍhram*. In the group beginning with *nyaṅku* (VII.3.53), *meghaḥ*. (1041)

The root *kit* is used in the senses of dwelling and removing disease. By the rule *guptij* (Pāṇini III.1.5), the suffix *san* occurs in the sense of origination: *cikitsati*; because of the inclusion of "and" (*ca*), it is also used in the sense of doubt: *vicikitsati*. In the sense of dwelling, there is no [application of *san*]: *ketati*, *ketana*, *saṃketa*, *ketu*, *ketakī*. In the *curādi* group, *keta* is used in the sense of making known (X.345): *saṃketayati*. (1042) These roots ending in vowels are anudātta and udātetta. 978. *dāna* in the sense of cutting; from here until the end of the section (1053), ten roots are aniṭ and are both parasmaipada and ātmanepada. After the roots *mān*, *badh*, *dān*, and *śān*, there is lengthening of the vowel of the reduplication in the aorist (III.1.6).

I, 6) Thus, with the suffix *san*: *dīdāṃsate*, *dīdāṃsati* (1043). The root *śān* means "to sharpen": *śīśāṃsate*, *śīśāṃsati* (1044) a weapon. *Ḍupacaṣ* means "to cook. The nasalized vowel *a* is a characteristic feature of all [these roots].

The purpose [of this rule] is so that the technical designation *it* may apply to the non-nasal vowel (*anunāsika*) when taught [by the rule] *upadeśe ’j anunāsika id* (Pāṇini I.3.2). For example: *pacate*, *pacati*; *paktrimam* (where *aṅ* is applied because of the suffix marker *ṣit*, III.3.104); *pacā* (where *ktin* is applied in the sense of the abstract state by III.3.95); *paktiḥ*; *pakvam* (where *va* is substituted by VI.1.52); *śvapacaḥ* (from the class beginning with *pac-* at III.1.134); and *śvapākaḥ* and *māṃsapākaḥ* (where *aṇ* is also desired). Furthermore, in the case of *nyaṅkvādi-* (VII.3.53), the suffix *uñ* is applied there itself by way of irregular derivation (*nipātana*) in the sense of the reflexive agent (*karmakartṛ*).

*dūrepākuḥ*, *phalepākuḥ* [formed by] *parimāṇe pacaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.33), [the suffix] *khaś*: *droṇaṃpacaḥ*; [by the rule] *mitanakhe ca* (III.2.34): *mitaṃpacaḥ*, *nakhaṃpacaḥ*; [by the rule] *rājasūyasūrya-* (III.1.114): *kṛṣṭapacyaḥ*; [by the rule] *alaṃkṛñ-* (III.1.96, Kāśikā): *pacelimā māṣāḥ*; [by the rule] *māṃsasya paci yuḍ-ghañor* (VI.1.63, 144, Kāśikā), there is optionally elision [of the final -a]: *māṃspākaḥ* / *māṃsapākaḥ*; *māṃspacanam* / *māṃsapacanam*. (1045)

The root *bhaj* is used in the sense of "to serve. One uses the forms *bhajate* or *bhajati*. According to Pāṇini VI.4.122 (*tṛphalabhaja*), the perfect forms are *bheje* and *bhejuḥ*. By Pāṇini III.2.62 (*bhajo ṇviḥ*), the suffix *ṇvi* is applied to form *ardhabhāk* ("sharing half"). By Pāṇini III.2.142 (*saṃpṛcānurudha*), the suffix *ghin* is applied to form *bhāgī* ("a sharer"). Regarding the word *bhaga*: by the rule *khalaṃ bhagaḥ padaṃ ca* (as noted in the Kāśikā on III.3.125), it is derived with the suffix *ghan* (III.3.18–19) to form *bhāgaḥ* ("a portion"), as well as the gerund *bhaktum* and the past passive participle *bhaktaḥ*. In the *curādi* group (the tenth class), *bhāja* is listed for the sense of "dividing" (*pṛthakkarmaṇi*) at X.340: *vibhājayati* ("he causes to divide"). [1047] 9

The root *rañj* means "to color" (*rāge*). By the rule *rañjeś ca* (VI.4.26), there is the elision of the nasal (*na*) before the suffix *śap*: *rajate* and *rajati*. By the rule *kuṣirajoḥ prācāṃ śyan parasmaipadaṃ ca* (III.1.90), [the suffix] *śyan* is applied and the *parasmaipada* occurs: *rajyati vastraṃ svayam eva* ("the cloth colors itself"). By the rule *ghañi ca bhāvakaraṇayoḥ* (VI.4.27), there is the elision of the nasal: *rāgaḥ* ("coloring"); in the sense of a locus (*adhikaraṇe*), as noted in the Kāśikā on VI.4.27, it is *raṅgaḥ* ("stage" or "arena"). By the rule *rañjer ṇau mṛgaramaṇe* (VI.4.24, vārttika 3), [the nasal is elided when the causative suffix] *ṇi* follows in the sense of "pleasing deer": *rajayati mṛgān* ("he pleases the deer"), but not here: *rañjayati naṭaḥ* ("he pleases the actor").

Regarding the *kitva* [application of the *guṇa* substitute] in *rajanarajakarājaḥsu* (cf. Pāṇini VI.4.24.5), the suffix *ṣvun* is applied in the sense of an artisan (*śilpin*) according to Pāṇini III.1.145 and the Bhāṣya: *rañjakaḥ* (a dyer). *Mahārajanaṃ* refers to the plant *kusumbha*. In the group beginning with *gaura-* (Pāṇini IV.1.41), we have *rajanī*. Because of the rule that assigns the technical designation *mit* to the roots *jan*, *jṝ*, *ṣknas*, *suranj*, and those ending in *am* (Dhātupāṭha I.862–865), others state that this applies elsewhere as well, for example: *rājarṣikalpo rajayan manuṣyān* (a quasi-sage king who pleases people). From the root *saṃpṛc* (Pāṇini III.2.142), we derive *rāgī* (one who is passionate). From the rule *pṛṣirañjibhyāṃ kit* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.111), the suffix *atac* is applied to form *rajatam* (silver). (1048)

*Śap* [is used] in the sense of reviling (*ākrośe*). Reviling is hostile contemplation; because it has multiple meanings, it also refers to verbal [insult] and physical contact. [Examples: *śapate*, *śapati*. In the sense of "imprecation" (*upalambhane*), according to Pāṇini I.3.21, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied. By Pāṇini I.4.34, the recipient (*saṃpradāna*) is designated: *śapate Caitrāya* ("he curses at Caitra"); *śapati ripuṃ purodhāḥ* ("the priest curses the enemy"). By the rule *śīṅ-śapi-ruhi-* (Uṇādi III.113), the suffix *athac* is added: *śapathaḥ* ("an oath"). By the rule *śāśapibhyāṃ dadanau* (Uṇādi IV.97), the suffixes *dan* and *dan* are added: *śabdaḥ* ("sound"). By the rule *śaper baś ca* (Uṇādi I.107), the suffix *kala* is added: *śabalaḥ* ("variegated color") (1049).

The root *tviṣ* means "to shine. It takes the forms *tveṣate* and *tveṣati*. According to Uṇādisūtra 96 (*tviṭ, naptṛ-neṣṭṛ*), the word *tvaṣṭṛ* denotes the Sun. Durga states that when preceded by the prefix *ava*, it signifies both "giving" and "casting away"; "casting away" means "removing": *avatveṣati gāḥ dvijāya* ("he gives cows to the twice-born"), *avatveṣate malam* ("he casts away impurity"). (1050)

The root *yaja* is used in the senses of worshiping the gods, forming an alliance, and giving. It takes the forms *yajate* and *yajati*. By the rule *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* (Pāṇini VI.1.15), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *ijyate*, *iṣṭaḥ*, *iṣṭiḥ*. By the rule *iṭy abhyāsasyobhayeṣām* (Pāṇini VI.1.17), [the augment *iṭ* is added to the reduplicated syllable]: *iyāja*. By the rule *yajayācaruca* (Pāṇini VII.3.66), there is no change to the guttural (*kutva*): *yājyam*. By the rule *yajñāṅge* (Pāṇini VII.3.62), [the form] *prayājānuyājau* is used for the limbs of a sacrifice; elsewhere, it is *prayāgaḥ* and *anuyāgaḥ*. By the rule *karaṇe yajaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.85), the suffix *ṇini* is applied: [forming *yajñī*].

One who performs the *agniṣṭoma* sacrifice: *yajvā*, by [Pāṇini III.2.103] *suyajo ṅvanip*; one performing a sacrifice: *yajamānaḥ*, by [Pāṇini III.2.128] *pūṅyajoḥ śānan*; a priest who sacrifices at the proper time: *ṛtvik*, by [Pāṇini III.2.59] *ṛtau yajati*; one who habitually sacrifices: *yāyajūkaḥ*, by [Pāṇini III.2.166] *yajajapadaśāṃ yaṅaḥ* with the suffix *ūka*; sacrifice: *yajñaḥ*, by [Pāṇini III.3.90] *yajayāca* with the suffix *naṅ*; the act of sacrificing: *ijyā*, by [Pāṇini III.3.98] *vrajayajor bhāve kyap*; the sacrificial post: *yaṣṭiḥ*, from the *uṇādi* group [IV.179]; the *Yajus* formula: *yajuḥ*, by [Uṇādi II.118] *artipṝvapi* with the suffix *us*; specifically, the *Kāṭhaka*. (1051)
1. *Kāñcana* and *kusumbha* [in the sense of "gold," the correct form is *mahārajata*]; 2. he uttered a sound; 3. Tvaṣṭṛ is the Sun. 1.98.

The root *ḍuvap* means "to sow" (*bījasaṃtāne*). The "continuation of seeds" (*bījānāṃ saṃtānaḥ*) refers to their spreading in a field. [Examples: *vapate*, *vapati*, *praṇivapati* (Pāṇini VIII.4.17); [passive] *upyate*; [agentive] *vaptā*; [preterite] *uvāpa*, *ūpuḥ*, *ūpe*. [Past passive participle] *uptaḥ*. By rule III.1.126 (*āsuyuvapi*), the suffix *ṇyat* is applied: *vāpyaḥ*. [Derivative] *uptrimam*. By rule Uṇādi II.27 (*gṛdhivapibhyāṃ ran*), [the suffix] *ran* is added: *vapraḥ* (a mound). By rule Uṇādi II.118 (*artipṝvapi*), [the suffix] *us* is added: *vapus* (beauty/form). By rule Uṇādi IV.124 (*vasivapivadirāji*), [the suffix] *iñ* is added: *vāpiḥ* (a pond). In the *bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III.3.104), [the suffix *aṅ* is added]: *vapā* (omentum/fat) [as per rule 1052].

The root *vah* is used in the sense of "carrying" (*prāpaṇe*). One uses the forms *vahate*, *vahati*, *praṇivahate*, and *praṇivahati* (Pāṇini VIII.4.17). The perfect forms are *uvāha*, *ūhuḥ*, and *ūhe*. By the rule *sahivahor od avarṇasya* (VI.3.112), the vowel *o* is substituted for the *a* of *vah*: thus, *voḍhā*. According to *adikhādinīvahīnām* (I.4.52, 5), the object (*karman*) of these roots does not receive the designation of *karma-kāraka* when they are used with the causative: *vāhayati bhāraṃ Caitreṇa Maitraḥ* ("Maitra causes Caitra to carry the load"). The word *vahyam* is derived as an instrument (*karaṇa*) by III.1.102. Furthermore, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied after *naś* and *vah* when the agent (*kartṛ*) is either a living being (*jīva*) or a person (*puruṣa*): III.4.43.

It carries a person; *vāha* means that by which one is carried. *Skandha* and *aśva* [mean "shoulder" and "horse"]. Regarding the rule *gocarasaṃcara* (Pāṇini III.3.119), *vaha* is correct [as a noun]. From the rule *vaho dha ca* (Uṇādi I.85), *ūḥ* is added: *vadhūḥ*. From the rule *vahi-śri-śru-yud-glu-hā* (Uṇādi IV.51), *niḥ* is added: *vahniḥ*. From the rule *aśitrādibhya itrotrau* (Uṇādi IV.172): *vahitram*. (1053) These roots ending in a svarita vowel are anudātta. 988.

The root *vas* means "to dwell. It is marked with both the anudātta and udātta accents. [Examples: *vasati*, *uvāsa*, *ūṣuḥ*, *uṣyate*. By the rule *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (VIII. 3. 60), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*; thus, *nivatsyati* (VII. 4. 49). By the rule *na pādami* (I. 3. 89), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *vāsayate*. According to the rule *bhāṣāyāṃ sadavasaśruvaḥ* (III. 2. 108), we have *ūṣivān*. Regarding the form *amāvāsyad*, it is optional according to *anyatarasyām* (cf. III. 1. 122).

*Amāvāsyā* [is derived from] *amā-vasyā*; by Pāṇini VII.2.52 (*vasatikṣudhor iṭ*), and III.4.72 (*gatyarthākarmaka*), the suffix *kta* is applied: *uṣitaḥ*. By I.2.7 (*mṛḍamṛda*), the suffix *ktvā* is *kit*: *uṣitvā*. From the root *vas*, the suffixes *tavyat* and *ṇic* are applied to the agent by III.1.96: *vāstavyaḥ*. From *am* [with suffix] *ati*, and by Uṇādi IV.59–60 (*vahivasyartibhyaś cit*), *vasatiḥ*. By Uṇādi I.11 (*śṝsvṛsnihi*), the suffix *u* is applied: *vasu*. By Uṇādi I.76 (*vases tun*), *vastu*. [And] with respect to a dwelling (*agāra*), the suffix *ṇic* is applied by Uṇādi... [etc.]

I.77): From the roots *vās*, *arti*, *kami*, *bhrami*, and *devi* (cf. Uṇ. III.132), the suffix *aran* is applied: *vāsaram*. From *vas* and *vap* (Uṇ. IV.124), the suffix *iñ* is applied: *vāsiḥ*; a chisel (*vāsī*) is the tool of a carpenter. From *vas* (Uṇ. II.13), the suffix *rak*: *usraḥ* means a ray of light; the change to *ṣatva* is not desired here. From the roots *dhā*, *pṛ*, *vas*, *aj*, and *ati*, the suffix *naḥ* is applied (Uṇ. III.6): *vasnam* means price. From *vas*, the suffix *saraḥ* (cf. Uṇ. III.71): *vatsaraḥ*. From *vas*, the suffix *kasun* (cf. Uṇ. IV.233): *uṣas*. [From *vas* with a prefix... (Uṇ.)...

III. 114) Thus, the meaning is: *āvasathaḥ* [a dwelling]; [the suffix] *jhac* is applied according to *tṛbhūvahivasi* (Uṇ. III. 128), resulting in *vasantaḥ*. From the root *vas-* with the suffix *tip* (cf. Uṇ. V. 179), we have *vastiḥ*, which refers to the region above the penis and below the navel; *vastayaḥ* refers to the fringes of a garment. The root *bast* (*gandha*) in the sense of "to strike" (I.
767) is [derived from] *vahaḥ* and *skandhadeśaḥ*. *Skandhaḥ* also means "horse" (all manuscripts read this). 9. 1.

(X, 144), *basta* means a goat; *vas* in the sense of covering (*ācchādane*) belongs to the first group (I I, 13): *vaste*, *vastra*, *vāsas*; *vas* in the sense of supporting (*stambhe*) belongs to the fifth group (I V, 105): *vasyati*; in the tenth group (*curādau*), *vasa* is used in the senses of affection, cutting, and taking away (X, 204); and *vāsa* in the sense of service (*upasevāyām*) belongs to the tenth group (X, 338): *vāsayati* (1054).

In the continuous series of verbal roots (*dhātupāṭha*), three roots ending in *i* are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*). From the root *veñ*, we have *vayate* and *vayati*. By Pāṇini VI.1.41, *veñ* becomes *vayi*; by VI.1.16, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) [of the *i*]. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, by VI.1.38, the substitution of *ya* for *vayi* does not apply [to the reduplication], as in *ūyuḥ*. By VI.4.121, [the substitution of *u* for *i*] occurs in the *thali* suffix: *uvayitha*. Furthermore, by VI.1.39, the substitution of *u* for the *va* of this [root] optionally occurs before a *kit* suffix.

Regarding *ūvuḥ*: by the rule *liṭy anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini I.2.40), when there is no substitution of *vayi*, there is a prohibition of *saṃprasāraṇa* for both the root *veñ* and its reduplication; thus: *vavau*, *vavuḥ*. By the rule *śāchāsāhvāvyāvepāṃ yuk* (VII.3.37): *vāyayati*. By the rule *hvāvāmaś ca* (III.2.2), with the suffix *aṇ*, [we get] *tantuvāyaḥ* (2). By the rule *lyapi ca* (VI.1.41), there is no *saṃprasāraṇa*; thus: *pravāya*. By the rule *ūtiyūtijūti* (III.3.97), *ūtiḥ* means weaving (*vayanam*). Regarding *veño ḍiḥ* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra).

(IV, 133): From the root *vi* [meaning] "bird," by means of the suffix *manin* (Uṇ. IV, 144, cf. 149), we have *vimā*; from *mṛ* and *kaṇi*, by means of *īciḥ*; and from *veñ*, by means of the *ḍit* suffix (cf. Uṇ. IV, 70, 72), we have *vīciḥ* (1055).

The root *vī* is used in the sense of "covering" (*saṃvaraṇe*). Covering means concealing. [In the forms] *vyayate*, *vyayati*, and *vīyate*—because of the rule *na vyo liṭi* (Pāṇini VI.1.46), there is no substitution of *ā* for the *ec* vowel; thus: *saṃvivyāya*. Because of the rule *iḍ attyartivyayatīnām* (Pāṇini VII.2.66), [the suffix] *iṭ* is added: *saṃvivyayitha*. Because of the rule *anabhyāsasya* (Pāṇini VI.1.8), there is no lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*); however, because of the rule *svapisyamivyeñāṃ yaṅi* (Pāṇini VI.1.19), there is *saṃprasāraṇa*: *saṃvevīyate*. By the rule *vyaś ca* (Pāṇini VI.1.43), there is no *saṃprasāraṇa* when the suffix *lyap* follows.
