Regarding *saṃvyāya*, by Pāṇini VI.1.44 (*vibhāṣā pareḥ*), there is an option: *parivīya* or *parivyāya*. By VII.3.37 (*śāchāsāhvā*), the suffix *yuk* is applied: *saṃvyāyayati*. Regarding *nīvi*: by Uṇādi-sūtra IV.135 (*nau vyo yalopaḥ pūrvasya ca dīrghaḥ*), [the suffix] *i* is added after *vyā*, with the elision of *y* and the lengthening of the preceding vowel: *nīviḥ*; [in the feminine] *nīvī*. (1056)

The root *hve* is used in the sense of "to contend" (*spardhā*) and "to call" (*śabda*). *Hvayate*, *hvayati*. By *ni-sam-upa-vi-bhyaḥ hvaḥ* (Pāṇini I.3.30), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *nihvayate*, *saṃhvayate*, *upahvayate*, *vihvayate*. By *spardhāyām āṅaḥ* (Pāṇini I.3.31): *mallo mallam āhvayate* ("one wrestler challenges another wrestler"). *Āhūyate*. By *hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam abhyastasya ca* (Pāṇini VI.1.32–33): *juhuvuḥ*. By *ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (Pāṇini VI.1.32): *juhāvayiṣati*, *ajūhavat*. By *lipi-sici-hvaś ca* (Pāṇini III.1.53), the suffix *aṅ* is applied.

*āhvat*, according to *ātmanepadeṣv anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini III.1.54): *āhvata* or *āhvāsta*. By the rule *śāchāsā* (Pāṇini VII.3.37), the suffix *yuk* is applied: *hvāyayati*. By the rule *hvāvāmaś ca* (Pāṇini III.2.2), the suffix *aṇ* is applied: *svargāhvāyaḥ* (5). By the rule *ātaś copasarge* (Pāṇini III.1.136): *prahvaḥ*. By the rule *hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca nyabhyupaviṣv* (Pāṇini III.3.72), the suffix *ap* is applied: *nihavaḥ*. 1. [The root *hve*] is used in the senses of affection (*sneha*), cutting (*cheda*), and withdrawing (*upasaṃharaṇa*). 2. *tantravāyaḥ* (according to KC). 3. *saṃvīyate* (according to KC). 4. [The root *hve*] means "to add principal capital" (*mūladhanam*). 5. All manuscripts read this. (I 100)

*āṅi yuddhe* (III, 3, 73): *āhavaḥ*; *nipānam āhāvaḥ* (III, 3, 74); *bhāve ’nupasargasya* (III, 3, 75): *havaḥ*; in the *chitvarādi* group (Uṇ. III, 1): *upahvaraḥ*; by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), [we have] *āhvayaḥ*. (1057)

The root *vad* is used in the sense of "articulate speech. It is marked with the acute accent (*udātta*) and takes the acute accent when so applied. Regarding *vadati* and *vaditā*: according to Pāṇini I.3.47, "the root *vad* [takes Ātmanepada endings] in the senses of shining, addressing, knowing, effort, disagreement, and inviting. Thus: *cārvī lokāyate vadate*—"the follower of Cārvāka shines" (i.e., appears); *gehe vadate*—"he exerts himself at home" (i.e., makes an effort); *kṣetre vivadante*—"they disagree in the field" (i.e., they speak variously); *paradārān upavadate*—"he addresses another's wife" (i.e., he seduces her in secret). According to Pāṇini I.3.48, [the root *vad* takes Ātmanepada] in the utterance of articulate speech.

The *dvijas* speak together (*saṃpravadante*). According to Pāṇini I.3.50, *vibhāṣā vipralāpe*: "The astrologers dispute" (*vipravadante*), "they dispute" (*vipravadanti*). According to I.3.49, *anor akarmakāt*: "The Kaṭha repeats after the Kālāpa. According to I.3.73, *apād vadaḥ*, when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent: "he reviles" (*apavadate*), "he reviles" (*apavadati*). In the case of the root *vad*, the vowel substitution *vṛddhi* occurs according to VII.2.3: *udyate*.

He said: [The rule] *na pādamyāṅyamāṅyasaparimuharucinṛtivadavasa* (I, 3, 89) prescribes the *ātmanepada* ending for the causative (*ṇic*): *vādayate vīṇām* ("he causes the lute to be played"). [The word] *avadya* is derived from *avadya-paṇya-varyā garhya* (III, 1, 101); thus, *avadya* is correct when meaning "blameworthy. [The word] *mṛṣodyam* is derived from *rājasūya-sūrya-* (III, 1, 114). From the root *vad* with a *sup*-ending, there is the suffix *kyap* according to *vadaḥ supi kyap ca* (III, 1, 106): *brahmodyam* and *brahmavadyam*. From the root *vad* with the words *priya* and *vaśa*, there is the suffix *khac* according to *priyavaśe vadaḥ khac* (III, 2, 38):
*priyaṃvadaḥ* and *vaśaṃvadaḥ*. According to *yajajapadaśāṃ yaṅaḥ* (III, 2, 166), the suffix [is prescribed after these]; it is also desired [to apply] after the root *vad*.

(Vgl. Uṇ. IV, 41): *vāvadūkaḥ*; [from *ud*] *uttiḥ*; by the rule *titutra* (VII, 2, 9), the augment *iṭ* is prohibited, yet *iṭ* is also desired: *uditiḥ*; by the rule *mṛḍamṛda* (I, 2, 7), the suffix *ktvā* is *kit*: *uditvā*; by the rule *accha gatyarthavadeṣu* (I, 4, 69), [the prefix *accha*] receives the designation *gati*: *acchodya*; by the rule *vṝtṝvadi* (Uṇ. III, 62), [the suffix] *sa* is applied: *vatsaḥ*; by the rule *vader ānyaḥ* (Uṇ. III, 104): *vadānyaḥ* means "a giver"; *vadanyaḥ* is also desired; by the rule *vasivapivadi* (vgl. Uṇ. IV, 124), [the suffix] *iñ* is applied: *vādiḥ*;
by the rule *bhūvadigṝbhyo ṇitran* (vgl. Uṇ. IV, 170): *vāditram*. (1058)

The root *ṭuośvi* means "to move" and "to increase. It is *seṭ*. [Present tense: *śvayati*; [future: *śvayitā*. [Derivative noun: *śvayathuḥ* (swelling). Because it belongs to the *odit* group (Pāṇini VIII.2.45), there is the substitution of *ṇatva* for the final consonant in the *niṣṭhā* suffix; and because it has *ī* as its *it* (Pāṇini VII.2.14), there is no insertion of *iṭ*: *śūnaḥ* (swollen). Because it belongs to the *yajādi* group (Pāṇini VI.1.15), it undergoes *samprasāraṇa* in the passive: *śūyate*. By the rule *vibhāṣā śveḥ* (VI.1.30), there is optionally *samprasāraṇa* in the *liṭ* and *yaṅ* affixes: *śiśvāya* / *śuśāva*, *śiśviyuḥ* / *śuśuvuḥ*. In the *yaṅ* formation: *śeśvīyate* / *śośūyate*. And by the rule *ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (VI.1.31): [there is *samprasāraṇa* before the causative suffix *ṇic* and before the *saṃ* and *caṅ* substitutes].

*śuśāvayiṣati*, *śiśvāyayiṣati*; *aśūśuvat*, *aśiśvayat*. According to *vibhāṣā dheṭśvyoḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.49), there is optionally *caṅ*: *aśiśviyat*, *aśvayīt*. By the rule *hmyantakṣaṇa* (Pāṇini VII.2.5), there is no *vṛddhi*; by *jṝstanbhv* (cf. III.1.58), there is *aṅ*; and by *śvayater aḥ* (Pāṇini VII.4.18): *aśvat*. [The word] *śvan* is derived from the root *śvi* with the suffix *niti* according to *śvanukṣan* (Uṇādi-sūtra I.158); thus, *mātariśvā* (1059). All manuscripts read this. 2. KCS reads *pravadante*. 3. P adds *vā*. 4. P reads *Kālāpakasya*, C reads *Kalāpasya*. 5. P reads *dānaśīlaḥ*. 101.
Vṛtti: The internal group beginning with *yaj* has been presented.
In the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on verbal roots composed by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin, son of Bhaṭṭeśvarasvāmin, the *bhūvādi* class, characterized by the *śap* suffix, is complete and finished. 1.

*Oṃ!* *ada* [is used] in the sense of eating. These two [roots] are *aniṭ* and *parasmaipadī*. [In the present tense: *atti*; by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapo luk* (Pāṇini II.4.72), the *śap* affix is elided; [in the dual: *adan*; [in the feminine singular: *adatī* (by VII.1.80). In the sense of mutual action (*vyatihāra*), [the suffix *śānac* is applied]: *vyatyadante* (by I.3.14). By *luṅsanor ghasḷ* (II.4.37), [the root is replaced by *ghas*]: *aghasat*; *jighatsati*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), optionally: *jaghāsa* (by II.4.40).

In *jakṣuḥ*, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs by the rule *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (VI. 1. 60); thus, *āda*. In *atsyati*, [the augment] *iṭ* is applied by *iḍ attyartivyayatīnām* (VII. 2. 66); thus, *āditha*. In the *laṅ* [past tense], *aṭ* is added by *adaḥ sarveṣām* (VII. 3. 100); thus, *ādat*. By the rule *adikhādinīvahīnām* (I. 4. 52), these roots do not receive the designation of "object" (*karma*): [one causes] Caitra to eat a ball of food (*piṇḍī*). When the suffix *lyap* follows a *kit* suffix, the root *ad* becomes *jagdhi*: thus, *jagdham*, *jagdhvā*, *prajagdhya*. In the *uṇādi* group, [the word] *anna* is derived [from this root] (cf. Uṇ. 3. 106).

Pāṇini III.2.160: *sṛghasyadaḥ kmarac* [forms] *admarah*, *ghasmaraḥ*; Pāṇini II.4.37, vārttika 1: *ghasḷbhāve 'cy upasaṃkhyānam* [provides for the substitution of *ghasḷ* before the suffix *ac*]: *praghasaḥ* (one who eats much); Pāṇini III.3.59: *upasarge 'daḥ* [forms] *vighasaḥ* (remnants of food); not here: *ghāsaḥ* (grass/food), where by Pāṇini II.4.38, *ghañ* and *ap* cause the substitution of *ghasḷ*; Pāṇini III.3.60: *nau ṇa ca* [forms] *nyādaḥ*, *nighasaḥ*; Pāṇini III.2.68: *ado 'nanne* [with the suffix] *kvip*: *āmāt* (one who eats raw food); not here: [the example would be *ādam*].

*annādaḥ*, by [Pāṇini] III, 2, 1; *kravye ca* (III, 2, 69): *kravyāt*, *kravyādaḥ*; by *adi-śada-* (Uṇ. IV, 65), the suffix *krin*: *adriḥ*; by *ades trin triniś ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 68): *Atrir muniḥ*, *attrī krimiḥ*; by *jatrvādāv* (Uṇ. IV, 102), *attruḥ*; by *ader dhaś ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 115), the suffix *kvanip*: *adhvā mārgaḥ*; by *ado num dhau ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 205), the suffix *asun*: *andho 'nnam*; by *ghaseḥ kic ca* (Uṇ. IV, 34), the suffix *īran*: *kṣīram*.

The root *han* means "to kill" and "to go. From *han*, the forms *hanti* ("he kills") and *hantā* ("he will kill") are derived. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sya* (VH 2.70), the augment *iṭ* is added: *haniṣyati* ("he will kill"). By the rule *ho hanter ñṇinneṣv* (VII 3.54), *ha* is substituted for *han* before suffixes beginning with *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *n*: *aghāni* ("it was killed"). In *ghnanti* ("they kill"), the substitution of *gh* occurs. By the rule *ner gada* (VIII 4.17), there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*: *praṇihanti* ("he strikes forward"). By the rule *hanter atpūrvasya* (VIII 4.22), [the substitution of *gh* applies]: *prahaṇanam* ("killing"). By the rule *vmor vā* (VIII 4.23), [the substitution of *gh* is optional]: *prahaṇvaḥ* or *prahanvaḥ*, *prahaṇmaḥ* or *prahanmaḥ*. By the rule *āṅo yamahana* (I 3.28), when the root is intransitive (*akarmaka*), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used.

[The rule] *āhate, svāṅgakarmakāc ca* (Pāṇini I.3.28, 1) [applies]: *āhate śiraḥ* ("he strikes his own head"). Not here: *āhanti śiraḥ śatroḥ* ("he strikes the enemy's head"). [The rule] *vyatihāre na gatihiṃsārthebhyaḥ* (Pāṇini I.3.15) [applies]: *vyatighnanti* ("they strike one another"). By the rule *gamahana* (Pāṇini VI.4.98), there is elision (*allopa*) of the penultimate vowel; by the rule *abhyāsāc ca* (Pāṇini VII.3.55), the substitution of *gh* occurs: *jaghāna*. Thus ends the *bhūvādi-gaṇa* in the *Dhātuvṛtti* of the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, conceived by the venerable Kṣīrasvāmin. 1 P. *vyatyatte* 2 P. All manuscripts read *so*. 3 See Hemacandra, *Uṇādisūtra* 809. 4 II. 102.

They struck (*jaghnuḥ*). Regarding *jaghanvān* and *jaghnivān*, the suffix *iṭ* is optionally applied by *vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām* (Pāṇini II.2.68). Regarding *ghāniṣyate*, the *iṭ* augment is applied as if it were *ciṇ* by *syasicsīyuṭtāsiṣu* (VI.4.62). By *hanteḥ jaḥ* (VI.4.36), [the substitution of] *ja* occurs: "Kill the enemy" (*jahi śatrum*). By *hano vadha liṅi* (II.4.42), the form *vadhyāt* is used; here, the substitution of *vadha* and the application of *sīyuṭ* as if it were *ciṇ* occur by way of conflict (*vipratiṣedhena*): *vadhiṣīṣṭa* and *ghāniṣīṣṭa*. And in the *luṅ* [tense], by [II.4.43]: [the substitute *vadha* applies].

*avadhīt*, according to *ātmanepadeṣv anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini I.4.44): *āhata* or *āvadhiṣṭa*. By *hanaḥ sij* (Pāṇini I.2.14), there is *kittva*; by *ajjhanagamāṃ sani* (Pāṇini VI.4.16), there is lengthening: *jighāṃsati*. With *yaṅ* (Pāṇini VII.3.55): *jaṅghanyate*. In the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*), by *hanteḥ hiṃsāyāṃ ghnī* (Kāśikā on Pāṇini VII.4.30): *jeghnīyate*. By *hanas to 'ciṇṇaloḥ* (Pāṇini VII.3.32): *ghātayati*, *ajīghatat*. Optionally, by *hano vā vadha ca* (Pāṇini III.1.97, 2), the suffix *yat* [is applied]: [e.g., *vadhyam*].

*vadhyaḥ* means "one who is to be killed" (*ghātyaḥ*). By the rule *hanas ta ca* (Pāṇini III.1.108), the suffix *kyap* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*), yielding *brahmahatyā* ("the killing of a Brahmin"). By the rule *laṣapatapada* (Pāṇini III.2.154), the suffix *ukañ* is applied, yielding *ghātukaḥ* ("a killer"). By the rule *hanaś ca vadhaḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.76), the form *vadhaḥ* is derived; thus there are the forms *vadhaḥ* or *ghātaḥ*. By the rule *mūrtau ghanaḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.77), the suffix *ghan* is applied to mean a solid mass (*mūrti*), as in *dadhighanaḥ* ("thick curd"). By the rule *antarghano deśe* (Pāṇini III.3.78), [the same suffix is applied] when referring to a region, as in *agāraika-* [referring to a single house].

The suffix *ghan* occurs after the root *han* when preceded by *pra* in the sense of a porch (*praghaṇaḥ*, *praghāṇaś ca*), and after *ud* in the sense of placing upon (*udghanaḥ*). That wooden block upon which one wood is placed and then carved is called *udghanaḥ*. The suffix *ghan* occurs after *apa* in the sense of a limb (*apaghanaḥ*). When preceded by *ayas*, *vidru*, or *us*, it occurs in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*): *ayoghanaḥ*. When preceded by *stamba*, the suffix *ka* as well as *ghan* occurs: *stambaghnaḥ* and *stambaghanaḥ*. When preceded by *pari*, the suffix *gha* occurs: [e.g., *parighaḥ*].

*parighaḥ*, *upaghna* in the sense of "support" (III.3.85); *saṃgha* and *udgha* in the senses of "multitude" and "praise" respectively (III.3.86); *nigha* means "measure" (III.3.87); *vighnaḥ* [is derived] from the rule for the suffix *ka* in the sense of *ghan* (III.3.58, 4); *nighna* means "dependent" (cf. Amarakośa III.1.16); with the suffix *ṇamul* in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe hana*, III.4.37): *upalaghātaṃ hanti* ("he strikes with a blow on the stone"); and with the roots *han*, *kṛ*, and *grah* in connection with *samūla*, *akṛta*, and *jīva* respectively (III.4.36).

The rule *samūlaghātaṃ hanti* [Pāṇini III.4.48] applies to verbs meaning "to injure" (*hiṃsārtha*) that have the same object; for example: *daṇḍaghātaṃ gāḥ kālayati* ("he drives the cows while striking them with a stick"). Alternatively, for the roots *car*, *cal*, *pat*, and *vad*, there is reduplication, the suffix *āc* is added after the reduplicated stem, and for the root *han*, the substitution of *gh* occurs.

(VI, 1, 12 Kāś.): *ghanāghanaḥ*; by [the rule] *āśiṣi hano ḍaḥ* (III, 2, 49): *arātihaḥ*, *timihaḥ*; by *ape kleśatamasoḥ* (III, 2, 50): *kleśāpahaḥ*, *tamopahaḥ*; by *anyebhyo ’pi* (III, 2, 75): it forms *varāhaḥ* (he strikes what is desirable); *paṭahaḥ* (it is struck upon a cloth); *kalahaḥ* (it strikes discordantly); by *kumāraśīrṣayor ṇiniḥ* (III, 2, 51): *kumāraghātī*, *śīrṣaghātī*; by *lakṣaṇe jāyāpatyoṣ ṭak* (III, 2, 52): [it forms *jāyāghnyaḥ* and *patighnyaḥ*].

*Jāyāghna* means "killing his wife"; *patighna*, "killing his husband. According to Pāṇini III.2.54, *śaktau hastikapāṭayoḥ*: *hastighna* ("killing an elephant") and *kapāṭaghna* ("killing a door-panel"). According to III.2.55, *pāṇighatāḍaghau śilpini*, and because it must be stated (*vaktavyāt*) [as an exception], *rājagha* ("king-killer"). According to III.2.49, *dārāv āhano ’ṇ antyasya ca ṭaḥ saṃjñāyām*: *dārvāghāṭa* ("woodpecker," so called because it strikes wood). 1. The suffixes *suṭ*, *sīyuṭ*, and the state of being like *ciṇ* (*ciṇvadbhāva*). 2. *ghātayati*. 3. *timirahaḥ* (variant reading). 4. *kavāṭa°* (variant reading for *kapāṭa*). 103.ii.

*dārvāghātaḥ* (wood-smasher), and in *cāru*: *cārvāghāṭaḥ*, *cārvāghātaḥ* (cf. Pāṇini III.2.49.2); in *sam* when [the object] is a color (*varṇa*): *varṇasaṃghāṭaḥ*, *varṇasaṃghātaḥ* (cf. III.2.49.3); with the suffix *ṇini* after the root *han* when [the object] is an action (*karman*): *pitṛghātī* (patricide); with the suffix *kvip* after *brahman*, *bhrūṇa*, and *vṛtra*: *brahmahā* (slayer of a Brahmin); with *abhyāghātī* from *saṃpṛca* (cf. III.2.142); with the suffix *u* by *śṝ-svṛ-snihi* (Uṇādi I.11): *hanuḥ*; [and] *hi* after the root *han*.

And [the suffix] *ca* (cf. Uṇ. I, 146): *himam*. From the root *han*, *vadhaḥ* with the suffix *kvuṃ* (cf. Uṇ. II, 36): *vadhakaḥ*. By the rule *vṛtṝvadi* (Uṇ. III, 62), [the suffix] *sa*: *haṃsaḥ*. From *han*, with the augment *muṭ* and the replacement *hi* (cf. Uṇ. III, 129): *hemantaḥ*. From *han*, with the replacement *aṃha* (Uṇ. IV, 62): *aṃhatiḥ*. By the rule *vasivapi* (Uṇ. IV, 124), [the suffix] *iñ*: *ghātiḥ*. By the rule *āṅi śrihanibhyāṃ hrasvaś ca* (Uṇ. IV, 137): *ahiḥ*. By the rule *nañy āhana eha ca* (Uṇ. IV, 223), [the suffix] *asun*: [the word *an-ahaḥ*].

*anehā* means time (*kālaḥ*). [The suffix *asun* is applied] by [Pāṇini] VII.1.94: *uśanas-purudaṃso’nehasām*. [The word] *ghoraḥ* is derived from the root *han-* with the suffix *ghur* (cf. Uṇādi V.64); [the word] *jaghanam* is derived from the root *han-* with the suffix *yu* (cf. Uṇādi V.32). [The word] *parighaḥ* is derived from the root *han-* with the suffix *yu*, and there is the substitution of *gh* for the initial and final [consonants] of the root: "a bolt" (*parighaḥ*) is that which strikes around (*pari-ghātanaḥ*) [cf. Amarakośa II.8.92]. These two [roots *han-*] are anudātta and udātetta. (2) Anudāttāv udāttetau 2.

The root *dviṣ* (to hate) is used in the sense of being displeased. From here on, four roots are *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and are *ubhayapadin* (conjugated in both voices). *dveṣṭe*, *dveṣṭi*, *dveṣṭā*. By the rule *satsūdviṣa* (Pāṇini III.2.61), the suffix *kvip* is applied: *brahmadviṭ* (one who hates Brahmins). By the rule *dviṣo 'mitre* (Pāṇini III.2.131), the suffix *śatṛ* is applied: *dviṣan* (hating). Regarding the rule *dviṣaḥ śatur vāvacanam* (Vārttika II.3.69.6): *caurasya dviṣan* (hating the thief) or *cauraṃ dviṣan* (hating the thief). By the rule *dviṣaś ca* (Pāṇini III.4.112), the substitution of *jus* optionally occurs: *adviṣuḥ* or *adviṣan*. (3)

The root *duh* is used in the sense of "filling" (*prapūraṇa*). Here, "filling" means the absence of filling; the prefix (*upasarga*) overrides the primary meaning of the verbal root, as in the case of *pra-sthā*. Examples: *gāṃ dugdhe*, *dogdhi*, *dogdhā*. Regarding the rule *na duhasnunamāṃ yakciṇau* (Pāṇini III.1.89): [the suffixes] *yak* and *ciṇ* are not applied after the roots *duh*, *snū*, and *nam*. Thus: *dugdhé gaur svayam eva* (the cow milks herself), *adugdha*. Regarding the rule *śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.45): [the suffix] *ksa* is applied after a root ending in *śal* that has a penultimate *i*, *u*, or *ṛ*, provided it does not take the augment *iṭ*. Thus: *adhukṣat*, *adhukṣata*. *adugdha gaur svayam eva*; and by the rule *duhaś ca* (Pāṇini III.1.63), [the suffix *luṅ* takes the *ām* substitute]: *adohi gaur svayam eva*.

In the plural, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *kṣa* before a vowel by rule VII.3.72; or, by rule VII.3.73, there is optionally elision of *kṣa* after the roots *duh*, *diha*, etc.: *adugdha*, *adugdhāḥ*; *adhukṣata*, *adhukṣathāḥ*. By rule III.1.109 (Kāśikā), the suffix *kyap* is applied: *duhyam*; the suffix *ṇyat* is also seen: *dohyam*. By rule III.2.61, the suffix *kvip* is applied: *godhuk*. By rule III.2.70, the suffix *kap* is applied to *duh*, with *gh* as the replacement for *h*: *kāmadughā*. [The suffixes] *naptṛ*, *neṣṭṛ*, etc., [are taught in] Uṇ. [...]

[The word] *duhitṛ* [is derived from the root *duh*] with the suffix *yuc* according to [Pāṇini III.3.130]: *anyebhyo ’pi dṛśyate*. Thus we have *sudohanaḥ* ("one who milks well") and *godohano ghaṭaḥ* ("a jar for milking cows"). According to [Pāṇini IV.1.41], *gaurādi*, it is *godohanī* ("a cow that yields milk"). In the *uṇādi* [list], *dohadaḥ* refers to a specific longing or desire. 1. Nominative singular of the present participle suffix *śatṛ*. 2. All manuscripts read thus. 3. Pāṇini reads *anyeṣv api* (III.2.101). 4. See Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 244.104.

*Diha* means accumulation (*upacaya*). Here, "accumulation" refers to smearing (*lepa*). By the rule *ner gadanada* (VIII. 4. 17), there is the substitution of *ṇ*: *praṇidegdhi*; the rest is as before. *Digdha*, *saṃdigdha*. *Dehana* refers to a jar. In the *gaurādi* group (IV. 1. 41), it is *dehanī*. In the *uṇādi* list, *dehalī* refers to the wooden beam at the bottom of a door; *deha* (5).

The root *lih* means "to taste. [Present tense: *leḍhi*, *līḍhe*; [Aorist: *alikṣat*. By [Pāṇini] VII.3.72, *ksasyāci*: *alikṣātām*. By [Pāṇini] VII.3.73, *lug vā duha*: *alīḍha*, *alīḍhāḥ*; [Aorist middle: *alikṣata*, *alikṣathāḥ*. By [Pāṇini] III.1.141, *śyādvyadha*, the suffix *ṇa* is applied: *lehaḥ*. By [Pāṇini] III.2.32, *vahābhre lihaḥ*, the suffix *khaś* is applied: *vahaṃlihaḥ*, *abhraṃlihaḥ*. By [Pāṇini] III.3.18–19, with the suffix *ghañ*: *lehaḥ*, *ālīḍhaḥ* (6).

The root *cakṣiṅ* is used in the sense of "distinct speech. It is *anudātta* and has an *anudātta* *it*. The addition of the marker *ṅ* is for the purpose of prohibiting *num*; for in that rule (Pāṇini VI.1.58), the term *anta* is understood to carry over. Furthermore, it serves to indicate that what is established by a *gaṇa*-list is not universally obligatory (cf. Paribhāṣā 93.3), as in the example: "This very same elephant endures the insults from young elephants" (*Subhāṣitāvalī* 631). [From this root: *ācaṣṭe*; by the rule *cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ* (I.4.54), [one forms] *ākhyātā*; or, by the rule *vā liṭi* (III.4.55), [one forms *cakhyau*, etc.].

*cakhyau*, *cakhye*; *cacakṣa*, *cacakṣe*. By the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo ’ṅ* (Pāṇini III.1.52), [the form] *ākhyat* is derived. By the rule *na dhyākhyā* (VIII.2.57), [the substitution of *kha* for *khya* does not apply], hence *khyātaḥ*. By the rule *cakṣeḥ śic ca* (Uṇādi II.120), *us* is added: *cakṣuḥ*. By the rule *cakṣer bahulaṃ śic ca* (Uṇādi IV.232), *asun* is added: *nṛcakṣāḥ* (a Rākṣasa); *avacakṣāḥ*. (7) *īr* means "to go. From here up to *pṛc* (verse 20), these twelve roots are *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*) and take the Ātmanepada endings. *īrte*, *īritā*. In the *curādi* class, *īra* means "to insult" (X.268): *īrayati*. Some say it also means "to shake. (8)

*Īḍ* means "to praise. From *īḍate*, *īḍitā*; and by [Pāṇini] VIII.2.78, *īḍajanor dhve ca*, there is the augment *iṭ* in the forms *īḍiṣe* and *īḍidhve*. *Īḍā*: because of the evidence of the rule *iḍāyā vā* (VIII.3.54), it is *iḍā*. *Īḍyaḥ* (9). *Īś* means "to have sovereignty. From *bhuvam īṣṭe*; and by [Pāṇini] VII.2.77, *īśaḥ se*, there is the augment *iṭ* in *īśiṣe* and *īśitā*. By [Pāṇini] II.3.52, *adhīgarthadayeśāṃ karmaṇi*, the genitive case is used [for the object]. *Īśānaḥ*, *īśaḥ*; and by [Pāṇini] III.2.175, *stheśabhāsa*, the suffix *varac* is applied: *īśvaraḥ* (10).

The root *ās* is used in the sense of sitting. [Examples: *āste* (he sits), *āsitā* (one who has sat). According to Pāṇini I.4.46, "the object of the roots *adhi-śī*, *adhi-śīṅ*, and *adhi-sthā* [is called *karman*]: *khaṭvām adhyāste* (he sits upon the bed). According to VII.2.83, *īd āsaḥ*: *āsīnaḥ* (seated). According to III.1.37, *dayāyāsaś ca*, the suffix *ām* is applied: *āsāṃcakre* (he has sat repeatedly). According to III.4.72, *gatyarthākarmaka*, the suffix *kta* is applied: *upāsito guruṃ Caitraḥ* (Caitra has attended upon his teacher). According to III.3.107, *ṇyāsaśrantho yuc*, the suffix *yuc* is applied: *āsanā* (the act of sitting).

The root *āṅ-śās* is used in the sense of "desire" (*icchā*): *āśāste*, *āśāsitā*. However, *śās* in the sense of "instruction" (*anuśiṣṭi*) is a different verbal root, applicable in contexts such as the prohibition of shortening [of the penultimate vowel]: by the rule *nāglopiśāsvṛditām* (Pāṇini VII.4.2), we have *aśaśāsat*; by the rule *śāsa id aṅhaloḥ* (VI.4.34), we have *aśiṣat*. There is an extension of the application [of the latter rule] to the suffix *kvip*: *āśīḥ*; and with the suffix *kta* (VII.2.15), *āśāstaḥ*. (See Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 465; KC vā 105).

From roots ending in an *anudātta* vowel and beginning with a consonant, the suffix *yuc* is applied (Pāṇini III.2.149): *āśāsanaḥ*, *āśāstiḥ*. [The suffix *ktin*] does not apply by virtue of Pāṇini III.3.103 (*guroś ca halaḥ*), because it is stated that the *niṣṭhā* suffixes take the augment *iṭ* when they are *seṭ*. Regarding the augment *iṭ* after a root marked with *udit*, there is an option (Pāṇini VII.2.56): *āśāstivā* or *āśāsitvā*. According to the followers of Durga, the form *āśāsitvā* is derived from the root *śās* with the prefix *āṅ*: *āśāsitvā*, *āśāsitaḥ*. (12)

The root *vas* means "to clothe. One clothes oneself in a garment (*paṭa*); thus, the agent is *vasitā*, the present participle is *vasānaḥ*, and the past passive participle is *vasitaḥ*. From the *bhū*-class (DhP I.1054), the past participle is *uṣitaḥ*. By [Pāṇini III.1.134], the noun *vasaḥ* ("dwelling") is formed. By [Pāṇini III.3.104], with the suffix *aṅ* belonging to the *bhidādi* group, we have *vasā* ("fat") and *vasanam* ("clothing"). With the suffix *tip* (according to Uṇādi IV.179), we have *vastiḥ* ("the bladder," specifically the part above the penis). With the suffix *ṣṭran* (Uṇādi IV.158), we have *vastram* ("garment"). With the suffix *ṇit* (Uṇādi IV.217), we have *vāsaḥ* ("clothing"). Regarding the rule [Pāṇini VI.4.126] concerning the substitution of *vā* for *vas*: in the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), the substitution of *e* and the elision of the reduplication do not occur; thus, we have *vavase* and *vavasiṣe*. (13)
The root *kas* is used in the senses of "going" (*gati*) and "teaching" (*śāsana*). It forms *kaṃste*, *kaṃsitā*, *kaṃsanaḥ*, and *Kaṃsaḥ*. According to some, it is also *kas*.

(14) The root *ṇis* is used in the sense of "kissing. It forms *niṃste*; by the rule *vā niṃsanikṣanindāṃ* (YI H, 4, 33), there is optionally the substitution of *ṇ*: *praṇiṃste* or *praniṃste*. (15) The root *ṇij* is used in the sense of "purification. It forms *niṅkte*, *praṇiṅkte*, and *niñjitā*. (16)

*Śiji* means "inarticulate sound. One *śiṅkte*, *śiñjānaḥ*, *śiñjitā*. According to Kauśika, *śiji* and *pijiti*: one *piṅkte*; *piñjaraḥ*. From *piñjara*, *khaja*, and *piñja*, etc., [the suffixes] *ūra* and *lac* are applied (Uṇ. IV, 90): *piñjūlaḥ*, *piṅgaḥ*. (17, 18) *Vṛjī* means "to avoid" (*varjane*), according to the followers of Durga. One *vṛkte*, *varjitā*; *vṛktaḥ*. (19) *Pṛcī* means "contact" (*saṃparke*). Contact is mixing. One *pṛkte*, *saṃpṛktaḥ*. In the *rudhādi* class (VII, 25), it is *pṛṇakti*. According to Kauśika, it is *pṛci*: one *pṛṅkte*. (20)
The roots beginning with *ṣūṅ* and ending with *ūrṇuñ* are nine that take the augment *iṭ* (*seṭ*).

*Ṣūṅ* [is used] in the sense of "the release of the fetus from living beings. From here onwards, up to *ūrṇuñ*, there are nine roots that take the augment *iṭ*. In *sūte*, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied by the rule *svaratisūtisūyatidhūjūdito vā* (VII. 2. 44): [thus we have] *sotā* or *savitā*. In *suṣuve*, there is no *guṇa* substitution because of the rule *bhūsuvos tiṅi* (VII. 3. 88): [thus we have] *suvāvahai*. In *suṣāvayiṣati*, the change to *ṣ* occurs by the rule *stautiṇyor eva ṣaṇi* (VIII. 3. 61).

By the rule *su-vinir-dur-bhyaḥ supi-sū-ti* (Pāṇini VIII.3.88), we have *suṣūtiḥ*; by *rāja-sūya-sūrya-* (III.1.114), *rājasūyaḥ* is correct. From the root *sū*, we have *sūtaḥ* and *sūtakam*, with the suffix *kan* added after a word ending in the abstract suffix *ktā* (III.3.114). Regarding the form *sūtakā*, it should be stated that [the feminine suffix] optionally applies to *sūtakā*, *putrakā*, and *vṛndāraka* (cf. VII.3.45, 10); thus we have both *sūtakā* and *sūtikā*. By the rule *su-sū-dhā-gṛdhibhyaḥ kran* (Uṇādi II.24), we have *sūraḥ* meaning "the sun"; by *suvaḥ kit* (Uṇādi III.35), we have *sūnuḥ*; and by *krin* (cf. Uṇādi...).

(IV, 64): *sūriḥ*. From the *divādi* group, *ṣūṅ* in the sense of "procreation of living beings" (I, 24): *prasūyate*; from the *tudādi* group, *ṣū* in the sense of "impelling" (VI, 115): *suvati* (21). *Śīṅ* in the sense of "sleeping": *śete*. Regarding the rule "the object of *adhi-śī*, *adhi-sthā*, and *adhi-ās*" (I, 4, 46): *grāmam adhiśete*. Regarding the rule "*ruṭ* after *śīṅ*" (VII, 1, 6): *śerate*. Regarding the rule "guṇa for *śīṅ* before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix" and "the substitution of *ayaṅ* for *śī* before a *yi*-ending *kṅit* suffix" (VII, 4, 21–22): *śayyate*. [The rule] "the locus of the action of *śī*" (III, 4, 45)... [omission from *ac* to *vasā*]. Piṅgala.

(II 106 2, 15): *khaśayaḥ* ("lying in the sky"); by [the rule] *pārśvādibhyaḥ karaṇe* (cf. III, 2, 15, 1): *pārśvaśayaḥ* ("lying on one's side"); the suffix *kta* is applied by [the rule] *gatyarthākarmaka-* (III, 4, 72), and by [the rule] *niṣṭ̣hā śīṅsvidi-* (I, 2, 19) there is no *kit*-status: *śayitaḥ*; from the statement that *āluc* should be prescribed (cf. III, 2, 158, 1): *śayāluli*; by [the rule] *vrate* (III, 2, 80) the suffix *ṇini*: *sthaṇḍilaśāyī*; by [the rule] *er ac* (III, 3, 56): *saṃśayaḥ*; by [the rule] *vyupayoḥ śeteḥ paryāye ghañ* (III, 3, 39): [the word *viśayaḥ* and *upaśayaḥ*].

Today, [the word] *rājopaśāya* is derived from the root *śī* with the suffix *kyap* according to Pāṇini III.3.99 (*samaja* etc.), meaning "lying down" or "bed. From the roots *bhṛ*, *mṛ*, and *śī*, the suffix *u* is applied (Uṇādi I.7), resulting in *śayu*, meaning a python. From the root *śīṅ*, the suffixes *dhuk*, *lan*, *valan*, *valan*, and *vālana* are applied (cf. Uṇādi IV.38), yielding *śīdhu* (liquor), *śīla* (character/habit), *śaivala* (moss), and *śeva*.

From the roots *lā* and *śevāla*, and from *vṛṅśī*, the suffix *asun* is applied [to form words denoting] form and body parts respectively; furthermore, the augment *puṭ* is added (*Uṇ.* IV.200). Thus, *śepas* means the male organ (*liṅga*). From *śīṅ*, the suffix *asun* is applied with the *kittva* marker and a short vowel (*Uṇ.* V.24): *śikhā*, *śikhara*, and *śekhara*. *Śākhā*, however, is derived from *śākhati* (*DhP.* I.130). From *ānaka* and *śīṅbhī*, the suffix *an* is applied (*Uṇ.* III.82): *śayānaka*. That in which they rest is *niśītha* (*Uṇ.* II.9). From *iṇ* and *śī*, the suffix *van* is applied (*Uṇ.* I.152): *śeva* means happiness (*sukha*) (22).

The root *yu* is used in the sense of "mixing. From *yauti*, [we derive] *yavitā* by [Pāṇini] VII.3.89: "There is vṛddhi for *u* when there is elision (*luk*) before a consonant. By [Pāṇini] VII.2.49: "In the *san* [desiderative] suffix, after roots ending in *i*, *u*, or *ṛ*, and after *vṛt*, etc., there is optionally *iṭ*," we have *yuyūṣati* and *yiyaviṣati*. By [Pāṇini] III.1.126: "*āsuyuvapī*," the suffix *ṇyat* applies: *yāvyam*. By [Pāṇini] III.3.57: "*ṝdor ap*," we have *yavaḥ*. With the suffix *aṇ* in its own sense (*svārthe*), we have *yāvaḥ*. With the suffix *kan* (V.4.29), *yāvakaḥ* means "lac. By [Pāṇini] III.3.23: "*sami yududruvaḥ*," the suffix *ghañ* applies.

*Saṃyāvaḥ* is a food mixed with molasses (*guḍa*). Regarding the suffixes *ud*, *śri*, *yauti*, *pū*, and *dru*: from *yu*, by [Pāṇini III.3.49], we have *udyāvaḥ*. From *yu* in the sense of "to rejoice" etc., by [Pāṇini III.1.134], the suffix *lyu* gives *yavanaḥ*. By [Uṇādi I.156] *kanin yuvṛṣi*, the suffix *kanin* gives *yuvā*. By [Uṇādi II.12] *tithapṛṣṭha*, we have *yūthaḥ*. By [Uṇādi III.27] *kusuyubhyo dīrghaś ca*, we have *yūpaḥ*. By [Uṇādi III.47] *ajiyudhūnībhyo dīrghaś ca*, we have *yūkā*. By [Uṇādi III.81] *sṛyuvacibhyo 'nyujāgūjaknucaḥ*, [we have... *Saṃyāvaḥ* is a food mixed with molasses (*guḍa*). Regarding the suffixes *ud*, *śri*, *yauti*, *pū*, and *dru*: from *yu*, by [Pāṇini III.3.49], we have *udyāvaḥ*. From *yu* in the sense of "to rejoice" etc., by [Pāṇini III.1.134], the suffix *lyu* gives *yavanaḥ*. By [Uṇādi I.156] *kanin yuvṛṣi*, the suffix *kanin* gives *yuvā*. By [Uṇādi II.12] *tithapṛṣṭha*, we have *yūthaḥ*. By [Uṇādi III.27] *kusuyubhyo dīrghaś ca*, we have *yūpaḥ*. By [Uṇādi III.47] *ajiyudhūnībhyo dīrghaś ca*, we have *yūkā*. By [Uṇādi III.81] *sṛyuvacibhyo 'nyujāgūjaknucaḥ*, [we have...]

From the root *yu*, the suffix *asac* is applied according to *vahiyubhyāṃ ca* (Uṇ. III, 119): *yavasaḥ* means fodder; from *vahi-śrī-dru-* (Uṇ. IV, 51) comes the suffix *ni*: *yoniḥ*; from *pūṅ-yvoḥ lopaś ca* comes the suffix *ūṣan*: *yūṣaḥ* (broth); from the Vedic root *yuṣ* comes *yoṣā* (Uṇ. III, 62); from *hṛ-sṛ-ruhi-* (Uṇ. I, 99) comes *yoṣit*; *yavāsaḥ* is *durālabhā* (according to Uṇ. IV, 2); *yūtiḥ* is formed by *ūti-yūti-jūti-* (Pāṇini III, 3, 97). Some maintain that the root *yu* means "to mix," based on such observations as "a collection (*saṃgha*) of things that are not established separately."
In the *kry-ādi* group, *yuñ* means "to bind" (*I* IX, 9): *yunakti*; in the *cur-ādi* group, *yu* means "to feel aversion" (*X* 170): *yāvayate*, *yāvyaḥ* (23).

The root *ru* means "to sound. From *rauti*: by *turustuśamyamaḥ sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini III.1.75), there is optionally *īṭ* before an affix beginning with a consonant: *ravīti*, *ravitā*. By *sani grahaguhoś ca* (Pāṇini VII.2.12), *iṇ* is not applied: *rurūṣati*. By *ṝdor ap* (Pāṇini III.3.57), the suffix *ap* is added: *ravaḥ*. By *upasarge ruvo ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.22), the suffix *ghañ* is added: *saṃrāvaḥ*. By *vibhāṣāṅi rupluvoḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.50), there is an option: *āravaḥ*, *ārāvaḥ*. In the *bhvādi* class, *ruṅ* (I.1008) means "motion" and "desire": *ravate*. 1. A confection of jaggery and wheat. 2. Cf. Hemacandra, *Uṇādisūtra* 541.107.2.

From the roots *ru* and *śāti*, the suffix *krun* is applied (cf. Uṇ. IV, 103): *ruru* is a deer; from *ac*, the suffix *iḥ* (Uṇ. IV, 138): *ravi*; with the suffix *asun* (Uṇ. IV, 188): *Purūravas* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 231); "he cries on the earth" (VI, 3, 109 Kāś.): *mayūra*. The root *ṇu* means "to praise. From it: *nauti*, *praṇavitā*. With the prefix *āṅ*, the suffix *taṅ* is applied according to I, 3, 21, 6: *ānute*; *nunūṣati*. *navaḥ*, *praṇavaḥ*. According to "there is *guṇa* [vṛddhi] for *nud* and *daṃś*" (cf. Uṇ. I, 156), there is *nava* (26).

The root *kṣu* is used in the sense of "sound. One sneezes (*kṣauti*). [The derivatives are: *kṣavathuḥ*, *kṣavitā*, *kṣavaḥ*, and *kṣutam*. By the rule *vau kṣuśruvo ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.25), the suffix *ghañ* is applied: *vikṣāvaḥ* (by rule 27). The root *kṣṇu* is used in the sense of "sharpening. One sharpens a weapon (*kṣṇauti*). By the rule *samaḥ kṣṇuvaḥ* (Pāṇini I.3.65), the suffix *taṅ* (ātmanepada) is applied: *saṃkṣṇute*. [The desiderative form is] *cukṣṇūṣati* (by rule 28).

Listen: in the case of *sru* (to flow), by the rule *snu-s-nukramor anātmanepadanimitta* (Pāṇini VII.2.36), the augment *iṭ* is applied [in the future tense]: *prasnavitā*. In the desiderative: *susnūṣati*. Regarding the rule *na duhasnunamāṃ yak-ciṇau* (Pāṇini III.1.89): "The cow flows (*prasnute*) of its own accord"; [in the aorist] *prāsnoṣṭa*. By the rule *snu-vraśca* (Uṇādi III.66), the suffix *sa* is added as a *kit*: *snuṣā* (daughter-in-law). (29)

The root *ūrṇu* is used in the sense of "covering. According to *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VII.3.90), there is optionally *vṛddhi* before a *pit* suffix beginning with a consonant in the *sārvadhātuka* category; otherwise, there is *guṇa*. Thus: *prorṇauti* or *prorṇoti*. According to *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā* (VII.2.6), there is *vṛddhi* in the aorist: *praurṇāvīt* or *praurṇavīt*. By *guṇo 'pṛkte* (VII.3.91), there is *guṇa* in the imperfect: *praurṇot*. According to *sanīvantardha* (VII.2.49), there is optionally *iṭ*: *prorṇunaviṣati*, *prorṇunuviṣati*, or *prorṇunūṣati*. According to *sūcisūtri* (III.1.22, Kāśikā), the suffix *yaṅ* is applied: [prorṇonūyate].

*prorṇonūyate*. By the rule *vibhāṣorṇoḥ* (Pāṇini I.2.3), there is optionally the status of being *kittva*: *prorṇuvitavyam* or *prorṇavitavyam*. From the root *ūrṇoti*, [the suffix] *ḍaḥ* (Uṇādi V.47) yields *ūrṇā*. By the rule *ūrṇoter nulopaś ca* (Uṇādi I.31), [the suffix] *kuḥ* yields *ūruḥ*. By the rule *mahati hrasvaś ca* (Uṇādi I.32), [the same suffix] yields *uruḥ*. (30) The roots beginning with *dyu* "to go" and ending with *mā* (53) are twenty-three and are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*). *dyauti*; *dyotā*. *dyauḥ*. (31)

The root *sū* is used in the senses of procreation and sovereignty. From the roots *sū*, *su*, *dhū*, and others, the suffix *iṭ* is added before *sic* when followed by parasmaipada endings (Pāṇini VII.2.72): *asāvīt*; *sutaḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I.988), it is *savati*, *savitā*; in the *Svādi* class (V.1), it is *sunoti*. Furthermore, according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* III.26 (*kusuyubhyaś ca*), the word *sūpaḥ* is formed. (32)

The root *ku* is used in the sense of "sound. From *kau-ti*, we have *kotā*; from *kū-paḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I, 999), there is *kuṅ*: *kavate*. In the *Tudādi* class (VI, 108), there is *ku* in the sense of sound (*śabda*): *kuvati*. Even when the meaning is "sound" (*śabdatva*), among these [roots], *kauti* refers to sound in general, *kuvati* to a cry of distress (*ārtasvara*), and *kavati* to indistinct sound. (33) 1. From the roots *ru* and *śat*, [the suffix] *KC* is applied in the sense of covering (*chādane*). 2. See Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 867. 3. All manuscripts read thus, but see rather VI, 115. 4. All manuscripts read thus. 5. All manuscripts read thus. II, 108.

The root *ṣṭu* (*ṣṭu ñ*) is used in the sense of praising (*stuti*). In the forms *stauti*, *abhiṣṭauti*, *stotā*, and *prastotā*, the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs according to Pāṇini 8.3.65 (*upasargāt sunoti...*). In *tuṣṭotha*, the augment *iṭ* does not apply because of Pāṇini 7.2.13 (*kṛsṛbhṛ...*). In *paryaṣṭaut* and *paryastaut*, the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs according to Pāṇini 8.3.71 (*sivādīnāṃ vāḍvyavāye ’pi*). In *tuṣṭūṣati*, the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs in the reduplicated syllable before the suffix *san* according to Pāṇini 8.3.61 (*stautiṇyor eva ṣaṇy abhyāsāt*). In *pariṣṭauti*, the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs according to Pāṇini 8.3.70 (*parinivibhyaḥ seva*).

From the rule *etistuśāsv* (Pāṇini III, 1, 109), the suffix *kyap* is applied: *stutyaḥ*. From *ap* (III, 3, 57): *stavaḥ*. From *pre drustusruvaḥ* (III, 3, 27), the suffix *ghañ*: *prastāvaḥ*. From *yajñi sami stuvaḥ* (III, 3, 31): *saṃstāvaḥ*; elsewhere, it is *saṃstavaḥ*. From *bhrājabhāsa* (III, 2, 177), the suffix *kvip*: *grāvastut*. Regarding the instrument (*karaṇa*), the suffix *ktin* is desired (III, 3, 95, 3): *stutiḥ*. From *dāmnī* (III, 2, 182), the suffix *ṣṭran*: *stotram*. [From *artistusv* (Uṇādi)].

The word *man* means "praise" (*stoma*). From the root *ṣṭ̣ubh*, meaning "to support" or "to fix," comes *stobha*; it is a liturgical utterance (*śrauta*) that is meaningless [in itself] but serves to fill out the Vedic recitation. (34)

The root *brūñ* is used in the sense of "articulate speech. According to Pāṇini VI.1.93, *īṭ* is added after *bruva*: *bravīti*. Regarding the passive (*yak*) and the *ciṇ* suffix in the case of the reflexive object (*karmakartṛ*), the Vārttika on III.1.89 states: "An addition [should be made] for *ṇi*, *śranthi*, *granthi*, *brūñ*, and roots that are intransitive when used in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*). Thus, *yak* and *ciṇ* do not occur here: *brūte kathā svayam eva* ("the story tells itself"), *avocat*. According to Pāṇini III.4.84, *āh* replaces the five initial forms of *bruva*: *āha*, *āhuḥ*. By the rule I.1.56, there is a prohibition of *īṭ* after *āhi* and *bhū*: *āha*. Furthermore, by VIII.2.35, *tha* is substituted [for *t*] after *āha*.

Regarding the rule *āttha*, *bruvo vaciḥ* (Pāṇini II.4.53), [the form] *vaktā* is derived from the root *vac*. Regarding the rule *bhavyageya* (Pāṇini III.4.68), which prescribes the agentive suffix: *pravacanīyaś caitro ’nuvākasya* ("Caitra is one who should recite a section"). Because of the indicative mark (*liṅga*) in *celaḍbruvaḥ* (Pāṇini VI.3.43), the suffix *ka* is applied: *brāhmaṇabruvaḥ* ("one who merely calls himself a Brahmin"). Regarding the rule *kvasuś ca* (Pāṇini III.2.107), [we have] *ūcivān* ("he has spoken"). And because of the inclusion of the root *vac* in the rule *upeyivān anāśvān anūcānaś ca* (Pāṇini III.2.109), [the forms] *upeyivān*, *anāśvān*, and *anūcānaḥ* are established. (35)

The root *iṇ* means "to go. In *eti*, there is *vṛddhi* by the rule *etyedhatyūṭhsu* (Pāṇini VI.1.89): *upaiti*. In *itaḥ*, [the same applies]. In *yanti*, *yaṇ* replaces [the final *i*] of *iṇ* by *iṇo yaṇ* (VI.4.81). In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), there is lengthening of *iṇ* before a *kit* suffix by *dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti* (VII.4.69): *īyuḥ*. In *etā*, [the same applies]. In the optative (*liṅ*) of *eti*, there is shortening after a prefix by *upasargād dhrasvaḥ* (VII.4.24): *samiyāt*. In the aorist (*luṅ*) of *iṇ*, *gā* is substituted by *iṇo gā luṅi* (II.4.45). By the rule *gātisthā* (II.4.77), the *sij* suffix is elided (*luk*). Because of the inclusion of both *iṇ* and *pibati* within the mention of *gā-pau* (see II.4.77, 1), [the substitution applies].

*agāt*, *aguḥ*. Regarding the rule *ṇau gamir abodhane* (Pāṇini I.2.15): *gamayati*; in the sense of "making known," *pratyāyayati*. Regarding the rule *sani ca* (Pāṇini I.2.16): *jigamiṣati*; in the sense of "making known": *arthān pratīṣiṣati*. Regarding the rule *upeyivān anāśvān* (Pāṇini III.2.109): *upeyivān*. Regarding the rule *eti-stu-śāsv-* (Pāṇini III.1.109): the suffix *kyap* [is applied], resulting in *ityaḥ*. Regarding the rule *śyād-vyadha-* (Pāṇini III.1.141): the suffix *ṇaḥ* [is applied], resulting in *atyāyaḥ*. Regarding the rule *iṇ-naś-jī-* (Pāṇini III.2.163): the suffix *kvarap* [is applied], resulting in *itvaraḥ*. Regarding the rule *er ac* (Pāṇini III.3.56): [the suffix *ac* is applied].

*Ñuṇ*: *jarāyuḥ*; *duuṇo lopaś ca* (Uṇ. II, 20): *dūram*; *eter ṇic ca* (Uṇ. I, 119): *āyuṣ*; *iṇsidīṅuṣyavibhyo nak* (cf. Uṇ. III, 2): *inaḥ*; *iṇbhīkā* (Uṇ. III, 43): *ekaḥ*; *hasimṛgriṇvā* (Uṇ. III, 86): *etant* (variant: *etaḥ*); *varṇaḥ*; *iṇaḥ kid* (Uṇ. III, 153): *ibhaḥ*; *adhyāyanyāyodyāva* (Pāṇini III, 3, 122): *nyāyaḥ*; *iṇa āgasi* (Uṇ. [III, 157]).

From the root *i* with the suffix *asu*, there is also the augment *nuṭ*: *enas* (1). From *as* with the suffix *asu* (Uṇ. IV.188): *ayaḥ* means "iron" or "weapon. From *iṇ* with the suffix *āgan* (referring to Uṇ. IV.211): *āgas* means "offense. From *rak* (referring to Uṇ. II.28): *irā*. From *samīṇ* (Uṇ. II.11) with the suffix *thak*: *samithaḥ* means "conjunction. From *sānasivarṇasi* (Uṇ. IV.107) with the suffix *ilvala*: *asuraḥ*. From *kuvaś caḍ dīrghaś ca* and *samīṇa* (Uṇ. IV.91–92): *samīcaḥ* means "the ocean. From *eti* with the suffixes *e-ṇ-au*: *mṛgaḥ* (36).

The root *iṅ* means "to study. Its connection with the prefix *adhi-* is obligatory; as someone has said, one follows that [usage]. Thus: *adhīte*, *adhīyate*. By the rule *akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.25), there is lengthening; and by *gāṅ liṭi* (Pāṇini 2.4.49), the substitute *gāṅ* is used in the perfect tense: *adhijage vedam*. By *vibhāṣā luṅlṛṅoḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.50), *gāṅ* is optionally used in the aorist and conditional. By *gāṅkuṭādibhyo ’ñṇin ṅit* (Pāṇini 1.2.1), it acquires the property of being *ṅit*; and by *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisām hali* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), there is the substitution of *i* for the vowel.

*adhyagīṣṭa*, *adhyaiṣṭa*; *adhyagīṣyata*, *adhyaiṣyata*. By the rule *iṅaś ca* (Pāṇini II.4.48), the root *gam* is substituted for *iṅ* when the suffix *san* follows; by the rule *ajjhanagamāṃ sani* (VI.4.16), there is lengthening: *adhijigāṃsate*. By the rule *krīṅjīnāṃ ṇau* (VI.1.48), there is substitution of *ā* [for the final vowel] before the causative suffix *ṇic*: *adhyāpayati*. By the rule *budhayudha* (I.3.86), the *ātmanepada* endings are used; and by the rule *ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (II.4.51): *adhijigāpayiṣati*, *adhyāpipayiṣati*; *adhyajīgapat*, *adhyāpipat*.

In the case of the roots *iṅ* and *dhṛ*, the suffix *śatṛ* is applied when there is no difficulty (*akṛcchriṇi*) [Pāṇini III.2.130]: "one who is studying the *pārāyaṇa*" (*adhīyan pārāyaṇam*). From the root *iṅ*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied by [the rule] *iṅaś ca* (III.3.21), resulting in *upādhyāyaḥ*. When used in the sense of the ablative (*apādāne*), the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* may optionally be added (cf. III.3.21.1), yielding *upādhyāyī* or *upādhyāyā*. The word *adhyāyaḥ* is correctly formed by [the rule] *adhyāyanyāyodyāva* (III.3.122). (37)

The root *i* is used in the sense of remembering (*smaraṇa*). The letter *k* is for the purpose of qualifying it as having the meaning of *adhi-i* (Pāṇini II.3.52). From the mother he has learned (*adhyaiḥ*), because of the extended application (*atideśa*) that "the *ik* [roots] behave like *i*" (Pāṇini I.4.45, vārttika 1); likewise: *adhyagāt*, *adhiyanti*, *adhigamayati*, *adhijigamiṣati*; and *adhītya* (38).

The root *vi* is used in the senses of going (*gati*), procreation (*prajana*), beauty (*kānti*), throwing (*asana*), and eating (*khādane*). *Prajana* means the first conception of a fetus. Regarding *asana*, some say it means "throwing" (*kṣepa*), while others say it means "pervasion" (*vyāpti*). As for the form *veti*: in the sense of procreation (*prajane*), there is optionally an *ā*-substitution in the causative (*ṇau*) according to Pāṇini VI.1.55: *purovāto gāḥ pravāpayati* or *pravāyayati* ("the east wind causes the cows to conceive"). From the roots *vī* and *pati*, the suffix *tanan* is applied (Uṇādi III.150): *vetanam* ("wages"). From the root *vī* with the suffix *asac* and the augment *tuṭ* (cf. Uṇādi III.118), we have *vetasaḥ* ("cane"). From the suffix *asun* (Uṇādi IV.188), we have *vayas* ("age"). From the roots *vīj*, *yaj*, and *jvar*, the suffix *ni* is applied (Uṇādi...).

(IV, 48): From the roots *veṇi*, *guhṛ*, *vīpac*, and *vac* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 166), the suffix *tran* [is applied]: *vetra*. 1. See I, 767; 2. P adds *gaur*, *bhūḥ*, *vāk*; 3. cf. Hem. Uṇ. 182. •^ All manuscripts read thus; H 110.

By the rule *ajivṛrībhyo nic ca* (Uṇ. III, 38), the suffix *ṇu* is applied: *veṇuḥ*. [In the sense of] "having discarded" (*vīta*) what is worthless, such as elephants and horses, the suffix *ktic* (Pāṇ. III, 3, 174) is applied: *vītiḥ* means "a horse. (39)

The root *yā* is used in the sense of "going. By the rule *ner gada* (Pāṇini VIII.4.17), there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*: *praṇiyāti*. By the rule *āc chīnadyor num* (VII.1.80), the augment *num* is optionally added: *yāti* or *yāntī*. By the rule *laṅaḥ śākaṭāyanasyaiva* (III.4.111), the suffix *jhi* is optionally replaced by *jus* in the imperfect (*laṅ*): *ayān* or *ayuḥ*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (VII.2.73), the suffix *suk* is added and the augment *iṭ* is applied: *ayāsīt*. By the rule *yaś ca yaṅo* (III.2.176), the suffix *varac* is added: *yāyāvaraḥ*. By the rule *yo dve ca* (Uṇādi I.22), the word *yayus* means "horse. [The rule] *kamimanijani* (Uṇādi... [is also applied].

The particle *tu* [is used] as follows: from the root *yā*, by [the rule] *huyāmā* (Uṇ. IV, 167), we have *yātrā*; by [the rule] *gamyādau* (III, 3, 3), *yāyī*; and by *mṛgayvādayaś ca* (Uṇ. I, 38), *mṛgayuḥ* is correctly formed; and by *artistusv* (Uṇ. I, 139), we have *yāmaḥ*. (40)

The root *vā* is used in the senses of "going" and "blowing. From *vāti*, by rule VIII.4.17 (*ner gadā*), there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*: *praṇivāti*. [Present tense forms: *vāti*, *vānti*. For the sense of "shaking," the suffix *juk* is added by rule VII.3.38: *pakṣakenopavājayati*. However, *vījayati* is a common (laukika) verbal root [not listed in the Dhātupāṭha]. [The word] *nirvāṇaḥ* is correct when not referring to wind, according to rule VIII.2.50; but when referring to wind, *nirvātaḥ* means "the wind has ceased," i.e., it has gone. [The word] *vāmaḥ* is derived from the *uṇādi* rule I.139 (*artistusv...*) with the suffix *man*. [The word] *vāyuḥ* is derived from the *uṇādi* rule I.1 (*kṛvāpāji...*) with the suffix *uṇ*. [The word] *vātaḥ* is derived from the *uṇādi* rule III.86 (*hasimṛgriṇvā...*) with the suffix *tan*. (41)

The root *bhā* means "to shine. It forms *bhāti*. From the rule *dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ* (Uṇ. III.32), we have *bhānuḥ*. From the rule *cintipūji* (III.3.105), because of the letter *ca*, we have *bhānam* and *bhā*. *Bhās* comes from the root *bhās* (I.655). By the rule *na bhābhūpūkami* (VIII.4.34), we have *prabhānam* and *prabhā* (III.3.106). Because it is listed among the words beginning with *sarva* (I.1.27), [the form] *bhavatu* (42) [is established].

The root *ṣṇā* is used in the sense of cleansing (*śauce*). One says *snāti*, *niṣṇāti*. By the rule *glā-snā-vanuvamāṃ ca* (Pāṇini I.868), there is the designation *mit*: *prasnapayati*. Or, by the rule *anupasargād vā* (I.867): *snāpayati* or *snapayati*. By the rule *ninadībhyāṃ snāteḥ kauśale* (VIII.3.89), there is the substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*]: *niṣṇātaḥ*, *nadīṣṇaḥ*. By the rule *ghañ-arthe kaḥ* (III.3.58.4): *prasnaḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class, *ṣṇai* is used in the sense of binding (*veṣṭane*) (I.970): *snāyati*. By the rule *snā-madi* (Uṇādi IV.112), the suffix *vanip* is applied: *snāvā*, *snāyuḥ* (43).

The root *śrā* is used in the sense of cooking (*pāka*). Regarding the form *śrāti*, they say it is used in the reflexive-passive construction (*karmakartari*) where "it cooks by itself. According to Pāṇini I.3.71 (*ṇāu mit*), one forms *śrapayati*. *Śrāṇā* refers to barley gruel (*yavāgū*); *śṛtam* is used in the sense of cooking, as prescribed by Pāṇini VI.1.27 and the Bhāṣya for milk and sacrificial oblations (*kṣīra-haviṣoḥ*), which is a specific grammatical substitution (*nipātana*) for both the causative and non-causative forms.

The root *drā* means "to go in a contemptible manner" (*kutsitāyāṃ gatau*). A contemptible movement is fleeing, as well as sleep (*nidrā*). One says *drāti*. By Pāṇini VIII.4.17 (*ner gada*), there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*: *praṇidrāti*. From the rule III.2.158 (*spṛhigṛhipati...*), the suffix *āluc* is applied: *nidrāluḥ* ("sleepy") and *nidrāṇaḥ* ("asleep"). In the *Bhvādi* class, *drai* means "to sleep" (I.955): *drāyati*. (45)
P adds *gandhanam* and *mardanam*.
*ṣā* in the sense of eating (*bhakṣaṇe*). *praṇipsāti* (Aṣṭādhyāyī VIII. 4. 17); by [the rule] *ṣvanukṣan* (Uṇādi-sūtra I. 158), *viśvapsāgniḥ* is formed. (46)

The root *pā* means "to protect. From *pāti*, by the rule *pater lug* (Pāṇini VI.1.37, 2), the suffix *ṇiC* is applied: *pālayati*. By the rule *naptṛneṣṭṛ* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.96), [from *pitṛ*] we have *pitā*; by *rak* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra II.28), *vipraḥ*. With the suffix *asun*, from *pāti* comes *thak* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra IV.203): *pāthaḥ* means water; by *pānīviṣibhyaḥ paḥ* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.23), *pāpam*. By *iṇbhīkāpā* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.43), *kan*: *pākaḥ* means a child; by *pāter ḍatiḥ* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.57), *patiḥ*. By *nabhrāṇnapād* (Pāṇini VI.3.75), *napāt*; by *pāter ḍumsun* (Uṇādi-sūtra...).

(IV, 177): *pumān* ("man"); (III, 2, 3; 1, 136): *nṛpaḥ* ("king"), *adhipaḥ* ("lord"); from the root *pā* with the suffix *man* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 150), *pāpmā* ("sin"); from *ṣṭran* (Uṇ. IV, 158), *pātram* ("vessel"); from *manin* (Uṇ. IV, 144), *pāmā* ("scabies"). In the *Bhvādi* class: *pā* in the sense of drinking (I, 972), *pibati*; *pai* and *ovai* in the sense of drying (I, 968–969), *pāyati*. (47) *rā* in the sense of giving. *rāti*. From the root *rā*, by [the rule] *rāter ḍaiḥ* (Uṇ. II, 66), *rā* means wealth; with the suffix *kan* (cf. Uṇ. III, 40), *rākā* means the full moon day; from the roots *rā* and *śad*, with the suffix *trin* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 67), *rātriḥ* ("night"). (48)

The root *lā* means "to take. In the sense of "smearing" (*snehavipāṭana*), after the roots *lī* and *lā*, the augment *nuk* or *luk* is optionally applied before the causative suffix (*ṇau*) (cf. Pāṇini VII.3.39): *ghṛtaṃ vilālayati* or *vilāpayati* ("he causes the ghee to melt"). By the rule *āto ’nupasarge kaḥ* (III.2.3), the suffix *ka* is added: [the word *vilāya* is formed]. The root *dāp* means "to cut" (*lavane*). The letter *p* is for the purpose of including it in the group *dā-dhā-ghu-adāp* (I.1.20). [Examples: *kṣetraṃ dāti* ("he cuts the field"), *vrīhayaḥ dāyante* ("the rice grains are being cut"), *dātā* ("one who cuts"). By the rule *dāmnī-śas-yu-yuja-stu-tuda-si-sica-miha-pata-daśā-ha-āt-ṣṭran* (III.2.182), the suffix *ṣṭran* is added: *dātram* ("a sickle").

The root *khyā* means "to expand" (*prathane*). [Examples: *ākhyāti*, *khyātā*. By the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo ’ṅ* (Pāṇini III.1.52), [the aorist] is *ākhyat*. By the rule *na dhyākhyā* (VIII.2.57), the substitution of *ṇatva* for the *t* does not occur: *khyātaḥ*. By the rule *samāne khyaś ca* (Uṇādi IV.136), [we derive] *sakhā* (51). The root *prā* means "to fill" (*pūraṇe*). [Examples: *prāti*; by the rule *kte* (VIII.2.43), [we derive] *prāṇaḥ* (52).

Do not [apply] *māna*. *Māna* is the act of measuring. It is measured (*māti*) in a vessel; it measures out (*praṇimāti*); *mātī* and *māntī*. There is no substitution of *i* by rule VI.4.66 (*ghumāsthā...*), because the term *pām* is used everywhere [in that rule] to refer to the root with the *alug*-suffix (*pā-√mā*), excluding the form with the *ṇatva* suffix: *māyate*. With the desiderative suffix (*san*), by rule VII.4.54 (*mīmā...*), there is the substitution of *i* for the vowel: *mitsati*. From the roots *hu*, *yā*, *mā*, *śru*, *vas*, and *bhas*, the suffix *tran* is applied (cf. Uṇ. IV.167): *mātrā*. By Uṇ. IV.227 (*candre mo ḍit*), *mo* is added: *candramāḥ*. By rule VII.4.40 (*dyatisyatimā...*), there is the substitution of *i*: *mitaḥ*. *maḥ saḥ*.

*māsaḥ*, *māpaḥ*, *rur* and *ī* [are derived from the root *mā*] (cf. Uṇ. IV.101): *Meruḥ*; *mā-chā-sa-si-sū-bhyaḥ yaḥ* (Uṇ. IV.109): *māyā*; *ṛj-rendra-* (Uṇ. II.28): *mālā*. (53) 1. K: *viśvapsā agniḥ*. 2. P adds: "However, this derivation [of *tanūnapāt*] from the root *pat* is more appropriate: *Tanūnapāt* (Pāṇini VI.2.140 G.). 3. KC: *°vipādane*. 4. P: *bahulam*. 5. P: "Thus, for the sake of the *piṭ* augment. 6. So KC; P: *prakathane*. 7. All manuscripts: *khyātaḥ*. ³ Cf. Hemacandra, Uṇādisūtra 564; II.112.

anudāttāḥ 51. *vaca* in the sense of speaking (*bhāṣaṇe*). It is anudātta and udāttet. *vakti*, *vaktā*. By the rule *vacisvapi* (VI.1.15), there is *saṃprasāraṇa*: *uvāca*, *uktam*. By the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo ’ṅ* (III.1.52), [the suffix *aṅ* is applied]. By the rule *vaco ’śabdasaṃjñāyām* (VII.3.67), [the substitution of *um* occurs]: *avocat*. By the rule *bhavyageya* (III.4.68), [the suffix *anīyar*] is used in the sense of the agent: *Caitraḥ pravacanīyo ’nuvākasya* ("Caitra is one who is to recite a section"). By the rule *yajayācaruca* (VII.3.66), there is no *kutva* [substitution of *v* for *y*]: *pravācyam*. By the rule *vaco ’śabdasaṃjñāyām* (VII.3.67): [the substitution of *um* occurs].

The word *vācya* is derived from the root *vac*. Regarding the word *vākya*: it is formed with the suffix *ghañ* or *anaḥ*; alternatively, according to *ślokavacaḥ pacādau* (Pāṇini III.1.134) and *kṛke vacaḥ kaś ca* (Uṇādi I.6), the suffix *ñuṇ* is applied to form *kṛkavākuḥ*, meaning "cock. From *pātṝtudivaci* (Uṇādi II.7), the suffix *thak* is applied to form *uktham*, meaning "Sāman hymn. From *gudhṛvīpacivaci* (Uṇādi IV.166), the suffix *tran* is applied to form *vaktram*, meaning "mouth. From *kvib vaci* (Uṇādi II.57), the vowel is lengthened to form *vāk*. With the suffix *asun* (Uṇādi IV.188), one forms *vacas*. According to *puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.118), the suffix *gha* is applied to form *vakaḥ*, meaning "heron."

It is not accepted that [the root] *vac* means "to speak," because it is not so stated. In the *cur*-class (*curādi*, X, 298), one says *vācayati*. According to the *Pārāyaṇikas*, this [root] *vid* in the sense of "knowing" is not recited [in that class]. From here on, four [roots] are *seṭ* (having the augment *iṭ*) and take the *parasmaipada* endings. From the root *vid*: *vetti*, *vittaḥ*, *vidanti*. By the rule *vido laṭo vā* (III, 4, 83), the *ṇal* and other substitutes may optionally apply: *veda*, *vidatuḥ*, *viduḥ*. By the rule *daś ca* (VIII, 2, 75), the *d* may optionally become *r*: *aveḥ* or *avet*. By the rule *samo gami* (I, 3, 29), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *saṃvitte*. By the rule *vetter vibhāṣā* (VII, 1, 7), the augment *ruṭ* is added: *saṃvidrate budhāḥ* or *saṃvidate*.

Regarding *rudavidamuṣa* (Pāṇini I.2.8), the suffixes *saN* and *ktvā* are optionally *kit*: *vividiṣati*, *vivediṣati*; *viditvā*, *veditvā*. Regarding *uṣavidajāgur anyatarasyām* (cf. III.1.38), the suffix *ām* is optional: *vidāṃcakāra*. It is stated in the Kāśikā on III.1.38 that there is no *guṇa* substitution for *vid* when *ām* follows: *viveda*. Regarding *sijabhyastavidibhyaś ca* (III.4.109), the *jus* replaces *jhi*: *aviduḥ*. Regarding *vidāṃkurvantv ity anyatarasyām* (III.1.41), in the alternative case [the form] is *vidantu*.

From the root *vid* preceded by the prefix *ni*, the suffix *śa* is applied according to Pāṇini III.1.138 (*ṇāv anupasargāl limpavinda*), resulting in *vedayaḥ*. From the same root with no prefix, the suffix *kvip* is applied according to Pāṇini III.2.61 (*satsūdviṣa*), resulting in *vedavit*. With the suffix *kta* (Pāṇini I.1.26), it becomes *viditaḥ*. According to Pāṇini III.2.162 (*vidibhidichideḥ kurac*), we have *viduraḥ*. According to Pāṇini III.2.169 (*vindur icchur*), *vinduḥ* means "one who knows" (*vidvān*). However, from the root *bidi* meaning "to divide" (Dhātupāṭha I.65), the word *binduḥ* is derived.

*Jalakaṇaḥ*: beginning with a labial (*oṣṭhyādi*). In the sense of a technical name (*saṃjñā*), [the suffix] *kyap* is applied by Pāṇini III.3.99 (*samaja-*): *vidyā*. By Pāṇini III.3.107 (*ghaṭṭivandividibhyo yuc*), [the suffix] *yuc* is applied: *vedanā*. In the sense of the object (*karman*), [the suffix] *ṇamul* is applied to the roots *dṛś* and *vid* when there is totality (*sākalya*) by Pāṇini III.4.29: *brāhmaṇavedaṃ bhojayati* (“he feeds the Brahmins, making them see [the food] all”). After the root *vid*, [the suffix] *śatṛ* optionally becomes *vasu* by Pāṇini VII.1.36: *vidvān* / *vidan*. By Pāṇini VII.2.68 (*vibhāṣā gamahana-*), the augment *iṭ* is optional: *vividvān* / *vividivān*. By Uṇādi IV.118 (*hṛpiśiruhi-*), [the suffix] *in* is applied: *vediḥ*. By Pāṇini III.3.121 (*halas ca*), [the suffix] *ghañ* is applied in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*).
1. [The root] *paribhāṣ* in the sense of reviling; 2. all manuscripts [read thus]; 3. see I, 767; 4. an error, for according to I, 2, 8, only the forms without guṇa are established.

Regarding the word *veda*: according to Pāṇini VI.3.75 (*nabhrāṇnapāt*), the negative particle *na* is not elided, resulting in *na-vedaḥ*. From the root *as* (Uṇādi IV.226), we have *sarva-vedaḥ*, referring to one who performs a sacrifice where his entire property is given as the sacrificial fee (*sarvasva-dakṣiṇa-kratu-yājī*). The root *vid* appears in several groups: 1. In the *divādi* group (IV.62), meaning "to exist": *vidyate*. 2. In the *tudādi* group (VI.138), meaning "to obtain": *vindati*. 3. In the *rudhādi* group (VII.13), meaning "to discern" (*vicāraṇe*): *vinte* and *vinatti*. 4. In the *curādi* group (X.168), meaning "cognition," "narration," and "dispute" (*cetana-ākhyāna-vivādeṣu*), it takes the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffixes: *vedayate*. (55)

*As* means "on earth. *Bhū* means existence (*bhavanaṃ bhūḥ*, *sattā*). [The root *as* becomes] *staḥ*, *santi* by [the rule] *asti-śnasor allopaḥ* (Pāṇini VI.4.111). [In the case of the suffix *san*: *san*. [By the rule] *upasargaprādurbhyām astir yacparaḥ* (VIII.3.87), there is the substitution of *ṣ*: *abhiṣyāt*, *abhiṣanti*, *prāduḥṣyāt*, *prāduḥṣanti*. But not here: *abhistaḥ*. [By the rule] *tāsastyor lopaḥ* (VII.4.50): *tvam asi*. [In the case of the root *as* with the prefix *vyati*: *vyatise*. [By the rule] *ri ca* (VII.4.51): *vyatire*. [By the rule] *ha eti* (VII.4.52), there is the substitution of *ha* for *s*: [e.g., *vyatihe*].

*vyatihe*, *ghvasor ed dhāv abhyāsalopaś ca* (VI, 4, 119): *edhi*; *astisico 'pṛkta* (VII, 3, 96) provides the augment *iṭ*: *āsīt*; *aster bhūḥ* (II, 4, 52); *gātisthā* (II, 4, 77) causes the elision of *sij*; by *āhibhuvor īṭpratiṣedhaḥ* (I, 1, 56, Vārttika 21), there is a prohibition of *īṭ*; by *bhūsuvos tiṅi* (VII, 3, 88), there is an absence of *guṇa*: *abhūt*. However, in the case of subsequent application (*anuprayoga*), *bhū* does not supersede *as* (II, 4, 52, Kāśikā): *kārayāmāsa*. By *kṛbhvastiyoge cviḥ* (V, 4, 50): *śuklīsyāt* (56).

The root *mṛj* means "to clean. By the rule *vraścabhrasja* (Pāṇini VIII.2.36), the letter *ṣ* is substituted [for the final *j*]; by the rule *mṛjer vṛddhiḥ* (VII.2.114), there is *vṛddhi*: *mārṣṭi*. When a suffix beginning with a vowel follows *mṛj*, there is optionally *vṛddhi* in the case of *saṃkrama* (the substitution of *ṛ* for *r*): *parimṛjanti* or *parimārjanti*. Because it is marked with the indicatory letter *ū* (in *mṛj ū*), there is optionally *iṭ* (by VII.2.44): *mārṣṭā* or *mārjitā*. [The past passive participle] is *mṛṣṭaḥ*. By the rule *mṛjer vibhāṣā* (III.1.113), there is optionally the suffix *kyap*: *parimṛjyaḥ* or *parimārgyaḥ*. By the rule *tundaśokayoḥ parimṛjāpanudoḥ* (III.2.5), the suffix *ka* is applied: [forming *parimṛjaḥ* and *apanudaḥ*].

From *mṛj* with the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III, 3, 18–19), we have *mārgaḥ* (“path”). From the same root in the *bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III, 3, 104), we have *mṛjā* (“cleansing”). From *kañji-* and *mṛji-* with the suffix *ciṅ* (Uṇādi III, 137), we have *mārjāraḥ* (“cat”) and *mārjālaḥ*. From *mṛj* with the suffix *kalac* and the elision of the *ṭi* (Uṇādi I, 109), we have *malaḥ* (“dirt”). In the *curādi* class (*mṛjūṣ* in the sense of “cleansing” and “adornment,” X, 304), we have *mārjayati*, *mārjanā*, and *mārjitaḥ*; furthermore, *mārjitā* is a conventional term for the plant *rasālā* (see Amarakośa II, 9, 44). (57)

The root *rud* is used in the sense of shedding tears. By the rule *rudādibhyaḥ sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini VII.2.76), the augment *iṭ* is applied: *roditi*. By the rule *aṅi rudaś ca pañcabhyaḥ* (VII.3.98), the augment *iṭ* is applied: *arodīt*. By the rule *aḍ gārgyagālavayoḥ* (VII.3.99), the augment *aṭ* is optionally applied: *arodat*. Regarding the forms *rudyāt* and *rudet*, the suffix *yāsuṭ* (III.4.103) and the suffix *aṅ* (III.1.57, by the rule *irito vā*) supersede the augments *iṭ* and *aṭ* through the principle of priority (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*).

*arudat*, *arodīt*: although the prohibition [of *iṭ*] by rule I.2.26 (*ralo vyupadhāt*) would have applied, rule I.2.8 (*rudavidamuṣaḥ*) states that for the roots *rud*, *vid*, and *muṣ*, both the suffix *saN* and *ktvā* are optionally *kit*. Thus: *rurudiṣati*, *rurodiṣati*; *ruditvā*, *roditvā*. By rule Uṇ. II.22 (*roder ṇiluk ca*), the suffix *rak* is added: *Rudraḥ*. (58) Those [roots] with an acute accent on the first syllable are udāttetah. 56 1 All manuscripts. 2 Cf. Mādh. II p. 90. 3 S. II, 55 n. 1. 11 114.

*ñiṣvapa* means "to sleep. It is *anudātta* when it is *udāttet*. [Present tense: *svapiti*; [perfect tense: *suṣvāpa*. By the rule *suvinirdurbhyaḥ* (VIII. 3. 88), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs: *suṣupyate*. By the rule *vacisvapi-* (VI. 1. 15), there is *saṃprasāraṇa*: *suṣupuḥ*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *asvapīt* or *asvapat*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *asvāpsīt*. By the rule *rudavidamuṣagrahi-* (I. 2. 8), [the desiderative form] is *suṣupsati*. [The gerund: *suptvā*. In the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) of the root *svap*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* by the rule *svāpeś caṅi* (VI. 1. 18).

*asūṣupat*, according to *svapisyamivyeñāṃ yaṅi* (VI.1.19): *soṣupyate*. According to *svapo nan* (III.3.91): *svapnaḥ*; according to *ñitaḥ ktaḥ* (III.2.187): *suptaḥ*; according to *svapitṛṣor najiṅ* (III.2.172): *svapnakaḥ* (59).

*Śvas* [is used] in the sense of breathing. Breathing is life. From here up to *vaṣṭi* (Dhp. 1.1059), twelve [roots] are *seṭ*. [He] breathes: *śvasiti*; [in the imperfect: *aśvasīt*, *aśvasat*. In the *luṅ* [tense], there is optionally a *vṛddhi* [substitution] for a light vowel following *a* after a consonant-initial suffix (Pāṇini VII.2.7): *aśvasīt*, *aśvāsīt*. By [the rule] *śyādvyadha...* (Pāṇini III.1.141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied: *śvāsaḥ*. The followers of Kāśakṛtsna state that this root is *aniṭ* in the *niṣṭhā* [suffixes] (cf. Kāśikā on Pāṇini VII.2.16): *āśvastaḥ*, *viśvastaḥ*. By [the rule] *calanaśabdārthād...* (Pāṇini III.2.148), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *śvasanaḥ*.

And here: from the root *cā* (DhP. I.476) in the sense of breathing, preceded by *pra*: *prāṇiti*, *prāṇīt*, *prāṇat*. By [Pāṇini] VIII.4.19, there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* [in *an*]; by VIII.4.20, it becomes *prāṇ*. By VIII.4.21, both [the radical and the reduplicated syllable] become *ṇ* when the suffix *san* follows: *prāṇiṇiṣati*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.10 (*kṝ-vṝ-jṝ-si*), the suffix *na* is applied: *annam* (food). By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.188 (*asun*), *anaḥ* (a cart). By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.111 (*aghnay-ādiṣu*), another form [is derived]: *anyaḥ* (another; cf. Uṇādi IV.109). By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.17 (*ani-dṛśibhyāṃ cit*), *anīkam* (army/front). [The words] *prāṇa* and others are formed with the suffix *ghañ* [by Pāṇini III.3.18–19]. (61)

The root *jakṣ* means "to eat" and "to laugh. [Present indicative: *jakṣiti*, *jakṣati*; [imperfect: *ajakṣīt*, *ajakṣat*. The six roots beginning with *jakṣ* (Pāṇini VI.1.6) are designated as *abhyasta* (repeated). Because of the rule *nābhyastāc chatuḥ* (VII.1.78), the augment *num* is not applied: *jakṣat*. By the rule *vā napuṃsakasya* (VII.1.79), it is optionally so for the neuter: *jakṣati* or *jakṣanti* kulāni ("the families eat"). [Imperfect third person plural: By the rule *sijabhyasta* (III.4.109), *jus* is substituted for *jhi*: *ajakṣuḥ*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rules III.1.43–44, [the form is] *ajakṣiṣuḥ*. (62)

The five roots beginning with *rud* have been stated; they are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*) and take the augment *iṭ*. *Jāgṛ*, meaning "to wake from sleep," is also *seṭ*. Examples: *jāgarti*, *jāgrataḥ*, *jāgrati* (the wise ones wake).

When *r i ṅ* [is expected] by rule VII.4.28, the *guṇa* [substitution] applies by rule VII.3.85 (*jāgro ’viciṇṇalṅitsu*), resulting in *jāgaryate*. By rule III.1.38 (*uṣavidajāgṛbhyo ’nyatarasyām*), the suffix *ām* is optionally applied: *jāgarāṃcakāra* or *jajāgāra*. By rule VII.1.91 (*ṇal uttamo vā*), the final *ṇal* is optionally treated as having a *ṇit* marker: *jajāgāra* or *jajāgara*. By rule VII.2.5 (*hmyantakṣaṇa*), the *vṛddhi* substitution does not apply: *ajāgarīt*. According to the Vārttika on III.3.101, the vowel *a* may optionally replace the root *jāgarti*: [resulting in *jāgāra*].

*jāgarā*, *jāgaryā*, *jāgurūkaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.165): *jāgarūkaḥ*; *jṝ-śṝ-stṝ-jāgṛ-bhyaḥ kvin* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.54): *jāgṛviḥ*. (63) 1 [so all manuscripts] 2 [s. jedoeh VII.2.5 und I.763] 3 P because of the word *ca* 4 P °jāgṛbhyo 115 11

*Daridra* means "poor" or "in a miserable state. It is *seṭ*. [In the present tense: *daridrāti*; by *idaridrasya* (Pāṇini VI.4.111): *daridritaḥ*; by *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (VI.4.112), there is elision (*lopa*) of the *ā*: *daridrati*. In the non-*sārvadhātuka* [suffixes], [the *ā* of] *daridrāti* [is elided] (cf. VI.4.114, 1): *daridryate*, *daridrāte*...

According to some, [the root] is *yat* (in the sense of "to beg"); or, according to Pāṇini III.1.134, from *daridrā*, there is *ām* by virtue of III.1.35 Bh.: *daridrāñcakāra*; or *dadaridrau*. From the reduplicated stem (*abhyasta*), the suffix *jhi* becomes *jus*: *adaridruḥ*. In the *luṅ* tense, there is optionally [the augment *iṭ*] by virtue of VI.4.114.3: *adaridrīt* or *adaridrāsīt*. According to VII.2.49 Kāś., there is optionally *iṭ* for *tan*, *pat*, and *daridrā* before the desiderative suffix (*san*).

*didaridrāsati* and *didaridriṣati*; [however], elision is not desired in the causative (*daridrāyaka*) nor in the present participle (*daridrāṇa*). Some say *didaridrāsatīti* or *didaridriṣatīti* (Pāṇini VI.4.114 Bhāṣya). In *daridritaḥ*, because of the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* (VII.2.15), there is no prohibition of *iṭ*. This is because the term *ekācaḥ* (VII.2.10) continues to apply there. From the root *daridrāti*, by the rule *daridrāter yālopaś ca* (Uṇādi I.92), the suffix *ū* is applied: *dardrūḥ* (64), both acutely accented. These two are not acutely accented on the first syllable, because of the traditional teaching that *daridrā* and *jāgṛ* do not take the augment *it* (anittva). 62

The root *cakās* means "to shine. It forms *cakāsti*, *cakāsati*, and *cakāsat*. Because of the rule regarding the inclusion of multi-syllabic roots in the formation of the periphrastic perfect (*ām*), we have *cakāsāṃcakāra*. By the rule *tippy anasteḥ* (Pāṇini VIII.2.73), the *s* is changed to *d*: *acakād bhavān*. By the rule *sipi dhāto rur vā* (Pāṇini VIII.2.74), there is optionally an *r* after the root in the second person singular ending *sip*: *acakāt tvam* or *acakās tvam*. The imperfect is *acakāsīt*, and the future is *cakāsitā*. (65)

The root *śās* means "to instruct. Instruction (*anuśiṣṭi*) is an injunction (*niyoga*). [From the root] *śās*, we have the forms *śāsti*, *śāsati*, and *śāsitā*. By the rules *śāser id aṅhaloḥ* (Pāṇini VI.4.34) and *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (Pāṇini VIII.3.60), the dental *s* is replaced by the retroflex *ṣ*: thus, *śiṣṭaḥ*. By the rule *śā hau* (Pāṇini VI.4.35), [the *ś* is changed to *ṣ*]: *śādhi*. In the case of the suffix *tiP*, by the rule *aster mūrchimidyeditām* (Pāṇini VIII.2.73), the *s* is replaced by *d*: *aśād* bhavān. In the case of the suffix *sip*, by the rule *sipi dhāto rurvā* (Pāṇini VIII.2.74), there is optionally the substitution of *r*: *aśāt* tvam or *aśās* tvam. For the suffix *jhi*, by the rule *jher jus* (Pāṇini III.4.108), there is *jus*: *aśāsuḥ*. And by the rule *sartiśāstyartibhyaś ca* (Pāṇini III.1.56), the suffix *aṅ* is applied.

He taught (*aśiṣat*). According to *nāglopiśāsvṛditām* (Pāṇini VII.4.2), the form is *aśaśāsa*. From the rule *etistuśāsv* (III.1.109), the suffix *kyap* is applied: *śiṣyaḥ* (student). From the rule *tṛntṛcau śaṃsikṣadādibhyaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ cāniṭau* (Uṇādi II.94), the suffixes *tṛn* and *tṛc* are added: *śāstā* (the Teacher, i.e., the Buddha); *praśāstā* (the presiding priest). With the suffix *ktin*, according to *ābādibhyaḥ* (III.3.94, Kāśikā), we have *śiṣṭiḥ* (instruction). In the *uṇādi* list, *śāstiḥ* is formed (IV.179). In common usage (*bhāṣā*), according to *śāsiyudhi* (III.3.130, 1), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *duḥśāsanaḥ* (one who is difficult to govern). By the rule *udito vā* (VII.2.56), the augment *iṭ* is optionally added: *śiṣṭvā* or *śāsitvā* (having taught). *Śiṣṭaḥ* (66). These two are marked with an acute accent on the radical vowel (*udātta*) and are treated as having an acute-accented radical (*udāttet*). 64.

The root *dīdhīṅ* is used in the senses of shining and playing (*devana*). Playing (*devana*) means sporting. [Examples: *ādīdhīte*; by rule VI.4.53 (*yīvarṇayor dīdhīvevyor lopaḥ*), there is elision [of the *ī*]: *ādīdhyate*, *ādīdhitā*. By rule I.1.6 (*dīdhīvevīṭām*), guna and vṛddhi substitutions do not occur: *ādīdhyanaṃ*, *ādīdhyakaḥ*; *dīdhitiḥ*. Because of the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) in rule VII.2.9.1 (*agrahādīnām*), the prohibition of *iṭ* by rule VI.1.2.9 (*titutra...*) does not apply. (67) 1. According to Mādhava, *dadaridrau* occurs; according to Kāśyapa and the Pārāyaṇikas, [it occurs] after *au*. 2. KC reads *tṛṃstṛcau*. 11 III 116.

The root *vevī* is equivalent to *veti*. The root *vī* belongs to the class beginning with "motion" (*gaty-ādi*, DhP I.1.39); when used in a sense equivalent to that, the reading *vetanātulya* is a corruption. *Āvevīte*; the remainder is as before (sūtra 68), and both [roots] are udātta. They are not udāttet because of the traditional rule regarding their being *anit* (sūtra 66). The group beginning with *jakṣ* has been explained, as have the intensives (*prabhava*) and the reduplicated present stems (*abhyasta*). The root *ṣas* means "to sleep. *Sasti*. From *mā-chā-sas-i-sū* comes *ya*: *sasyam*; also *rāsnā-sāsnā* (Uṇ. III.15). Some read *ṣasti* and *sasana*; *saṃsti* (sūtra 69).

The root *vaś* means "to desire" (*kānti*). Desire is longing (*icchā*). [From the root *vaś*: *vaṣṭi*—here, by Pāṇini VI.1.16 (*grahijyāvayi*), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *uṣṭaḥ*, *uśanti*, *uśan*, *uśatī*, *vaśiṣyati*, *vivaśiṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*) suffix, by Pāṇini VI.1.20 (*na vaśaḥ*), there is no vocalization: *vāvaśyate*. From the causative form (*ṇyantāt*), the suffix *lyu* (Pāṇini III.1.134) is applied: *vāśanaḥ*. By the rule "from *vaś*, [the suffix] *īran* with the *kit* designation" (Uṇādi IV.31), we have *uśīram*. By the rule "from *vaś*, [the suffix] *kanas*" (cf. Uṇādi IV.238), we have *Uśanāḥ* and *uśik*. Regarding the application of the *ap* suffix, there is an addition to the rule Pāṇini III.3.58 for the roots *vaś* and *raṇ*: *vaśaḥ*. (70) These are the roots with an acute accent on the first syllable (*udāttā udāttetaḥ*). 69.

And there is the *carkarīta* [formation]. *Carkarīta* is a term for the *parasmaipada* [voice] used by the ancient teachers (*pūrvācārya*) for the elision of *yaṅ*; its purpose is the elision of *śap*. Examples are *vāvadīti* and *narnartti*. (71) Verbs such as *dīdhīṅ* are Vedic; *hnuṅ* means "to conceal" (*apanayana*). It is *anudātta* [accented with a low tone]. "Concealing" (*apanayana*) means denial (*apalāpa*). In the expression *nihnute Caitrāya*, [Caitra] is the recipient (*saṃpradāna*) according to Pāṇini 1.4.34 (*ślāghahnusthāśapām jñīpsyamānaḥ*); thus, he is one who denies (*apahnotṛ*). (72)
Vṛtti. For the sake of the vowels, the first seventy-one roots have been turned [into examples].

In the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on verbal roots composed by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin, son of Bhaṭṭeśvarasvāmin, the section on roots with elided suffixes (*lugvikaraṇa*) belonging to the *adādi* class is completed and finished. Om! [The root] *hu* [is used] in the senses of giving and eating; here, "giving" refers to the casting of oblations (*havis*).

*Ādana* means eating. From this point on, ten roots ending in *ḍudhāñ* are *aniṭ*. By the rule *juhoty-ādy-ahyaḥ śluḥ* (II.4.75), there is *ślu*-elision; by *ślau* (VI.1.10), there is reduplication: *juhoti*, *juhutaḥ*. By *hu-śnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke* (VI.4.87), there is *yaṇ*: *juhvati*. [In the case of the *ad* class: *ad abhyastāt* (VII.1.4). By *bhī-hrī-bhṛ-huvāṃ śluvac ca* (III.1.39), there is optionally the *vām* affix: *juhavāṃcakāra*, *juhāva*. By *hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ* (VI.4.101), *hi* is replaced by *dhi*: *juhudhi*. [The future form is] *hotā*.

By the rule *arci-śuci-hu-sṛpi-chādi-chardi-bhya isiḥ* (Uṇ. II.109), the suffix *isi* is applied: *haviḥ* (oblation). By *artistusvas* (Uṇ. I.139), the suffix *man*: *homaḥ* (offering). By *huyāmā* (Uṇ. IV.167), the suffix *tran*: *hotram* (sacrificial act). According to *dyuti-gami-juhotīnāṃ dve ca* (Pāṇini III.2.178, vārttika 3): *juhūḥ* (the sacrificial ladle). (1) All manuscripts read this. 2 P [Note]: Thus ends the section on roots with elided conjugational markers (*lugvikaraṇa*) belonging to the *adādi* class in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*.
117 III.

The root *bhī* means "to fear. In the expression *caurebhyo bibheti* ("he fears from thieves"), the ablative case is used for the cause of fear according to *bhītrārthānāṃ bhayahetuḥ* (Pāṇini I.4.25). Regarding the forms *bibhitaḥ* and *bibhītaḥ*, the substitution of *i* for *ī* is applied by *bhiyo ’nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini VI.4.115). By the rule *bhīhrī* (Pāṇini III.1.39), the periphrastic perfect forms are *bibhayāṃcakāra* and *bibhāya*. When the fear is caused by a specific agent, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used according to *bhīsmyor hetubhaye* (Pāṇini I.3.68). In this context, the suffix *ṣuk* is added to *bhī* when the fear is caused by an agent, as in *muṇḍo bhīṣayate* ("the shaven-headed man causes fear"). Alternatively, by *bibheter hetubhaye* (Pāṇini VI.1.56), the vowel *ā* may replace the root vowel, resulting in *muṇḍo bhāpayate*. This [substitution] does not apply here: [in cases where there is no external cause of fear].

He frightens him with a key. From the root *bhī* ("to fear"), the suffixes *kruluka* and *na* are applied (Pāṇini III.2.174), yielding *bhīruḥ* and *bhīlukaḥ*. According to the Vārttika on III.2.174, *krukan* is also added, resulting in *bhīrukaḥ*. By the rule *bhiyaḥ ṣuk vā* (Uṇādi I.147), the suffix *mak* is added, giving *Bhīmaḥ* and *Bhīṣmaḥ*. Regarding the formation of words from *bhaya* etc., the Kāśikā on III.3.56 provides the supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyānam*), yielding *bhayam*, *bhītiḥ*, and *bhīḥ*. From the rule *ṛjrendrāgra* (Uṇādi II.28), we have *bhelaḥ* and *abhelaḥ*. From the rule *ānakaḥ śīṅbhiyaḥ* (Uṇādi III.82), we have *bhayānakaḥ*. Finally, by the rule *iṇbhīkā* (Uṇādi III.43), the suffix *kan* is added, yielding *bhekaḥ* (a frog). (2)

The root *hrī* is used in the sense of shame (*lajjā*). From the rule *bhī-hrī-*, we have *jihreti* and *jihriyati*; from *jihrayāṃcakāra* and *jihraya*. By the rule *arti-hrī-vlī-*, the suffix *puK* is added: *hrepayati*. By the rule *nudavidondatrā-*, the substitution of *na* for *ta* is optional: *hrīṇaḥ* or *hrītaḥ*. [The noun] *hrīḥ*. (3)

The root *pṝ* (pṝ1) means "to protect" and "to fill. *Piparti*, *pipūrtaḥ*, *pipurati*. By the rule *artipipartyoś ca* (Pāṇini VII.4.77), the vowel of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) becomes *i*. By the rule *śṝdṝprāṃ hrasvo vā* (Pāṇini VII.4.12), there is optionally a short vowel: *nipapruḥ* or *nipapuruḥ*. By the restrictive rule *krādiniyamāt* (Pāṇini VII.2.13), the augment *iṭ* is added: *papri-va*. Nandī maintains that this root ends in a short vowel: *papariva*. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sye* (Pāṇini VII.2.70), the future form is *pariṣyati*. By the rule *dhāripāri* (Pāṇini III.1.138), the suffix *śa* is applied after the causative (*ṇic*) stem: *pārayaḥ*. The root *pāra* is listed as *pāra tīra* (Dhātupāṭha X.363).

364) Regarding this [root *pṛ*], by Pāṇini’s rule *ṝdor ap* (III, 3, 57), the suffix *ap* follows; by *na dhyākhyā* (VIII, 2, 57), there is no substitution of *ṇatva* for the final letter of the *niṣṭhā* suffix: *pūrtaḥ*, *pūrtiḥ*. Alternatively, from the causative (*ṇyantāt*) form, by *dāntaśānta* (VII, 2, 27), we have *pūrṇaḥ*, *pūritaḥ*. From the root *pūrī* in the sense of "to swell" (IV, 43), however, we derive *pūrṇaḥ*. In the *kryādi* class (IX, 19), the form is *pṛṇāti*; we shall discuss the remaining cases of its inclusion in that very class later (4).

The root *ḍubhṛñ* is used in the senses of "supporting" and "nourishing. By the rule *bhṛñām it* (Pāṇini VII.4.76), the vowel is marked with the *it*-sign: *bibharti*, *bhartā*. From this root, by the rule *ktriḥ* (III.3.88), we have *bhāraḥ*; and by the rule *trer mam nityam* (IV.4.20), we have *bhṛtrimam*. According to the Dramiḍas, who read the root as *ṭubhṛñ*, we have *bharathuḥ* (III.3.89). By the rule *bhīhrī* (III.1.39), the suffixes *vāṃś* and *luṅ* apply, and the root undergoes elision (*ślū*): *bibharāṃcakāra*, *babhāra*; the past passive participle is *bhṛtaḥ*. In the *kryādi* class, the root *bhṝ* is used in the sense of "supporting" (IX.21): *bhṛṇāti*, *bharaḥ*, *bharitā*, *bharītā*.

From *phale-grahi* and *ātmaṃ-bhari* (Pāṇini III.2.26), and by the addition of *kukṣiṃ-bhariḥ* (Kāśikā on III.2.26), and from *saṃjñāyāṃ bhṛt* (III.2.46), we have *viśvaṃbharā*. From *saṃjñāyāṃ samaja-* (III.3.99), we have *bhṛtyā*, *bhṛtiḥ*. Regarding *bhṛño ’saṃjñāyām* (III.1.112): *bhṛtyaḥ*; because it is observed in the masculine when used as a proper name (*saṃjñā*), the form *bhāryā* is not established by that rule (Bhāṣya on III.1.112). *Śṛṅgāra-*...
