1. *pṛ* 2. *om.* 3. *piprati* 4. *pāraḥ* 5. In the *Paddhati*, there is a section on abstract states (*bhāva*) for feminine nouns; by this, the word *bhāryā* is established. 111. 118.
Regarding *bhṛṅgārau ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra III, 136), *bhṛṅgāraḥ* is correct. In the *pacādi* group (III, 1, 134), *jārabharā*. In the *bhvādi* group (I, 946), *bharati* (5).

The root *mā* is used in the senses of measuring (*māne*) and sound (*śabde*). [In the desiderative: *mimīte*; by rule VI.4.76, *bhṛñām it*, the vowel is shortened; [in the benedictive: *māsīṣṭa*—because the suffix has no *k*-marker, the substitution of *ī* does not occur; [in the desiderative with *san*: by rule VII.4.54, *sani mīmā*, one forms *mimīṣati*. In the *adādi* class, *mā* in the sense of measuring (II.53): *māti*. In the *bhvādi* class, *meṅ* in the sense of exchange (*praṇidāne*) (I.1010): *vinimayate*. (6)

The root *ohāṅ* means "to go. According to Pāṇini VI.4.76 (*bhṛñām it*), the vowel becomes short: *jihīte*, *pannāni nābhyujjihate tṛṇāni* ("fallen leaves do not rise up again"), *hāyate grāmaḥ* ("the village declines"). By Pāṇini III.1.148 (*haś ca vrīhikālayoḥ*), the suffix *ṇyuṭ* is applied: *hāyana* refers both to a type of rice and to a year. By Pāṇini VIII.2.45 (*oditaś ca*), the *niṣṭhā* suffix takes the form *na*: *hānaḥ*; and *hātvā*. (7)

The root *ohāk* means "to abandon. The inclusion of the letter *k* [in the root *ohāk*] is for the purpose of preventing the general application of the rule *kakāro haś ca vrihikālayoḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.148); some say it is for the purpose of prohibiting the lengthening of the reduplicated syllable by the rule *akitaḥ* (Pāṇini VII.4.83). From the roots *jahāti* and *jahāteḥ*, the substitution of *i* occurs optionally by the rule *jahāteś ca* (Pāṇini VI.4.116), resulting in *jahitaḥ* or *jahītaḥ*. In the case of the *yaṅluk* (elision of *yaṅ*), the substitution of *i*, *ī*, and *ā* occurs by the rule *ā ca hau* (Pāṇini VI.4.117), resulting in *jahihi*, *jahīhi*, or *jahāhi*. By the rule *lopo yi* (Pāṇini VI.4.118), [the *ā* is elided].

One should abandon [the root *hā*]. By the rule *ghumāsthā* (Pāṇini VI.4.66), there is the substitution of *ī*: *hīyate*. By the rule *er liṅi* (VI.4.67): *heyāt*. By the rule *vātaśunītilaśardheṣv ajadheṭtudajahātibhyaḥ* (III.2.28), there is the suffix *khaś*: *śardhaṃjahā mṛgāḥ* ("deer abandoning the herd"). *Hīnaḥ*. By the rule *glājyāhābhyo niḥ* (III.3.95), there is the suffix *ni*: *hāniḥ*. By the rule *jahāteś ca ktvi* (VII.1.43), there is the substitution of *ī*: *hitvā*. By the rule *nau ha* (Uṇādi 111.44), there is the suffix *kan*: *nihākā* ("a lizard"). By the rule *nañi jahāteḥ* (Uṇādi I.157), there is the suffix *kanin*: *ahaḥ* ("day"). One who abandons what is low (*kalaṃ*) is a *kalahaḥ* ("quarrel"). The suffix *kaḥ* (III.2.3). (8)

The root *dā* (in the form *ḍudāñ*) is used in the sense of giving (*dāne*). In the case of *datte*, by the rule *ner gadanada* (YHI 4, 17), one says *praṇidadāti*. By the rule *nābhyastāc chatur* (VII, 1, 78), the augment *num* does not apply: *dadat*. By the rule *ghumāsthā* (VI, 4, 66), there is the substitution of *ī*: *dīyate*. By the rule *āṅo do 'nāsyaviharaṇe* (I, 3, 20), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *vidyām ādatte*. By the rule *ghvasor ed dhāv abhyāsalopaś ca* (VI, 4, 119), [the forms] *dehi* and *adāt* are derived; in the latter, by the rule *gātisthāghv* (II, 4, 77), the *sij* suffix is elided. By the rule *sthāghvor ic ca* (I, 2, 17), the *sic* suffix is marked with *k* (making it *kit*).

By the rule *aditaḥ sani mīmā* (Pāṇini VII.4.54), the root *dā* takes the augment *iṭ* when followed by the suffix *san*, as in *ditsati*. By *ḍu* (Pāṇini III.3.88), [the suffix *tumun*] is applied to form *dātum*. By *dadāti-dadhātyor vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini III.1.139), the suffix *śa* is optionally applied; in the alternative case, by *śyādvyadha* (Pāṇini III.1.141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied, resulting in *dadaḥ* and *dāyaḥ*. By *pre dājñaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.6), [the suffix *ka* is applied after *pra*], as in *vidyāpradaḥ*. By *do dad ghoḥ* (Pāṇini VII.4.46), *da* is substituted for *dā* before the suffix *kta*, resulting in *dattaḥ*. By *aca upasargāt taḥ* (Pāṇini VII.4.47), *ta* is substituted for *da* after a prefix, resulting in *prattam*. By *dādheṭsi* (Pāṇini III.2.159), the suffix *ru* is applied.

*dāru* [is derived from] *dāna* (giving), by *upasarge ghoḥ kiḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.92): *ādiḥ*; [and] by *āto yuc* (III.3.128): *sudāno gaus tvayā*. *Dāyādaḥ* (heir). The root *ḍudhāñ* means "giving" and "supporting. [Examples: *dhatte*, *praṇidadhāti*, *dadhat*, *dhīyate*, *dhehi*, *adhita*, *adhāt*. By *dadhas tathoś ca* (VIII.2.38), there is the substitution of *it* [for the *s*]. [Note: 1. *ittvaṃ*; 2. *KC praṇidhāne*; 3. *KC parṇāni*; 4. all manuscripts; 5. *P godhikā*; 6. *K ādita*; 7. *dānam* is the accusative, cf. II.3.69; 8. *P dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*].

119. III. *itibhaṣ*: *dhattaḥ*, *dhatsva*. By [Pāṇini III. 1. 129] *pāyya-sāṃnāyya-nikāyya-dhāyyāḥ*, *dhāyyā* refers to a *sāmidhenī* verse. *Dadhaḥ*, *dhāyaḥ*. From the root *dhā*, [by Pāṇini VII. 4. 42] *hi* is substituted: *hitam*. According to the view of Bhāguri, there is elision (*alopa*) [of the penultimate vowel]: *pihitam*, *pidhānam*. By [Pāṇini III. 2. 158] *spṛhigṛhipatidayinidrātandrāśraddhābhya āluc*: *śraddhāluḥ*; here *śrad* functions as a prefix (*upasarga*). In the common language (*bhāṣā*), by [Pāṇini III. 2. 171, vārttika 3] *dhāñ-kṛ-sṛ-bhyaḥ kikinau*: [the suffixes *ki* and *kin* are applied].

*dadhiḥ* [is derived from] *dadhāti* by [the rule] *āto ’nupasarge kaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.3): *godhā*. By *ātaś copasarge kaḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.136): *vidhaḥ*, *vidhā*. *Karkandhūḥ* is a *badarī* (jujube tree) [according to] *Uṇ.* I.95. By *vayasi dhāñaḥ* and *purasi ca* (*Uṇ.* IV.228, 230), the suffix *asi* is applied: *vayodhāḥ* (one who bestows vitality), *purodhāḥ* (a domestic priest). By *vidhāño vedha ca* (*Uṇ.* IV.224): *vedhāḥ* (a creator). By *sitanigami* (*Uṇ.* I.70), the suffix *tun* is applied: *dhātuḥ* (an element). By *dadhāter yan nuṭ ca* (cf. *Uṇ.* V.48): [the form *dhāyanaḥ*].

From the *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.24: *dhānya-* (grain), derived from the roots *su*, *sū*, *dhā*, and *gṛdh* with the suffix *kran*. From *Uṇādi-sūtra* II.81: *kṝpṝvṛjimandi-* etc., with the suffix *kyun*: *nidhana-* (destruction). From [the rule] *ānaka lūśiṅghidhāñbhyaḥ* (cf. *Uṇādi-sūtra* III.83): *dhānaka-* (a coin). From *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.95: *andūdṛnbhv-* etc., [with the suffix *kan*]: *didhiṣṭṛ* refers to an elder brother whose younger sister is unmarried (*jyeṣṭhānūḍhā*). From *Uṇādi-sūtra* [I.106]: *dhāpṝvasyajyatibhyo naḥ*... [the suffix *na*].

(III, 6): *dhānāḥ*; by Uṇādi IV, 111, *sandhyā*; by III, 3, 92 (*upasarge ghoḥ kiḥ*), *sandhiḥ* and *vidhiḥ*; by III, 3, 93 (*karmaṇy adhikaraṇe ca*), *oṣadhiḥ*, *vāladhiḥ*; by III, 3, 104 (*bhidādau*), *śraddhā*; by III, 3, 128 (*āto yuc*), "the burden was easily borne by you" (*sudhānas tvayā bhāraḥ*). In the *divādi* class, by IV, 28, *dhīṅ* [is used] in the sense of a locus: *dhīyate*. (10) Tenth group: the anudātta roots. (10)

*ṇijir* [means] "purification and nourishing. These three [roots] are *aniṭ* and are both active-voice (*ubhayapadin*). By the rule *nijāṃ trayāṇāṃ guṇaḥ ślau* (Pāṇini VII.4.75), there is *guṇa* [substitution] for the three roots beginning with *ṇij*: *nenekti*. By the rule *nābhyastasyāci piti sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini VII.3.87), there is *guṇa* [before an affix beginning with a vowel]: *nenijāni*. [The forms] *anijat* and *anaikṣīt* follow from Pāṇini III.1.57. (11) *vijir* [means] "separation": *vevekti*, *vevijāni*. According to the refined grammarians, *vicir* [is used]: *vevicāni*, *vivecanam*, *vivekaḥ*. (12)

The root *viṣ* means "to pervade. It forms *veveṣṭi* and *aviṣat* (Pāṇini III.1.55). According to some, it takes the augment *iṭ*, as in *avikṣat*. From it are derived *viṣṭvā* and *veṣitvā* (Pāṇini VII.2.56). *Pariveṣaḥ* ("the act of serving food") is formed from *viṣ* with the suffix *ka* when meaning "pervasion" (Pāṇini III.1.135): hence *viṣam* ("poison"). From *viṣ* with the suffix *kin* and the augment *nu* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra III.39): *Viṣṇuḥ*. With the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.18–19): *veṣaḥ* ("costume" or "attire"). (13)

The root *ghṛ* is used in the senses of "flowing" (*kṣaraṇa*) and "shining" (*dīpti*). Flowing means trickling (*sravaṇa*). By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini VI.4.78), the substitution of *i* for the radical vowel occurs: *jigharti*. By [the rule] *man* (Uṇādi I.139): *gharmaḥ* (cf. Uṇādi I.148). By the rule *añjighṛsibhyaḥ ktaḥ* (Uṇādi III.89): *ghṛtam*, *ghṛṇā*. By the rule *ghṛṇipṛśni* (Uṇādi IV.52): *ghṛṇiḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I.985) it is *gharati*; in the *Curādi* class (X.108) it is *ghārayati*. (14) 1. All manuscripts read *dadhi*. 2. P reads *karkandhur*. 3. KC reads *vau dhāño III 120*.

The root *hṛ* is used in the sense of acting with force (*prasahyakaraṇe*) and in the sense of seizing by force (*balānmoṣe*). It appears as *jiharti*. In the *Bhvādi* class, *hṛ ñ* is used in the sense of carrying away (*harati*). The root *ṛ* is used in the sense of going (*gatau*). By the rule *artipipartyoś ca* (Pāṇini VII.4.77), there is the substitution of *i* for the radical vowel: *iyarti*. By the rule *guṇo 'rtisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini VII.4.29), there is *guṇa*: *aryate*. By the rule *sartiśāstyartibhyaś ca* (Pāṇini III.1.56), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *ārat*. By the rule *iḍ attyartivyayatīnām* (Pāṇini VII.2.66), the augment *iṭ* is added: *āritha*. By the rule *smipūṅrañjv* (Pāṇini VII.2.74), the augment *iṭ* is added: *aririṣati*. By the rule *yaṅi ca* (Pāṇini VII.4.30), there is *guṇa*.

*Arāryate*: because of the rule *dīrgho ’kitaḥ* (Pāṇini VI.4.83), there is no lengthening due to the absence of *kit*; *ṛcchati* occurs in the *bhvādi* class (I.983). *Sisarti*: by the rule *sarti-śāsty-artibhyaś ca* (III.1.56), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *asarat*. *Sarati* occurs in the *bhvādi* class (I.982); the various forms derived from it have been stated therein. In the *curādi* class (cf. X.322), *sārayati* [occurs]; *ki* means "to know. *Ciketi*, *cikitaḥ*, *cikyati* (19).

The root *bhas* is used in the senses of "threatening" and "shining. It forms *babhasti*. Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*) [Pāṇini VII.4.78], the substitution of *i* for the radical vowel does not occur here. From the negative prefix *na-* and *bhas*, we derive *nabhaḥ* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra IV.210). *Bhasitaṃ* means "ashes," derived with the suffix *manin* (Uṇādi IV.144). From the roots *hu*, *yā*, *mā*, *aśru*, and *bhas*, the suffix *tran* is applied (Uṇādi IV.167): *bhastrā* (a bellows). From the roots *śṝ*, *dṛ*, and *bhas*, the suffix *adiḥ* is applied (Uṇādi I.129): *bhasad* means "the vulva" (18).

The root *kit* is used in the sense of knowing (*jñāna*). [Examples: *ciketti*, *cikitāni*; *kitavaḥ* (a gambler), or [derived from] "what do you have? (*kiṃ tavāsti*); with the suffix *u*: *ketuḥ* (a banner/sign; cf. *Uṇādi-sūtra* I, 74), *ketanaṃ*. In the *Bhvādi* class, *kita* is used in the sense of dwelling (*nivāsa*) and so forth (I, 1042): *ketati*, *cikitsati*; in the *Curādi* class (X, 345): *ketayati*.
(20) *Tura* is used in the sense of hastening (*tvaraṇa*). [Examples: *tutorti*; *turagaḥ* (a horse), *turitaḥ*.

(21) *Dhiṣ* is used in the sense of sound (*śabda*). [Examples: *didheṣṭi*. *Dhiṣaṇā* (the intellect); or [it is derived] by the suffix *kyuṅ* according to *dhiṣer dhiṣa ca* (*Uṇādi-sūtra* IV, 82); or by *andū* (*Uṇādi-sūtra* I, 95), as in *didhiṣūḥ* (a second husband); or by *sānasivarṇasi* (*Uṇādi-sūtra* IV, 107), as in *dhiṣṇyam*. (22)

In *dhana* and *dhānya*, [the suffix] *ū* is applied by the rule *kṛṣicamitanidhani* (Uṇ. I, 82); thus *dhanū* means a heap (*rāśi*). By the rule *artipṝvapi* (Uṇ. II, 118), [the suffix] *us* is applied; thus *dhanus*. By the suffix *vanip* (cf. Uṇ. I, 156): *dhanvā*. By the suffix *ac* (III, 1, 134): *dhana*. In the *bhvādi* class (I, 481), there is *dhanati* (23).

In *jana* meaning "birth" (*janane*): [they] are born (*jajanti*). By the rule *īḍajanor dhve ca* (VII, 2, 78), the augment *iṭ* is added; thus *janiṣe*. Because this belongs to the Vedic language (*chāndasatvāt*), the doubling [of the root] does not occur. In the *divādi* class (IV, 41), *janī* means "manifestation" (*prādurbhāve*): *jāyate* (24).

The root *gā* is used in the sense of "praising" (*stuti*) and, in the Vedic language (*chandas*), also in the sense of "birth" (*janana*). Furthermore, according to the rule *bhṛñām it, bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini VII.4.76–78), the augment *it* is added: *jigāti*, *jigītaḥ*, *jigati*. In the *Bhvādi* class: *gāṅ* in the sense of "going" (*gati*) [I.998]: *gāte*. *Kai* and *gai* in the sense of "sound" (*śabda*) [I.964–965]: *gāyati*. By the rule *iṇo gā luṅi* (Pāṇini II.4.45), *iṇ* becomes *gā* in the *luṅ* tense: *agāt*. By the rule *iṅo gāṅ liṭi* (Pāṇini II.4.49), *iṅ* becomes *gāṅ* in the *liṭ* tense: *adhijage*. (25) 1. *prasahyaharaṇe* (in the sense of seizing by force); 2. *ārivān*; 3. all manuscripts [read] *iti kittvāt*; 4. *C* reads *sasarti*; 5. see I.767. 121 III IV.

Vṛtti: The twelve roots beginning with *jigharti* are unaccented (*anudātta*) and are Vedic (*cchāndasa*). Thus, in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on the roots composed by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin, the *juhoty-ādi* class, characterized by the *ślu*-suffix, has been completed. (1)

*om!* [The root] *div* is used in the senses of playing (*krīḍā*), desiring victory (*vijigīṣā*), dealing (*vyavahāra*), shining (*dyuti*), praising (*stuti*), and going (*gati*). "Dealing" refers to buying, selling, and so forth. From here up to the end of the section on roots ending in *ṣu* (sūtra 21), twenty-one roots are *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment) and take the *parasmaipada* (active voice). By the rule *divādibhyaḥ śyan* (Pāṇini III.1.69), the suffix *śyan* is applied: *dīvyati*. By *divo 'vijigīṣāyām* (VIII.2.77), the substitution of *v* for *y* occurs: *devitā*. By the rule *divaḥ karma ca* (I.4.43), the word *akṣān* ("dice") becomes the object: *akṣān dīvyati* or *akṣair dīvyati*. By the rule *divas tadarthasya* (II.3.58), the genitive case is employed: *divasa dyūtam*.

He plays for a hundred: by *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini VII.2.49), there is optionally *iṭ*, thus *dudyūṣati*; by *chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca* (VI.4.19), *dideviṣati*. Having played: *dyūtvā* or *devitvā*; by *na ktvā seṭ* (I.2.18), there is an absence of *kit*-treatment. *akṣadyūḥ* (one who plays with dice); *devaḥ* (in the *pacādi* group, III.1.134); *devī*. By *divo 'vijigīṣāyām* (VIII.2.49), there is the substitution of *ṇatva*: *ādyūnaḥ* (one who is gluttonous). In the sense of desiring victory, it is *dyūtam*; [the suffix] *cit* is added after *vṛṣa* and others (Uṇādi I.108).

*Devala*: [from *div*] by *śakādibhyo ’ṭan* (Uṇ. IV, 81): *devaṭaḥ*. From *div*, by *ṛn* (cf. Uṇ. II, 100): *devāḥ*. The younger brother of a husband (*patyuḥ kaniṣṭhaḥ bhrātā*); likewise, by *artikamibhrami* (Uṇ. III, 132): *devaraḥ*. By *kṛvighṛṣvi* (Uṇ. IV, 56): *kikīdiviḥ*, which is the blue jay (*cāṣaḥ*). By *divo dve dīrghaś cābhyāsasya* (Uṇ. IV, 55), with the suffix *kvin*: *dīdiviḥ*, meaning food (*annam*). By *diver ḍiv*: *dyauḥ* (1).

The root *ṣivu* means "to sew" (*tantusaṃtāne*). From it we derive *sīvyati*, *siṣeva*. By the rule *parinivibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini VIII.3.70), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*: [thus we have] *pariṣīvyati*, *niṣīvyati*, *viṣīvyati*. By the rule *sivādīnāṃ vā* (VIII.3.71), there is optionally no substitution: thus *paryasīvyat*. For the future forms *susyūṣati* and *siseviṣati*, the substitution of *ṣ* does not occur because of the restriction in the rule *stautiṇyoḥ* (VIII.3.61). The gerundives are *syūtvā* and *sevitvā*; the past participles are *syūtam* and *sitam*. Regarding the form *paryasīṣivat*, the rule *stanbhusivusahāṃ caṅy upasargāt* (VIII.3.116) applies.

From the rule *sivaḥ kit* (Uṇ. IV.93), the suffix *caṭ* [is applied], yielding *sūcaḥ* (needle) and *sūcī* (needle). From the rule *sivimucyoṣ ṭer ū ca* (Uṇ. IV.162), *sūtram* (thread/sutra) is formed. From the rule *sivuṣṭhivor lyuṭi vā dīrghaḥ* (Candra-S. I.3.98), there is optionally a lengthening of the vowel in the *lyuṭ* suffix, yielding *sīvanam* or *sevanam* (sewing). *Prasevakaḥ* refers to a bag or similar object. (2) The root *srivu* is used in the senses of "motion" and "drying. It forms *srīvyati*. By the rule *jvaratvara* (Pāṇini VI.4.20), the substitution of *ūṭ* occurs: *srūtvā* or *srevitvā* (having dried). (3) The root *ṣṇasu* is used in the sense of "casting out. It forms *snasyati*. Some authorities hold that it is marked with the *mit* designation; thus, the desiderative form is *siṣṇasayiṣati*. The school of Pāṇini (*pāṇinīyāḥ*) holds that *ṣṇusa* is used in the sense of "tormenting. (5)

1. Thus, in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, the *juhotyādi* verbs characterized by the *ślu*-suffixation are completed. 2. *addit*: in the senses of beauty and motion. 3. *devaṭ* (cf. the *pacādi* group and Pāṇini IV.1.15). 4. *ūrṇājīvī* was added by P. 5. Omitted by K and C. 6. = Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 949. 7. *vīṇāṅgam* (a variant for I.864; cf. Mādhava). 8. *adarśana* (IV.122). 9.
*knasu* in the senses of crookedness (*hvaraṇa*) and shining (*dīpti*). *Hvaraṇa* means tortuousness. *Knasyati*. By the rule *caricali* (Pāṇini VI.1.12.6), [the form] *caknasam* is derived. (6)

*pyuṣ* in the sense of division: *pyuṣyati*. (7) *pluṣ* in the sense of burning: *pluṣyati*; having burned (*ploṣitvā*). In the *bhvādi* class (I, 736): *ploṣati*; in the *kryādi* class (IX, 56): *pluṣṇāti*. (8)

The root *nṛt* is used in the sense of "shaking the limbs. Shaking the limbs is acting (*nāṭya*). One dances: *nṛtyati*. Regarding the forms *nartsyati* and *nartiṣyati*, as well as *ninṛtsati* and *ninartiṣati*, the suffix *iṭ* is optionally applied by the rule *se'sici kṛtacṛtachṛdatṛdanṛtaḥ* (Pāṇini VII.2.57). As for the word *nṛtta*, although its lack of the suffix *iṭ* is already established by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* (VII.2.15), the fact that it is marked with the indicator *ī* is for the sake of the form without the *yaṅ* suffix (*yaṅluganta*): *narīnṛttaḥ*. Due to its inclusion in the *kṣubhnādi* group, there is no substitution of *ṇ* for *n* by the rule *kṣubhnādiṣu ca* (VIII.4.39). By the rule *na pādamyāṅyamaḥ* (I.3.89), the *ātmanepada* endings are not used; thus, one causes to dance: *nartayate*. (9)

*tras* means agitation. Agitation is fear. Alternatively, by [Pāṇini III.1.70] *vā bhrāśabhlāśa*, the suffix *śyan* is applied: *trasati* or *trasyati*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by [Pāṇini VI.4.124] *jṝbhramutrasāṃ*, there is the substitution of *e* for the root vowel and the elision of the reduplication: *tresasuḥ* or *tatrasuḥ*. By [Pāṇini III.2.140] *trasigṛdhi*, the suffix *knu* is applied: *trasnuḥ*. (10) *kuth* means becoming putrid. Becoming putrid is a foul odor or moisture. [The verb] *kuthyati*. [The past participles] *kothitvā*, *kuthitam*, *kotlitam*; [the noun] *kothaḥ*. (11) *puth* means injury. [The verb] *puthyati*; [the verbal noun] *pothanam*. (12) [End of section.]

The root *gudh* means "to envelop. It forms *gudhyati*. From *gudh*, [the suffix] *-ūma-* (Uṇ. V. 2) yields *godhūmaḥ* (wheat). In the *Bhidādi* group (III. 3. 104), it forms *godhā* (an iguana). According to *undyami-gudhi* (cf. Uṇ. III. 68), the suffix *-sa-* is kit: *gutsaḥ* (a cluster). In usage, it appears with a final *-ch-*: *gucchaḥ* (a bunch). The root *kṣip* means "to propel. It forms *kṣipyati*. In the imperative, "throw these two stones into the water," there is no *iṭ* augment: *kṣeptā* (one who throws); this is a new form. In the *Tudādi* group (VI. 5), it forms *kṣipate* and *kṣipati* (14). The root *puṣp* means "to blossom. It forms *puṣpyati*. In the *Pacādi* group (III. 1. 134), it forms *puṣpam* (flower). In the *Tārakādi* group (V. 2. 36), it forms *puṣpitaḥ* (blossomed) (15).

*tima*, *tīma*, *ṣṭ̣ima*, *ṣṭ̣īma*: "to become moist. [Present forms: *timyati*, *tīmyati*, *stimyati*, *stīmyati*; [Desiderative forms: *tiṣṭ̣ema*, *tiṣṭ̣īma*. By the rule *iṣitimi* (Uṇ. I.52), the suffix *kirac* is applied: *timiraṃ* ("darkness"). By the rule *ik* (Uṇ. IV.121), [the suffix *ik* is applied]: *timiḥ* ("fish"). *Temanaṃ* means "condiment. *v r ī ḍ a c o d a n e* (Dhātupāṭha 16.17). *Codanaṃ* means "shame. [The verb] *vrīḍyati*. [Past participle: *vrīḍitaḥ*; [noun: *vrīḍā*. By virtue of the rule regarding "excessiveness" (*bāhulakāt*) [Uṇ. X.392], [we have]: *vrīḍād amuṃ devam avīkṣy eti* (18) ("Out of shame, she does not look at this god").

The root *iṣ* means "to go. He seeks (*anviṣyati*). Having sought (*eṣitvā*), [the suffix] is not *kit* because of the rule *na ktvā seṭ* (Pāṇini I.2.18). [Examples: *preṣitaḥ*, *praiṣaḥ*, *praiṣyaḥ*. Regarding the forms *prād ūhoḍhoḍhyeṣaiṣyeṣu* (Pāṇini VI.1.89), see VI.1.12.5 Bh.
2 KC adds: *udvejane*; *udvejanam*. 3 P adds: in the *curādi* group, the root *tras* has the meaning "to hold" (X.201): *trāsayati*. 4 P adds: *pothayāmāsa*. 123 IV.

Thus there is *vṛddhi* [strengthening]. From the root *iṣ* in the sense of "not desiring" (*anicchārtha*), by [Pāṇini] III.3.107.2, the suffix *yuc* is applied: *eṣaṇā*, *anveṣaṇā*; or, by III.3.107.3, from the prefix *pari*: *paryeṣaṇā*. [The word] *parīṣṭiḥ* [is formed with the suffix *ktin*]. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.148, *takan* is added to *iṣ* and *aśi*: *iṣṭakā*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.157, *ksu* is added to *iṣ*: *ikṣuḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class, *eṣṛ* means "to go" (I.649): *anveṣate*. In the *Tudādi* class, *iṣu* means "desire" (VI.59): *icchati*. In the *Kryādi* class, *iṣa* is used in the sense of repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*) (IX.53): *iṣṇāti*. (19)

*ṣuha* is used in the sense of "capability. Capability here means "satisfaction. *suh-yati*, *suṣoha*. "Satisfied with rice" (*odanāya suhitaḥ*). Durga says that *ṣaha* and *ṣuha* mean "to share in" (*saṃbhakti*). *viṣahyati*. These [roots] ending in an udātta vowel are udāttet. *jṝṣ* and *jhṝṣ* mean "loss of vitality. These four [roots] beginning with *itaḥ* take the augment *iṭ*. *jiryati*, *jarā*.

By *vā jṝbhramutrasām* (VI.4.124), there is optionally the substitution of *e* for the root vowel and the elision of the reduplicated syllable: *jajaruḥ* or *jeruḥ*. By *jṝstanbhv* (III.1.58), there is optionally the suffix *vāṅ*: *ajarat* or *ajārīt*. By *vṛto vā* (VII.2.38), there is optionally the lengthening of the augment *iṭ*: *jaritā* or *jarītā*. By *iṭ sani vā* (VII.2.41), there is optionally *iṭ* in the desiderative: *jijīrṣati*, *jijariṣati*, or *jijarīṣati*. By *liṅsicor ātmanepadeṣu* (VII.2.42), *iṭ* is optional in the *ātmanepada* forms of the optative (*liṅ*) and the aorist (*sic*): *jīrṣīṣṭa* or *jariṣīṣṭa*; however, by *na liṅi* (VII.2.39), there is no lengthening in the optative.

*Ajīrṣṭa*, *aja11ṣṭ̣a*, *ajarīṣṭ̣a*. From the root *janījṝṣ* (I, 863), with the suffix *in*: *jarayati*. "The union is ageless" (*ajaryam saṃgatam*, III, 1, 105). From *kumijīryati*: *kuñjaraḥ* (an elephant), by [the rule] *ac* (III, 1, 134). By the rule *gatyarthākarmaka* (III, 4, 72), the suffix *kta* is applied: *anujīrṇo vṛṣalīm Caitraḥ* (Caitra has grown old after the low-caste woman). From the root *jṝ*, by the rule *atṛn* (III, 2, 104): *jaran*, *jaratī*. By the rule *dārajārau kartari ṇiluk ca* (III, 3, 20, 4), the suffix *ghañ* is applied [to form *dāra* and *jāra*].

The word *jāraḥ* [is derived from the root *jṝ*]; by the rule *jṝvraścyoḥ ktvi* (Pāṇini VII.2.55), the augment *iṭ* is applied: *jaritvā*, *jarītvā*; *jarjaraḥ* [is formed] by *yaṅluk* with the suffix *ac* (Pāṇini III.1.134; II.4.74). From the roots *jṝ* and *viśi*, the suffix *jhac* is applied (Uṇādi-sūtra III.126): *jarantaḥ* (an old buffalo). In the *kryādi* class, *jṝ* means "decay of age" (IX.24): *jṛṇāti*. [From *jhṝ*: *jhīryati*, *jharjharaḥ*, *jharaḥ*, *nirjharaḥ*, *jharjharīkaḥ* (22, 23).

The root *ṣūṅ* means "to bring forth living beings. A woman gives birth (*sūyate*). According to [Pāṇini] VI.1.44, there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *sotā*, *savitā*. From this point on, nine roots ending in *vrīṅ* are marked with the indicatory letter *u* (VIII.2.45): *sūnaḥ*, *sūnavān*, *prasūnaṃ* (flower). For this very reason, others maintain that this [root *ṣūṅ*] refers to the bringing forth of non-living things. In the *adādi* class (II.21), there is *sūte*; [the past participle] *sūtaḥ*. In the *tudādi* class (VI.115), *ṣū* means "to impel": *suvati*. *Dūṅ* means "affliction" (*paritāpaḥ*); affliction is distress. [The forms are: *dūyate*, *davītā*, *dūnaḥ*. These are the roots with the acute accent. (25)

*dīṅ* [means] "to fade away. These thirteen roots, ending with *dop*, are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*). From *dīyate*, *dīnaḥ*; by rule VI.4.63 (*dīṅo yuḍ aci kṅiti*), we have *upadidīye*, *upadidīyāte*.

1P says: "It is consistent with the noble ones" (*āryasaṃgatam*). Regarding *jṝ* and *viśi*, according to AutTecht, there is naturally a printing error. 3P says: "They say" (*āhuḥ*). Others [say] IV.124.

By the rule *mīnātiminotidīṅāṃ lyapi ca* (VI.1.50), there is the substitution of *ā* [for the vowel of the root *dī*]: *upadātā*, *upadāya*, and *upadeśa*. Because of this *ā*-substitution, by the rule *śyādvyadha* (III.1.141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied (cf. VI.1.50.1 and the *Bhāṣya*): *upadāyaḥ*. Regarding the rule *sthāghvor ic ca* (VI.4.66), there is a prohibition for the root *dī* (as per I.1.20.6): *upādāsta svaraḥ śikṣakasya*; *upadedīyate*; and *upadidīṣate* is also desired, as is *upadidāsate* (26).

The root *ḍīṅ* means "to fly. From it are derived *ḍiyate* and *ḍīnaḥ*. In the *bhvādi* class (I, 1017), there is *ḍayate* and *ḍayitaḥ*. Some maintain that the reading of *ḍī* here [in the *adādi* class] is for the sake of the *śyan* affix and for the sake of its being marked with the *odit* designation: thus, *ḍīnaḥ*. However, Vyāghrabhūti states that *ḍīṅ* is *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment) without distinction, based on the rule: "In the case of roots ending in *ś*, *ḍīṅ*, and those ending in *i*, as well as *śīṅ* and *śriñ*" (Kārikā 1 on Pāṇini VII, 2, 10). (27) The root *dhīṅ* means "to support. The remainder [of the meaning] is "to rest upon" (*bhuvaṃ dhīyate*). From it is derived *dhīnaḥ*. (28)

The root *mīṅ* is used in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*). From it: *mīyate*, *mīnaḥ*, *mīnavān*; and by [Pāṇini] VI.1.50, *mātā*. With the suffix *san*, by VII.4.54, there is the substitution of *mīm*: *mitsate*. In the *kryādi* class, *mīñ* (IX.4): *mīnāti* (29). The root *rīṅ* is used in the sense of flowing (*sravaṇa*). From it: *rīyate*, *rīṇaḥ*; and by VII.3.36, the augment *puk* is added: *repayati*. From the form ending in *vij*, the suffix *matup* is applied (cf. VI.1.37, 6): *Revatī*. By Uṇādi IV.201, *asun* with the augment *tuṭ* after *srū* and *rī*: *retaḥ*. By Uṇādi III.38, *ṇu* with the augment *nic* after *aj*, *i*, *vṛ*, and *rī*: *reṇuḥ*. In the *kryādi* class, *rī* is used in the sense of movement and seeking (*gati-reṣaṇayoḥ*) (IX.30): *riṇāti* (30).

The root *lī* means "to adhere" (*śleṣaṇe*). [Its forms are: *līyate*, *vililye*, *līnaḥ*. According to the rule *vibhāṣā līyateḥ* (Pāṇini VI.1.51), the substitution of *ā* for *i* is optional: [the futures] *vilātā* or *viletā*; [the conditionals] *vilāsyate* or *vileṣyate*. Regarding the prohibition of the suffixes *khal* and *ac* after the roots *ni*, *mī*, and *lī*, as stated in *nimimīliyāṃ khalacoḥ pratiṣedhaḥ* (Pāṇini VI.1.50.2): [we have] *durlayaḥ*, *nilayaḥ*, *pralayaḥ*, *vilayaḥ*. According to the rule *liyaḥ saṃmānanaśālīnīkaraṇayoś ca* (Pāṇini I.3.70), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: [e.g., *līyate* when meaning "to honor" or "to cause shame"].

[The root] *lī* is used with the suffix *ṇic* in the sense of "causing to adhere" (*ālāpayate*) and "making bashful" (*pralambhana-śālīnīkaraṇa*); in these cases, the substitution of *ā* for *i* is always desired. Regarding the rule *līlor nug lukāv anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini VII.3.39), which concerns the melting of fat (*sneha-vipāṭana*): one says *ghṛtaṃ vilīnayati*. Because of the explicit mention of the long vowel *ī* in the rule, the augment *nuk* is desired only after a form ending in *ī*; thus, it does not apply here: *vilāpayati*, *vilāyayati*. By the rule *śyādvyadha* (Pāṇini III.1.141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied: *vilāyaḥ*.

In the *kry-ādi* class (*I*, IX, 31), [the root] is *līnāti*; in the future tense, *leṣyati*. In the *cur-ādi* class (*X*, 269), *lī* means "to liquefy" (*dravīkaraṇa*); it belongs to the *ādhṛṣīya* group: *vilāpayati*, *vilayati*, and *ullāpayate* (31). *vrīṅ* is used in the sense of "to choose" (*vṛṇoti*). The meaning of "choosing" (*varaṇa*) is the sense of "to choose. [Examples: *vrīyate*, *vrīṇaḥ*. In the *kry-ādi* class (*I*, IX, 33), *vrī* means "to choose": *vrīṇāti* (32). [The roots] beginning with *svād* (24) are marked as *odit*. (32)

*Pīṅ* means "to drink. Even when tormented by intense thirst, one does not drink water found on the road. *Petā* means "measured" (*māṅmāna*), according to Durga; it is derived from the root *mā*, which belongs to the *hvādi* group (III, 6), as in *mimīte*. *Īṅ* means "to go. Everyone understands their own self-interest (*svārtha*). 1. KC reads *°vipādane*.

1.5 The root *prī* is used in the sense of "pleasure. It takes the form *prīyate*. By the rule *ig-upadha-jñā-prī-kiraḥ kaḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.135), the suffix *ka* is applied: *priyaḥ*. In the *kry-ādi* class (IX), the root *prīñ* is used in the senses of "satisfying" and "desire": *prīṇīte*, *prīṇāti*. In the *ādhṛṣīya* group (X), the root *prīñ* is used in the sense of "satisfying": *prīṇayati*, *prayate*, *prayati*. (36)

The root *śo* is used in the sense of "making thin" (*tanūkaraṇe*). In the present tense (*śyani*), there is elision [of the long vowel] according to *otaḥ śyani* (Pāṇini VII.3.71). Regarding the aorist, there is optionally no *luk* elision of the suffix *sic* due to *vibhāṣā ghrādheṭśāchāsa* (II.4.78): *aśāt*, *aśāsīt*. By the rule *śāchor anyatarasyām* (VII.4.41), the substitution of *it* occurs: *niśitam* or *niśātam*. However, in the case of *saṃśitavrataḥ*, the form with *it* is required as a constant rule (VI.4.41, 1). [Other forms include] *śitiḥ* and *śātiḥ*. In the causative (*ṇau*), the augment *yuk* is applied by *śāchāsāhvā* (VII.3.37): *niśāyayati*. By *ātaś copasarge* (III.3.106), the feminine suffix *ā* is added: *niśā*. [The following is from the Uṇādi-sūtra: *śaḥ kit sanvac ca* (Uṇ. III.89).

I.21) *ku-*: *śiśuḥ*. From the rule *śāśapibhyāṃ dadanau* (Uṇ. IV.97): *śādaḥ* means mud. (37) *cho* [in the sense of] cutting (*chedane*). One cuts down (*avacchyati*), one has cut down (*avācchāt*), one has wished to cut down (*avācchāsīt*), one causes to cut down (*avacchāyayati*). *chitaḥ*, *chātaḥ*. By the rule *māchāsasi* (Uṇ. IV.109), the suffix *ya-* is applied: *chāyā*. By the rule *kṛvighṛṣvi* (Uṇ. IV.56), *chaviḥ*. By the rule *chāpūkhaḍibhyo gak* (Uṇ. I.123), *chāgaḥ*; in the sense of a young goat (*chagalaḥ*) and so forth. (38)

The root *ṣo* [belongs to] the *antakarmaṇ* [group]; *antakarma* means destruction (*vināśaḥ*). [In the forms] *syati*, *avasyati*, and *praṇiṣyati* (Pāṇini VIII.4.17), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs by [the rule] *upasargāt* (VIII.3.65). By [the rule] *prāk sitād aḍvyavāye ’pi* (VIII.3.63), [the substitution applies] even when there is an intervention by the augment *aṭ*: *abhyaṣyat*. By [the rule] *vibhāṣā ghrā* (II.4.78), there is optionally the elision (*luk*) of the *sij* suffix: *avāsāt* or *avāsāsīt*. By [the rule] *ghumāsthā* (VI.4.66), there is the substitution of *ī* [for the radical vowel]: *avasīyate*. By [the rule] *śāchā* (VII.3.37), there is the addition of *yuk*: *avasāyayati*. [The suffix] *ṇaḥ* [is applied] by [the rule] III.1.141.

*Avasāyaḥ*: by *dyatisyati* (VII, 4, 40), there is the substitution of *i* [for *a*], resulting in *avasitaḥ*. By *ūtiyūtijūtisāti* (I, 3, 97), *sāti-* is formed; by *sātibhyām* (Uṇ. IV, 152), *manin* is added: *sāmā* [and *sātma*]; the state of being *sātman* is *sātmyam*. (39) The root *do* is used in the sense of "cutting. *Dyati*; by *gātisthā* (II, 4, 77), the *sij* suffix is elided: *avādāt*. *Avadātum*; by *dyatisyati* (VII, 4, 40), there is the substitution of *i* [for *a*]: *nirditam*, *avattam*; by *aca upasargāt taḥ* (VII, 4, 47), *ta-* is substituted. (40) The *ghu*-grahaṇas are the same as the *samāna*s. 38. They are *anudātta*. 38.

The root *jan* is used in the sense of manifestation (*prādurbhāva*). Manifestation means origination (*utpatti*). From here, fourteen roots ending in *śr* are *seṭ* (possessing the augment *iṭ*) and *ātmanepadī* (taking the middle voice). [In the case of the roots *jñā* and *jan*, the substitution of *jā* occurs: *jñā-janor jā* (Pāṇini VI.1.79).

The root *jan* occurs [in the following forms]: by the rule *ye vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VI.4.43), we have *jāyate*, *janyate*, *jājāyate*, *jañjanyate*, and *janitā*. From *janaḥ*; from *abhijāyate* with the sense "by means of this," we derive *abhijanaḥ*. By the rule *īḍajanor dhve ca* (Pāṇini VII.2.78), the augment *iṭ* is applied: *janiṣe*, *janidhve*. By the rule *gamahanajana* (Pāṇini VI.4.98), there is elision of the penultimate vowel: *jajñe*. By the rule *dīpajanabudha* (Pāṇini III.1.61), the suffix *ciṇ* is optionally applied in the sense of the agent: *ajani*, *ajaniṣṭa*. By the rule *janivadhyoś ca* (Pāṇini VII.3.35), the *vṛddhi* strengthening does not occur. By the rule *janikhanasanāṃ sañjhaloḥ* (cf. Pāṇini VI.4.42), there is elision [of the nasal].
1. See Uṇ. I.112 and Hem. Uṇ. 471; P chāgaI aḥ. 2. See Hem. Uṇ. 916. 3. KC omits. 1V 126.

*Jātaḥ*: by [the rule] *janījṝṣ* (Pāṇini I.1.862), it is *mit*; [thus] *janayati*. By [the rule] *bhavyageya* (Pāṇini III.4.68), in the sense of the agent: *caitro janyaḥ*. By [the *uṇādi* suffix] *manin* (Uṇādi IV.144): *janma*. By *janeḥ usiḥ* (Uṇādi II.116): *januḥ*. By *janeḥ aṭharaḥ* (cf. Uṇādi V.38): *jaṭharam*. By *janeḥ ko jaṅgha ca* (cf. Uṇādi V.31): *jaṅghā*. By *janighasibhyām iṇ* (Uṇādi IV.129), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi* by *janivadhyoś ca* (Pāṇini VII.3.35): *janiḥ*. By *dṝsani* (Uṇādi...)*. *(Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly. The translation reflects the grammatical derivations up to that point.)*

I, 3) thus *ñuṇ*: *jānu* (knee); from *phalipāṭ* (Uṇ. I, 19), *jatu* (lac); from *kamimanijanibhyaḥ* (Uṇ. I, 73), *tun*: *jantuḥ* (living being); from *yajimani* (Uṇ. III, 20), *yuc*: *janyaḥ* (kinsman); from *janer yak* (Uṇ. IV, 110): [the suffix *yak*].

From *jan* [the suffix] *raṅ* is applied: *jarat*. From *stan*, *hṛṣ*, *puṣ*, *gad*, *mad*, *ghuṣ*, *gaḍi*, *maṇḍi*, and *jan*, with the elision of *ṇi*, the suffix *itnuc* is applied: *janayitnuḥ*. From *jan*, with the elision of *ṭ*, [the suffix *ṭāp* is applied] (*jaṭā*). And from *jati* and others (*Uṇ.* IV.102), *jatru* is formed. From *andū*, *dṛnbhū*, etc. (*Uṇ.* I.95), *jambūḥ* is formed. From *kṛñ* and others, when used as a proper name (*saṃjñā*), the suffix *vun* is applied (*Uṇ.* V.35).

*Janakaḥ*: [He] is born from this, thus *jananī* (mother); by the rule *upasarge ca saṃjñāyām* (Pāṇini III.2.99), the suffix *ḍaḥ* is applied: *prajā* (offspring). By the rule *anau karmaṇaḥ* (cf. III.2.100): one born after a woman is *stry-anujaḥ*; by the rule *anyeṣv api* (III.2.101): *pūrva-jaḥ* (elder brother). By the rule *gaty-artha-karmaka-* (III.4.72), the suffix *ktaḥ* is applied: one born after a man is *janaḥ* (person); [the suffix] *iṣṇuc* is applied by the rule *alaṃ-kṛñ-* (I.2.136).
*Prajaniṣṇuḥ*: [the suffix] *viṭ* is applied by [Pāṇini Sūtra] I 3 2 67, *janasana*. By [Pāṇini Sūtra] VI 4 41, *viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt*, we have: *abjāḥ*, *gojāḥ*, *ṛtajāḥ*, *adrijāḥ*. (41)

The root *dīp* means "to shine. It forms: *dīpyate*, *dīpitā*, *dīptaḥ*. According to *dīpajanabudha* (III.1.61), the suffix *ciṇ* is optionally applied in the sense of the agent: *adīpi* or *adīpiṣṭa*. According to *bhrajabhāsa* (VII.4.3), the vowel is optionally shortened: *adīdipat* or *adidīpat*. By *sūdadīpadīkṣaś ca* (III.2.153), the suffix *tṛn* is applied (where *yuc* would otherwise have been expected by III.2.149): *dīpitā*. By *namikampismi* (III.2.167), the suffix *raḥ* is applied: *dīpraḥ*. By *ac* (III.1.134), [the suffix *ac* is applied]: *dīpaḥ*, *pradīpaḥ*. (42)

The root *pṛ* is used in the sense of filling (*āpyāyana*). Filling means increase (*vṛddhi*). [From this root we derive] *pūryate*, *pūritā*, *pūrṇaḥ*, and *pūrtiḥ*. According to *dīpajanabudha* (Pāṇini III.1.61), the *ciṇ* affix is optionally applied when the agent is expressed: *apūri* or *apūriṣṭa*. According to *vā dāntaśānta* (Pāṇini VII.2.27), from the causative form (*ṇyantāt*), we have *pūrṇaḥ* or *pūritaḥ*. By the rule *carmodarayoḥ pūreḥ* (Pāṇini III.4.31), the suffix *ṇamul* is added: *carmapūraṃ bhuṅkte* ("he eats until his skin is full"). By the rule *varṣapramāṇe ūlopaś cāsyānyatarasyām* (Pāṇini III.4.32), there is optionally the elision of the vowel *ū*: [e.g., *prasthapūram*].

"The god has rained a cow’s footprint," "the god has rained a cow’s footprint-full. Regarding *ūrdhve śuṣipūrau* (Pāṇini III.4.44): *ūrdhvapūraṃ pūrṇaḥ*. (43) The root *tūr* [is used] in the senses of going, hastening, and injuring; that is, in going, hastening, and injuring. *tūryate*, *tūritā*; *tūṛṇaḥ*, *tūryam*. Durga [says] *tūri* (44). 1. See I.767. 2. All manuscripts read *jānuḥ*. 3. So all manuscripts. 4. Cf. Hemacandra, Uṇādi-sūtra 200. 5. Cf. Hemacandra, Uṇādi-sūtra 797. 6. Pāṇini reads *jatruḥ*. 7. Cf. Hemacandra, Uṇādi-sūtra 27: *Janakaḥ* [the father of Sītā].

127. *Ghūrī* and *jūrī* mean to injure and to go. [From *ghūrī*: *ghūryate*, *ghūritā*; *ghūrṇaḥ*. [From *jūrī*: *jūryate*, *jūritā*; *jūrṇaḥ*. Durga [also lists] *gūrī* (47, 48, 46). *Dhūrī* means to injure and to go. [From *dhūrī*: *dhūryate*, *dhūḥ* (45). *Śūrī* means to injure and to paralyze. [From *śūrī*: *śūryate*, *śūraḥ* (49). *Cūrī* means to burn. [From *cūrī*: *cūryate*, *cūrṇaḥ* (50). *Tapa* means sovereignty. [From *tapa*: *tapyate*. Others, however, [list] *tapa* as "to heat" (*saṃtāpa*) [Dhātupāṭha I, 1034].

Thus, some maintain that for this very root *bhū* and others, the suffixes *śyan* and *taṅ* optionally apply in the senses of sovereignty (*aiśvarya*) and heating (*saṃtāpa*). Because of the mention of "optionally" (*vā*), some hold that they also apply to the sense of sovereignty for *bhū* and others: *pratapati*. [In the section on] *nandī* etc. (Pāṇini III.1.134), there is *tapanaḥ* when it is a proper name (*saṃjñāyām*); [examples are] *dviṣantapaḥ* and *parantapaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.39). The Dramiḍas say *pateti*: [it means] "he is protected" (*patyate*) and "he falls" (*patati*); [the forms are] *apātiṣṭa* and *apaptat* (51).

The root *vṛ* (vāvṛtu) means "to choose" (*varaṇe*). From it, one forms *vāvṛtyate*; thus, Bhaṭṭi [writes] that "turning back, she entered Rāma’s dwelling" (*Bhaṭṭik. I V, 28*). Others hold that this root belongs only to the *bhū*-class (I, 795), or alternatively, they consider it to belong to the *div*-class for the sense of choosing; consequently, the grammatical operations specific to the *dyutādi* class do not apply to the sense of choosing: *avartiṣṭa*, *vartiṣyate*, *vivartiṣate* (52).

The root *kliś* is used in the sense of "to afflict" (*upatāpe*). Its grammatical form is *kliśyate*; however, when it means "being afflicted for the sake of another," it is the object of the definition. In the *kry-ādi* group, *kliśū* is listed as meaning "to torment" (*vibādhane*) [Pāṇini VIII, 2, 50]: *kliśnāti*. Regarding the suffixes *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā*, there is an optional *iṭ* augment according to Pāṇini VII, 2, 50: *kliṣṭvā* or *kliśitvā*. By applying Pāṇini I, 2, 7, the suffix is *kit*: *kliṣṭaḥ* or *kliśitaḥ*. According to Pāṇini III, 2, 146, the suffix *vuñ* is added: *kleśakaḥ*. Furthermore, by the rule *kliśer ī copadhāyāḥ kal lopaś ca lo nām ca* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra V, 56): [the following forms are derived].

*Kīnāśaḥ*: from the root *kliś* with the suffix *al* and the elision of *la* (cf. Uṇ. V, 33); *keśaḥ*; and *kiśora* etc. (Uṇ. I, 66), thus *kiśoraḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class: *kleś* in the sense of "articulate speech" (I, 638): *kleśate* (52a). *Kāśṛ* in the sense of "shining": *kāśyate*, *kāśaḥ*, *acakāśat*. There is lengthening [of the vowel] before *kāśa* according to Pāṇini VI, 3, 123 (*ikaḥ kāśe*): *pratīkāśaḥ*, *saṃkāśaḥ*, *nīkāśaḥ*, *avakāśaḥ*. In the *Uṇādi* section (II, 2): *kāṣṭham*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I, 678): *kāśate* (53).

The root *vāśṛ* means "to sound. It forms *vāśyate*, *vāśitam*, and *avavāśat*. According to some, these two [roots] do not take the augment *ṇi* (*anṛdita*): *acīkaśat*, *avīvaśat*. How then are [the forms] *cākaśīti* and *vāvaśīti* explained? They are due to being different verbal roots (*prakṛtyantara*). From *vāśā* and *vāśikā*; from the causative (*ṇyantāt*) of the group beginning with *nandi* (Pāṇini III.1.134), we have *vāśanaḥ*; and from the rule *mandivāśi* (Uṇādi I.39), we have *urac*: *vāśuraḥ* is a donkey. (54) The roots with raised initials (*udātta*) that have a low-pitched final vowel (*anudātteta*) are fifty-two.

The root *mṛṣ* is used in the sense of "endurance. Five roots from here onwards have the svarita accent; two are *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment), and three are *aniṭ* (not taking the *iṭ* augment). *mṛṣyate*, *mṛṣyati*, *marṣitā*. By the rule *paremṛṣaḥ* (Pāṇini I.3.82), the *parasmaipada* is used: *parimṛṣyati*. By the rule *mṛṣas titikṣāyām* (Pāṇini I.2.20), the *niṣṭhā* suffix does not take the *kit* designation when preceded by *sa*: *marṣitaḥ*. In the common language (*bhāṣā*), according to the *Kāśikā* on Pāṇini III.3.130, [the suffix *kta* is added after the roots *śās*, *yudh*, etc.]... [all manuscripts omit *ca*]... [P adds *sadṛśaḥ*]... [P adds *bhvādau vāśate*]. IV 1⁸.

Thus, with the suffix *yuc*, we have *durmarṣaṇaḥ*; under the rule for the *nandigrahipacādigaṇa* (III.1.134), we have *marṣaṇaḥ*. According to the rule *tṛṣimṛṣikṛśeḥ Kāśyapasya* (I.2.25), the suffix *kta* may optionally be *kit*: hence *marṣitvā* and *mṛṣitvā*. Under the *curādigaṇa* (X.305), from the root *dhṛṣ* onwards, it is optional: *marṣayati* and *marṣati*. In the *tudādigaṇa* (VI.131), *mṛśa* means "touching" (*āmarśana*); the suffix *ktvā* is added, and by the rule *avyāntaḥ* (55), [the form is established].

The root *śucir* (in the sense of) "putrefaction" (*pūtibhāva*). Putrefaction is moisture (*kleda*). [From this root: *śucyate*, *śucyati*; [aorist] *aśucat*, *aśocīt*; [perfect] *aśuciṣṭa*; [past participle] *śuktam*. In the *bhvādigaṇa* (I.198), *śuca* means "sorrow" (*śoka*): *śocati*. In the *bhvādigaṇa* (I.546), *śucyī* means "pressing" (*abhiṣava*): *śucyati* (56).

The roots *udāttau* and *svaritetau* [are treated as follows]: 54. *ṇaha* in the sense of "binding. *nahtyate*, *nahtyati*, *naddhā*. By *naho dhaḥ* (VIII. 2. 34), the *h* of *naha* becomes *dh*. By *nahivṛtivṛṣi...* (VI. 3. 116), there is lengthening before the suffix *kvip*: *upānat* ("shoe"). Bhāguri maintains that there is elision (*allopam*) of the *a* of the prefixes *ava* and *api*: thus *pinahyati*, *apinahyati*. By *ṣṭran* (III. 2. 182): *naddhrī* ("leather thong"). By *ṛnahibhyām uṣac* (cf. Uṇ. IV. 75): *Nahuṣaḥ*. By *naho bha ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV. 125), the suffix *iñ* [is applied]: [the word *nābhi*].
*nābhiḥ*: from the root *nah* with the suffix *div-i-bha* and the augment *cit* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra IV.210), [we derive] *nabhas*. *saṃnāhaḥ*.

The root *rañj* means "to color" (*rāge*). [Derivatives: *rajyate*, *rajyati*, *raṅktā*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.1048), it is *rajati*; the various grammatical forms have been explained there. Its inclusion here is for the sake of its being marked as *svaritet* and for the sake of the *vikaraṇa* suffix. Similarly, *śap* (58): *śap* means "to curse" (*ākrośe*). [Derivatives: *śapyate*, *śapyati*, *śaptā*; [gerund] *śaptvā*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.1049), it is *śapati* (59).

The roots *anudātta* and *svarita* [are listed] as ending in *i*. The root *pad* means "to go" (*gati*). "Going" (*gati*) implies both movement (*yāna*) and knowledge (*jñāna*). From here until the end of the section on *liṭ* (70), these nine roots are optionally without the augment *iṭ* (*an-iṭ*) and are *ātmanepada*. By the rule *ner gada* (Pāṇini VIII.4.17), one says *praṇipadyate*. By the rule *ciṇ te padaḥ* (III.1.60), in the sense of the agent (*kartari*), one has *udapādi bhaikṣam* ("alms were obtained"). The form *prapattā* is derived from the same root. By the rule *sani mīmā* (VII.4.54), one has *pitsate*. By the rule *nīg vañcu* (VII.4.84), one has *panīpadyate*. By the rule *jucaṅkramya* (III.2.150), one has *padanaḥ*. By the rule *laṣapatapada* (III.2.154), one has the suffix *ukañ*.

*Upapādukaḥ*. [In the rule] *pada-ruja-* (Pāṇini III.3.16), the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartari*), resulting in *pādaḥ*. [In the rule] *khala-bhaga-pada-iḥ ca* (cf. III.3.125, Kāśikā—see footnote), the suffix *gha* is applied in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe*), resulting in *padam*. [In the rule] *viśi-pati-padi-* (III.4.56), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied: *gehānuprapādam āste*, meaning "he sits down at every house" (*gehaṃ geham anuprapādam*). [In the rule] *saṃ-pad-ādibhyaḥ* (III.3.108), the suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*), resulting in *saṃpat* and *pratipat*. [In the rule] *saṃ-aja-* (III.3.99), used for naming (*saṃjñāyām*), the suffix *kyap* is applied.

Regarding this very [root], Durga states that *khida* means "dejection" (*dainya*): *khidyate*, *khettā*. Vamana, however, maintains that it is used in the sense of the reflexive-passive (*karmakartari*), as in *khidyate* (cf. *Kāvyālaṃkāravṛtti* V, 2, 7). In the *rudhādi* class (VII, 12), it is *khinte*; in the *tudādi* class (VI, 142), *khida* in the sense of "tormenting" (*paritāpa*) is *khindati*. [The derivatives are] *khedaḥ* and *khinnaḥ* (61).

The root *vid* is used in the sense of "existence" (*sattā*). Existence is being. [From this root we derive: *vidyate*, *vettā*, *vittaḥ*. In the *adādi* class, *vid* means "to know" (I, 55): *vetti*, *veditā*. In the *tudādi* class, *vidl* means "to obtain" (VI, 138): *vindati*. In the *rudhādi* class, *vid* means "to investigate" (VII, 13): *vinte*, *vinatti*. In the *curādi* class, *vid* is used in the sense of "perception" and so forth (X, 168): *vedayate*. (62)

The root *budh* is used in the sense of "understanding. It forms *budhyate* ("he understands") and *boddhā* ("one who understands"). Alternatively, by rule III.1.61 (*dīpajana*), the suffix *ciṇ* is applied: *abodhi* ("the wise man understood") and *abuddha*. By rule I.3.86 (*budhayudha*), it forms *bodhayati* ("he causes to understand"). By rule III.1.135 (*ke*), it forms *budhaḥ* ("wise"). By rule III.2.188 (*matibuddhi*), the suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the present tense: *rājñāṃ buddhaḥ* ("known by kings"). In the *Bhvādi* class, under the meaning "to perceive" (I.924), it forms *bodhati*. (63)

In the sense of *saṃprahāra* (combat). *Saṃprahāra* means striking or killing. [The roots] *yudh* (to fight), *yoddhṛ* (fighter), and *yodhayati* (causes to fight). By the rule *rājani yudhikṛñaḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.95), the suffix *kvanip* is applied: *rājayudhvā* (one who has fought with a king). By the rule *sahē ca* (III.2.96): *sahayudhvā* (one who has fought together). By the rule *ghañarthe kaḥ* (III.3.58.4): *āyudham* (a weapon). By the rule *bhāṣāyāṃ śāsiyudhi* (III.3.130.1), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *suyodhanaḥ* (one who fights well). (64) *anu* [is a prefix] in the sense of desiring (*kāma*). The root *rudh* preceded by *anu* belongs to the *divādi* class and means "to desire": *anurudhyate*. It does not mean this here: *ruṇaddhi* (he obstructs), *rodhayati* (he causes to obstruct). (VII.1) (65)

In the case of *mana* [meaning] "to think," the dative case is used according to Pāṇini II.3.17 (*manyakarmaṇi*). For example: *na tvā tṛṇāya manye* ("I do not consider you as even a blade of grass"). Regarding the form *ehi manye*, Pāṇini VIII.1.46 states that the future tense (*lṛṭ*) is used in jest when *manye* follows; and I.4.106 states that when *manye* is the governing word in a jest, the first person singular is used for the verb *manye*: *ehi manye rathena yāsyasi* ("Come, I think you will go by chariot"), which implies "you will not go" or "your father has already gone. According to Pāṇini III.2.82 and the Kāśikā, the suffix *ṇini* is added to *man* [in the sense of one who thinks well]: *śobhanamānī*. Furthermore, in this context, the word *manas* is treated like a masculine noun (according to VI.3.36).

One considers oneself clever (*paṭvīṃ manyate*); [the suffix] *khac* is applied after *ātma-māna*: *śūramānī*, *śūraṃmanyaḥ*. In the sense of a name, [the suffix] *kyap* is applied by [Pāṇini III.3.99]: *samaja-*; [thus] *manyā* means "the nape of the neck. By [Pāṇini III.2.188], *mati-buddhi-*, the suffix *kta* is applied in the present sense: *rājñāṃ mataḥ* ("esteemed by kings"), *matiḥ*. By [Uṇādi I.11], *śṝ-svṛ-snihi-*, [we have] *Manuḥ*. By [Uṇādi I.73], *kami-mani-*, [we have] *mantuḥ*. By [Uṇādi III.20], *yajimani-*, [we have] *yuc*: *manyuḥ*. By [Uṇādi I.11], *phali-pāṭi-*,...

I. 19) *madhu*: [from the root *mad*] by *maner dīrghaś ca* (Uṇ. III. 64). *māṃsa*: [from the root *man*] by *maner uc ca* (Uṇ. IV. 122). *muni*: [from the root *man*] by *asun* (Uṇ. IV. 188). *manas*. *maṭharo mūḍhaḥ*: [from the roots *mani* and *bhi*] by *vanimanibhyāṃ cid vā* (cf. Uṇ. V. 39). *vittaḥ*: [from the roots *gudh*, *ṛ*, *vī*, *pac*, and *vac*] (cf. Uṇ. IV. 166). Your grandfather. See I. 767. 1Y 130. (Note: The text contains references to various grammatical rules from the *Uṇādisūtra* and citations from other works such as the *Kāśikāvṛtti* [KC] and the *Śabdakalpadruma* [P]. The numbers refer to specific entries or sections.)

Thus ends the mantra. Regarding *tan* and its derivatives: *manu* in the sense of "awakening" (VIII, 9): *manute*; in the *cur*-class (*curādi*), *mana* in the sense of "stopping" (X, 169): *mānayate*, *mānaḥ*. (67) *Yuj* in the sense of "concentration" (*samādhi*). Concentration is the cessation of the fluctuations of the mind (cf. Patañjali, *Yogasūtra* I, 2). [From it derive: *yujyate*, *yoktā*; [according to] *sṛji-yuji-dhūñām* (cf. III, ...).

1.87.15) The treatment as a *karmavadbhāva* and the suffix *śyan*: "The chariot yokes itself" (*yujyate rathaḥ svayam eva*). [In the sense of] "good for a yoke" (*yugye sādhuh*), one has *goyugaḥ* ("one who yokes a cow"). This is derived by adding *aṇ* in the sense of the object (*karman*) according to Pāṇini III.2.1, and it belongs to the *nyaṅkvādi* group (VII.3.53). By the rule *añcuyuji* (III.2.59), the suffix *kvin* is applied; by *yujer asamāse* (VII.1.71), the augment *num* is added; and by *kvinpratyayasya kuḥ* (VIII.2.62), the final consonant is changed to *k*: thus, *yuṅ*, *yuñjau*. But not here: *aśvayuk* ("yoked with horses"). [By adding] *ṣṭran* (III.2.182): [one has *yoktrā*].

*Yoktra*, *man* (cf. Uṇ. I.145): *yugma*, belonging to the *nyaṅkvādi* group (Pāṇ. VII.3.53); and by *ke* (III.1.135): *yuga*, *yojana*, *yojanā*, *yoga*; these are the respective derivations. In the *rudhādi* class, *yujir* in the sense of "joining" (VII.7): *yuṅkte*, *yunakti*; or with *ṇic* from *yuj* and *pṛc* in the sense of "mixing" (*saṃparcana*) in the *curādi* class (X.264, 265): *yojayati*, *yojati* (68).

*Sṛja* [means] "in the act of emitting. In the sense of being emitted (*sṛjyate*), there is the status of being treated like the object (*karmavadbhāva*) and the suffix *śyan* according to Pāṇini III.1.87 and 15: *mālā sṛjyate svayam eva* ("the garland emits itself"). According to VI.1.58, *sṛjidṛśor jhaly am akiti*, the vowel *am* is substituted [for the radical *ṛ*] before a suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant that does not have *kit*: *sraṣṭā* ("the creator"). According to III.1.124 and 1, the suffix *ṇyat* is applied after *sṛj* when preceded by *pāṇi*: *pāṇisargyā rajjuḥ* ("a rope for binding the hands"). Also, according to III.1.124 and 2, when preceded by *samava*: *samavasargyā*. According to III.2.59, *ṛtvigdadhṛg...*, the word *srak* ("garland") is formed; and according to Uṇādi I.16, *sṛjer asum ca*, the word *rajjuḥ* ("rope") is formed. In the *tudādi* class (VI.121), it is *sṛjati*. (69)

*Liś* in the sense of becoming small: *liśyate*, *leṣṭā*, *leśaḥ*. In the *tudādi* class (VI. 127), *liśati*. (70) Those beginning with *anudātta* and ending with *anudāttet* [are listed]. (66) *Rādh* when intransitive is used only in the sense of "prosperity. From here up to *snih* (91), twenty-one roots are *aniṭ* and take the *parasmaipada* endings. From *rādh* (V. 16), when intransitive and signifying prosperity, the suffix *śyan* is applied: *rādhyati*. When transitive and other than in the sense of prosperity, the suffix *śnu* is applied: *rādhnoty odanam*, meaning "he cooks the rice. In the *curādi* class (?), *rādhayati*. (71)

The root *vyadh* means "to pierce. By the rule *grahijyā* (Pāṇini VI.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *vidhyati*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by the rule *abhyāsasya* (VI.1.17), we have *vivyādha* and *vyaddhā*. By the rule *śyādvyadha* (III.1.141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied: *vyādhaḥ*. By the rule *nahivṛti* (VI.3.116), there is lengthening when the suffix *kvip* follows: *marmāvit*. By the rule *pṝvyadhibhidi* (Uṇādi I.24), the suffix *ku* is applied: *vidhuḥ*. By the rule *vyadhajapor anupasarge* (III.3.61), [the suffix *ghan* is applied]: *vyadhaḥ*, *āvyādhaḥ*. By the rule *ghñarthe kaḥ* (III.3.58, 4), [the suffix *ka* is applied]: *āvidham*. (72)

1. Here, in manuscript P, folio 74 begins; folio 73 ends with *sṛja vi-* and folio 75 begins with *kṣudha bubhukṣāyām* (Dhātupāṭha IV, 79). 2. Regarding *asuś*, see *asum* in Aufrecht; cf. I, 1, 47. 131 IV.

The root *puṣ* means "to nourish. They say this one is intransitive: "he thrives like a boar" (*varāha iva puṣyati*). By the rule *puṣādidyutādi* (Pāṇini III.1.55), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *apuṣat*. The *puṣādi* group extends up to the end of the list; [the agentive suffix] *tṛc* yields *poṣṭṛ* ("nourisher"). By the rule *puṣyasidhyau nakṣatre* (Pāṇini III.1.116), [the word *puṣya* denotes the asterism]. In the *Bhvādi* class (I.732), it is *poṣati*; in the *Kryādi* class (IX.57), *puṣṇāti*; and in the *Curādi* class, *puṣa* in the sense of "supporting" (X.210): *poṣayati* (73).

The root *śuṣ* means "to dry. It forms *śuṣyati* (present) and *aśuṣat* (imperfect). By the rule *śuṣeḥ kaḥ* (Pāṇini VIII.2.51), [the suffix] *ka* is applied: *śuṣkaḥ* ("dried"). By the rule *ūrdhve śuṣipūroḥ* (Pāṇini III.4.44), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied: *ūrdhvaśoṣam śuṣkaḥ* ("dried while standing upright"). By the rule *avisiviśuṣibhyaḥ kit* (Uṇādi-sūtra I.143), the suffix *man* is applied: *śuṣmam* means "strength"; *śuṣma* is an attested form [in the Veda], as in *śuṣmā barhiḥ* ("the strength of the sacrificial grass"). The root *tuṣ* means "to be pleased. It forms *tuṣyati* (present) and *atuṣat* (imperfect); the future form is *toṣṭā*.

The root *duṣ* means "to become deformed. Deformation (*vaikṛtya*) is the loss of natural form. [From *duṣ*: *aduṣat*, *doṣṭā*. By the rule *doṣo ṇau* (Pāṇini VI.4.90), the penultimate vowel is replaced by *ū*: *dūṣayati*. Or, by the rule *vā cittavirāge* (VI.4.91): *cittaṃ doṣayati*, *cittaṃ dūṣayati*. In the *nandy-ādi* group (Dhātupāṭha III.1.134), [the agentive suffix *anaṭ* gives] *dūṣaṇaḥ*. By the rule *kaṣidūṣibhyām īkan* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.16), [we have] *dūṣīkā*, meaning "eye-secretion" (*netramala*). (76)

The root *śliṣ* is used in the sense of embracing (*āliṅgane*). It forms *śliṣyati*, *aśliṣat*. Regarding the rule *śliṣa āliṅgane* (III, 1, 46): after the root *śliṣ*, the suffix *ksa* replaces *cli* only when it refers to the embracing of living beings; thus, *āślikṣat kanyām* ("he embraced the girl"), but not here: *samāśliṣaj jatu ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca* ("the lac and the wood adhered together"). The feminine form is *śleṣṭrī*. By the rule *śyādvyadha* (III, 1, 141), the suffix *ṇa* is applied: *śleṣaḥ* ("adhesion"). By the rule *gatyarthākarmaka* (III, 4, 72), the suffix *kta* is applied: *āśliṣṭaḥ kanyāṃ caitraḥ* ("Caitra has embraced the girl"). By the rule *śliṣer ac copadhāyāḥ* (Uṇ. III, 19), [the suffix *na* is applied]: *ślakṣṇam* ("smooth"). By the rule *manin* (Uṇ. IV, 144), [the suffix *man* is applied]: *śleṣmā* ("phlegm").
In the *bhvādi* class (I, 734), it has the meaning of "burning": *śleṣati*; in the *curādi* class (X, 38), *śliṣa* means "to cause to adhere": *śleṣayati*. (77)

The root *śak* is explained as meaning "to endure" (*marṣaṇe*). Regarding the root *śak*, there is a difference of opinion concerning the substitution of *śyan*: it is optionally substituted for the *parasmaipada* affixes, or *aṅ* is substituted, or *iṭ* is added. Thus: *śakyate*, *śakyati*; *aśākīt*, *aśakat*; *śakitā*, *śaktā*. Elsewhere: *śaknoti*, *śaktā*. With the desiderative suffix (*san*), by rule VII.4.54 (*mīmā*), it becomes *śikṣati*. By rule III.1.99 (*śakisahoś ca*), the suffix *yat* is applied: *śakyam*. With the suffix *vanip* (Uṇ. IV.112): *śakvā*, *śakvarī*. By Uṇ. I.111 (*śakiśamyor nit*), *śakalaḥ*. With the suffix *rak* (Uṇ. II.13): [the form *śakraḥ*].

From the root *śak* (to be able), by Uṇādi-sūtra II.49 (*śaker unontontyunayaḥ*), we derive: *śakunaḥ*, *śakuntaḥ*, *śakuntiḥ*, *śakuniḥ* (bird). By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.58 (*śaker ṛtin*), we derive: *śakṛt* (excrement). By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.81 (*śakādibhyo ’ṭan*), we derive: *śakaṭaḥ* (cart); as well as *śakaṭiḥ*, *śakaṭī*, and *śaktiḥ*, *śaktī* (power/ability). Regarding the form *śakyate bhoktum* ("it is possible to eat"), this follows Pāṇini III.4.65 (*śakadhṛṣajñā*). (78)

*ṣvid* [is used] in the sense of the exuding of the limbs. The exuding of the limbs is the flow of perspiration (*gharmasruti*). [From this root we have: *svidyati*, *siṣveda*, *asvidat*, *asiṣvidat*, *svettā*. [Past passive participle: *svinnaḥ*; [instrumental forms: *svinnam anena*, *sveditam anena*, *prasvinnaḥ*, *prasveditaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.17). In the *Bhvādi* class (1.780), there is *svedate* (79). *krudh* [is used] in the sense of anger. [In the sentence] *Caitrāya krudhyati* ("he is angry with Caitra"), [Caitra] is the recipient (*saṃpradāna*) according to Pāṇini 1.4.37: *krudhadruherṣyāsūyārthānāṃ yaṃ prati kopaḥ*. [Aorist: *akrudhat*; [future: *kroddhā*. According to Pāṇini 3.2.151: *krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaś ca*, the suffix *yuc* is applied: *krodhanaḥ* (80). 1V 132.

The root *kṣudh* is used in the sense of hunger (*bubhukṣā*). It forms *kṣudhyati*, *akṣudhat*, and *kṣoddhā*. By rule I.2.154 (*ukañ*), the suffix *ukañ* is desired: *kṣodhukaḥ*. By rule VII.2.52 (*vasatikṣudhor iṭ ktvāniṣṭhayoḥ*), the augment *iṭ* is applied before the suffixes *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā*: *kṣudhitaḥ*, *kṣudhitvā*, and *kṣodhitvā*. By rule I.2.26 (*ralo vyupadhāt*), there is optionally the status of being *kit*. The root *śudh* is used in the sense of purification (*śauca*). Purification is stainlessness (*nairmalya*). It forms *śudhyati*, *aśudhat*, and *śoddhā*. (82)

The root *ṣidh* is used in the sense of "accomplishment" (*saṃrāddhi*), which means "completion. [Conjugations: *sidhyati*, *asidhat*, *siṣedha*, *seddhā*. According to Pāṇini VI.1.49, the substitution of *ā* for the vowel of *sidh* occurs before the causative suffix *ṇi* when it does not refer to a matter concerning the next world: *kāryaṃ sādhayati* ("he accomplishes the task"). It does not occur here: *sedhayati dharmaṃ* ("he causes [someone] to perform their duty"). [Gerunds: *siddhvā*, *sidhitvā*, *sedhitvā*. [In the rule] *puṣyasidhyau nakṣatre* (Pāṇini III.1.116), [the term *sidhya* refers to a lunar mansion]. In the *Bhvādi* class (Dhātupāṭha I.48), the form *niṣedhati* (83) [is derived from the same root].

The root *radh* means "to injure" and "to cook. *Saṃrāddhiḥ* means cooking. [In the present tense: *radhyati*. By the rule *radhādibhyaś ca* (Pāṇini VII.2.45), the augment *iṭ* is optional: *radhitā* or *raddhā*. By the rule *radhijabhor aci* (Pāṇini VII.1.61), the augment *num* is applied: *randhayati*. By the rule *neṭy aliṭi radheḥ* (Pāṇini VII.1.62), *num* is applied: *radhiṣyati*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form is] *rarandhiva*. [In the imperfect: *aradhat*; by the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini VI.4.24), there is elision of the nasal (*n*). [In the conditional: *aratsyat* or *aradhiṣyat*. [The past participle is] *raddhaḥ*; [the verbal noun is] *randhanam*. (84)

*ṇa-ś-a-da-rśa-ne*. Non-perception (*adarśana*) means non-apprehension (*anupalabdhi*). In *praṇaśyati*, because of the rule *naśeḥ ṣāntasya* (Pāṇini VIII.4.36), the substitution of *ṇa* for *na* does not occur: *pranaṣṭaḥ*, *pranaṅkṣyati*. By the rule *masjinaśor jhali* (VII.1.60), the augment *num* is added: *naṃṣṭā*, *naśitā*. By the rule *naśer vā* (VIII.2.63), there is optionally the substitution of *ku* (i.e., *ka*): from the root *naś*, we have *nak*; as in *jīvo naśyati*: *jīvanak* (the living perishes), *jīvanaṭ*; [and] *jīvanaṭ* (an oblation of life).

By the rule *budhayudha* (I.3.86), [the suffix *ṇic*] causes the elision [of the penultimate vowel]; by *nandyādau* (III.1.134), [the suffix *lyu* is added] to form *vittanāśanaḥ*; by *nindahiṃsa* (I.2.146), [the suffix *ṇvul* is added] to form *vināśakaḥ*; by *iṇnaśaji* (III.2.163), [the suffix *kvarap* is added] to form *naśvaraḥ*; and by *kartror jīvapuruṣayoḥ* (I.4.43), [the suffix *ṇamul* is added] to form *jīvanāśaṃ naṣṭaḥ*. (85)

The root *tṛp* is used in the sense of "satisfaction" (*prīti*). Satisfaction is the state of being satiated (*sauhityam*). [Conjugations: *tṛpyati*, *tarpitā*, *traptā*, *tarptā*; by the rule *anudāttasya cardupadhasya* (Pāṇini VI.1.59), the augment *am* is optionally applied: *tṛptaḥ*. By the rule *spṛśamṛśakṛṣatṛpadṛpaḥ sij vā* (Pāṇini III.1.44, vārttika 7): *atṛpat*, *atrāpsīt*, *atārpsīt*. In the *tudādigaṇa*, there are the roots *tṛpa* and *tṛnpa* in the sense of "satisfaction" (cf. VI.24.25): *tṛpati*, *tṛmpati*. [From *tṛp* with suffix] *rak* (Uṇādi II.13): *tṛpram*. In the *svādigaṇa*, its inclusion should be inferred as belonging to the *kṣubhnādi* group (Pāṇini VIII.4.39): *tṛpnoti*, *atarpīt*, *tṛpitam* (86).

The root *dṛp* is used in the sense of pride (*harṣa*) and delusion (*mohana*). Delusion here means arrogance (*garva*). One is proud: *dṛpyati*. The forms are *draptā*, *darptā*, *darpitā*, and *dṛptaḥ*. [Aorist: *adṛpat*, *adrāpsīt*, *adārpsīt*.

(87) The root *druh* is used in the sense of wishing to harm (*jighāṃsā*). According to *krudhadruheḥ* (Pāṇini I.4.37), one bears malice toward an enemy: *śatrave druhyati*. Alternatively, by the rule *vā druhmuhaṣṇuhaṣṇihāṃ* (Pāṇini VIII.2.33), there is the substitution of *k*: *drogdhā*, *droḍhā*, *drohitā*. By the rule *satsūdviṣa-* (Pāṇini III.2.61), the suffix *kvip* is applied: *mitradhruk*, *mitradhruṭ*. [Aorist: *adruhat*. (88) [Note: All manuscripts read "so" at this point.]

133. *muh* in the sense of mental confusion. Confusion (*vaicittya*) is a lack of discrimination. [Conjugations: *muhyati*, *mogdhā*, *moḍhā*, *mohitā*; *mugdhaḥ*, *mūḍhaḥ*; *amuhat*. Because of the rule *na pādamy-āṅyam-aśa-vas-av-ā-tām* (Pāṇini I.3.89), the *ātmanepada* ending is used: *parimohayate*. From *muh* with the suffix *kha*, there is the substitution of *mūr*: *mūrkhaḥ* (Uṇādi V.22). (89) *ṣṇuh* in the sense of vomiting. [Conjugations: *snuhyati*, *suṣṇoha*, *snogdhā*, *snoḍhā*, *snohitā*; *snugdhaḥ*, *snūḍhaḥ*; *asnuhat*. (90)

The root *ṣṇih* means "to love. [Present: *snihyati*; [Perfect: *siṣṇeha*; [Periphrastic Future: *sneḍhā*, *snehitā*; [Past Passive Participle: *snigdhaḥ*, *snīḍhaḥ*. [Aorist: *asnihat*, according to *ṛtvigdadhṛk* (Pāṇini III.2.59); [Metre: *uṣṇik chandaḥ*. In the *cur*-class (cf. X.36), it is *snehayati* (91). The *radhādi* group has concluded. Some maintain that this ends the *puṣādi* group; therefore, they have cited the following examples for the subsequent roots: *aśamīt*, *atamīt*, *adamīt*, *aśramīt*, *abhramīt*, *akṣamīt*, *aloṭīt*, *akledīt*, *akopīt*, *aharṣīt*, and so forth. These are *anudātta* roots with *udāttet* indicatory vowels. 87.

*Śam* means "to become calm. There are forty-six roots beginning with *ito gṛdhyantāḥ* (DhP 1.136), which are marked with *seṭ* and are *parasmaipada*. Regarding the rule *śamām aṣṭānāṃ dīrghaḥ śyani* (Pāṇini VII.3.74): [the vowel of] the eight roots beginning with *śam* is lengthened before the suffix *śyan*. Thus: *śāmyati*, *aśamat*. By the rule *śamo 'darśane* (DhP I.870), the root is designated as *mit*; thus: *śamayati rogam* ("he calms the disease"). But when meaning "to see," as in *niśāmayati rūpam* ("he observes the form"), it is not *mit*. [The past participle is] *śamitā*. [The gerunds are] *śāntvā* and *śamitvā*. [The past passive participle is] *śāntaḥ*. By the rule *por adupadhāt* (Pāṇini III.1.98): *śamyam*. [The noun *śam* is formed] by the suffix *kvip* (Pāṇini III.2.76).

In *praśān*, by [Pāṇini] VIII.2.64 (*mo no dhātoḥ*), the substitution of *na* for *m* occurs; however, because that rule is considered *asiddha* with respect to what precedes it (VIII.2.1), the elision of the final *n* of the nominal stem (VIII.2.7) does not take place. From the eight roots beginning with *śam*, the suffix *ghin* is applied (cf. III.2.141): *śamī*; from the same roots, the suffix *ghañ* (III.3.18–19): *śamaḥ*; in the *gaurādi* group (IV.1.41), *śamī* refers to a tree. *Śāntiḥ*; by the rule *vā dāntaśānta* (VII.2.27), *śāntaḥ* means "pacified" or "calmed"; from the roots *śak* and *śam*, the suffix *nit* is applied (Uṇ. I.111): *śamalam*; from the roots *jan*, *dā*, and *cyu*... (Uṇ.)... [and so forth].
(IV, 104) Thus, *śaṇṭhaḥ*; from the root *śam*, with the suffix *kha* (Uṇ. I, 104): *śaṅkhaḥ*; from the root *śam*, with the suffix *ḍha* (Uṇ. I, 101): *śaṇḍhaḥ* (92).

The root *tam* is used in the sense of longing (*kāṅkṣā*). [Derivatives: *tāmyati*, *atamat*. From the gerundives *tāntvā* and *tamitvā*, and from the past participle *tāntaḥ*. With the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini I.3.18–19), *tamaḥ* ("darkness"). In the *gaura-ādi* group (Pāṇini IV.1.41), *tamī* means "night. By the rule *amitamyor dīrghaś ca* (Uṇādi II.16), *tāmram* ("copper"). With the suffix *asuṇ* (Uṇādi IV.188), *tamas* ("darkness"). By the rule *kramitamistanbhām ata ic ca* (cf. Uṇādi IV.121), *timir* means "fish. By the rule *atyavicami* (Uṇādi III.117), the suffix *asac* is added: *Tamasā* is the name of a river. (93)

The root *dam* means "to pacify. From it we derive: *dāmyati*, *adamat*, *dāntvā*, and *damitvā*. According to rule I, 3, 89 (*na pādami*), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *damayate*. In the *nandigraha* group (III, 1, 134), we have *kuladamanaḥ*; in the sense of a proper name (III, 2, 46), *Arindamaḥ*; and by the rule *vā dānta-śānta-* (VII, 2, 27), we have *dāntaḥ* and *damitaḥ*. Due to the optionality established by the rule of restricted option (*vyavasthitavibhāṣā*), [the form] *dāntaḥ* [is also used].
[Notes: 1. KC: forty-four; 2. P: *tamaḥ* is a small portion; 3. s. I, 767; 4. KC: called *Tamasā* IV, 134.

*brahmacārin*, *damer ḍos* (cf. Uṇ. II, 69): *dor* means "arm"; *hasimṛgriṇvā* (Uṇ. III, 86) results in *tan*: *dantaḥ* ("tooth"); *damer ūnasiḥ* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 234): *damūnāḥ* means "fire" (*vahni*). With the suffix *ghinṇ* (cf. III, 2, 141): *damī*. (94) The root *śramu* is used in the sense of "exertion" (*tapas*) and "weariness" (*kheda*). One exerts oneself (*śrāmyati*), one exerted oneself (*aśramat*). Having exerted oneself: *śrāntvā*, *śramitvā*; past participle: *śrāntaḥ*; gerundive: *śramyam*. In the group beginning with *nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ* (III, 1, 134), we have *śramaṇaḥ* ("ascetic"); *viśrāmaḥ*. The form *viśramaḥ* is also desired. (95)

The root *bhram* is used in the sense of "not remaining fixed" (*anavasthāna*). Not remaining fixed means moving to another place. According to Pāṇini III.1.70, *bhrāśa*, etc., we have *bhrāmyati*, *bhramati*, and *abhramat*. From *bhrāntvā* and *bhramitvā*, by Uṇādi-sūtra II.68 (*bhrameś ca ḍūḥ*), we derive *bhrūḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class, *bhramu* is listed as meaning "movement" (I.903): *bhramati*, *bhramyati* (96).

The root *kṣam* means "to endure. It forms *kṣāmyati*, *akṣamat*, *kṣantā* / *kṣamitā*; and *kṣāntvā* / *kṣamitvā*. In the *bhvādi* class (I, 469), it is *kṣamate*, *akṣamiṣṭa*; because it has the marker *ṣit* (III, 3, 104), the feminine form is *kṣamā*; and by virtue of the rule for diversity (*bāhulaka*) (X, 392), there is *kṣāntiḥ*. For this very reason, the learned say that *kṣamū* means "endurance" (97). The root *klam* means "weariness. It forms *klāmyati* and *klāmati*; [the latter] follows the rule *vā bhrāśa* (III, 1, 70), and there is lengthening [of the vowel] by the rule *ṣṭhivuklamvācamāṃ śiti* (VII, 3, 75); [the imperfect is] *aklamat* (98).

The root *mad* means "to rejoice. From it we derive: *mādyati* (he rejoices), *amadat* (he rejoiced), *maditā* (he will rejoice), and *mattaḥ* (intoxicated). Regarding the senses of "rejoicing" and "stupefaction," the rule *mit* (Pāṇini I.853) applies: *madayati* (he causes to rejoice), whereas in other senses, *unmādayati* (he causes madness). By the rule *mado 'nupasarge* (Pāṇini III.3.67), the suffix *ap* is applied: *madaḥ* (intoxication). By *pramadasaṃmadau harṣe* (Pāṇini III.3.68), the forms *pramadaḥ* and *saṃmadaḥ* denote joy. By *gadamad-* (Pāṇini III.1.100), the suffix *yat* is applied: *madyam* (liquor). By *ugrapaśya-* (Pāṇini III.2.37), the suffix *irañ* is applied: *īraṃmadaḥ*, meaning a cloud of light. By *alaṃkṛñ-* (Pāṇini III.2.136), the suffix *iṣṇuc* is applied: *unmadiṣṇuḥ* (one prone to madness). [The rule] *iṣitimimadi-* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra).

From the root *mad* with the suffix *kirac*: *madirā*. From *kṛ*, *dhūma*, etc., with the suffix *kit* (Uṇ. III, 73): *matsaraḥ*. From *ṛtanyañji* (Uṇ. IV, 2): *matsyaḥ*; *matsī* belongs to the *gaurādi* group (I Y, 1, 41). From *janidācyv* (Uṇ. IV, 104): *matsaḥ*; some say *maccha*. In the *curādi* class, from *mada* in the sense of "satiety" or "purification" (X, 165): *mādayate* (99); it is included in the *vṛt* group. It is a sub-group (*antargaṇa*) beginning with *śam*.

The root *asu* is used in the sense of "throwing" (*kṣepaṇe*). *Asyati*, *asyate*. Regarding *thuk* (VH 4.17): *nirāsthat*. In the case of the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) for the reflexive agent (*karmakartṛ*), the suffix *aṅ* is applied by the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo ’ṅ* (HI 1.52): *upāsthetāṃ kuṇḍe svayam eva* ("the two pots offer themselves up"). By the rule *upasargād asyatyūhor vā* (I 3.29.3), the *taṅ* (middle endings) are optionally used: *nirasyate*, *nirasyati*. By the rule *ner gada* (VH 4.17), [the suffix *aṅ* is applied]: *praṇyasyate*. [Gerunds: *astvā*, *asitvā*. [Past participle: *astaḥ*. [Future passive participle: *asyam*. By the rule *śṝsvṛsnihi* (Uṇ. I.11), the suffix *u* is applied: *asavaḥ*. By the rule *aser uran* (Uṇ. [1.40]), [the suffix *uran* is applied].

I, 43): *asuraḥ* [is derived from] *asu* with the suffix *ṛn* (*Uṇ.* I, 97); *svasā* [from] *as* and *sañj* with the suffix *kthin* (*Uṇ.* III, 154); *asthi*. 1 P *agniḥ*; 2 cf. *Candra-Vṛtti* VI, 1, 42 and *Hem. Dh.* IV, 90; 3 P *matsyaḥ*; 4 P *matsa*. 135 IV.

The suffix *ṇamul* is applied according to the rule *asyatitṛṣoḥ kriyāntare kāleṣu* (Pāṇini III, 4, 57): "He causes the goats to drink [so that they do so] two days before [the time]. From the root *yas-* (Uṇādi IV, 117), the form *asiḥ* (100) is derived. From the root *yas-* meaning "exertion" (*yatna*), the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied according to the rules *yaso 'nupasargāt* and *saṃyasaś ca* (Pāṇini III, 1, 71–72). Thus, one says *yasyati* or *yasati*; *saṃyasyati* or *saṃyasati*; and *ayasat*. The forms *yastvā* and *yasitvā* are derived from the same root. From the past passive participle *āyastaḥ*, the suffix *taṅ* (i.e., *ātmanepada*) is applied according to the rule *na pādami* (Pāṇini I, 3, 89): *āyāsayate* (101).

The root *jas* is used in the sense of liberation (*mokṣaṇa*). It forms *jasyati* and *ajasat*. From the suffixes *-tvā* and *-it*, by the rule *namikampi-* (Pāṇini III.2.167), we have *ajasram*. In the *curādi* class, *jas* is used in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*): *ujjāsayati*. (102) The root *tas* is used in the sense of wasting away (*upakṣaya*). It forms *tasyati*; in the imperative (*loṭ*) with *sip*, *tasya*; and *atasat*. From the suffixes *-tvā* and *-it*, we have *tastvā* and *tasitvā*. By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.181, we have *vitastiḥ* and *Vitastā*. (103)

And *das*: it bites (*dasyati*), it bit (*adasat*). Having bitten (*dastvā* or *dasitvā*), [the form] *dasta* or *dāsita* occurs according to *dānta-śānta* (VH 2.27). With the suffix *rak* (Uṇ. II.13), we have *Dasrau*, the two Aśvins. With the suffix *yuc* according to *yajimaniśundhi* (Uṇ. III.20), we have *dasyuḥ*. (104) *vasu* in the sense of stiffening: it stiffens (*vasyati*), it stiffened (*avasat*). Having stiffened (*vastvā* or *vasitvā*), *vastaḥ* is a goat; *vastiḥ* is the part above the penis (Uṇ. IV.179). (105) *pyuṣ* in the sense of separation: it separates (*pyusyati*), it separated (*apyusat*); *pyuṣitaḥ*. Durga reads *pyuṣeti*; some read *puseti*: *pustakam* (book), *pustam* (work involving modeling with clay, etc.). (106) *pyuṣeti Durgaḥ*, *pusety eke*: *pustakam*, *pustaṃ lepyādi karma*.

*pluṣ* in the sense of burning. *pluṣyati*, *apluṣat*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I, 736): *ploṣati*; [gerunds] *pluṣṭvā*, *pluṣitvā*, *ploṣitvā*. In the *Kryādi* class (IX, 56): *pluṣṇāti* (107). *bis* in the sense of impelling. *bisyati*, *abisat*. By Pāṇini III, 1, 135, [the word] *bisam* [is derived] (108). *kus* in the sense of clinging. *kusyati*, *akusat*. *kusitaḥ*; *kusumam* (Uṇ. IV, 106). Durga says [it means] "grass" (*kuśa*); [by Pāṇini IV, 1, 42, the feminine form] *kuśyāyasī* [is formed]; *kośaḥ* refers to a treasury and so forth; *kośī* (109).

In *busa-utsarge*. *Utsarga* means abandonment (*tyāga*). [The root] *bus* [is used]: *busati*, *abusat*. By [Pāṇini III.1.135], *ke*, [we have] *busaṃ* as chaff (*tuṣaḥ*) (110). [The root] *mus* in the sense of breaking (*khaṇḍane*): *musyati*, *amusat*. In the *uṇādi* [section], *mustaḥ* (Uṇ. I.108) and *musalam* (Uṇ. I.108) [are derived] (111).

*Mas-* in the sense of transformation (*pariṇāma*). Transformation means modification (*vikāra*). [Root *mas-*: *masyati*, *amasat*. Having transformed: *masitvā*. By the rule *śvīdito niṣṭhāyām* (VII. 2. 14), the augment *iṭ* is not applied: *mastaḥ*, *mastakaḥ*. With the suffix *ghañ* (I. 3. 18–19): *māsaḥ*. *Mās* is another verbal root; [the time] joined with the full moon (*pūrṇamāsā yuktaḥ kālaḥ*) is *paurṇamāsī*. By the rule *sitanigamimasi* (Uṇ. I. 70), the suffix *tun* is added: *mastu*. Kaṇṭha (112) states that *bas-* is also [used here]. [Root *luṭ-*: *luṭa* in the sense of rolling about (*viloṭana*). [Conjugation: *luṭyati*, *aluṭat*. In the *bhvādi* class (I. 336): *loṭati*, *aloṭīt*. In the *curādi* class (X. 214), it has the meaning of shining (*bhāsārtha*): *loṭayati*. (113)

1. Cf. Hem. Uṇ. 200. 2. Cf. Hem. Uṇ. 201. 9. P adds *muṣṭiḥ*. 4. See I. 767. 5. KC: *uc* in the sense of churning (IV. 136); *uc* in the sense of collection (*samavāya*). Collection (*samavāya*) means unity (*aikyam*). From *ucyati*, *uvoca*, *aucicat*. By [the rule] *oka ucaḥ ke* (VII. 3. 64), we have *ucitam*. By *ucaḥ kuś ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV. 215), the suffix *asun* is applied: *okas*. Regarding those for whom heaven (*dyu*) is their abode (*okas*), they are called *divaukasaḥ*; this applies in cases where there is vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*). Some say that the word *div* exists ending in a short *u*; they state that in the case of land and water, the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) is used: *sthalokāḥ* / *sthalaukāḥ*, *jalokāḥ* / *jalaukāḥ* (114).

The roots *bhṛśu* and *bhranśu* mean "to fall down. These four [roots] end in palatal consonants (*tālavya*), and the first has *ṛ* as its penultimate vowel. *bhṛśyati*, *abhṛśat*. *bhṛṣṭvā* or *bharśitvā*; [the suffix] *ktvā* is not *kit* when followed by *seṭ* (Pāṇini I.2.18). *bhṛṣṭam*, *barībhṛśyate*; with the suffix *ka* (Pāṇini III.1.135), *bhṛśam*. *bhraśyati*, *abhraśat*. *bhraṣṭvā* or *bhraṃśitvā*; *bhraṣṭaḥ*; *bābhraśyate*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.792): *bhraṃśate*, *abhraṃśiṣṭa*, *bhraṃśitā*; *banībhraśyate*; *vāhābhraṭ* (cf. Pāṇini III.2.76, Kāśikā). (115)
The root *vṛś* means "to choose" (*varaṇe*). It forms *vṛśyati* (present) and *avṛśat* (aorist). By rule III, 1, 135, with the suffix *ka*, *vṛśaḥ* means "the plant *yavāsa*.

The root *kṛś* means "to make thin" (*tanūkaraṇe*). It forms *kṛśyati* (present) and *akṛśat* (aorist). By rule III, 1, 135, with the suffix *ka*, it forms *kṛśaḥ*. When the suffix *kta* follows without a prefix, by rule VIII, 2, 55, the form is *phulla-kṣība-kṛśa-*, thus *kṛśaḥ*; however, when preceded by a prefix, it is *prakṛśitaḥ*. According to rule I, 2, 25, "after the roots *tṛṣ*, *mṛṣ*, and *kṛś*, [the suffix *ktvā*] may optionally be *kit* according to Kāśyapa," one obtains both *kṛśitvā* and *karśitvā*. By rule Uṇ IV, 2, *kṛśānuḥ* ("fire") is derived.

The root *tṛṣ* (with the prefix *ñi*) is used in the sense of thirsting. It forms *tṛṣyati* (he thirsts) and *atṛṣat* (he thirsted). From the rule *tṛṣimṛṣikṛśeḥ ktaḥ* (I.2.25), we have *tarṣitvā*. By the rule *ñītaḥ ktaḥ* (III.2.187), we have *tṛṣitaḥ* (thirsty) and *tarṣaḥ* (thirst). By the rule *asyatitṛṣoḥ* (III.4.57), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied: *dvyahatarṣaṃ gāḥ pāyayati* (he makes the cows drink [water] after two days of thirst). By the rule *svapitṛṣor najiṅ* (III.2.172), we have *tṛṣṇak* (thirsty). With the suffix *kvip* (III.2.178), we have *tṛṭ* (thirst). By the rule *tṛṣiśuṣirasibhyaḥ kit* (Uṇ. III.12), we have *tṛṣṇā* (thirst). (118)

The roots *hṛṣ* and *tuṣ* mean "to be pleased. From *hṛṣ*: *hṛṣyati*, *ahṛṣat*; past passive participle *hṛṣitaḥ*. In the *bhvādi* class (*hṛṣu alīke*, I. 741), it means "to bristle" or "to be excited": *harṣati*, *aharṣīt*, *hṛṣṭaḥ*. According to the rule *hṛṣer lomasu* (VII. 2. 29), there is optionally the suffix *iṭ*: *saṃhṛṣṭāni lomāni* ("the hairs are bristling") or *saṃhṛṣitāni*. And according to *vismitapratīghātayoś ca* (cf. Vārttika on VII. 2. 29, Kāśikā): *hṛṣṭaś Caitraḥ* ("Caitra is delighted") or *hṛṣitaḥ*; *hṛṣṭā dantāḥ* ("the teeth are set on edge") or *hṛṣitāḥ*. Nandī also states that this root has the marker *ud*. (119)

*ruṣ* in the sense of anger: *ruṣyati*, *aruṣat*. By the rule *tīṣusahalubharuṣariṣaḥ* (cf. VII.2.48), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *roṣṭā* or *roṣitā*; by the rule *ruṣyamatvaraḥ* (VII.2.28), the past passive participle is *ruṣṭaḥ* or *ruṣitaḥ*. In the *bhvādi* class, *ruṣ* means "to injure" (I.724): *roṣati*. (120) *ḍip* in the sense of throwing: *ḍipyati*, *aḍipat*. In the *tudādi* class (VI.78), it is *ḍipati*. In the *curādi* class, *ḍip* and *stip* mean "to throw" (X.133): *ḍepayati*. (121)

Regarding the root *stūp* in the sense of "to erect" (*samucchrāya*): *stūpyati*, *astūpat*, *tustūpayiṣati*. In the *curādi* group (X, 134), it is *stūpayati*; the noun is *stūpaḥ*. Durga [states] that the root is *ṣṭup*: *stupyati*.

Regarding *kup* in the sense of "anger" (*krodha*): *kupyati*, *akupat*. In the *pacādi* group (III, 1, 134), the noun is *kopaḥ*. By the rule *krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaś ca* (III, 2, 151), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *kopanaḥ*. (See I, 767).
