137. IV. *Gup* in the sense of agitation (*vyākulatva*). It forms *gupyati* and *agupat*. By the rule *rājasūyasūrya* (Pāṇini III.1.114), *kupya* refers to wealth other than gold and silver; it is that which is to be agitated, while other [wealth] is to be protected (*gopya*). In the *Bhvādi* class, *gup* in the sense of protection (*gopana*) [is listed as I.1019]: *jugupsate*. In the sense of protecting (*rakṣaṇa*), *gupū* [is listed as I.422]: *gopāyati*. In the *Curādi* class, it has the meaning of shining (*bhāsārtha*) [as X.231]: *gopayati*. (123)

The roots *yup*, *rup*, and *lup* mean "to delude" (*vimohana*). From *yup*: *yupyati*, *ayupat*; by rule I.2.26 (*ralo vyupadha*), there are the forms *yupitvā* and *yopitvā*, and *ynyupiṣati* and *yuyopiṣati*. From *rup*: *rupyati*, *arupat*; *ropaḥ*, *śaraḥ*, and *rūpyam*. From *lup*: *lupyati*, *alupat*. In the *tud*-class (VI.137), *lup* means "to cut":

*lumpati* (cf. 124–126). The root *lubh* means "greed" (*gārddhya*). Greed is intense longing (*abhikāṅkṣā*). From *lubh*: *lubhyati*, *alubhat*; by rule VII.2.48 (*tīṣasaha*), the forms are *lobdhā* and *lobhitā*. By rule VII.2.54 (*lubho vimohane*), the form *vilubhitāḥ* refers to hair; otherwise, one who is greedy is called *lubdhaḥ* (cf. 128).

The root *kṣubh* means "to move" (*saṃcalane*). Moving is the alteration of form (*rūpānyathātva*). [Examples: *kṣubhyati*, *akṣubhat*, *kṣobhitā*. According to the rule *kṣubdhasvānta* (Pāṇini VI.4.18), if *kṣubdha* refers to a churning-stick (*mantha*), then it is *kṣubdha*; otherwise, it is *kṣubhita*: as in the description of the agitated ocean (*kṣubhitāmbhodhi*). In the *kryādi* class (IX.47) one says *kṣubhnāti*; in the *bhvādi* class (I.787) one says *kṣobhate*. (129)

The root *ṇabha* is used in the sense of "to injure. One says *praṇabhyati*; the past participle is *anabhat*. In the *bhvādi* class (*I*, 788) it is *nabhate*; in the *kryādi* class (*IX*, 48) it is *nabhnāti*. By the rule *atyavicami* (*Uṇ.* III, 117), the suffix *asac* is added: *nabhasam* (neuter), *nabhaḥ* (masculine/neuter); *nabhaḥ* is formed from *babhasti* with the negative particle *nañ* (*III*, 18); *nābhiḥ* is derived from *nah* (*Uṇ.* IV, 125). *tubhyati*, *atubhat* (rules 130, 131).

The root *klidū* is used in the sense of "becoming moist. One says *klidyati*; the imperfect is *aklidat*; the future forms are *klettā* and *kleditā*. The past participle is *klinnaḥ*. By the rule *caricali* (*VI*, 1, 12, 6) and others, there is reduplication and the suffix *dve*: *ciklidaḥ* (rule 132).

The root *mī* [in the sense of] liquefying (*snehana*) undergoes *guṇa* substitution by Pāṇini II.4.82: *medyati*, *amidad*. By III.2.187 (*niṣṭhā* after roots ending in *ī*) and VII.2.16 (*āditaś ca*), the augment *iṭ* is not applied: *minnaḥ*. By VII.2.17 (*vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ*), there is an option: *prameditaḥ* or *praminnaḥ*; *meditam* by him, or *minnam*. By I.2.19 (*niṣṭhā śīṅ-svidi-*), the *niṣṭhā* suffix is not *kit* when preceded by *seṭ*. By III.1.134 (*ac*), we have *Medākhyaḥ* as the name of a region. By Uṇādi IV.188 (*asun*), we have *medo* (fat) and *medinī* (the earth).

In *bhvādi* (I, 779): *medate*, *amediṣṭa*; in *curādi* (X, 8), *mida* in the sense of "moistening": *medayati* (133). *ñi-kṣvidā* in the senses of "moistening" and "deluding": *kṣvidyati*, *akṣvidat*. *kṣviṇṇaḥ*, *prakṣviṇṇaḥ*, *prakṣveditaḥ*; "moistened by this": *kṣviṇṇam*, *kṣveditam*. In *bhvādi* (I, 1027), in the sense of "indistinct sound": *kṣvedati* (134).

The root *ṛdh* means "to increase. [Present: *ṛdhyati*; [Imperfect: *ārdhat*; [Optative: *mā ṛdhat*; [Aorist: *ānṛdhuḥ*. According to the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini III.1.7), there is optionally *iṭ*: *ardidhiṣati* or *īrtsati*. By the rule *āpjñapṛdhām īt* (Pāṇini VI.1.58), the vowel is changed to *ī*: [Causative: *ardhayati*; [Aorist of the causative: *ārdidhat*. [By the rule] *ṛdupadhāc ca* (Pāṇini III.1.110)...
[Note 1: cf. Hemacandra’s Uṇādisūtra 364; Note 2: KC reads *tīṣusaha* before 122; Note 3: cf. rather Pāṇini VII.1.12; Note 4: all manuscripts read thus]. IV V 138.

Thus, from the root *ṛdh*, [the suffix] *kyap* [is applied]: *ṛdhyaḥ*; by [the rule] *ghañ* (Pāṇini 3.3.18–19): *ardhaḥ*; [the gerunds] *ṛddhvā* and *ardhitvā*; [the prohibition applies] by *na ktvā seṭ* (Pāṇini 1.2.18); [the past passive participle] *ṛddhaḥ*. [In the sense of] "to prosper" (*svādau*), it is *ṛdhnoti* (135).

The root *gṛdh* is used in the sense of longing (*abhikāṅkṣā*). *gṛdhyati*, *agṛdhat*, *jighṛtsati*. Regarding the form *ajarghāḥ* or *ajarghāt*: by Pāṇini VIII.2.74, the substitution of *ru* for the final *s* of the root occurs optionally before the *sip* suffix; thus, from the *laṅ* of the *yaṅ*-luṅanta [reduplicated stem], we have *ajargardhīt* in the *luṅ*. By Pāṇini III.2.140 (*trasigṛdhi*), the suffix *knu* is applied: *gṛdhnuḥ*. By Pāṇini III.2.150 (*jucaṅkramyadandramyasṛgṛdhijvala*), the suffix *yuc* is applied: *gardhanaḥ*. By Pāṇini III.2.151 (*susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran*; cf. Uṇādi-sūtra II.24), the suffix *kran* is applied: *gṛdhraḥ*. The gerund forms are *gṛddhvā* or *gardhitvā*; the nouns are *gardhaḥ* and *gṛddhaḥ*.

In the *cur*-class (*curādi*), according to Pāṇini I.3.69, the roots *gṛdh* and *vañc* take the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings when meaning "deceiving": *gardhayate*. (136) Those [roots] which have an acute accent on the first syllable (*udātteta*) have been concluded. The *puṣ*-class (*puṣādi*) has been completed. In the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on the roots conceived by the illustrious Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin, the *divādi-gaṇa* is finished. Om! The root *ṣuñ* is used in the sense of "pressing" (*abhiṣava*). Pressing (*abhiṣava*) is moistening, known as "fermentation" (*saṃdhāna*).

From here onwards, seven roots ending in *kṛ* are *aniṭ*. According to *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (III.1.73), the suffix *śnu* is applied: *sunoti*, *sunute*, *abhiṣuṇoti*, *abhyaṣuṇot*. Although the substitution of *ṣ* would have been required by *upasargāt sunoti* (VIII.3.65), it does not occur due to the restrictive rule *sthādiṣv abhyāsena* (VIII.3.64). Thus we have *abhisuṣāva*, *abhisuṣuve*. By the rule *sunoteḥ syasanoḥ* (VIII.3.117), we have *abhisosyati* and *abhisusūṣati*.

*sunvaḥ*, *sunuvaḥ*, *sunmaḥ*, *sunumaḥ*; [in the case of the suffixes] *m* and *v*, there is optionally elision (*lopa*) [of the *s* of *as*] according to Pāṇini VI.4.107; and by VII.2.72, the augment *iṭ* is added to the root *su* when followed by the suffix *sic*: [thus] *asāvīt*. By III.2.132, *sunvan* [is formed] when connected with a sacrifice (*yajña-saṃyoga*); [and] by III.3.99, [the suffix *kvip* is applied] when it is a name (*saṃjñā*), as in *samaja*.

Thus, from the root *su* [to press], we have *sutyā* by [Pāṇini] III.1.114; *rājasūya* by III.1.114; and *āsāvyam* by III.1.126, where the suffix *ṇyat* is applied. From *su* with the prefix *som-* [in the sense of Soma-pressing], the suffix *kvip* is applied by III.2.90, yielding *somasut*. By III.2.103, the suffix *ṅvanip* is applied to *su* and *yaj*, yielding *sutvā*. By IV.1.7, the feminine form is *sutvarī*. By Uṇādi I.139, the suffix *man* is applied, yielding *soma*. By [Uṇādi II.24], the suffix *kran* is applied to *su*, *sūdhā*, and *gṛdh*, yielding *surā*. By Uṇādi II.74, the suffix *yuc* is applied to *su*, *yu*, *ru*, and *vṛñ*, yielding *savana*.
By Uṇādi III.13, the suffix *na* is applied to *su* with a long vowel, yielding *sūnā*, meaning a place of slaughter. [The suffix *ka* is applied] to *ku*, *su*, and *yu*.
And [from the root *sū*] by the rule *ca* (Uṇ. II. 26–27), we have *sūpaḥ* (1).

From the root *ṣiñ* in the sense of "binding" (*bandhane*): *sinoti*, *sinute*, *siṣāya*. With the suffix *ṇvul* (III. 1. 133): *sāyakaḥ*. By the rule *parinivibhyaḥ seva* (VIII. 3. 70), there is the substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*]: *viṣayaḥ*. With the suffix *kta* (III. 2. 102): *prasitaḥ*. From the roots *añji*, *ghṛ*, and *si* by the rule *añjighṛsibhyaḥ ktaḥ* (Uṇ. III. 89): *sitaḥ*. By the rule *dādheṭsi* (III. 2. 159), there is the suffix *ru*: *seruḥ*. [Also] from the roots *si*, *tan*, *gam*, etc., by the rule *sitanigami* (Uṇ. I. 70).

1. Cf. Hemacandra’s *Dhātupāṭha* IV, 44. 2. P: Thus ends the section on the *divādi* [verbs] in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, the *Dhātuvṛtti* conceived by Kṣīrasvāmī. 3. Nominative singular of *śatṛ*; P: *śatrā*. 4. P adds: From *suñ* with the suffix *rir*, there is also lengthening: *sūriḥ*. 139. By the rule *tuṇ*: *setuḥ*; and from *śu-si-ci-mi* there is lengthening (*Uṇ.* II, 25): *sīram*; from *i-ṇ-si-dīṅ-uṣi-ava-bhiḥ* there is *nak* (*Uṇ.* III, 2): *sino* bound; from *kṝ-vṛ-jṝ-si* (*Uṇ.* III, 10) there is *naḥ*: *senā* (2).

The root *śi* is used in the sense of sharpening (*niśāna*), which means making thin. One says *śinoti*, *śinute*, or *śetā*. The root *√miñ* (with prefix *ud-*) is used in the sense of throwing (*prakṣepaṇa*). One says *minoti*, *minute*. By the rule *mīnātiminoti* (Pāṇini VI.1.50), there is the substitution of *ā*: *mātā*, *māsyati*. By the rule *lyapi ca* (VI.1.41), one says *pramāya*. In the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *sani mīmā* (VI.4.54), and because the term "beginning with *ga*" includes no distinction [between the roots *mā* and *mi*] according to Paribhāṣā 106, one says *mitsati*, *mitsate*. From this root, *mitrimam* is formed. By the rule *kṛvāpājī* (Uṇādi I.1), the suffix *uṇ* is applied: *māyuḥ* (bile). By the rule *bhṛmṛśītṝcaritsaritanimimasjibhya ur* (Uṇādi I.7), the suffix *ur* is applied: [the word *māyuḥ* is thus derived].

*Mayuḥ* and *kinnaraḥ* do not undergo the substitution of *ā* because they are listed among many [other words] (Pāṇini III.3.1). *Vātapramīḥ* (Uṇādi IV.1); *jāmātā* is derived from *naptṛneṣṭṛ* (Uṇādi II.96). From the roots *mī* and *ci* (cf. Uṇādi II.25): *mīrā*.

Regarding *ci* in the sense of "accumulating" (*cayane*): one says *cinoti* or *cinute*. According to *ner gada* (Pāṇini VI.4.17), one says *praṇicinoti*. According to *vibhāṣā cer* (Pāṇini VII.3.58), there is optionally the substitution of *ku* for the *c* before *sa* and *liṭ*: *cikīṣati* or *cicīṣati*; *cikāya* or *cicāya*. According to *cisphuror ṇau* (Pāṇini VI.1.54), there is the substitution of *ā* in the causative: *uccāpayati*. Because it is marked with *mit* in the *cur*-group (X.86), one says *capayati*.

In the sense of a sacrifice (*kratu*), [the suffix *ghañ* is applied] to form *kuṇḍapāyya* and *saṃcāyya*; in the sense of fire (*agni*), to form *paricāyya*, *upacāyya*, and *samūhya*; and for *cityā* and *agnicityā* (Pāṇini III.1.130–132). By the rule *ktin* (III.3.94), we have *citiḥ*. By the rule *agnau ceḥ* (III.2.91), [the suffix] *kvip* is applied to form *agnicit*. By the rule *karmaṇy agnyākhyāyām* (III.2.92), [the suffix *kvip* is applied after the root *ci* when the object is a fire]: that which is piled like a hawk is *śyenacit*. By the rule *hastādāne cer asteye* (III.3.40), [the suffix] *ghañ* is applied to form *puṣpapracāyaḥ*. By the rule *nivāsacitiśarīropasamādhāneṣv ādeś ca kaḥ* (III.3.41), [the suffix *ghañ* is applied and the initial vowel is changed to *ka*]: *nikāyaḥ*. One should pile the fire in the shape of a body (*ākāyam agniṃ cinvīta*); hence *kāyaḥ* and *gomayanikāyaḥ*.

Regarding *saṃghe cānauttarādharye* (Pāṇini III.3.42): [the suffix] *caṅkhillika* (III.3.44) applies; elsewhere, by *grahivṛdṛniści* (III.3.58), the suffix *ap* is applied: *niścayaḥ*. By *śusicimyāṃ dīrghaś ca* (cf. Uṇādi II.25): *cīram*. By *amicimidi* (Uṇādi IV.163), the suffix *ktra* is applied: *citram*. [The root] *stṛñ* in the sense of covering (*ācchādane*): *stṛṇoti*, *stṛṇute*. By *guṇo 'rtisaṃyogādyoḥ* (VII.4.29): *āstaryate*; *vistṛtaḥ*. In the *kryādi* group, *stṝñ* (IX.14): *āstṛṇāti*, *āstīryate*, *āstīrṇaḥ*.

The root *kṛ* is used in the sense of "to injure. It forms *kṛṇoti* and *kṛṇute*; in the *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes, it follows the pattern of *karoti* (Pāṇini VIII.4.17): *cakāra*, *cakre*. (7) [Roots] with the anudātta accent. 7.1 See Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 392. 2 KC: *caye*. 3 All manuscripts read thus. 4 Regarding this name, see III.3.41 and the commentary in the *Kāśikā*; C reads *pakṣinikāyaḥ* here, which must be a scribal error for *bhikṣunikāyaḥ*. 5 KC: *chādane*. 6 P: *āstṛṇoti*.

V 140 v: *vṛ* in the sense of "covering" (*varaṇe*) and *dhūñ* in the sense of "shaking" (*kampane*) are both udātta [roots]. From *vṛ*: *vṛṇoṣi*, *vṛṇute*; *prāvaritā* / *prāvarītā*. By the rule *vṝto vā* (VII, 2, 38), there is optionally a lengthening of the *iṭ* augment. In the *parasmaipada* forms with the suffix *sic*, by the rule *sici parasmaipadeṣu* (VII, 2, 40), the *iṭ* is applied: *prāvārīt*, *prāvāriṣṭām*. In the *ātmanepada* forms with *liṅ* and *sic*, by the rule *liṅsicor ātmanepadeṣu* (VII, 2, 42), the *iṭ* is optional: *prāvariṣātām* / *prāvṛṣātām*. In the benedictive (*liṅ*), *vṛṣīṣṭa* / *variṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *na liṅi* (VII, 2, 39), the lengthening does not occur. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), the *iṭ* is optional: *vṛṣīṣati* / *viriṣīṣati*.

*vuvūrṣati*, *vivariṣati*, *vivarīṣati*. Regarding the rule *avadyapaṇyavaryā* (Pāṇini III.1.101), *varyā* is used in the sense of "not obstructing"; otherwise, it is *vāryaḥ*. From the rule *etistuśās* (III.1.109), the suffix *kyap* applies: *vṛtyam*; the suffix *ṇyat* is also desired: *vāryam*. In the sense of a name, by the rule *bhṛtr* (III.2.46), we have *patiṃvarā* for a maiden. By the rule *grahavṛdr* (III.3.58), the suffix *ap* applies: *varaḥ*. By the rule *nau vṛ dhānye* (III.3.48), the suffix *ghañ* applies: *nīvāraḥ*. [The form *vāraḥ*] is derived from the root *vṛ* in the sense of "covering" (III.3.54).

*Prāvāraḥ*; from *kṛ*, *sṛ*, *bhṛ*, *vṛñ* [the suffix] *aṇḍan*: *varaṇḍaḥ*; from *jṝ* and *vṛñ* [the suffix] *ūthan* (cf. Uṇ. I.128): *varūthaḥ*, meaning the protection of a chariot; from *su*, *yu*, *ru*, and *vṛñ* [the suffix] *yuc* (Uṇ. II.74): *varaṇaḥ*; from *aj*, *i*, *vṛ*, and *rī* [the suffix] *nic* (Uṇ. III.38): the river named *Varṇuḥ*; from *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, *vṛñ*, and *cati* [the suffix] *ṣvarac* (cf. Uṇ. II.123): *varvaraḥ*, meaning curly hair; from *sṛ*, *vṛ*, *bhū*, *śuṣi*, and *muṣi* [the suffix] *kit* (Uṇ. III.41): *vṛkaḥ*; from *vṛñ* [the suffix] *cit* (Uṇ. III.107): [the word *varvaraḥ*].

*Varatrā* means a leather thong. [The word *vāśikā*] is derived from the root *vṛś* with the suffix *i* according to *Uṇ.* IV, 104 (*janidācyv*). [The word *vāri*] is derived from the root *vas*, *vap*, *vap*, or *raj* with the suffix *iñ* according to *Uṇ.* IV, 124; or, from the causative form of the root *vah* with the suffix *kvip*, it becomes *vāḥ*. Thus, [he is] the "repository of waters" (*vārāṃ nidhiḥ*). (8)

*dhūñ* means "to shake. Regarding this root *dhūñ*, Śivasvāmī states that it has a long vowel: *dhūnoti* (he shakes), *dhūnute* (he shakes for himself). By the rule *svaratisūti* (Pāṇini VII.2.44), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *vidhotā* or *vidhavitā* (the shaker); *vidhūtaḥ* (shaken). By the rule *dhūñprīñor nuk* (Pāṇini VII.3.37, vārttika 1), the suffix *nuk* is added: *vidhūnayati* (he causes to shake). Candra (see Candra-Dhātupāṭha V.9) gives the form as *dhūñ*: *dhunoti*, *vidhutaḥ*. By the rule *artilūdhūsūkhanasahacara itra* (Pāṇini III.2.184), the word *dhavitram* (a fan) is formed; by the rule *iṣiyudhi* (Uṇādi-sūtra I.144), the suffix *mak* is added.

*Dhūmaḥ* [is derived from] *kṛ-dhūm-ādibhyaḥ kit* (Uṇ. III.73): *dhūsaraḥ*. In the *kryādi* class (IX.17), *dhunāti*; in the *tudādi* class (VI.105), *dhū* in the sense of "shaking": *dhuvati*. (9) *ṭudu* in the sense of "affliction. These four [roots] are *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment). *dunoti*, *dotā*; *davathuḥ* (VIII.3.89). There are also forms derived from the *bhauvādika* [root]. *du* and *dru* in the sense of "going" (I.991, 992): *davati*. (10)

The root *hi* means "to go" and "to grow. By [Pāṇini] VIII.4.15, *hinumīnā*, there is the substitution of *ṇ*: *prahiṇoti*. By [Pāṇini] VII.3.56, *her acaṅi*, there is the substitution of *k* (*kutva*): *prajighāya*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] I.73, *kamimani*, there is the suffix *tu*: *hetuḥ*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] I.146, *mak*: *himam*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.144, *manin*: *hema*. By [Pāṇini] III.3.97, *ūtiyūti*, there is *hetiḥ*, meaning "a weapon. (1) *saṃvaraṇe* (to cover/conceal), but see IX.38 and X.308. (2) *anirodhane* (non-obstruction). (3) Cf. Hemacandra’s Uṇādi-sūtra 944, 141 V.

The root *pṛ* is used in the sense of "to please. [Examples: *pṛṇoti*, *partā*, *pupūrṣati*. Regarding the rule *iṭ sani vā* (Pāṇini VII.2.41), the augment *iṭ* is not applied here because of the governing context of "original instruction" (*upadeśa*) in rule VII.2.10. (12) The root *smṛ* is used in the senses of "pleasure" and "strengthening" (*balana*). Strengthening means living. [Examples: *smṛṇoti*, *sasmāra*. Some say it is *spṛ*. These two roots are mostly Vedic (*chāndasa*). (13) They are anudātta (unaccented). They do not take the augment *iṭ* after a vowel because they consist of a single syllable (*ekāc*). (13)

The four roots beginning with *āp* in the sense of "pervasion" (*vyāpti*) are *aniṭ* (without the *iṭ* augment). *āpnoti* ("he attains"); *āpat* (by Pāṇini III.1.55); *āptā* ("attained"). *Āpjñapṛdhām īt* (Pāṇini VII.4.55): *īpsati* ("he desires to attain"). *Ambhaḥ* ("water") is derived by [Uṇādi-sūtra IV.209]: *udake num bhau ca*. In the case of the suffix *lyap*, there is optionally the elision of *ṇi* after a root preceded by a light vowel, according to *vibhāṣāpa* (Pāṇini VI.4.56–57): *prāpya* or *prāpayya*. When *aṅ* would apply by *guroś ca halaḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.103), *ktin* is used instead of *āp* etc., according to *ābādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini III.3.94, vārttika 1): *āptiḥ* ("attainment"). (14)

The root *śak* means "to be able. One says *śaknoti* ("he is able") and *śaknuvanti* ("they are able"). Other forms have been explained under the *divādi* group (Pāṇini IV.1.78). With the suffix *san*, by the rule *mīmā-śaka-sahāṃ cca* (VII.4.54), one says *śikṣati*. In the aorist, *aśakat*; since the suffix *aṅ* would already be established here due to its inclusion in the *puṣādi* group (Pāṇini VII.2.51), the fact that it is marked with *ḷ* is for the sake of causing the *ātmanepada* endings in the sense of reciprocal action (*karmavyatihāra*) according to Pāṇini I.3.14: *vyatyaśakata*. By the rule *śakadhṛṣajñāglāghaṭarabhalabhakramasahārhāstyartheṣu tumun* (III.4.65), the suffix *tumun* is used: *śakto ghaṭaṃ kartum* ("able to make a pot"). The past passive participle is *śakitaḥ*. (15)

The roots *rādh* and *sādh* signify "accomplishment" (*saṃsiddhi*), which is the attainment of a result. Regarding the rule *rādhīkṣyor yasya vipraśnaḥ* (Pāṇini I.4.39): "He accomplishes for Caitra" (*caitrāya rādhnoti*). Regarding the rule *rādho hiṃsāyām* (VI.4.123), there is the substitution of *e* and the elision of the reduplication: "on the following day" (*aparedyuḥ*). According to the Kāśikā on *rādho hiṃsāyāṃ sanīsvaktavyāt* (VII.4.54): "he desires to injure" (*pratiritsati*). By the rule *ktin ābādibhyaḥ* (III.3.94, vārttika 1): "success" (*rāddhiḥ*). In the *divādi* class, according to *rādho 'karmakād vṛddhāv eva* (Dhātupāṭha IV.71): "he prospers" (*rādhyati*).

He accomplishes (*sādhnoti*), he desires to accomplish (*siṣātsati*). According to some, because it is not taught with the upadhmanīya (*aṣopadeśa*), it is *sisātsati*. From the root listed in the *nandigrahipacādigaṇa* (Pāṇini III.1.134), with the causative suffix (*ṇic*), comes *sādhanaḥ*; from *kṛvāpāj...* (Uṇādi I.1), the suffix *uṇ* gives *sādhuḥ*. In the *divādigaṇa* (Pāṇini IV.1.104), it is *sādhyati*. [Roots] ending in an udātta vowel that are marked with an indicatory letter *ṅ* (anudāttet) [are ātmanepada]. 17.17.

The root *aś* means "to pervade" (*vyāpti*). - *aśnute* (he pervades). - *aṣṭā* (past participle), *aśitā*. - By the rule *aśnoteś ca* (Pāṇini VII.4.72), the augment *nuṭ* is added: *vyānaśe* (he has pervaded). - By the rule *smipūṅranjvaśāṃ sani* (Pāṇini VII.2.74), the augment *iṭ* is added: *aśiśiṣate* (he desires to pervade). - By the rule *aṭyartyaśūrṇotīnāṃ* (Kāśikā on Pāṇini III.1.22), the suffix *yaṅ* is added: *aśāśyate* (he pervades repeatedly). - By the rule *kṛvāpāji* (Uṇādi I.1), the suffix *u* is added: *āśu* (quickly). - By the rule *śāv aśer āptāv* (Uṇādi I.45), the suffix *uran* is added: *śvaśuraḥ* (father-in-law). - By the rule *aśūpruṣi* (Uṇādi I.151), the suffix *kvan* is added: *aśvaḥ* (horse). - By the rule *aśe raśa ca* (Uṇādi II.75), the suffix *yuc* is added: [forming *āśā*, hope].

From the root *aś* [to pervade]: by the rule *raśanā, aśe raś ca* (Uṇ. IV, 46), the suffix *mi* is applied, yielding *raśmiḥ* (rein); by *aśipaṇāyyo ruḍāyalukau ca* (Uṇ. IV, 132), *rāśiḥ* (heap); by *artisṛdhṛdhami* (Uṇ. II, 103), the suffix *ani* is applied, yielding *aśaniḥ* (thunderbolt); by *manin* (Uṇ. IV, 146), *aśmā* (stone); by *aśer devane* (Uṇ. III, 65), the suffix *sa* is applied, yielding *akṣaḥ* (die); by *aśeḥ saran* (Uṇ. III, 70), *akṣaram* (syllable); by *aśer nid* (Uṇ. III, 156), the suffix *kṣi* is applied, yielding *akṣi* (eye); by *aśer devane yuṭ ca* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 190), *yaśaḥ* (fame).
In the *kryādi* class (*aśa* meaning "eating"), as in *aśnāti* (he eats). (18)

1. *P*: not after a root with an udātta vowel; 2. *S*: Candra-Dhātupāṭha IY 22; 3. *KC*: *ānaśe*; 4. *P*: *vane*, *KC*: *dhane*. V 142: *ṣṭigha* in the sense of leaping (*āskandana*). *stighnute* (19). Two roots with udātta vowels that are anudāttet: 19. *tika* and *tiga*. From here [V 143] up to the end of the *cam* group (28), nine roots are *seṭ* and take the *parasmaipada* endings.
And *dina*. Because of the word "and" (*ca*), [the suffix *ka* is applied] also after *āskandana*. [Thus: *tiknoti*, *tignoti*. By rule III.1.135, *tikaḥ*.

(20) *ṣagha* in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*). [Thus: *saghnoti*, *sisaghiṣati*, *siṣāghayiṣati*. According to Durga, this [root] is not taught with an initial *ṣ* (*aṣopadeśa*): [thus] *sisāghayiṣati*. Some say: *tika*, *tigha*, and *caṣagha* in the sense of injury: [thus] *tighnoti*, *caṣaghnoti*. (21)

The root *dhṛṣ* is used in the sense of boldness (*prāgalbhya*). One says *dhṛṇoti*. From it, *dhṛṣṭaḥ*, *pradhṛṣṭaḥ*, and *pradharṣitaḥ*; and [the neuter] *dhṛṣṭam* by him, [meaning] *dharṣitam*. According to the rule *niṣṭhā śīṅsvidi* (Pāṇini I.2.19), there is no *kittva* (the prohibition of guṇa and vṛddhi). By the rule *trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.140), one has *dhṛṣṇuḥ*. In the common language (*bhāṣā*), by the rule *śāsiyudhi* (Pāṇini III.3.130, 1), one has *yuc*: *durdharṣaṇaḥ*. By the rule *dhṛṣer dhiṣa ca saṃjñāyām* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.82), one has *kyuḥ*: [namely, *dhiṣṇyaḥ*].

*Dhiṣaṇā* means intellect (*dhī*). According to *śakadhṛṣajñā* (Pāṇini III.4.65), the suffix *tumun* is used: *dhṛṣṇoti bhoktum* ("he dares to eat"). According to *ṛtvigdadhṛg* (Pāṇini III.2.59), the form *dadhṛk* is derived. In the *curādi* class, *dhṛṣa* is listed as "to overpower" (X.306): *dharṣayati*. (22)

The root *dambh* means "to deceive. It forms *dabhnoti*. According to Pāṇini I.2.6 (as cited in the Kāśikā), there is the substitution of *kiṭ* for the roots *śranth*, *granth*, *dambh*, and *svañj*, and the elision of *na*: *debhuḥ*. By the rule VII.2.49 (*sanīvantardha*), the augment *iṭ* is optional: *didambhiṣati*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is not applied, by YH 4.56 (*dambha ic ca*), one forms *dhipsati* or *dhīpsati*. Regarding the rule I.2.10 (*halantāc ca*), when *kittva* applies, the class of consonants (*haljāti*) is taken as the basis. From the gerundive suffixes, we have *dabdhvā* or *dambhitvā*; and the past passive participle *dabdhaḥ*. The root *ṛdh* means "to increase" or "to prosper. It forms *ṛdhnoti*. In the *divādi* class (IV.135), it forms *ṛdhyati*; the specific applications of this root have already been stated in that very section. (24) 1.

In the *Chandas* [Vedic language], there is [the root] *ah* in the sense of pervading (*vyāpti*). *Ahnoti* (26). *Dagh* in the sense of striking down (*ghātana*). From here up to the end of the section on *gaṇas*, the scope of *chandas* applies. *Daghnōti* (27). *Camu* in the sense of eating (*bhakṣaṇa*). *Ācamnoti*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I.497), *ācāmati* (28). *Ṛkṣi*, *ciri*, *jiri*, *dāśa*, and *dṛ* in the sense of harming (*hiṃsā*). *Ṛkṣṇoti*; *ānarkṣa*.

Some say that *ṛṇoti* means "he destroys" (*kṣiṇoti*). [Others say] *ciriṇoti* and *jiriṇoti*; however, because of the rule *ekācāṃ ca cirer jirer* (cf. Pāṇini I.1.5), these do not possess an indicatory letter (*anubandha*). *Dāśnoti* and *dāśaḥ* [are derived from *dāś*]. *Dṛṇoti*. But Durga says: *tika tigha ṣagha ṛkṣa kṣi ri ciri jiri dāśa dru hiṃsāyām* ("*tika*, *tigha*, *ṣagha*, *ṛkṣa*, *kṣi*, *ri*, *ciri*, *jiri*, *dāśa*, *dru* are used in the sense of harming"). These are Vedic roots with restricted scope, like *jigharti* and others (Pāṇini III.1.48). Thus ends the *svādigaṇa* in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on the verbal roots conceived by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin.

1–25, cf. IV.86. 2. *caṣagha* (P). 3. Thus ends the *svādi-gaṇa* in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on roots (*dhātuvṛtti*) conceived by Kṣīrasvāmin. 143. VI. *tud* in the sense of "paining" (*vyathane*). From here until the end of the *kṛṣ* group (6), these six roots are *aniṭ* and *ubhayapadins* (taking both parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings). By the rule *tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ* (III.1.77), and because [the affix] is marked with *ṅ* by *sārvadhātukam apit* (I.2.4), it is treated as *ṅit*: *tudati*, *tudate*; future *tottā*. *pratodaḥ* ("goad"), *todaḥ* ("paining"). Optionally, by *āc chīnadyor num* (VII.1.80), [the feminine forms are] *tudatī* or *tudantī*. By *vidhvaruṣos tudaḥ* (III.2.35), the suffix *khaś* is applied [to form *vidhutudaḥ* and *aruṣtudaḥ*].

*vidhuntudaḥ* (the moon-eclipsing demon); *aruntudaḥ* (one who pierces the vital parts); by [Pāṇini III.2.28] *vātaśunītila*, we have *tilantudaḥ* (one who torments sesame seeds); with the suffix *kta*, [we have] *tunnaḥ* (VIII.2.42); by [Pāṇini III.2.182] *dāmnīśasa*, we have the suffix *ṣṭran*: *tottraṃ* (a goad); by [Uṇādi II.7] *pātṝtudi*, we have *thak*: *tutthaṃ* (a type of collyrium and a specific mineral). The root *ṇud* means "to impel. One impels (*praṇudati*), one impels for oneself (*praṇudate*). It cannot be used in the passive sense (*nottā*). By [Pāṇini VIII.2.56] *nudavidondatrā*, there is optionally the substitution of *ṇatva* (nasalization) in the past participle (*niṣṭhā*): *nuttaḥ* or *nunnaḥ*. From the roots *glā* and *nud*, the suffix *ḍau* is applied (cf. Uṇādi II.64): *nauḥ* (a ship).

The root *diś* is used in the sense of "bestowing" (*atisarjana*). Bestowing is relinquishment (*tyāga*). [It forms]: *diśati*, *diśate*. By the rule *ktin* (Pāṇini III.3.94): *diṣṭiḥ* (a measure), *vitastiḥ*. By the rule *ṛtvigdadhṛk* (Pāṇini III.2.59), the suffix *kvin* is applied: *dik* (direction). By the rule *nāmny ādiśigrahoḥ* (Pāṇini III.4.58), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied: *nāmādeśam āmantrayate* (he addresses him by name). *Diṣṭam* means fate (*daivam*). (3)

The root *bhrasj* means "to cook. By the rule *grahijyāvayi* (Pāṇini VI.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *bhṛjjati*, *bhṛjjate*. By the rule *bhrasjo ropadhayo ram anyatarasyām* (VI.4.47), the augment *ram* is optionally applied: *bhraṣṭā* or *bharṣṭā*. This [augment] is not desired in the scope of vocalization, because of the evidence of the forms *bhṛṣṭa* and *lucita* (cf. II.2.31, G.): [the optative is] *bhṛjjyāt*. [The perfects are] *babhrajja* or *babharja*; there is no distinction for the roots *vṛśc*, *pṛcch*, and *bhrasj* by the rule *vṛścatipṛcchatibhṛjjatīnām* (VI.1.16). By the rule *sanīvantardha* (VII.2.49), the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied.

*bibharjiṣati*, *bibhrajj-iṣati*, *bibhar-kṣati*, *bibhra-kṣati*. By the rule *vraśc-bhrasj-...* (VIII.2.36), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs: *bhṛṣṭaḥ*, *bhṛṣṭiḥ*. By the rule *prathi-mṛdi-bhrasj-ām saṃprasāraṇaṃ sa-lopaś ca* (Uṇ. I.29): *Bhṛguḥ*; it belongs to the *nyaṅkv-ādi* group (VII.3.53). From the roots *bhrasj*, *bhū*, *sū*, *yudh*, and *dhūñ*, with the *kit* suffix (cf. Uṇ. II.80): *bhṛjjanam*. With the suffix *lyuṭ* (III.3.115): *bhrājanam*, *bharjanam*. By the rule *bhrasj-i-gami-* (Uṇ. IV.159), the suffix *ṣṭran* is applied: *bhrāṣṭram* (4).

The root *kṣip* means "to throw" (*preraṇe*). One says *kṣipati* or *kṣipate*. By the rule *abhikṣipati*, *pratikṣipati*, *atikṣipati* (Pāṇini I.3.80), the *parasmaipada* [active voice] is used after the prefixes *abhi*, *prati*, and *ati*. By the rule *saṃpṛca* (Pāṇini III.2.142), one is called a *parikṣepī* ("one who surrounds"). By the rule *nindahiṃsa* (Pāṇini III.2.146), one is called a *parikṣepakaḥ* ("one who censures"). By the rule *trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.140), one is called *kṣipnuḥ* ("one who throws"). In the list beginning with *bhidādi* (Pāṇini III.3.104), there is *kṣipā*. By the rule *rak* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.13), [the form *kṣipaḥ* is derived].
From the root *kṣip*, by [Uṇādi-sūtra] II.108, *ani* with the augment *ki* is added: *kṣipaṇiḥ* or *kṣipaṇī*. In the *divādi* group (IV.14), it is *kṣipyati*.

(5) The printed edition of the Kāśikā (as well as Bo. reads *mṛṣṭaluñcitam*, whereas the very correct manuscript IOL No. 2440 indeed reads *bhṛṣṭalucitam*. The form *lucita* in this *gaṇa* (without the suffix *ñ*) is also attested by Mādhava I p. 214; *bhṛṣṭa* and *mṛṣṭa* are attested by Vardhamāna in the Gaṇaratnamahodadhi 78, VI.144.

The root *kṛṣ* is used in the sense of "plowing" (*vilekhana*). It takes both parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings: *karṣati* and *karṣate*. According to Pāṇini VI.1.59 (*anudāttasya cardupadhasyānyatarasyām*), the substitution of *ṛ* for *r* is optional: *karkṣyati* or *krakṣyati*. Regarding the aorist, Pāṇini III.1.44 (*spṛśamṛśakṛṣatṛpadṛpaḥ sij vā*) prescribes the optional use of the *sic* suffix: *akṛkṣat*, *akrākṣīt*, or *akārkṣīt*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I.1039), *karṣati* is listed, and the relevant grammatical rules have already been stated there. However, *kṛś* in the sense of "making thin" (*tanūkaraṇa*) belongs to the *Divādi* class (IV.117); it ends in a palatal (*tālavya*) and is marked with an *anudātta* and a *svarita* accent. (6) Anudāttas and Svaritets. (6)

The roots *ṛṣ* and *gatau* (to go). [The root] *udātta* is *udāttet* (accented on the first syllable). In *ṛṣati*, there is a single substitute *vṛddhi* by [Pāṇini] VI.1.91 (*upasargād ṛti dhātau*): *upārṣati*, *arṣitā*. By [Uṇādi] III.66 (*snuvraścikṛtyṛṣibhyaḥ kit*), [we have] *ṛkṣaḥ*; by [Uṇādi] IV.119 (*ik*), *ṛṣiḥ*; by [Pāṇini] III.3.94 (*ktin*), *ṛṣṭiḥ*; by [Uṇādi] III.123 (*ṛṣivṛṣibhyāṃ kit*), *ṛṣabhaḥ*; by [Pāṇini] VII.2.14 (*śvīdito niṣṭhāyām*), *ṛṣṭaḥ*. (7)

The root *juṣ* means "to take pleasure in" and "to serve. From here, four roots are *seṭ* (having the augment *iṭ*) and *ātmanepadin* (middle-voice). [Examples: *juṣate*; [future] *joṣitā*. [Absolutives] *joṣitvā*, *juṣitvā*. Because it has the marker *īt*, [the past passive participle is] *juṣṭaḥ* (Pāṇini VI.1.214). By [the rule] *eti-stu-śāsa-kyap* (Pāṇini III.1.109), the suffix *kyap* is applied: *juṣyaḥ*. [In the sense of] "those who enjoy together," *sajūḥ* (Pāṇini VI.2.66). (8) The root *ovijī* means "fear" and "trembling. [Examples: *udvijate*. By [the rule] *vija iṭ* (Pāṇini I.2.2), the suffix beginning with *iṭ* is *kit*: [future] *udvijitā*. By [the rule] *karaṇe halaś ca* (Pāṇini III.3.121), the suffix *ghañ* is applied: *vegaḥ* ("impulse"). [Past passive participle] *vignaḥ*. From the causative (*ṇyanta*), [one forms] *udvejitaḥ*. (9)

The root *olajī* (or *olasjī*) means to be ashamed. [It forms] *lajate*, *lajitā*; [and] *lajitaḥ*. Regarding *lagno*, however, it is correct according to the rule *lagnas tu lagnamliṣṭaḥ* (YH 2.18), which refers to that which is stuck (*sakta*). *Lagitaḥ* is something else. If [the root were] *īdit*, then its status as such would be useless; therefore, this is a *nipātana* (irregular formation) from *lager* (DhP I.823). For this very reason, Candra [states] *onajī* (Ca. Dh. VI.100): [from which we derive] *nagnaḥ*. [From the root *lajj*: *lajjate*, *lajjitā*. Since there is no purpose for these two roots in the *tudādi* class, their placement in the *bhvādi* class is appropriate. (10) These are the roots with raised initial vowels (*udātta*) that have a low-pitched final vowel (*anudāttet*). 11.

The root *ovraścū* means "to cut. From here until the end of the section (sūtra 96), there are three hundred roots that take the augment *iṭ* and are conjugated in the *parasmaipada*. By the rule *grahijyāvayi* (Pāṇini VI.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *vṛścati*, *vraṣṭā*, *vraścitā* (VII.2.35). In the case of *mūlavṛṭ* and *vṛkṇaḥ*, it should be stated that the substitution for the *niṣṭhā* [suffix] is established when there is the substitution of *ṣ* (VIII.2.6.7). By the rule *jṝvraścyoḥ ktvi* (VII.2.55), there is the augment *iṭ*: *vraścitvā*. From *vraśc* and *kṛṣ*, the suffix *kikan* is applied (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra II.40): *vṛścikaḥ* ("scorpion"). By the rule *snuvraści* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.66), the suffix *ksa* is applied: *vṛkṣaḥ* ("tree").

In the sense of "spreading" (*vyaca-sambhave*). [The root] *vyaci* (VI 1.16); by the rule *vyaceḥ kuṭāditvam anasi* (I 2.1 Kāś.), there is the designation *kuṭādi* for *vyaci* before a suffix beginning with *a*: *vicitā*. But not here: *uruvyacāḥ* (12). [The root] *vyaja* in the sense of "making a pretext" (*vyājīkaraṇe*). [One] *vyajati*. Because it is a *liṅga* (indicative mark) in the sense of making a pretext, there is an absence of *kutva* when the suffix *ghañ* is applied (III 3.18–19): *vyājaḥ* (12a). [The root] *ucchi* in the sense of "gleaning" (*uñche*). Gleaning (*uñcha*) is the picking up of grains. [One] *uñchati*; [the future participle] *uñchitā* (13). 1. Thirty; in K and C, "thirty" (*triṃśatis*).
145. VI. *ucchī* in the sense of "dawn. *Vivāsaḥ* means passing away. *Ucchati*, as in “the night has dawned” (*vyuṣṭā rātriḥ*).

The root *ṛch* is used in the senses of the dissolution of the senses and becoming embodied. It is used for the dissolution of the senses, for delusion (*moha*), and for becoming embodied. In the case of *ṛcchati*, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffix applies according to the rule *samo gamyṛchi* (Pāṇini I.3.29): *samṛcchate*. Regarding the form *ānarcha*: the *ām* suffix does not apply here because of the rule *ijāder gurumato ’nṛcha* (Pāṇini III.1.36). Thus, the form is *ānarcha*. (15)

*Mich* in the sense of agitation (*utkleśa*). Agitation means affliction. One agitates; the *Iramiḍas* say it is *picheti*. *Picchā* means gruel (*ācāma*). (16) *Jarj*, *jharj*, and *carc* in the sense of reviling. One reviles (*jarjati*); *jarjaraḥ*. *Jharjharaḥ*. And *carceti*—so says Durga.

(17) *Tvac* in the sense of covering (*saṃvaraṇa*). Covering means concealing. One covers (*tvacati*). With the suffix *kvip* (Pāṇini III.2.178), *tvak*; with the suffix *ac* (Pāṇini III.1.134), *tvacaḥ*. (18)

The root *ṛc* means "to praise. From *ṛcati*, with the suffix *kvip* (Pāṇini III.2.178), we derive *ṛk*. From *ānarca* and *ānṛcuḥ*. By the rule *arci-śuci-* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.109), the suffix *isi* is applied, yielding *arciḥ* (19).

The root *ubj* means "straightness" (*ārjava*). [In the forms] *ubjati* and *ubjijiṣati*, the *b* is not reduplicated because of the rule stating that "consonants following a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*) are not doubled" (Vārttika on Pāṇini 6.1.3). This root has *b* as its penultimate letter because it is established as such in *samudga* and other words; otherwise, if the *upadhmānīya* were the penultimate, the substitution of the voiced unaspirated stop (*jaś*) would be considered non-established (*asiddha*). From the rule *bhujanyubjau pāṇyupatāpayoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.61) and *ubjer bale balopaś ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.191), the suffix *asun* is applied with the elision of *bal*: thus, *ojas*. (20)

The root *ujjh* means "to abandon" (*utsarga*). One abandons (*ujjhati*); here the *d* and *p* are [the bases], and the change to *c* is according to the rule on technical derivations (*lākṣaṇikaṃ*, VIII. 4. 40). [Desiderative: *ujjijhiṣati*. With the suffix *ṇyat*: "The roots *bhid* and *udh* [form nouns] when referring to a river" (III. 1. 115); with the suffix *kvip* (III. 2. 178), [we have] *ut*. The root *lubh* means "to delude" (*vimohana*). Delusion is the act of confusing or agitating. [Present: *lubhati*. According to the rule "after *tīṣasū-*" (VII. 2. 48), the forms are *lobdhā* and *lobhitā*. By the rule "after *ubh* in the sense of deluding" (VII. 2. 54), the suffix *iṭ* is added: *vilubhitāḥ keśāḥ* ("the hair is disheveled"). In the *divādi* class, *lubh* in the sense of "covetousness" (IV. 128): *lubhyati*, *lubdhaḥ*. (22)

The root *ṛha* (ṛha5) is used in the senses of boasting, fighting, harming, and giving. It forms *ṛhati* and *arhayati*. The Dramiḍas [read] *riha*: they form *rihati* and *rehayati*. (23) The roots *ṛpha* and *ṛnpha* mean "to harm. They form *ṛphati* and *ṛmphati*. Because of the supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyāna*) for *ṛnpha* and others, the nasal *n* is elided by Pāṇini 6.4.24 (*aniditām...*), and then the augment *num* is added. According to some, this is done by the rule *tṛnphādīnām* (cf. 7.1.59, 1). (30) 1.

P: *jarca*, *jarcha*, *jarjha*, *jharja* in the sense of reviling (*paribhāṣaṇe*). [They form] *jarcati*, *jarchati*, *jarjhati*. *Jarjaraḥ*. *Jharjhati*; *jharjharaḥ*. Durga says *carceti*. 2P om. 3s I, 767. 4 All mss.; a scribal error for *kyapi*. 5 All mss. have *h* (not *ph*) VI 146. *tṛpha*, *tṛnpha* in the sense of satiating (*tṛptau*). [They form] *tṛphati*, [gerund] *tarphitvā*. *Tṛmphati*; by the rule *nopadhāt thaphāntād vā* (I, 2, 23), there is optionally *kittva*: [gerunds] *tṛphitvā*, *tṛmphitvā*. Some say *tṛpa*, *tṛnpha* (24, 25).

The roots *tupa*, *tumpa*, *tupha*, and *tumpha* mean "to injure. One forms *tupati*, *tumpati*, *tuphati*, and *tumphati*. The reading of *tump* and *tumph* in the *bhvādi* class (DhP I.432, 436) is redundant. According to Pāṇini VI.1.157 (with the Kāśikā), the augment *suṭ* is applied when preceded by *pra-* with the root *tump* and the cow as the agent: *prastumpati gauḥ*. [The roots] *dṛpha* and *dṛnpha* mean "to cause distress": [one forms] *dṛphati* and *dṛmphati*. (26–29)

*gupha* and *gunpha* mean "to tie" (*granthe*). [From *gupha*: *guphati*; having tied, *gophitvā* or *guphitvā*. [From *gunpha*: *gumphati*; according to rule I, 2, 23 (*nopadhāt thaphāntād vā*): *gophitvā* or *gumphitvā*. [With the suffix] *ghañ* (I, 3, 18–19): *gumpho bandhaḥ* ("a tying"). (31) *ubha* and *unbha* mean "to fill" (*pūraṇe*). [From *ubha*: *ubhati*; [the dual form] *ubhau* (III, 1, 135). [From *unbha*: *umbhati*; [future] *umbhitā*; [gerund] *umbhitvā*. (32)

*Śubha* and *śumbha* are used in the sense of beauty (*śobhā*). Precisely because of this irregular derivation (*nipātana*), *śobhā* is considered correct. [From the roots: *śubhati*, *śuśobha*, *śubham*, *aśobhīt*; in the *Bhvādi* class (I, 786): *śobhate*, *śuśubhe*, *aśubhat*. [With the suffix] *rak* (Uṇ. II, 13): *śubhram*. *Śumbhati*, *śuśumbha*; it belongs to the *tṛnphādi* group (VII, 1, 59, 1). In the *Bhvādi* class, there is a separate recitation for *śunbha* in the senses of "speaking" (*bhāṣaṇe*) and "injuring" (*hiṃsāyām*) (I, 460), due to the difference in meaning. In that case, it is a root with an initial *ṣ* (*ṣopadeśa*); some say it is used in the sense of "striking" (*sumbhati*) and "striking" (*sumbhanā*) and so forth (33).

The root *dṛbh* means "to tie" (*granthe*). It forms *dṛbhati*, and *dṛbdhaḥ*. By the rule *andūdṛnbhv* (Uṇ. I, 95), *dṛnbhūḥ* is formed, meaning "a snake. (34) The root *cṛt* means "to injure" and "to tie" (*hiṃsā-granthanayoḥ*). It forms *cṛtati* and *cṛttaḥ*. Regarding the future, by the rule *se 'sici kṛta* (Pāṇini VII, 2, 57), there is an optional *iṭ*: *cartiṣyati* or *cartsyati*. The designation *īdit* is for the purpose of making the prohibition of *iṭ* in the *niṣṭhā* (past participle) suffix non-obligatory according to the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VII, 2, 15); thus we have *patitaḥ* (fallen). Alternatively, it is for the sake of the *yaṅluganta* form: *carīcrttaḥ*. With the suffix *kvip* (Pāṇini III, 2, 178), we have *crt*; and with the suffix *yat* (Pāṇini III, 1, 97), we have *cartyam*. (35)

*Vidh* in the sense of arranging (*vidhāna*). *Vidhati*. With the suffix *asun* (Uṇ. IV, 188): *vedhāḥ* (36). *Jun* in the sense of going (*gati*). *Junati*. Durga reads *juḍeti* (37). *Mṛḍ* in the sense of delighting (*sukhana*), and *pṛḍ* as well. *Mṛḍati*; [the forms] *mṛḍaḥ*, *mṛḍam* [are formed]; by the rule *mṛḍamṛda* (I, 2, 7), the suffix *ktvā* is *kit*: *mṛḍitvā*. *Pṛḍati*; [the form] *parḍitvā* (38, 39). *Pṛṇ* in the sense of pleasing (*prīṇana*). *Pṛṇati*. By the rule *ke* (III, 1, 135): *pṛṇaḥ*; [in the expression] *lokasya pṛṇe* (VI, 3, 70, 4), because it means "filling the world" (*lokaṃ pṛṇati*), the augment *mum* is applied:
*lokaṃpṛṇaḥ* (40). *Mṛṇ* in the sense of harming (*hiṃsā*). *Mṛṇati*. *Mṛṇālam* (Uṇ. I, 117) (41). *Tuṇ* in the sense of crookedness (*kauṭilya*). *Tuṇati*. *Tundam* (42).
1. KC omits. 2. Before 24, 30. 3. All manuscripts read *cṛtitaḥ*, but cf. VII, 2, 15 Kāś. and VII, 2, 49 Kāś. 4. So all manuscripts; cf. Uṇ. IV, 98 and Hem. Uṇ. 170. 147. VI.
*puṇa* [is used] in the sense of action (*karman*) and in the sense of auspiciousness (*śubha*). From the root *puṇati*: *puṇya*. By [the rule] *ke* (III, 1, 135): *nipuṇaḥ* (43).

The root *muṇ* means "to perceive" (*pratijñāne*). One perceives (*muṇati*). (44) The root *kuṇ* means "sound" and "instrument. One makes a sound (*kuṇati*). By the rule *ig-upadhāt kit* (Uṇ. IV, 119), we have *kuṇiḥ*, meaning "one with a withered hand" (*kupāṇiḥ*). By the rule *kvādibhyaḥ kīt* (Uṇ. I, 114), we have *kuṇḍam*. In the Uṇādi list: *kuṇindaḥ* (IV, 85), *kuṇālam* (III, 76), and *kuṇapaḥ* (III, 143). (45) The root *śun* means "to go. It goes (*śunati*). *Śunakaḥ* means "dog"; it is formed by the suffix *kvun* (Uṇ. II, 32). *Śunaḥ* and *sīram*: thus, *śunāsīraḥ* (46).

The root *druṇ* is used in the senses of injury, motion, and crookedness. It forms *druṇati*. By [Pāṇini III.1.135] with the suffix *ke*, it becomes *druṇaḥ*; by *ghañ* [III.3.18–19]: *droṇaḥ* (a wooden trough), *droṇī* (a small boat).

*Ghuṇ* and *ghūrṇ* are used in the sense of wandering. It forms *ghuṇati*; *ghuṇaḥ* is a wood-worm, and *ghoṇā* (the nose). It forms *ghūrṇati*; *ghūrṇatī* and *ghūrṇantī* (feminine forms). In the *Bhvādi* class [Dhātupāṭha I.464–465], there are *ghoṇate* and *ghūrṇate* [48, 49]. *Sura* is used in the senses of sovereignty and shining. It forms *surati*; *suraḥ* (a god). Durga maintains that this is a root taught with a *ṣ* (a *ṣopadeśa*); thus [he gives the form] *suṣora* [50].

The root *kura* means "to sound. It forms *kurati*. From it come *koraka* (bud), *kura* (a type of bird), *kuraṅga* (deer), *kurara* (osprey), and by [Pāṇini VIII.2.79] *kuryāt*; [by VIII.2.51] *Kuru* (the name of a country). The roots *kṣura* and *khura* mean "to scratch. Scratching is cutting. *Kṣurati*; *kṣura* (razor). *Khurati*; *khura* (hoof). The root *mura* means "to envelop. *Murati*. *Mura* (the name of a demon); *murā* (a specific medicinal herb); *murmura* (embers).

*Ghur* [is used] in the sense of *bhīma* (terrible) and *artha* (meaning/purpose). *Ghurati*. With the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.19): *ghoraḥ*; *ghurghuraḥ* (55). 3. *Pur* [is used] in the sense of moving forward (*agragamana*). *Purati*. *Puram*, with the suffix *kvip* (III.2.178): *pūḥ*; *puruṣaḥ*. *Puru* means "much" (*bahu*) (56). *Bṛhū* [is used] in the sense of exertion (*udyama*). Exertion is lifting up (*uddharaṇa*). *Bṛhati*, *barhitā*, *barḍhā*. *Udbarhaḥ*, *barhaṇam*, *barhaḥ*; [the form] *parivṛḍhaḥ* [is used] in the sense of power (*prabhu*) (VII.2.21). In the *Bhvādi* class, *bṛh* is used in the sense of growth (*vṛddhi*) (I.771): *barhati* (57).

The roots *tṛhū*, *tṛṇhū*, *stṛhū*, and *stṛṇhū* mean "to injure. [In the *bhvādigaṇa*: *tṛhati*; [the forms] *tarhitā*, *taṛḍhā*; [and the noun] *tarhaṇam*. In the *rudhādigaṇa* (Pāṇini VI.1.18–19), under the root *tṛhi* meaning "to injure": *tṛṇeḍhi*, *tṛṇḍhaḥ*, *tṛṃhanti*; [also] *tṛṃhati*, *tṛṃhitā*, *taṛḍhā*. [And] *stṛhati*, *stṛṃhati*. Durga says that these two are *ṣopadeśa* (roots taught with an initial *ṣ*). The root *iṣu* means "desire. By Pāṇini VII.3.77 (*iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ*), [the *ṣ* becomes *ch*]: *icchati*. Regarding the suffix *san*, by Pāṇini VII.2.48 (*tīṣasaha...*), there is optional *iṭ*: [the forms] *eṣṭ̣ā*, *eṣitā*. [The word] *iṭ* [is derived from] *iṣyate*. [The mantra] *iṣe tvā*. All manuscripts read this; cf. Uṇādi-sūtra III.133 and Hemacandra’s Uṇādi-vṛtti 399.354 before 53.

*ūrje tvā* (Taittirīya Saṃhitā I.1.1.1 et passim); *bindur icchuḥ* (III.2.169); *iṣa āśvayujaḥ*; *iḍ* means food (*anna*), [the word *iḍā*] is formed with the suffix *ac* according to Pāṇini V.2.127; from the roots *iṣ* and *aś*, the suffix *takan* is applied (Uṇādi-sūtra III.148): *iṣṭakā*; from *iṣ* with the suffix *ksu* (cf. Uṇādi-sūtra III.157): *ikṣuḥ*; *icchā* is correct according to Pāṇini III.3.101; from the roots *śru*, *yaj*, *iṣ*, and *stu*, the suffix is applied in the sense of an instrument (cf. III.3.95, 3): *iṣṭiḥ*, *iṣṭaḥ*; in the *divādi* class, there is the root *iṣ* in the sense of "going" (IV.19).

*anviṣyati*, *iṣuḥ*; in the *kryādi* class, from *iṣ* with the sense of repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*), [we have] *iṣṇāti* (59). *miṣ* in the sense of rivalry: *miṣati*, *meṣitā*. By [the rule] *meṣo 'ci* (III, 1, 134) and *ke* (III, 1, 135), we have *āmiṣam*; by *ghañ* (I, 3, 18–19): *nimeṣaḥ* (60). *kil* in the senses of whiteness and playing: *kilati*. *keliḥ*; by *ke* (III, 1, 135), *kilakilā* is a sound, or it is an imitation of an indistinct sound; *kilāsam* is *sidhma* (leprosy) (61).

*Tila* means "to moisten. *Tilati*. By [Pāṇini III.1.135], *tilaḥ* (masc.). In the *curādi* group (X.67), *telayati* (62). *Cila* means "to wear" (*vasane*). *Cilati*. In the *pacādi* group (III.1.134), *celaḥ*, *celam*; by *celaṭ* (VI.3.43), [we have] *brāhmaṇicelī*, meaning "a despised Brāhmaṇī woman"; there is shortening by *gharūpakalpa-* (VI.3.43); by *celakheṭakaṭukakāṇḍaṃ garhāyām* (VI.2.126), there is the acute accent on the first syllable of the second member (63).

*cala* in the sense of sporting: *calati*, *calatī*, *calantī*. *cala* in the sense of trembling belongs to the *jvalādi* group (Pāṇini I.3.85): *calaḥ*, *cālaḥ*; by the rule *śapśyanor nityam* (VII.1.81), the augment *num* is added: *calantī*. In the sense of trembling, *cali* is *mit* (Pāṇini I.3.70): *calayati latām*. In the *curādi* group, *cala* means to support (X.68): *cālayati*. (64) *vila* in the sense of covering; it begins with a dental labial (*dantyoṣṭhya*). *vilati*. *āvilam*, *velā*. (66)

*ila*, in the sense of sending forth or casting (*svapna-kṣepaṇa*): *ilati*. *ilā* means "earth" (*bhūḥ*), as well as *elā* [cardamom]; *elayati* (65). *bila*, in the sense of splitting (*bhedana*): *bilati*. *bilālaḥ* (mongoose), *ābilam*, *bilmam*, *bilvam* (67). *ṇila*, in the sense of hiding or being dense (*gahana*): *praṇilati* (68). *hila*, in the sense of making a gesture of contempt or coquetry (*hāva-karaṇa*): *hilati*; *helā* (69). *mila*, in the sense of joining or uniting (*śleṣaṇa*)—so says Durga: *milati*; *melaḥ* (71). *śila* and *ṣila*, in the sense of gathering or picking up grain (*uñcha*): *śilati*; *śilam*, *śilā* (stone); *silam*, *selu* (the *śleṣmātaka* tree) (70).

*likha* means "to write" or "the arrangement of letters. One writes (*likhati*). From the root *likh*, with the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.18–19), we have *lekhya* ("that which is to be written") and *lekha* ("writing"); with the prefix *vi-*, *vilekha*. From the *bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III.3.104), we have *lekhā* (72). The root *kuṭ* means "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*). One crooks (*kuṭati*). By the rule *gāṅkuṭādibhyo 'ñṇin ṅit* (Pāṇini I.2.1), the suffixes beginning with *ñ* and *ṇ* are treated as having the marker *ṅ*; thus, the future participle is *kuṭitā*. Examples include: *utkuṭa* ("crouching"), *kuṭa* ("pot"), *koṭara* ("hollow of a tree"), *kuṭara* ("a type of tree"), *koṭi* ("tip, peak"), and *kuṭīra* ("small hut").

1. Cf. Hemacandra, *Uṇādisūtra* 575. 2. KC: *tilāḥ*. 3. KC: "The final syllable of the compound is udātta"; P omits this. 4. All Mss.: *āvelam*. 5. P: "in the senses of sleeping and throwing. 6. KC: "in the sense of producing a state (*bhāva*). 7. KC: "before *helā* in the *bhidādi* group. 149. VI.

By the rule *uṣikuṭi* (*Uṇādisūtra* III, 142), the suffix *kapan* is applied: *kuṭapaḥ* means "a measure of food. From a root with *i* as an upadhā, the suffix *ki* is applied (cf. *Uṇādisūtra* IV, 119): *kuṭiḥ*. From *kuṭi* and *kuṣi*, the suffix *kmalan* is applied (*Uṇādisūtra* IV, 186): *kuṭmalam* and *kuṭilaḥ*. How is *kuṭitvā* [formed]? For the status of *kit* is barred by the rule *na ktvā seṭ* (*Aṣṭādhyāyī* I, 2, 18); however, the status of *ṅit* is not [barred] (73).

The root *puṭ* means "to join together" (*saṃśleṣaṇe*). It forms *puṭati*. With the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.18–19), we have *puṭaḥ*, *puṭī*, *poṭā* (a hermaphrodite), *napuṃsakaṃ poṭakam* (a neuter child). In the *curādi* class, *puṭ* means "to crush" (*saṃcūrṇane*) (X.73), and likewise in the sense of "shining" (*bhāsārtha*) (X.213):

*poṭayati*. (74) Regarding *luṭ*, Durga says it means "agitating" (*viloḍana*): *luṭati*, *luṭitā*; having agitated (*luṭitvā*). Some say *luṭha* means "joining together" (*saṃśleṣaṇa*) (87). *Kuc* means "contraction" (*saṃkocane*). It forms *saṃkucati*; because the meaning involves "gathering together," the prefix *sam-* functions as an upasarga; *saṃkucitā*. Having contracted (*kucitvā*), *kucau*. In the *bhvādi* class, in the sense of "mixing thoroughly" (*saṃparcanādi*) (I.910), it forms *saṃkocati*. (75)

*Guj* in the sense of "sound": *gujati*, *gujitā*. In the *bhvādi* class (I, 218): *gojati*, *gojitā* (76). *Guḍa* in the sense of "protection": *guḍati*. *Guḍā* is an elephant's armor; *guḍaḥ* is a sweet substance, the earth, or a pair (*golakaṃ*); *gulikā* is a kind of pearl (77). *Ḍip* in the sense of "throwing": *ḍipati*, *ḍipitā*. In the *divādi* class (IV, 121): *ḍipyati*, *ḍepitā*; in the *curādi* class (X, 138): *ḍepayati* (78).

*Chur* means to cut (*chedane*). *Churati*, *ācchuritam*, *churyāt*; there is no lengthening [of the vowel] because of the rule *rvor na bhakurchurām* (Pāṇini VIII.2.79); *churikā*. *Sphuṭa* means to blossom or expand (*vikasane*). *Sphuṭati*, *sphuṭitā*, *asphuṭīt*; *sphuṭaḥ*. In the *Bhvādi* class, *sphuṭir* is used in the sense of breaking apart (*viśaraṇe*) [I.352]: *sphoṭati*, *sphoṭitā*, *asphuṭat*, *asphoṭīt*; *sphoṭaḥ*. *Muta* means to throw or to crush (*ākṣepapramardanayoḥ*). *Muṭati*, *muṭitā*. In the *Bhvādi* class [I.346], *moṭati*; [in the phrase] *vimoṭitakarāṅguliḥ* (with fingers crushed); in the *Curādi* class [X.73], *moṭayati*. (81)

The root *truṭ* means "to break. By the rule *vā bhras-bhlāśa* (Pāṇini III.1.70), the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied: *truṭyati* or *truṭati*; *truṭitā*; *troṭayati*. (82) *tuṭ* means "the act of quarreling": *tuṭati*; *tuṭitā*. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.119, the suffix *ik* is added: *tuṭiḥ*; *toṭakaṃ*. (83) *cuṭ* and *chuṭ* mean "to cut": *cuṭati*; *uccoṭanaṃ*. *chuṭati*; *choṭikā*. (84)
*juḍ* in the sense of binding: *juḍati*, *juḍitā*. *juḍ* in the sense of going (37): *juḍati*, *joḍitā* (85). 1P *loṭana* (rolling); 2P *prakṣepe* (throwing), V I 150.

*kaḍ* means "to eat. Eating is the act of consuming. *kaḍati*, *kaḍyate*. [Derivatives: *kalamaḥ* (a rice-plant), *kaḍaṅgaraḥ* (chaff), *kaliḥ* (strife), *kalahaḥ* (quarrel), *kaḍatram* (a wife and the hips), *kaḍitram* (gambling and a writing-skin). Because there is no fruit [of these meanings] in the *kuṭādi* group, this [root] has fallen away from that class. (86) *kuḍa* means "childishness. *kuḍati*. [Derivatives: *kuḍaḥ* (a tree), *kuḍaṅgaḥ* (a bower). (89) *kṛḍa* means "solidity. Solidity is density. *kṛḍati*. (88) *guḍa* means "obstruction. *guḍati*. [Derivative: *ayoguḍaḥ* (an iron ball). Durga reads it as *ghuṭa*.

*Ghuṭikā* is the ankle bone. (91) *Tuḍa* means to break. Breaking is splitting or separating. [From this root: *tuḍati*, *toḍaḥ*, *toḍanam*, *tuḍiḥ*. (92) *Sthuḍa* and *thuḍa* mean to cover. *Sthuḍati*; *sthūlaḥ* (a thick cloth) and *paṭakuṭiḥ* (a tent). *Thuḍati*. (94. 93) *Duḍa* and *huḍa* mean to sink. *Duḍati*; *doḍaḥ*, *dolā* (a swing). *Huḍati*.

*hoḍi*, *huḍa*, *huḍu*. According to some, *kruḍa* [is also used]. *vruḍa*, *bhruḍa* in the sense of covering: *vruḍati*, *bhruḍati*. *sphara*, *sphura*, *sphala*, *sphula* in the sense of moving: *spharati*; *spha-* [sphurati].

*Raḥ*; [the suffix] *ra* is applied after the root *sphāy-* according to *Uṇ.* I.13 (*sphāraḥ*). It quivers: *sphuraḥ*, a pustule. It strikes: *āsphālaḥ*, *āsphālanā*. Regarding the roots *sphur-* and *sphul-*, there is optionally the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* after the prefixes *niḥ*, *nir*, and *vi* (Pāṇini VIII.3.76): *niḥsphurati*, *niḥṣphurati*. After the prefix *vi*, there is optionally the substitution of *t* for *r* before the causative suffix *ṇi* (Pāṇini VI.1.54): *visphārayati*, *visphorayati*. In the past passive participle *sphuritam*, there is optionally the substitution of *t* for *r* before the suffix *ghañ* (cf. VI.1.47): *sphuritvam*, *sphulitvam*.

*Sphāraḥ*, *sphoraḥ*, *sphālaḥ*, *spholaḥ*—thus both [roots] have been handed down through negligence. [The root] *sphul* is used in the sense of "accumulation" (*saṃcaya*). It forms *sphulati*; [the word] *sphuliṅgaḥ*. (95, 96) These [roots] end in acute (*udātta*) vowels and are marked with the acute accent (*udāttet*). [The root] *gurī* is used in the sense of "exertion" (*udyama*). It is acute (*udātta*) and has an anudātta vowel as its indicatory letter (*anudāttet*). It forms *gurate*, *guritā*. [The past participle] *gūrṇaḥ*. After the verb *apagur* (in the sense of "threatening"), when followed by the suffix *ṇamul*, there is optionally the substitution of *v* for *r*: *apagāram apagāram*, *apagoram apagoram*. In the *curādi* group (X, 155), one forms *āgūrayate* from the root *gūr*. (103) 5

The root *ṇū* means "to praise. From this [root], four forms are with the augment *iṭ*: *praṇuvati*, *nuvitā*, *nūtaḥ*. Because of the rule *śryukaḥ kiti* (Pāṇini VII.2.11), the augment *iṭ* does not occur; others, however, say *nuvita*, because the status of being a *kit* is set aside by its being a *ṅit*. Similarly for *dhūta*, *dhuvitā*, and so forth. (104) The root *dhū* means "to shake. [In the present tense: *dhuvati*. In the *svādi* group (V.9), [it becomes] *dhūnoti* or *dhunoti*; in the *kryādi* group (IX.17), *dhunāti*. (105) 1 cf. Uṇādisūtra IV.84 and Hemacandra’s Uṇādivṛtti 347; 2 87 before 75; 3 all manuscripts read thus; 4 P adds: "an obstacle to the accomplishment of mantras"; 5 99–102 before 95.

151. *gū* in the sense of voiding excrement: *guvati*, *guvitā*. [The word] *gūtha* is formed by [the rule] *tithapṛṣṭ̣hagūtha* (Uṇ. II, 12). (106) *dhru* in the senses of movement and steadiness: *dhruvati*. By [the suffix] *ac* (Pāṇini III.1.134), [we have] *dhruvaḥ*; [the forms] *dhruvitā* and *dhrutaḥ*, *dhruvitaḥ*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.990), in the sense of steadiness, [it is] *dhravati*. (107)

Acute (udātta): 119. *kuṅ* in the sense of sound. From here on, seven roots are aniṭ (lacking the iṭ augment). *kuvate*, *kutā*. Some say *kūṅ*: *ākuvitā*, *ākūtam*. (*vṛt*) The roots beginning with *kuṭ* have been enumerated.

The root *pṛṅ* is used in the sense of exertion (*vyāyāma*). Exertion means effort (*udyoga*). [The forms] *vyāpriyate*, *vyāpṛtaḥ*, and *vyāpāraḥ* occur because the term "exertion" (*vṛtti*) is included in the definition [of the root's meaning]. (109)

The root *mṛṅ* means "to die. From the rule *mriyater luṅliṅoś ca* (Pāṇini I.3.61), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffix is applied: *amṛta*, *mṛṣīṣṭa*. Or, for this very reason, some have taught it as being marked with *ṅ* (indicating the *taṅ* suffix). [Examples: *mamāra*, *mariṣyati*. [Derivatives: *Māraḥ*, *mārakaḥ*; *abhimaraḥ* in the sense of sharpness (cf. Amarakośa III.3.53); *marma*, *marmaraḥ*; *amaraḥ* from the *pacādi* group (III.1.134); and by the rule *bhujimṛṅbhyāṃ yuktyukau ca* (Uṇādi III.21): *mṛtyuḥ*; by the rule *bhṛmṛśī* (Uṇādi I.7), *uḥ*: *maruḥ*; by the rule *mṛgror utiḥ* (Uṇādi...).

I, 96): From the roots *marut* and *mṛkaṇi*, the suffix *īci* [is applied] (Uṇ. IV, 70): *marīciḥ*; *marūka* means "biting" or "tearing. From *has*, *mṛg*, etc., the suffix *tan* [is applied] (Uṇ. III, 86): *martaḥ*; with the suffix *ya* in the sense of the base itself (cf. V, 4, 36, 7): *martyaḥ*. (110) *ri* and *pi* mean "to go. *riyati*; *piyati*; *pikaḥ* means "cuckoo. (111, 112) *dhi* means "to hold. *dhiyati*; *dhetā*. (113) *kṣi* means "to dwell" and "to go. *kṣiyati*; *kṣetā*. *Kṣayya* and *jayya* [are used] in the sense of "possible."

In the sense of "to be destroyed" (*rthe*), [the suffix *yat* is applied]: *kṣayyaḥ*; otherwise, *kṣeyaḥ*. In the sense of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) when not meaning "to be destroyed," there is lengthening [of the vowel] by Pāṇini VI.4.60; and by VIII.2.46, the substitution of *na* for the final *s* of the root *kṣi*: *kṣīṇaḥ*. In the senses of "cursing" or "dejection" (*vākrośadainyayoḥ*), [the substitution of *na* applies]: *jālmaḥ kṣīṇāyur* ("a wretch whose life is exhausted"), *kṣitāyuḥ*, *tapasvī kṣīṇaḥ* ("an ascetic whose penance is exhausted"), *kṣitaḥ*. By Uṇādi-sūtra I.139 (*artistusv... iti man*), the suffix *man* is added: *kṣemam*. By Uṇādi-sūtra IV.158 (*ṣṭran*), [the suffix *ṣṭran* is added]: *kṣetram*. [The suffix] *itiḥ* is added. By Pāṇini III.3.56 (*er ac*), the suffix *ac* is added.

*kṣaya-* in the sense of "house" [is derived from] *kṣi* in the *bhidādi* group (Pāṇini I.3.104); *kṣiyā* [is derived from] *kṣi* in the *svādi* group (V.30); *kṣiṇoti* [is derived from] *kṣi* in the *bhvādi* group (I.255); and *kṣayati*. (114) The roots with anudātta accent are as follows: 126. *ṣū* in the sense of "impelling. [From this root: *suvati*. By the rule *upasargāt sunotisuvatiḥ* (VIII.3.65), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*: *abhiṣuvati*. [Derivatives include: *savitā*, *soṣūyate*, *susūṣati*. By the restrictive rule *stautiṇyor eva ṣaṇi* (VIII.3.61), the substitution of *ṣ* does not occur [in the case of *su* when followed by the suffix *san*]. (115)
1. *Paddit-bhv-ādi* (I.997) *gavati*. 2. Cf. *Uṇ.* IV.39 and *Hem. Uṇ.* 58. 3. KC: *vi*, *viyati*, *vetā* (*v* and *dh* are easily confused in Śāradā script; cf. Bühler, *Palaeographie*, §25, B 6).

The root *kṝ* means "to scatter. From *kirati*: by the rule *harṣajīvikā-* (Pāṇini I.3.21), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied; and by *apāc catuṣpācchakuniṣv ālekhane* (VI.1.142), the augment *suṭ* is added: *apaskirate vṛṣabho hṛṣṭaḥ* ("the bull, being joyful, wallows"), *apaskirate kukkuṭo bhakṣārthī* ("the cock, seeking food, scratches"), *apaskirate śvāśrayārthī* ("the dog, seeking shelter, digs"). From *kirati* in the sense of "reaping" (*lavana*), *suṭ* is added [by VI.1.140]: *upaskāraṃ Madrakā lunanti* ("the Madrakas reap in a manner that involves preparation"). In the sense of "injury" (*hiṃsā*), [the augment *suṭ* is added] after *prati* as well (VI.1.141).

"O fool, let there be *upaskāra* for you, let there be *pratiskāra*; let there be death! [Thus he said]; [the verb] *praticaskare* [is used] with the fingernails (*śiśupālav.* I.47). Regarding the rule *kiraś ca pañcabhyaḥ* (VH 2.75), the long vowel is not desired after the suffix *san* with the augment *iṭ*, according to *asyeṭo vṝto vā* (VII.2.38): thus *vicikariṣati*, and optionally *vicikīrṣati*. By the rule *igupadha* (III.1.135), the suffix *ka* is applied: *kiraḥ* means "boar"; and by *ki11ś ca* (Uṇ.).

From the root *kṛ* with the suffix *kyu*: *kiraṇaḥ* ("ray"), according to *viṣkiraḥ śakunir vikiro vā* (VI, 1, 150) and *kṝpṝvṛji* (Uṇ. II, 81); with the suffix *abha*: *karabhaḥ* ("young camel"), according to *kṝśṝśalibhya abhaḥ* (Uṇ. III, 122); with the suffix *unan*: *karuṇaḥ* ("compassionate") and *karuṇā* ("pity"), according to *kṝvṛtṝdāribhya unan* (cf. Uṇ. III, 53); with the suffix *īṣan*: *karīṣaḥ* ("dry cow-dung"), according to *kṝtṝbhyām īṣan* (Uṇ. IV, 26); with the suffix *īran*: *karīram* ("sprout"), according to *kṝśṝpṝkaṭi* (Uṇ. IV, 30); and with the suffix *ki*: [from] *kṝ* and *gṝ*, according to *kṝgṝbhyāṃ kiḥ* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 142).

From the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, and *kṛpi*, the suffix *īṭan* is applied (cf. Uṇ. IV, 184): *kirīṭam* (diadem). From the roots *kṝ*, *vṝ*, and *jṝ*, the suffix *naḥ* is applied (cf. Uṇ. III, 10): *karṇaḥ* (ear/organ of hearing). From the roots *kṝ* and *gṝ*, the suffix *uc* is applied (cf. Uṇ. I, 25): *Kuruḥ* (the Kuru country). From the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, *pṝ*, *vṛ*, and *cāt*, the suffix *ṣvarac* is applied (cf. Uṇ. II, 123): *kaivaraḥ* (fisherman). From the root *kṝ* with the meaning "to scatter grain," the suffix *ghañ* is applied (Pāṇini III, 3, 30): *utkāraḥ* (a heap of grain), *nikāraḥ*; elsewhere, *utkaraḥ* and *nikaraḥ*.
In the sense of excrement, *avaskaraḥ* is used (Pāṇini VI, 1, 148); otherwise, it is *avakaraḥ* (rubbish).

The root *gṛ* means "swallowing" (*nigaraṇa*), which is the act of gulping down. From the forms *girati* and *gilati*, the suffix *laṭ* is applied according to the rule *aci vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VIII.2.21). According to *gro yaṅi* (VIII.2.20), the form *nijegilyate* is derived. The future form is *garitā*. The desiderative forms are *jigariṣati* and *jigīrṣati*. By the rule *avād gras* (I.3.51), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used: *avagirate* and *avajigariṣate*; there is no optional substitution of *vṝto vā* (VII.2.38). By the rule *samaḥ pratijñāne* (I.3.52), the *taṅ* endings are used: *saṃgirate*. And by the rule *nigaraṇacalana-arthebhyaś ca* (I.3.87), [the causative] *nigārayati* is formed.

In the *pac-ādi* group (Pāṇini III.1.134), there is *gara-*; *ajagara-* [is formed] from the root *gṛ* with the prefix *a-* as an upapada, following the rule for roots beginning with *a-* when no upapada is present. Since the suffix *aṇ* would otherwise apply by the rule "when a karma-upapada is present, by way of exception" (I.4.2), [the formation of *ajagara-* requires this specific list]. From *unni-* and *gṛ* (Pāṇini III.3.29): *udgāra-* and *nigāra-*. By the suffix *ap* (III.3.57): *gara-* and *gala-*. By means of *ghañ* due to *bāhulaka* (diversity of application) (see X.392): *nigāra-* and *nigāla-*. *Na-gāra-* becomes *agāram* (house). From *mṛ* and *gṛ*, the suffix *uti* (Uṇādi I.96): [forms *marut* and *garut*].

*garut* is a wing; *garmut* is grass (*Uṇ. I.97*); from *hasi-mṛ-gr-* etc., *tan* [is added]: *gartaḥ* (a pit); from *kṝ-gṝ-bhyāṃ kiḥ* (cf. *Uṇ. IV.142*): *giriḥ* (a mountain); from *mudi-groḥ gaggau* (*Uṇ. I.127*): *Gargaḥ* (a proper name); from *arti-gṝ-bhyāṃ bhan* (*Uṇ. III.152*): *garbhaḥ* (the womb/fetus); from *śevāyahva* (*Uṇ. I.154*): *grīvā* (the neck). (117) 1 K P apaskāraṃ 2 K P apaskāras 3 all manuscripts ac 153 VI.

Acute (udātta): 129. *dṛṅ* in the sense of respect (*ādara*), and *dhṛṅ* in the sense of staying (*sthāna*). These two are grave (anudātta). Regarding "respect" (*ādara*), because it is taken as a specific term (*āgrahaṇa*), we have: *ādriyate*, *ādartā*, *ādidariṣate*. From the rule *eti-stu-śāsa-kyap* (Pāṇini III, 1, 109), the suffix *kyap* is applied: *ādṛtyam*; *dṛtiḥ* means a leather bag (*bhastrā*). From the causative (*ṇyantāt*) of *dṛ*, with the suffix *khac* by the rule *pūḥ-sarvayor dāri-sahoḥ* (Pāṇini III, 2, 41), we have *Puraṃdaraḥ*. From the rule *grahi-vṛ-dṛ-niścigamaśca* (Pāṇini III, 3, 58), the suffix *ap* is applied: *ādaraḥ*. From the roots *dṛ* and *bhṛ*, the suffix *bhaḥ* is applied (cf. Uṇādi III, 151): *darbhaḥ*. *Dhriyate*, *dhartā*, *didhariṣate*. Other forms belong to the *bhvādi* class (I, 1009): *dharate* (sūtras 118, 119).

The root *prach* is used in the sense of desiring to know (*jñīpsā*). *Jñīpsā* means the desire to know (*jijñāsā*). From this point up to the root *ṣad*, fifteen roots are *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and take the *parasmaipada* endings. By the rule *grahijyāvayi* (Pāṇini VI.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *pṛcchati*. By the rule *samo gamyṛchiprachi* (I.3.29), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *saṃpṛcchate*. By the rule *āṅi nuprachyos* (I.3.21.6), the *taṅ* endings are applied: *āpṛcchate*. [In the desiderative], *pipṛcchiṣati*. By the rule *rudavida* (I.2.8), the suffix is *kit*: [e.g., *viditvā*].

Having asked [the question], one who asks is a *śabdaprāṭ* (one who brings forth words), derived from the root *vac* with the suffix *kvip* according to Pāṇini III.2.178 (Kāśikā). A *prāḍvivāka* (judge) is a decider; the substitution of *k* for *v* occurs because the root belongs to the *nyaṅku*-class (VH 3.53). The word *praśnaḥ* (question) is formed with the suffix *naṅ* according to Pāṇini III.3.90. By Pāṇini VI.4.19 (*chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca*), the vowel *u* is replaced by *ū*; and by the rule *pracher anaṅi* (Kāśikā on VI.1.16), there is no *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution). (120) *vṛt*. The five roots beginning with *kṝ* have been explained.

*Sṛj* in the sense of emission (*visarga*). [In the present tense: *sṛjati*, [in the agentive form: *sraṣṭā*. By the rule *vraścabhrasja* (VIII, 2, 36), the *ṣ* is substituted [for the *j*]. Regarding *sṛji-yuji-dhūñām karmavadbhāvaḥ śyaṃś ca* (cf. III, 1, 87, 15): "The roots *sṛj*, *yuj*, and *dhūñ* behave like reflexive objects (*karmavat*), and the suffix *śyan* is applied. Thus: *sṛjyati rajjuḥ svayam eva* ("the rope emits itself"). Regarding *vibhāṣā sṛjidṛśos thali* (VII, 2, 65): "There is optionally the augment *iṭ* after the suffix *thal* following *sṛj* and *dṛś*": *sasarjitha* or *sasraṣṭha*. When the suffix *am* is applied by *sṛjidṛśor jhaly am akiti* (VI, 1, 58), there is *vṛddhi* substitution by *vadavraja* (VII, 2, 3): *asrākṣīt*. In the *uṇādi* list (I, 16), [the word] *rajjuḥ* [is formed] (121).

The root *majj* means "to purify. Through the sense of purification, both bathing (*snāna*) and immersion (*vruḍana*) are indicated. In the form *majjati*, the augment *num* is applied by the rule *masjinaśor jhali* (Pāṇini VII.1.60). In the gerundive *maṅktā*, *num* is optionally applied before the suffix *ktvā* by the rule *jāntanaśāṃ vibhāṣā* (VI.4.32); thus we have *maṅktvā* or *maktvā*. By the rule *oditaś ca* (VIII.2.45), the substitution of *n* for *j* occurs, resulting in *magnaḥ*. From the suffix *athuc* (III.3.89) and the rule *guroś ca halaḥ* (III.3.103), we derive *majjathuḥ* and *majjanam*. According to the *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.158, which states *śvan-kṣan-...*, the word *majjā* denotes the marrow within the bone (*asthi-sāra*). [The same suffix applies to] *bhṛmṛśītr...* (*Uṇādi-sūtra* I.158).

I. 7) *ity uḥ*: *madguḥ* (water-fowl); by virtue of being included in the *nyaṅkv-ādi* group (Pāṇini VI. 1. 3. 53), there is the substitution of *ku* for *g*, and by the rule *masjer num ca* (Uṇādi IV. 77), the suffix *ūṣan* is added: *mañjūṣā* (a box, chest). The root *ruj* means "to break. It takes the form *rujati*. The past passive participle is *rugṇaḥ*. By the rule *padaruja* (Pāṇini III. 3. 16), the suffix *ghañ* is added in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*): *rogaḥ* (disease). In the *bhid-ādi* group (Pāṇini III. 3. 104), the feminine suffix *aṅ* is added: *rujā* (sickness) and *ruk* (pain). [The suffix *u* is added] after the prefix *ud* when meaning "on the bank" (cf. Uṇādi IV. 183 and Hemacandra’s Uṇādi 651). 2) *P*: the desire to know; 3) the locative case of *uktvā*.

VI 154: From the roots *ruj* and *vah*, the suffix *khaś* is applied (Pāṇini III 2, 31): *kūlamudrujaḥ* ("one who breaks the bank"). By the rule *nahivṛtivṛṣi...* (VI 3, 116), there is lengthening of the vowel: *vīruk* ("growing upwards"). From the root *ruc* with the prefix *rukmam* (cf. Dhātupāṭha I 781).

(123) The root *bhujo* is used in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*). *nirbhujati*. *bhugnaḥ* ("bent"); *bhogaḥ* ("the body of a serpent"). Because it moves by means of crookedness (*bhuja*), i.e., by coiling, it is called *bhujagaḥ* or *bhujaṃgaḥ* ("serpent"). In the *rudhādi* class, the root *bhuja* is used in the senses of "protecting" and "eating" (Dhātupāṭha VII 17): *bhunakti*, *bhuṅkte*. (124)

*chup* in the sense of touching: *chupati*, *choptā*. (125) *ruś* and *riś* in the sense of harming: *ruśati*, *arukṣat*; *riśati*. These two end in palatals (*tālavya*); because they are taught in the *bhvādi* class (I, 724–725), they end in retroflexes (*mūrdhanya*): *roṣati*, *reṣati*. In the *divādi* class, *ruṣ* in the sense of angering (IY, 120): *ruṣyati*. (126) *liś* in the sense of moving: *liśati*, *leṣṭā*. In the *bhvādi* class (? see IY, 70), *liś* in the sense of becoming small: *leśati*, *leśaḥ*. (127)

*Spṛś* means "to touch. It is conjugated as *spṛśati*, *spraṣṭā*, *sparṣṭā*. By the rule *anudāttasya cardupadhasyānyatarasyām* (Pāṇini VI.1.59), there is optionally the augment *am*; and by *spṛśamṛśakṛṣatṛpadṛpaḥ sij vā* (Hl. 1.44.7), the *sij* augment is optional in the aorist: *aspṛkṣat*, *asprākṣīt*, *aspārkṣīt*. By the rule *padaruja* (Pāṇini III.3.16), the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*), yielding *sparśaḥ* in the meaning "one who touches" or "that which is touched. By *spṛśo ’nudake kvin* (Pāṇini III.2.58), the suffix *kvin* is applied [to form *spṛk*]. By *kvinpratyayasya kuḥ* (Pāṇini VIII.2.62), the final consonant is changed to *k*.

Thus, there is *kutva* [the substitution of *k* for *s*]; otherwise, by the rule *vraścādi-* (Pāṇini VIII.2.36), there would be *ṣatva* [the substitution of *ṣ*] according to *chaśāṃ ṣaḥ*. Consequently, by internal affinity (*antarya*), *ṣ* would become *kh*, and by *khasya vāvasāne* (VIII.4.56), *kh* would become *k* through *cartva*; or alternatively, it would become *g* through *jaśtva*. Thus, the following textual examples would be incorrect: *pādaspṛk* and *udakasparśaḥ*. Furthermore, from the root *spṛś* with the suffixes *śvan* and *śuṇ* and the replacement of the root by *pṛ* (Uṇādi V.27), we derive *pārśvam* and *parśuḥ*. From *tithapṛṣṭha-* (Uṇādi II.12), we derive *pṛṣṭham*. (128)

The root *viccha* means "to go. By the rule *gupū-dhūpa-vicchi-āyaḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.28), the suffix *āya* is applied: *vicchāyati*. The inclusion of *vicch* in the list of roots beginning with *tud* (the *tudādi* class) is a sign (*liṅga*) that the suffix *āya* is not invariably present even before a *sārvadhātuka* affix, just as in the case of *paṇati*: *vicchati*, *vicchatī*, *vicchantī*; and thus the *Bhāṣya* states that [the suffix] is always present when *śap* follows. The Āryas hold that there is an option regarding the suffix *śe*, whereas the Dramiḍas, on the strength of the textual reading, maintain that the grammatical operation occurs even when separated by *āya*: *vicchāyantī*, *vicchāyatī*, just as in *jugupsate*, where the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffix occurs even when separated by the *san* suffix.
By the rule *yajayāca* (III.3.90), the suffix *naṅ* is applied; thus, *viśno ’ntarāyaḥ*. In the *curādi* group, it has the sense of shining (*bhāsārtha*); thus, *vicchayati* (129).

The root *viś* means "to enter. It takes the form *viśati*; with the prefix *ni*, by rule I.3.17 (*ner viśaḥ*), it takes the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings: *niviśate*. By rule I.4.47 (*abhiniviśaś ca*), it takes the object case: *grāmam abhiniviśate* ("he enters the village"). By rule VII.2.68 (*vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām*), there is optionally the augment *iṭ* before the suffix *kvasu*: *viviśivān* or *viviśvān*. By rule III.3.16 (*padaruja...*), the suffix *ghañ* is added in the sense of the agent: *veśaḥ* ("an entrance," "a brothel," "attire," or "pervasion" in the sense of *vyāpti*). By rule III.4.56 (*viśipatipadi...*), the suffix *ṇamul* is added:
*gehānupraveśam āste* ("he remains entering house after house"), or *geham geham anupraveśam* ("entering each house"). [Note: *so* refers to all manuscripts; *P* omits.]

155. VI. *Praveśam* means entry or penetration. [The suffix] *kvan* is applied according to *aśū-pruṣi* (Uṇ. 1.151); thus *viśvam*. *Viṣṭapa* means the world, according to *viṭapa-viṣṭapa* (Uṇ. III.145). *Veśantaḥ* means a pool or pond, according to *vi-śi-pam, jṝ-viśibhyāṃ jhac* (Uṇ. III.126). According to *veḥ śālaj* (V.2.28), *viśāla* and *viśaṅkaṭa* [are derived]. (130) *Mṛśa* means touching (*āmarśana*). Touching is contact. He touches (*parāmṛśati*), he touches (*ā-mṛśati*)...

Because it is stated as *darśana*, [the root] is accompanied by a prefix (*sopasarga*). [Examples of] *vimraṣṭā* and *vimarṣṭā*: by [Pāṇini III.1.44], there are *amṛkṣat*, *amrākṣīt*, and *amārkṣīt*. The root *ṇud* means "to impel. It forms *nudati*. By [Pāṇini III.2.5], *ka* is applied after *parimṛja* and *apanuda* when combined with *tuṇḍa* and *śoka* respectively; thus, *śokāpanudaḥ putraḥ* ("a son who dispels grief"). Since *nudi* is recited immediately after *tudi* (in VI.2) and is marked with the *svarita* accent, it should not be read here among the roots that take the *parasmaipada* endings.

The root *śad* is used in the sense of "falling" (*śātana*). By the rule *pāghrādhmā* (Pāṇini 7.3.78), there is the substitution of *śī*: *śīyate*. By the rule *śadeḥ śitaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.60), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied: *śatsyati*. With the causative suffix *ṇic*, by the rule *śader agatau taḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.42), the *t* is substituted for the root-final *d*: *phalāni śātayati* ("he causes the fruits to fall"). *Aśadat* is formed from *ṣadḷ*. The root *sad* is used in the senses of "falling apart," "going," and "sinking. There is the substitution of *sīd* for *sad*: *sīdati*, *sīdatī*, *sīdantī*. From it, *siṣatsati* and *asadat* are derived. *Sattā* is the abstract noun. We do not perceive any utility in the double listing of these two roots (*sad* and *sīd*) in the *bhvādi* class (Dhātupāṭha 1.908 and 1.907); one should rather infer that the purpose lies in the difference regarding the accent (*svara*) of the verbal suffixes (*vikaraṇa*).

Those roots with an *anudātta* accent that have an *udātta* indicatory letter (*it*) [beginning from Pāṇini 1.3.146]—namely, *mucḷ* "to release"—these five are *aniṭ* and are conjugated in both voices (*ubhayapadin*). By the rule *śe mucādīnām* (Pāṇini VII.1.59), the augment *num* is added: *muñcati*, *muñcate*; *amucat*, *amukta*; *moktā*. Regarding the form *mokṣate vatsaḥ svayam eva* ("the calf releases itself"), by the rule *muco 'karmakasya guṇo vā* (Pāṇini VII.4.57), there is optionally the substitution of *guṇa* for the root vowel before the suffix *san* (desiderative), and optionally the elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsalopa*): *mumukṣate*. From the rule *igupadhāt kiḥ* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.119), we derive *muciḥ*; likewise, *Namuciḥ*. In the compound *Namuciḥ*, the negative particle *naÑ* retains its original form according to the rule *nambrāṇnapād* (Pāṇini VI.3.75). Furthermore, by the rule *sivimuceṣ ṭer ū ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra IV.119), [the suffix *ki* is applied after *muc*, and the final vowel is replaced by *ū*].

(IV, 162): *mūtra* [is derived from the root] *vṛtṛ* with the suffix *saḥ* according to Uṇādi-sūtra III, 62; thus, *mokṣaḥ*. (136) *lup* in the sense of cutting off (*chedane*). [From] *lumpati*, *lumpate*, *alupat*, *alupta*; and with the suffix *yaṅ* according to Pāṇini III, 1, 24 (*lupasada-car-yaṅ*), [we have] *lolupyate*. (137)

The root *vid* means "to obtain. It forms *vindati*, *vindate*, *avidat*, and *avitta*. According to *ṇiśridrusrubhyo ’nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini III.1.48), the suffix *ām* may optionally be applied: *viveda* or *vidāñcakāra*. By the rule *vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām* (VII.2.68), the suffix *iṭ* is optional: *vividvān* or *vividivān*. By the rule *anupasargāl limpavindadhāripārivedyaudyudhodyuparivṛjāṃ ca* (III.1.138), the suffix *śa* is applied: *vindaḥ*, *Govindaḥ*, and *aravindam*. Furthermore, by the rule *vitto bhogapratyayayoḥ* (VIII.2.58), [the word *vitta* is used in the sense of enjoyment or trust].

*vitta* means wealth or property; *vittaḥ* with reference to hair means "possessed of" or "adorned with"; elsewhere, *vinnaṃ* means "obtained. [The suffix] *ṇamul* is applied after the roots *vid-* and *jīv-* according to the rule *yāvati vindajīvoḥ* (Pāṇini III.4.30): e.g., *yāvadvedaṃ adhīte* ("he studies as much as he knows"). [Note: The inclusion of the root *vid-* meaning "to know" [in the rule *vida jñāne* III.1.38] is because it is indicated there with a short vowel (*vid-*) ending in *-a*; however, for this [other root *vid-* meaning "to find"], [the form is] *viveda*. [Reference: Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī VI.VH 156].

*Lipa* means to smear; *upadeha* means increase. From the rule *lipisicihvaś ca* (Pāṇini III.1.53), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *alipat*. Regarding the middle voice (*ātmanepada*), by the rule *ātmanepadeṣv anyatarasyām* (I.3.54): *alipata* or *alipta*. By the rule *anupasargāl limpa* (I.3.138), the suffix *śa* is applied: *limpaḥ*. By the rule *nau limpeḥ* (I.3.138.1): *nilimpā devāḥ* (the gods who smear). (139)

The root *ṣic* means "to sprinkle. It takes the forms *siñcati* and *siñcate*. By the rule *upasargāt sunoti* (Pāṇini VIII.3.65), the initial *s* becomes *ṣ*: *abhiṣiñcati*. By the rule *sthādiṣv abhyāsena cābhyāsasya* (VIII.3.64), we have *abhiṣiṣeca*, *abhyaṣiñcat*, *asicat*, *asikta*, and *asicata*. By the rule *dāmnī* (III.2.182), the suffix *ṣṭran* is added: *sektram*. From the root *sic*, the suffix *kan* is applied when forming a proper name (*saṃjñā*), along with the augment *num* and the change to *h*: *siṃhalaḥ*. In the *yaṅ*-intensive, by the rule *sico yaṅi* (VIII.3.112), the change to *ṣ* does not occur: *abhisesicyate*. For the causative form, there is an extension of the rule: *asīsicat*. (140)

151. The roots *anudātta* (unaccented) and *svarita* (circumflex-accented) [are listed]. 151. *kṛtī* (in the sense of cutting). These three [roots] ending in *i* are *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*) and *parasmaipadī* (active-voice). *kṛntati*, *kartitā*; by the rule *se 'sici* (Pāṇini VII.2.57), [the forms are] *kartsyati* and *kartiṣyati*. *kṛttaḥ*; the designation *īdit* (having *ī* as its *it*-marker) is for the sake of the *yaṅluganta* (intensive without *yaṅ*): *carīkṛttaḥ*. From the root without a prefix (*nirupapada*), [the suffix] *kvip* (Pāṇini III.2.178) applies: *kṛt*. *Kartarī* means an instrument for cutting; *kṛttiḥ* means skin. By the rule *kṛteś chakrū ca* (Uṇādi II.21): *kṛcchram* and *krūraḥ*. By the rule *kṛtyaśūbhyāṃ ksnaḥ* (Uṇādi III.17): [the form *kṛtsnaḥ*].

The word *kṛttikāḥ* [is derived from] the root *kṛt* with the suffix *tikn*, according to [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.147: *kṛtsnam, kṛtibhidi*. In the *rudhādi* class, there is the root *kṛtī* in the sense of "enclosing" (VII.10):

*kṛṇatti*. [Next is] *khid* in the sense of "affliction" (*paritāpa*). It forms *khindati*; and in the *bhidādi* group (III.3.104), it forms *khidā*. In the *rudhādi* class, there is *khida* in the sense of "dejection" (*dainya*) (VII.12): *khinte*, *khidyate*—this latter being used in the sense of a reflexive object-agent (*karmakartari*). Alternatively, one should infer that it is listed in the *divādi* class (IV.61). [Next is] *piśa* in the sense of "dividing" (*avayava*). It forms *piṃśati*.
