By the rule *hṛpiśiruhi* (Uṇādi IV.118), the suffix *in* is applied: *peśiḥ* means a "bit of flesh"; *piśunaḥ*, *piśitam*, and *peśalaḥ*.

Those with an acute (udātta) accent follow those with an acute accent [in the preceding list] (154). The *muc*-class and others have been concluded in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, the *Dhātuvṛtti* conceived by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin;

thus ends the *tudādigaṇa*. Om! The root *rudh* is used in the sense of "obstructing" (*āvaraṇa*), where "obstructing" means pervasion (*vyāpti*). From here on, seven roots are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*).

And [the roots] that take both voices (*ubhayapadin*). From *rudh* and the following, *śnam* is added (Pāṇini III.1.78): *ruṇaddhi*. The *anusvāra* that has arisen [from the *n* of *śnam*] transcends the rule for *ṇatva*: *runddhe*. By "the elision of the *a* of *śna* and *as*" (VI.4.111), we have *arudhat* and *arautsīt* (by "after a root with indicatory *ir*", III.1.57). By "in the case of *sip*, there is optionally *ru* for the root" (VIII.2.74), we have *aruṇat* thou. *Aruṇaḥ*. By "not after *rudh*" (III.1.64), there is no *ciṇ* affix in the case of the object-as-agent (*karmakartṛ*): *aruddha* the cow by itself; [and thus] *roddhā*.

In the rule *saṃpṛcādāv* (III.2.142), [the suffix *kyap*] is applied when following [a word ending in] the locative case; and by the rule *saptamyāṃ copapīḍarudhakarṣaḥ* (III.4.49): *vraje uparudhya*, *vrajoparodhaḥ*.
Thus ends the *tudādi* group in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on roots (*dhātuvṛtti*) conceived by Kṣīrasvāmin.

He causes the cows to drink (*dhaṃ gāḥ pāyayati*). From the root *mad* with the suffix *kirac* according to *iṣitimimadi* (Uṇ. I.52), we have *rudhiram* (blood). The root *bhid* means "to split. - Present: *bhindati*, *bhinte*; - Aorist: *abhidat*, *abhaitsīt*; - Perfect: *abhitta*; - Future: *bhettā*. *bhittam* (a fragment) is used in the sense of a "piece" according to Pāṇini VIII.2.59; otherwise, it is *bhinnam*. According to Pāṇini III.1.115, *bhidyodhyau* refers to a river. *kāṣṭhabhit* (one who splits wood). From the roots *vid*, *bhid*, and *chid* with the suffix *kurac* (Pāṇini III.2.162), we have *bhiduram* (a thunderbolt) and *bhittiḥ* (a wall). With the suffix *kit* after the roots *kṛ*, *bhid*, and *lati* (Uṇ. III.147), we have *bhittikā* (a small wall). From the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, *pṝ*, and *kuṭi* (Uṇ. IV.142), the suffix *iḥ* is applied.

*vajra* means "thunderbolt"; according to *Kāśikā* III.1.96 (*karmakartari kelimaḥ*), *bhid* [takes the suffix] *kelima*: *bhidelimam kāṣṭham* ("wood that is easily split"). According to *Uṇādi-sūtra* II.13, [the suffix] *rak*: *bhidram*. According to *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.52 (*iṣitim-*, cf. *Uṇ.*), [the suffix] *kirac*: *bhidiram*. In the *Bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III.3.104), *bhidā* means "splitting" (2).

The root *chid* means "to split" (*dvaidhīkaraṇe*); it refers to the separation of that which was not previously divided (*advaidhasya pṛthaktve*). Conjugations: *chinatti*, *chintte*; *acchidat*, *acchaitsīt*, *acchitta*. Derivatives: *chiduraṃ*, *rajjucchit*, *rak* (Uṇ. I.13): *chidraṃ* (hole), *chidiḥ* (an axe), *chidiraḥ*, *chitvaraḥ*. In the *bhidādi* group (cf. Pāṇini III.3.104.2), *chidā* denotes the state of being split (*dvaidhībhāve*); *vicchittiḥ* occurs in other senses. (3)

*ric* is used in the sense of purging (*virecana*). Purging means causing to go out (*niḥsāraṇa*). [The forms are: *riṇakti*, *riṅkte*, *aricat*, *araikṣīt*, *arikta*. [The past passive participle is] *riktaḥ*; *riktham* means wealth; *rekṇas*—[also meaning wealth]. In the *curādi* group (X, 273), *rica* is used in the senses of separating and mixing: *recayati*. (4) *vic* is used in the sense of becoming separate (*pṛthagbhāva*). [The forms are: *vinakti*, *viṅkte*, *avicat*, *avaikṣīt*, *avikta*. [The noun is] *vivekaḥ*. In the *juhotyādi* group (III, 12), [the form is] *vevekti*, *vivikte*.

(5) *kṣud* is used in the sense of crushing (*saṃpeṣa*). [The forms are: *kṣuṇatti*, *kṣuntte*, *kṣottā*, *akṣudat*, *akṣautsīt*, *akṣutta*. [The past passive participle is] *kṣuṇṇaḥ*. By [the rule] *rak* (Uṇ. II, 13), [we have] *kṣudraḥ*. (6)

The root *yuj* is used in the sense of "joining" (*yoge*). [Its forms are: *yunakti*, *yuṅkte*, *ayujat*, *ayaukṣīt*, *ayukta*. According to Pāṇini I.3.64, *taṅ* (the ātmanepada endings) is applied after *yuj* when preceded by *pra* or *upa*, provided it does not refer to sacrificial vessels: *prayuṅkte*, *upayuṅkte*. It is not so here: *dvandvaṃ yajñapātrāṇi prayunakti* ("he joins the pairs of sacrificial vessels"). In the *divādi* class (IV.68), *yuj* means "meditation" (*samādhau*): *yujyate*. These very forms are included among the roots that have anudātta indicatory vowels (*anudāttetaḥ*) and those that have svarita indicatory vowels (*svaritetaḥ*).

*uchṛdir* means "to shine" and "to play"; *utṛdir* means "to injure" and "to disregard. Both are *udātta* and *svarita-it*. [Present: *chṛṇatti*, *chṛntte*; [Aorist: *acchṛdat*, *acchardīt*, *acchardiṣṭa*; [Periphrastic Perfect: *acacchardat*, *acicchṛdat*—here the vowel *ṛ* may optionally become *ṝ* by rule VI.4.7; and because of the suffix *iṭ* not being applied before *kṛt* suffixes (cf. VII.2.57), there is optionally *iṭ*: *chardiṣyati*, *chartsyati*. [Gerund: *chṛttvā*, *charditvā*—optionally so by rule VII.2.56; [Past Passive Participle: *chṛṇṇaḥ*; [Noun: *chardiḥ*—formed with the suffix *isi* by rule Uṇ. II.109.

In the *curādi* group, *chard* means "to vomit" (*vamana*): *chardayati*. *Tṛd* [means] "to pierce": *tṛṇatti*, *tṛntte*; *atṛdat*, *atardīt*; *tartsyati*, *tardiṣyati*. [Gerunds: *tṛttvā*, *tarditvā*; [past participle: *tṛṇṇaḥ*; [example: *vitardikā vediḥ* (a sacrificial altar with a railing). 1. S. I, 767; VII, 158.

The root *kṛtī* means "to twist" (*veṣṭane*). It is marked with the acute accent (*udātta*) because it ends in the suffix *udātteL*. From it, we derive *kṛṇatti*, *kartitvā*, *kartsyati*, and *kartiṣyati*. The vowel *ī* is added by virtue of being an *īdit* root (Pāṇini VII.2.14) for the sake of the *yaṅ* affix; thus, *carīkṛttaḥ*. Furthermore, there is a reversal of the initial and final sounds of *kṛti* (Uṇādi I.17), yielding *tarkuḥ*. In the *tudādigaṇa*, *kṛtī* means "to cut" (*chedane*); from it, we derive *kṛntati* and *kṛttiḥ* (10).

The root *indh* means "to shine" or "to kindle. It is marked with the acute accent (*udātta*) and is treated as having an unaccented vowel (*anudātta*). In *indhé*, by rule VI.4.23, there is the elision of the nasal (*nalopaḥ*) after the suffix *śnā*. Thus we have *iddham*. Regarding the forms *bhrāṣṭramindhaḥ* and *agnimindhaḥ*, by rule VI.3.70, the suffix *mum* is added [after *indh* when preceded by *bhrāṣṭra* or *agni*]. In *agnim inddhe*, the term becomes *agnīt* by rule VI.4.29. From the root *edh* (meaning "fuel"), the word *idhmaḥ* is derived. Regarding *edhas*, it is formed from the root *edh* with the suffix *asun* (according to Uṇādi-sūtra IV.188). By rule Uṇādi II.26, the suffix *rak* is added to *vī* and *nī* when combined with *indh*: thus *vīdhram* means "pure," and *nīdhram* means "the edge of a cataract" or "the fringe of a film."

*Khid* means "to feel dejection" (*dainye*), and *vid* means "to consider" (*vicāraṇe*). Both are *anudātta* roots with an *anudātta* indicatory letter (*anudāttetau*). From *khid*: in the *divādi* class (IV, 61), it is *khidyate*; in the *tudādi* class (VI, 142), it is *khindati*. From *vid*: by rule VIII, 2, 56 (*nudavidondatrā*), the *niṣṭhā* suffix optionally undergoes cerebralization (*ṇatva*): *vittaḥ* or *vinnaḥ*. (See 12.13).

The root *śiṣ* is used in the sense of "distinguishing" (*viśeṣaṇa*). Distinguishing is the production of another quality. From this [root], four forms are derived that are *aniṭ* and take the *parasmaipada* endings: *viśinaṣṭi*, *vyaśiṣat*. In the passive voice (*taṅ*), with the suffix *ksa* (Pāṇini III.1.45): *vyaśikṣata*, *viśiṣyate*. In the *curādi* class, *śiṣ* is used in the sense of "not using everything" (*asarvopayoga*): *śeṣayati*, *śiṣyate*; thus, it is called *śeṣaḥ* (remainder). (14)

The root *piṣ* means "to crush. In the example *caurasya pinaṣṭi* ("he crushes the thief"), the genitive case is used according to Pāṇini 2.3.56 (*jāsiniprahaṇa*). The forms are: *apiṣat*, *apiṣṭa*, *apikṣata*, and *peṣṭā*. According to Pāṇini 3.4.35 (*śuṣkacūrṇarūkṣeṣu piṣo ṇamul*), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied when the object is dry, powdered, or rough: *śuṣkapeṣaṃ pinaṣṭi* ("he grinds it dry"). According to Pāṇini 3.4.38 (*snehane piṣaḥ*), it is applied for the purpose of making something oily: *tailapeṣaṃ pinaṣṭi* ("he grinds it with oil"). In the *Uṇādi* list (IV.15), the words *pināka* and *piṇyāka* are derived from this root.

The root *bhañj* is used in the sense of "crushing" (*āmardane*). *bhañjati*, *bhaṅktā*, *abhāṅkṣīt*. By [Pāṇini] VI.4.33, *bhañjeś ca ciṇi*: *abhāji* or *abhañji*. By [Pāṇini] VII.4.86, *japajabha...*, there is an *anusvāra* for the reduplication: *bambhajyate* (VIII.4.58). By [Pāṇini] VI.4.32, *jāntanaśāṃ vibhāṣā*, there is optionally an augment *anunāsika* (*anum*): *bhaktvā* or *bhaṅktvā*. By [Pāṇini] III.2.161, *bhañjabhāsamido ghurac*: *bhaṅguraḥ*. By [Pāṇini] III.3.19, *ghañ*: that by which something is broken is a *bhaṅga*, meaning a wave (*taraṅga*). By [Pāṇini] VIII.2.45, *kte*: *bhagnaḥ*. *bhaṅgiḥ* (16).

The root *bhuj* has the meanings "to protect" and "to eat. "Eating" (*abhyavahāra*) means consuming food. In the example *bhunakti bhuvam* ("he protects the earth"), the suffix *taṅ* (the middle voice ending) is applied according to Pāṇini I.3.66, *bhujo 'navane* ("*bhuji* [takes the middle voice] except in the sense of protecting"). In the example *bhuṅkte 'nnam* ("he eats food"), the object is designated as such by Pāṇini I.4.52, *gatibuddhipratyavasānārtha*, which states that roots meaning motion, cognition, or eating take the object designation (*karmasaṃjñā*). In the causative example *bhojayati caitraṃ saktūn* ("he causes Caitra to eat the groats"), Caitra is the object of the causative verb.

The word *bhojya* is used in the sense of "fit to be eaten" (*bhakṣye*) [by Pāṇini II.3.69], whereas it means "enjoyable" (*bhogya*) in other contexts. By the rule *Bhojo 'ci* (III.1.134), we have *Bhoja*; by *Bhujanyubjau pāṇyupatāpayoḥ* (VII.3.61), we have *bhujam* and *nyubjam* in the senses of "hand" and "torment" respectively, while in other cases it is *bhogaḥ* (III.3.121) meaning "pleasure. Examples include *viśvabhojaḥ* and *Bhujyuḥ* as a Gandharva. [The suffix] *kiṣ* occurs after the roots *ruc* and *bhuj* [according to Uṇādi-sūtra 1]. [Note: 1. *tilapeṣam*, 2. *bhogyo*, 3. cf. Hemacandra’s Uṇādi-vṛtti 802, 159, VII].
(IV, 178): *bhujiṣya* means "a servant" (*dāsa*). In the *tudādi* group, *bhuja* is listed as meaning "crookedness" (VI, 124): *nirbhujati*.
(17) Those [roots] which have an anudātta accent and end in an udātta vowel. 17.

The roots *tṛh* and *hiṃs* mean "to injure. These eight [roots] beginning with *tṛh* are *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment) and take the *parasmaipada* endings. Regarding *tṛṇaha im* (Pāṇini VII.3.92): *tṛṇeḍhi*, *tṛṇḍhaḥ*, *tṛṃhanti*, *tṛṇḍhi*. From *tṛh*, the suffix *kna* is added and the *hal* (consonant) is elided (Uṇādi V.8): *tṛṇam* ("grass"). *hinasti*, *hindhi*. By the rule *dhi ca* (VIII.2.25), there is the elision of *s* [before the *dhakāra*]. By the rule *tipy anasteḥ* (VIII.2.73): *ahinat bhavān*. By the rule *sipi dhāto rur vā* (VIII.2.74): *ahinat tvam* or *ahinas tvam*.

By the rule *nindahiṃsa* (Pāṇini III.2.146), the word *hiṃsakaḥ* is formed; by the rule *namikampi* (Pāṇini III.2.167), the suffix *raḥ* is applied: *hiṃsraḥ*. [The words] *hiṃsā* and *hiṃsīraḥ* [are formed according to] Uṇādi-sūtra V.18, meaning a chain for dragging by the neck (18.19).

The root *und* means "to moisten. From it we derive: *unatti* (he moistens), *undidiṣati* (he wishes to moisten). With the suffix *ghañ*, by the rule *avodaidha* (Pāṇini VI.4.29), we have *avodaḥ*, meaning "moistening"; or, by the rule *nudavidondatrā* (VIII.2.56), there is the substitution of *n* for *d*: *samunnam*, *samuttam*. By the rule *under ic cādeḥ* (Uṇādi I.13), we have *induḥ* (the moon). By the rule *rak* (Uṇādi II.13), we have *udraḥ* (an otter). *Unduraḥ* means "a digger" (a rat). *Udakam* (water). By the rule *under nalopaś ca* (Uṇādi II.76), with the suffix *yuc*, we have *odanaḥ* (boiled rice). *Utsaḥ* means "a spring" or "a flow. (20)

The root *añj* is used in the senses of manifestation (*vyakti*), anointing (*mrakṣaṇa*), and motion (*gati*). Manifestation is visibility; anointing is the sprinkling of ghee and the like. [Examples: *anakti*, *aṅktā*, *añjitā*. Regarding the desiderative suffix (*san*), by Pāṇini VII.2.74 (*smiṅpūṅrañjaśāṃ sani*), one forms *añjijiṣati*. By Pāṇini III.1.109 (*añjer ṇyaty ājyam iṣyate*), the word *ājya* is derived from *añj* with the suffix *ṇyat*.

[Further examples: *aktaḥ*; by Uṇādi-sūtra IV.2 (*ṛtanyañji*), the suffix *ali* is applied: *añjaliḥ*; *añjiṣṭhu* refers to sesame seeds and the like. [Gerunds: *aṅktvā*, *aktvā*, *añjitvā*. (21) The root *tanj* is used in the sense of contraction (*saṃkocana*). [Present: *tanakti*. [Gerunds: *taṅktvā*, *taktvā*, *tañjitvā*. [Past participle: *taktaḥ*. The Draviḍas read the root as *tanc*: [Gerunds: *taktvā*, *tañcitvā*. (22)
The root *ovijī* means "to fear" and "to tremble. It forms *vinakti*; *udvignaḥ* ("agitated"); and *udvijate* in the *tudādi* class (VI.9).

(23) *vṛjī* means "to avoid" or "to exclude. It forms *vṛṇakti*, *avṛṇak*; *apavṛktaḥ*; *vargaḥ* ("class"); and *vṛjinaṃ* ("evil"). According to the Daurgas, *vṛcī* means "to cover," as in *varkaḥ*. It also occurs in the *adādi* class (I.19) as *vṛkte*. (24) *pṛcī* means "to join" or "to touch. It forms *pṛṇakti*, *saṃpṛktaḥ*; with the suffix *ghañ* (III.4.18, 19): *saṃparkaḥ* ("contact"), *madhuparkaḥ* ("honey-mixture"). It also occurs in the *adādi* class (I.20) as *pṛkte*. In the *curādi* class (*yuj pṛcī saṃparcane*, X.264–265), there is optionally the causative suffix *ṇic*: *saṃparcayati*, *saṃparcati*. (25)
In the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on verbal roots (*dhātuvṛtti*) conceived by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin, the *rudhādi* class [of roots] is completed.
2.1. Compare Hem. Uṇ. 423. 2. P. Thus ends the *rudhādi* class in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on verbal roots conceived by Kṣīrasvāmin, [ending with root number] VIII.160.

*om!* [The root] *tan* means "to expand. From here, six roots ending in *ṣ* are *ubhayapadin* (active and middle). By the rule *tanādikṛñbhya uḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.79), the suffix *u* is added: *tanoti*, *tanute*; *tanvaḥ*, *tanuvaḥ*; *tanmaḥ*, *tanumaḥ*. By the rule *tanoter yaki* (VI.4.44), we have *tāyate* and *tanyate*. Regarding *atanīt* and *atānīt*: by the rule *tanādibhyas tathāsoḥ* (II.4.79), there is optionally the elision (*luk*) of the *sij* augment; thus, *atata* and *atathāḥ*. By the rule *vanatitanotyādīnām* (VI.4.37), there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika*); thus, *ataniṣṭa* and *ataniṣṭhāḥ*.

By the rule *nahivṛti* (Pāṇini VI.3.116), there is lengthening before the suffix *kvip*: *parītat*, *tatvā*, *tanitvā*, *tataḥ*, *vitataḥ*. By the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini VII.2.49), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *titaniṣati*; in the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *tanoter vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini VI.4.17), there is lengthening: *titāṃsati*, *titaṃsati*. From the rule *tanoter ṇaḥ* (Pāṇini III.1.140.1): *avatānaḥ*; with the suffix *ghañ* (Pāṇini III.3.18–19): *vitānaḥ* (a sacrifice), *saṃtānaḥ*, *ekatānaḥ*. By the rule *bhṛmṛśī* (Uṇādi I.7), the suffix *u* is applied.

From the root *tan* (to stretch), by [Uṇādi-sūtra] I.82 (*kṛṣicamitani*), the suffix *ū* is applied: *tanūḥ* (the body). By [Uṇādi-sūtra] I.70 (*sitanigami*), the suffix *tun* is applied: *tantuḥ* (a thread); [also] *tuk* (the breath) and *tokam* (offspring). By [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.107 (*sānasivarṇasi*), the suffix *taṇ* is applied: *taṇḍulam* (rice). By [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.75 (*tanyṛṣibhyāṃ ksarac*), the suffix *ksarac* is applied: *tasaraḥ* (a shuttle for winding thread); however, *trasaraḥ* refers to silk thread. By [Uṇādi-sūtra] III.88 (*tanimṛṅbhyāṃ kic ca*), the suffix *ka* with the augment *iṭ* is applied: *tatam* (stretched) and *tātaḥ* (father); by [Uṇādi-sūtra] IV.99 (*taneḥ kayan*), the suffix *kayan* is applied.

*tanayaḥ* [is derived] by *ṣṭran* (Uṇ. IV, 158); *tantram*; [by the rule] *na ktici dīrghaś ca* (VI, 4, 39): *tantiḥ*, *tantrīḥ*; [by the rule] *ktini* (III, 3, 94): *tatiḥ*, *paṅktiḥ*; [by the rule] *tanoter ḍauḥ sanvac ca* (Uṇ. V, 52): *titauḥ* (a winnowing basket); [by the rule] *taneḥ anaś ca vaḥ* (cf. Uṇ. II, 63): *tvak*; [by the rule] *vā lyapi* (VI, 4, 38), there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika*): *prataty* or *pratanya*.

The root *ṣaṇ* means "to give. [It forms: *sanoti*, *sanute*; [gerunds] *sātvā*, *sanitvā*; [passives] *sāyate*, *sanyate*; [aorist] *asanīt*, *asānīt*; [aorist optative] *asāta*, *asaniṣṭa*; [aorist middle] *asāthāḥ*, *asaniṣṭhāḥ*. By the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini VII.2.49), [the desiderative forms are] *sisaniṣati* and *siṣāsati*. By the rule *sanoter anunāsikalopa ātvaṃ ca* (VI.4.42), [we have] *sātaḥ*; by the rule *na ktici dīrghaś ca* (VI.4.39), [we have] *santiḥ*; by the rule *lopaś cāsyānyatarasyām* (VI.4.45), [we have] *satiḥ*; and by the rule *ūtiyūti* (III.3.97), *sātiḥ* means "giving. By the rule *ñuṇ* (Uṇādi I.3), [we have] *sānuḥ*. (2)

The root *kṣaṇ* is used in the sense of "to injure. One forms *kṣaṇoti*, *kṣaṇute*, *kṣatvā*, and *kṣaṇitvā*. By the rule *hmyantakṣaṇa* (Pāṇini VII.2.5), there is no *vṛddhi* [strengthening of the vowel] in the aorist: *akṣaṇīt*. The past passive participle is *kṣataḥ*, and the verbal noun is *kṣatiḥ*. Durga says that the root is *kṣiṇ*; thus one forms *kṣiṇoti*; the participles are *kṣitaḥ* and *kṣitiḥ*. The root *ṛṇ* means "to go": one forms *ṛṇoti* and *ṛṇute*. The root *tṛṇ* means "to eat": one forms *tṛṇoti* and *tṛṇute*. The gerunds are *tṛtvā* and *tṛṇitvā*. Nandī states that the root *cṛṇ* means "to afflict."
6. These [roots] ending in an acute (*udātta*) or circumflex (*svarita*) vowel have ambiguous qualities when followed by a *sārvadhātuka* suffix: *arṇoti*, *tarṇoti*, *gharṇoti*.

*van* is used in the sense of requesting (*yācana*), and *man* in the sense of perceiving (*avabodhana*). Both are *udātta* roots and are *anudāttet*. [Examples: *vanute*, *vavane*, *vatvā* / *vanitvā*, *vataḥ*. By rule I.868, *glā-snā-van-ū-va-mām ca*, there is optionally the designation *mit*: *vanayati* or *vānayati*. Because of the continued application of the rule "provided it is not preceded by a prefix" (I.867), [the *mit*-designation] is obligatory when a prefix is present: *pravanayati*; this was stated previously (under I.868). [Derivatives: *vanitā*, *vaṇḍaḥ* (Uṇ. I.113), *vaniṣṭhuḥ* (cf. Uṇ. IV.2). In the *Bhvādi* class, *vanu* is not mentioned (I.841); [therefore, in that class, one says] *vanati*.

He thinks (*manute*); having thought (*matvā*), having thought repeatedly (*manitvā*); the past participle is *matam*; the aorist forms are *amata*, *amaniṣṭa*, *amathāḥ*, and *amaniṣṭhāḥ*. In the *divādi* class, the root *man* means "to know" (*jñāne*): *manyate* (VIII. 9).

The root *kṛñ* in the sense of "doing" (*karaṇe*) is unaccented (*anudātta*). In *karoti*, *kurute*, and *karoteḥ* (cf. Pāṇini VI.4.110), there is the substitution of *u* for the vowel. Because of the separate mention of *kṛñ* in the rule *tanādikṛñbhyaḥ* (III.1.79), no other grammatical operation belonging to the *tanādi* class applies to this specific root. Regarding the rule *anuparābhyāṃ kṛñaḥ* (I.3.79), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings do not apply: *anukaroti*, *parākaroti*. However, the *taṅ* endings do apply in the senses of "hinting" (*gandhana*) and so forth, according to *gandhanādau* (I.3.32): *śyeno vartikām apakurute* ("The hawk does harm to the quail"). Also, the *taṅ* endings apply after *adhi-* in the sense of "overpowering" (*prasahana*), according to *adheḥ prasahane* (I.3.33).

The augment *āṬ* is applied after the prefix *adhi* before the root *kṛ*, which has the meaning of "making sound" (*veḥ śabdakarmaṇaḥ*): *śvā vikurute svaram* ("the dog makes a sound"). And [the augment *āṬ* is applied] after [the same prefix] when the root is intransitive (*akarmakāc ca*): *vikurvate dāntāḥ* ("the tamed elephants display themselves"). The augment *suṭ* is applied before the root *kṛ* when preceded by *sam*, *pari*, or *upa*, in the sense of "ornamentation" (*bhūṣaṇe*) and "combination" (*samavāye*): *saṃskurute*, *pariṣkurute*, *upaskurute*. By the rule *nityaṃ karoteḥ* (Pāṇini VI.4.108), there is the elision of the *vikaraṇa* suffix *nu* before the endings *m* and *vas*: *kurvaḥ*, *kurmaḥ*. By the rule *kṛsṛbhṛvṛ...* (Pāṇini VII.2.13), the augment *iṭ* is not applied in the *liṭ* tense.

*cakārtha*, *cakṛva*, *cakṛma*. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sye* (Pāṇini 7.2.70), the augment *iṭ* is added: *kariṣyati*. By the rule *ye ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.109), there is the elision of the *vikaraṇa* suffix: *kuryāt*. By the rule *na bhakurchurām* (Pāṇini 8.2.79), the lengthening of the vowel does not occur. By the rule *hṛkror anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 1.4.53), [Caitra] receives the designation of object (*karman*): one causes Caitra to make a jar, expressed as *ghaṭaṃ kārayati Caitram* or *Caitreṇa*. Regarding the word *tiras* in the sense of disappearance, by the rules *vibhāṣā kṛñi* (Pāṇini 1.4.71–72), it optionally receives the designation of *gati*. When it has the sense of "going," by the rule *tiraso* (Pāṇini 8.3.42), the substitution of *s* for the *r* occurs.

*Tiraskṛtya* and *tiraḥkṛtvā*: by the rule *kṛbhvastiyoge cvih* (V.4.50), the suffix *cv-* is applied; [as in] *śuklīkaroti*. By the rule *mithyopapadāt kṛño ’bhyāse* (I.3.71), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used: *padaṃ mithyā kārayate*. [The word] *kṛtrimam*: by the rule *vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ* (III.1.120), the suffix *kyap* is applied; [thus] *kṛtyam*, *kāryam*. By the rule *ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsa...* (VIII.3.46), the substitution of *s* occurs: *ayaskāraḥ*. By the rule *kṛño hetutācchīlyānulomyeṣu* (III.2.20), the suffix *ṭa* is applied.

*vidyā* [is used] in the sense of "glory," as in *divāvibhā* (Pāṇini III.2.21), where the suffix *ac* is applied: *divākaraḥ* ("maker of the day"). In the sense of "wages for work" (*bhṛti*), according to *karmaṇi bhṛtau* (III.2.22): *karmakaraḥ* ("laborer"). According to *stambaśakṛtor in* (III.2.24): *stambakariḥ* ("a rice plant that causes a clump") and *śakṛtkariḥ* ("a calf that makes dung"). According to *meghartibhayeṣu kṛñaḥ* (III.2.43), the suffix *khac* is applied: *meghaṃkaraḥ* ("cloud-maker"). According to *kṣemapriyamadre ’ṇ ca* (III.2.44), the suffix *aṇ* is also applied: *kṣemaṃkaraḥ* ("one who brings security") and *kṣemakāraḥ*. 1. P adds *duḥpātram*. 2. P reads *apaskurute*. 3. P omits. 4. All manuscripts read *tiras* (VIII.9.162).

From *āḍhya-subhaga* (Pāṇini III.2.56), the suffix *khyun* is applied: *āḍhyaṃkaraṇam*. From *kartṛ-karmaṇoś ca bhū-kṛñoḥ* (III.3.127), the suffix *khal* is applied: *īṣad-āḍhyaṃkaraḥ*, *sv-āḍhyaṃkaraḥ*. From *su-karma-pāpa-* (III.2.89), the suffix *kvip* is applied: *sukṛt*. From *rājani yudhi-kṛñaḥ* (III.2.95), the suffix *kvanip* is applied: *rājakṛtvā*. From *sahe ca* (III.2.96), [the suffix *kvanip* is applied]: *sahakṛtvā*. From *alaṃkṛñ-nirākṛñ-* (III.2.136), the suffix *iṣṇuc* is applied.

*alaṃkariṣṇuḥ*, *nirākariṣṇuḥ*; by Pāṇini III, 3, 100, after the root *kṛ*, there is also the suffix *śa*: *kriyā*, *kṛtyā*, *kṛtiḥ*; by Pāṇini III, 3, 110, in the sense of questioning and narration, there is also the suffix *iñ*: "What deed (*kāṃ kārim*) have you done?"

I performed this *kāri* (act); [from the root *kṛ* with the causative suffix] *ṇi*, by Pāṇini III.3.107, we have *kāraṇā*; in the *bhidādi* group (III.3.104), *kārā* means "imprisonment. Regarding the suffix *khmuñ* after the root *kṛ* when expressing a censure toward an object (I.4.25): one censures a thief *cauraṃkāram*. With the suffix *ṇamul* after words meaning "good" or "sweet" (III.4.26): he eats *svāduṃkāraṃ* (making it sweet). With the words *anyathā*, *evam*, *katham*, and *ittham*, provided the action is already established (III.4.27): *anyathākāram*, *evaṃkāram*. With *yathā* and *tathā* when expressing dissatisfaction or a retort (III.4.28): [we have *yathākāram* and *tathākāram*].
Let it be as you wish; what business have you with this? Regarding the term *tiryak* in the sense of "setting aside" (*apavarga*)—that is, having set aside, or across.

The meaning is "having completed. Regarding the suffix *tva* applied to its own root (*svāṅge*), according to Pāṇini III.4.61, from the roots *kṛ* and *bhū*: *mukhataḥkṛtya*, *mukhataḥ kṛtvā*, *mukhataḥkāram*. Regarding the suffixes expressing the sense of "not" (*nañ*) or "becoming otherwise" (*cvyarthe*), according to Pāṇini III.4.62: *nānākṛtya*, *nānākāram*; *dvidhākṛtya*, *dvidhākāram*. In the *bhvādi* class, the root *kṛ* (I.949) in the sense of "making": *karati*, *karate*. In the *svādi* class, the root *kṛ* (V.7) in the sense of "injuring": *kṛṇoti*, *kṛṇute*. From the rule *kṛvāpājī* (Uṇ. I.1), the suffix *uṇ* [is applied].

*Kāruḥ* and *kārūḥ* [are derived] from the root *kṛ* by *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.25: *kṛgror uc ca*. *Kratuḥ* [is derived] from the root *kṛ* by *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.78: *kṛñaḥ katuḥ*. *Karaṇḍaḥ* [is derived] from the roots *kṛ*, *sṛ*, *bhṛ*, and *vṛñ* by *Uṇādi-sūtra* I.128: *aṇḍan kṛsṛbhṛvṛñaḥ*. *Kareṇuḥ* and *kareṇūḥ* [are derived] from the roots *kṛ* and *hṛ* by *Uṇādi-sūtra* II.1: *kṛhṛbhyām eṇuḥ*. *Karkaḥ* [is derived] by the suffix *ka* according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* III.40: *kṛdādhārā*. *Kṛsaraḥ* [is derived] by the suffix *saran* with the *kit* augment according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* III.73: *kṛdhūmadibhyaḥ kid*. *Kurīram* [is derived] by the suffix *īran* from the root *kṛ* according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* IV.33: *kṛña uc ca*. [Regarding the form *kāriṣu*: *kṛña udīcāṃ kāriṣu* (cf. *Uṇādi-sūtra*...).

Thus, from the root *i*, [the suffix] *iñ* [yields] *kāri*; from *kṛ*, [the suffix] *manin* [yields] *karman*; from *kṛ*, [the suffix] *pāsa* [yields] *karpāsa*; and from *kṛ*, with the doubling [of the radical], [the suffix] *ac* [yields] *cakra*.
Thus, in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, the commentary on verbal roots conceived by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin, the section on the *tanādi-gaṇa* is complete.

*Oṃ!* [The root] *krīñ* is used in the sense of "exchanging" (*vinimaya*). Exchange (*vinimaya*) means barter (*parivarta*). From here on, seven [roots] are *aniṭ* [roots that do not take the *iṭ* augment]. By the rule *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* (Pāṇini III.1.81), [the suffix] *śnā* is applied: *krīṇāti* (he buys), *krīṇīte* (he buys for himself). By the rule *ī haly aghoḥ* (VI.4.113), [the long vowel *ī* is substituted for the final *a* before a consonant beginning with *ha*]: *krīṇanti* (they buy). By the rule *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (VI.4.112), there is elision (*lopa*) of the *ā* of the suffix *śnā* and of reduplicated stems: [thus, the *ā* is dropped]. By the rule *parivyavebhyaḥ kriyaḥ* (I.3.18), the *taṅ* [ātmanepada] endings are applied: *parikrīṇīte* (he exchanges around/barters). By the rule *krīñjīnāṃ ṇau* (VI.1.48), the substitution of *ā* occurs before the causative suffix *ṇic*: *krāpayati* (he causes to buy). [The agentive suffix] *tṛc* gives *kretā* (buyer). [The word] *krayya* is used in the sense of "that for which something is bought."

1 All manuscripts; 2 KC *enuḥ*; 3 P adds: *kṛpeḥ kūḥ*: *kūrpāsaḥ* means a bodice (*kañcuka*). 4 P [states]: Thus, in the *Dhātuvṛtti* of the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī* conceived by Kṣīrasvāmin, the *tanādi* class is 163 (VI, 1, 82). Another [root] ending in *krī* takes *in* in the sense of the object [of the action]: *vikrayī* (III, 2, 93); a seller of Soma (*somavikrayī*). [The suffix] *ikan* is added after *krī* (Uṇ. II, 44): *krayikaḥ* (1).

The root *prī* is used in the senses of satisfying (*tarpaṇa*) and longing (*kānti*). Longing is desire. [From the forms] *prīṇāti*, *prīṇīte*, and by the rule *dhūñprīñor nuk* (Pāṇini VII.3.37), [we derive] *prīṇayati*. By the rule *igupadhajñā* (Pāṇini III.1.135), the suffix *ka* is applied: *priyaḥ*. In the *divādi* class, *prī* is used in the sense of satisfaction (*prīti*): *prīyate*. (2) The root *śrī* is used in the sense of cooking (*pāka*). [From it we derive] *śrīṇāti*, *śrīṇīte*, *śretā*; and *śrītiḥ*. (3)

The root *mī* is used in the sense of "injuring" (*hiṃsā*). From *mīnāti*, *mīnīte*, and by rule V.4.15 (*hinu-mīnā*), there is the substitution of *ṇ*: *pramīṇāti*. With the suffix *san*, by rule VII.4.54 (*mīmā*), there is the substitution of *is*: *mitsati*. By rule VI.1.50 (*mī-nā-ti-mino-ti-dīṅ-āṃ lyapi ca*), there is the substitution of *ā*: *pramāpayati* and *pramāya*. There is a prohibition of this substitution for the roots *mī*, *mīl*, and *mlai* when followed by the suffixes *khal* and *ac* (cf. VI.1.50, 2): *īṣanmayaḥ*, *pramayaḥ*, and *mītaḥ*. In the *Uṇādi* list, by rule I.68 (*mīnāter ūraḥ*), [the suffix] *ūra* is applied to *mīnāti*, resulting in *mayūraḥ* (4).

The root *ṣiñ* means "to bind. [It forms] *sināti*, *sinīte*, *asaiṣīt*. Because of the restriction [stated in Pāṇini VIII.3.61], "only after the roots *stu* and *ṇī* [the *ṣatva* occurs] before the suffix *ṣaṇ*," one has *sisīṣati*. In the *svādi-gaṇa* [it forms] *sinoti*; [as an example of] this very [root] having the eater as its agent [Pāṇini VIII.2.44.4 states]: *sino grāsaḥ* ("the morsel is bound by itself"). [In the sense of] "not flowing" (*āpravaṇa*), [it is] *skuñ*. "Not flowing" (*āpravaṇa*) means "lifting up" (*uddharaṇa*). The teachers say that this [root] belongs to the Sūtra [tradition]. From *stanbhu*, *stunbhu*, *skanbhu*, *skunbhu*, and *skubh*, there is also *śnu*: *skunāti*, *skunīte*, *skunoti*, *skunute*, *skotā*.

The root *yu* is used in the sense of binding (*bandhane*). It forms *yunāti*, *yunīte*, and *yotā*. In the *adādi* class (II.23), *yu* is used in the sense of mixing (*miśraṇe*): *yauti*, *yavitā*. In the *curādi* class (X.170), *yu* is used in the sense of loathing (*jugupsāyām*): *yāvayate*. (9) The [roots] ending with *knu* are unaccented (*anudātta*). 7. *knu* is used in the sense of sound (*śabde*). From this up to *gṝ* (there are twenty-eight roots), twenty of which are *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment). *knūnīte*, *knavitā*. (10)
The root *dru* means "to injure. [It forms] *drūṇāti*, *drūṇīte*, and *dravitā*. In the *svādi-gaṇa* (cf. V.
34), it forms *druṇoti* (11) and *knūnāti*; [the past participle is] *drūtaḥ*.

The root *pū* (pūñ) means "purification" (*pavana*). Purification is cleansing (*śuddhiḥ*). By the rule *pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* (VII. 3. 80), the vowel is shortened: *punāti*, *punīte*. Regarding the rule *pūño vināśe* (VIII. 2. 44, 3), there is the substitution of *ṇatva* [for *t*]: *pūnā yavāḥ* ("the barley has been purified"), whereas elsewhere it is *pūtaḥ*. By the rule *nirabhyoḥ pūlvor ghañ* (III. 3. 28), the suffix *ghañ* is applied: *niṣpāvaḥ* is a type of grain. In the *Bhvādi* class, *pūṅ* (pūṅ) means "purification" (I. 1015): *pavate*; in the *Divādi* class (cf. I. 513), it is *pūyate*. From this root derive: *potram*, *pavitram*, *putraḥ*, *potaḥ*. According to the rule *naptṛneṣṭṛ* (Uṇ. II. 96), *potā* refers to a sacrificial priest (*ṛtvij*). (12)

1. Even so, this is the correct (orthodox) reading according to the *Kāśikā*. 2. *māṃsavikrayī*. 3. All manuscripts read *grāma°* and *grāmaḥ*. 4. P reads *ācāryaḥ*. 5. P and K read *dravitaḥ* (contrary to Pāṇini VII.2.11). I. X. 164.

The root *lū* (meaning "to cut") forms *lunāti* and *lunīte*; its future is *lavitā*. Regarding the desiderative, there is no *iṭ* augment (VH 2.12): *lulūṣati*. The aorist is *alīlavat*. In the causative, *lilāvayiṣati*, the *it*-strengthening of the reduplicated syllable occurs by rule VH 4.80 (*oḥ puyaṇjy apara*). By rule VIII.2.44 (*lvādibhyaś ca*), there is the substitution of *ṇatva* for the final consonant in the past participle: *lūnaḥ*. By rule VI.1.44.1 (*ṝkāralvādibhyaḥ ktin niṣṭhāvat*), the suffix *ktin* is treated like the past participle: *lūniḥ*. By rule III.2.184 (*artilūdhv*), the suffix *itran* is added: *lavitram*. [The suffix] *āṇaka* is added to *lū*, *śi*, and *ṅghi* (Uṇ.).

(III, 83) thus *lavāṇaka*; *lūtā* [is derived from] *hasimṛgr* (Uṇ. III, 86), thus *tan*: *lotaḥ*; *pru-sṛ-lvaḥ samabhihāre vun* (III, 1, 149): *lavakaḥ*; *nāmansāman* (cf. Uṇ. IV, 150): *loman*; *nirabhyoḥ pūlvor ghañ* (III, 3, 28): *abhilāvaḥ* (13).

The root *stṝ* means "to cover. It forms *stṛṇāti* (active) and *stṛṇīte* (middle). Regarding the future, by the rule *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini VII.2.38), there is an optional long vowel for the augment *iṭ*: *āstaritā* or *āstarītā*. Regarding the optative (*liṅ*) and the aorist (*sic*) in the middle voice, by the rule *liṅsicor ātmanepadeṣu* (VII.2.42), there is an optional *iṭ*: *āstariṣīṣṭa* or *āstīrṣīṣṭa*; *āstariṣṭa* or *āstīrṣṭa*. Regarding the desiderative, by the rule *iṭ sani vā* (VII.2.41), there is an optional *iṭ*: *ātistīrṣati*, *ātistariṣati*, or *ātistarīṣati*. In the periphrastic aorist (*caṅ*), by the rule *at smṛdṝtvarapratha* (VII.4.95), the reduplication syllable becomes *at*: *atastarat*.

*Āstīrṇaḥ*, *stīrṇiḥ*; by Pāṇini III.3.32 (*pra-stro ’yajñe*), the suffix *ghañ* [is applied]: *prastāraḥ*; however, in the context of a sacrifice, *prastaraḥ* refers to the sacrificial grass for the oblations. By Pāṇini III.3.33 (*prathane vāv-aśabde*), [the suffix *ghañ* is applied]: *paṭasya vistāraḥ* (the spreading of a cloth); but when referring to sound, it is *vistaraḥ*. By Pāṇini III.3.34 (*chandonāmni ca*), [the suffix *ghañ* is applied]: *viṣṭārapaṅktiḥ* (a name of a meter). By Pāṇini VIII.3.93, *viṣṭaraḥ* means a seat made of woven grass. By Pāṇini III.3.120 (*ave tṛ-stror ghañ*), [the suffix *ghañ* is applied]: *avastāraḥ*. In the *svādi-gaṇa* (Pāṇini V.1.124), the root *stṛñ* [is included].

*vistṛṇoti* (he spreads), *vistṛtaḥ* (spread); *staraḥ* is a kind of garment; *starīḥ* (Uṇ. III, 158) means a cloud and a bed: having spread out the *starī*. (14) *kṝ ñ* in the sense of harming: *kṛṇāti*, *kṛṇīte*; *kīrṇaḥ*, *kīrṇiḥ*. *kṝ v ṝ ñ* in the sense of covering: *vṛṇāti*, *vṛṇīte*; *vūrṇaḥ*, *vūrṇiḥ*, *vivaraḥ*. From the roots *kṝ*, *vṛ*, *tṝ*, and *dṝ*, the suffix *unan* is applied (cf. Uṇ. III, 53): *Varuṇaḥ*. [The root] *vṛñ* is [also used] according to Nandī. (16)

The root *dhūñ* means "to shake. It forms *dhunāti* and *dhunīte*. By the rule *svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā* (VII.2.44), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *vidhotā* or *vidhavitā*. By the rule *dhūñprīñor nuk* (VII.3.37), the augment *nuk* is added: *vidhūnayati*. By the rule *stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (VII.2.72), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *adhāvīt*. The words *dhūnaḥ* and *dhūniḥ* are derived from it. In the group beginning with *svādi* (the fifth class), both *dhūñ* and *dhuñ* occur (V.9): *dhūnoti* and *dhunoti*. The past passive participle is *avadhūtaḥ* or *vidhutaḥ*. In the *curādi* group (X.292), one finds *dhūnayati*. In the *tudādi* group (VI.105), *dhū* in the sense of "shaking" forms *dhuvati*. (17)

The root *śṝ* is used in the sense of "injuring. [It forms: *śṛṇāti*, *śṛṇīte*, *śīryate*, *śīrṇaḥ*, *śīrṇiḥ*. According to *śṝdṝprāṃ hrasvo vā* (Pāṇini VI.4.122), there is optionally a short vowel: *viśaśaruḥ* or *viśaśruḥ*. By *laṣapatapada* (Pāṇini III.2.154), the suffix *ukañ* is applied: *viśārukaḥ*. By *śṝvandyor āruḥ* (Pāṇini III.2.173), the suffix *āru* is applied: *śarāruḥ* means "injurious. In the *uṇādi* section, by *kiṃjarayoḥ śriṇaḥ* (Uṇādi I.4), the suffix *āri* is applied: *kiṃśāruḥ* means "the awn of grain. By *śṝsvṛsnihi* (Uṇādi I.11), the suffix *u* is applied: [this forms *śaruḥ*]. 1 All manuscripts read this. 2 P adds *chinnalomā*. 3 See Hemacandra Dhātupāṭha IX.24. 165 IX.

*Śaru* means "a weapon that strikes" (*hiṃsra*). From the roots *khan* and *śṛ* with the prefix *āṅ*, [the suffix] *ḍi* is applied (Uṇ. I, 34): *paraśu*. From the root *śṛ* ("to destroy"), [the suffix] *u* is applied, the vowel is shortened, and *ga* and *nuṭ* are added (Uṇ. I, 125): *śṛṅga*, *śṛṅgāra*, *śiśira*. By [Pāṇini III, 1, 134], *śara* is formed with [the suffix] *ac*: *śaraṇa*. By [Uṇ. I, 126], *gaṇ* is applied to denote a bird: *śārṅga*. From the roots *śṝ*, *dṝ*, and *bhṛs*, [the suffix] *adi* is applied (Uṇ. I, 129): *śarad*. From the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, *dṝ*, and *bhṛ*, [the suffix] *va* is applied (Uṇ. I, 155): *śarva*. From the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, *vṛ*, and *cat*, [the suffix] *ṣvarac* is applied (cf. Uṇ. II, 123).

From the roots *śar* and *sṛśṝ*, with the suffix *ū* (cf. Uṇ. III.26): *śūrpaḥ* (“winnowing basket”); from *śṝ* with the suffix *kan* (cf. Uṇ. IV.3): *śarkarā* (“gravel”); from *śṝ* and *pṝ* with the suffix *iṣan* marked as *kit* (cf. Uṇ. IV.27): *śirīṣam* (“Acacia sirissa”); with the suffix *manin* (Uṇ. IV.144): *śarma* (“happiness”); from *śṝ*, *pṝ*, and *vṛñ* with the suffix *īkan*, doubling of the root, and *ruk* (insertion of *r*) for the reduplicated syllable (Uṇ. IV.19): *śarśarīkā*; from *kṝ*, *śṝ*, *pṝ*, and *kaṭi* with the suffix *īran* (Uṇ. IV.30): *śarīram* (“body”); with the suffix *asun* marked as *kit* (cf. Uṇ. IV.193): *śiraḥ* (“head”); and from *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, *pṝ*, *kuṭi*, *bhidi*, and *chidi* [with the suffix *asun*] (Uṇ. ...).

Thus, from the root *iṇ* with the suffix *kit*: *śiriḥ*, *śiraḥ* (both meaning "bird"; cf. Uṇādi-sūtra IV.127). From the root *iṇ* [with the suffix *ac*]: *śāriḥ*, *śārikā*. From the rule *ṝdor ap* (Pāṇini III.3.57): *śaraḥ*. From the root *śṝ* in the sense of "color" and "wind" (Dhātupāṭha III.3.21.2) with the suffix *ghañ*: *śāraḥ* means "color" and "wind. *Nīśāraḥ* is a garment that wards off cold winds; as it is said: "Generally, one who is emaciated in the winter season is like a cow that has not put on a *nīśāra* [garment]. (18)

The root *pṝ* is used in the senses of protecting (*pālan*) and filling (*pūraṇa*). In the forms *nipaparuḥ* and *nipapruḥ*, the rule *śṝdṝprāṃ hrasvo vā* (Pāṇini VI.4.122) applies. By the rule *ṝdor ap* (III.3.57), the suffix *ap* is added to form *paraḥ*. From the causative (*ṇyanta*) form, by the rule *vā dāntaśāntapūrṇadastaspaṣṭacchannajñaptāḥ* (VII.2.27), we have *pūrṇaḥ* and *pūritaḥ*. By the rule *na dhyākhyāpṝmūrchimadām* (VIII.2.57), the substitution of *ṛ* for *ra* does not occur, resulting in *pūrtaḥ* and *pūrtiḥ*. From the root *pūrī* in the sense of "to nourish" (*āpyāyana*), the form *pūrṇaḥ* is derived. By the rule *bhrājabhāsadhurvidyutorjipṝjuguprucharguṣṭikṣubhoyasṛgṛdhijvalaśucyaścaḥ* (III.2.177), the suffix *kvip* is applied to form *pūḥ*. By the rule *pṝbhidi* (Uṇādi I.24), the suffix *ku* is applied [to form *paruḥ*].

*puru* and *bahu*: from the root *pṛ* with the suffix *kuṣan* (Uṇ. IV. 74), we have *puruṣaḥ*. From *ṛ*, *pṛ*, *vapi* etc. (Uṇ. II. 118), we have the suffix *usi*: *paruḥ* (meaning joint). From *dhā*, *pṛ*, *vas*, *aj*, *ati* etc., we have the suffix *na* (Uṇ. III. 6): *parṇam*. From *śṝ* and *pṝ*, with the suffix *kit* (cf. Uṇ. IV. 27), we have *purīṣam*. From *pṛ* and *kali*, we have the suffix *uṣac* (cf. Uṇ. IV. 75): *paruṣam*. From *snā* etc., we have the suffix *vanip* (Uṇ. IV. 112): *parvan*. In the *juhoty-ādi* class (III. 4), there is *piparti*; in the *cur-ādi* class, *pṝ* in the sense of filling (X. 15): *pārayati*. (19) *mṛ* in the sense of injury: *mṛṇāti*. (22)
The roots *vṛ* and *bhṛ* mean "to support" (*bharaṇe*). [From *vṛ*: *vṛṇāti*; [from *bhṛ*: *bhṛṇāti*. The root *bhṛ* also means "to roast" (*bharjane*), where roasting is cooking (*pākaḥ*) (20.21).

The root *dṛ* means "to tear apart" (*vidāraṇe*). [Forms: *dṛṇāti*, *dīrṇaḥ*, *dīrṇiḥ*, *vidadaruḥ*, *vidadruḥ*. According to *at smṛdṝtvara* (Pāṇini VI.1.49), [we have] *vyadadarat*. By the rule *dṝsanijani* (Uṇādi I.3), the suffix *ñuṇ* is applied: *dāruḥ*. By the rule *kṝgṝśṝdṝbhyo vaḥ* (Uṇādi I.155), [we have] *darvaḥ*. By the rule *śṝdṝbhaso 'diḥ* (Uṇādi I.129), we have *Daradaḥ* as the name of a region. *Darad* is an indeclinable meaning "slightly. Its form *dareti* is a Prakrit corruption (*apabhraṃśaḥ*); that very word was used by poets through error.

Regarding the verse *daradalitaharidrā* (*Viddhaśālabhañjikā* III, 17): from the roots *kṝ*, *vṝ*, *tṝ*, and *dāri*, the suffix *unan* is applied (cf. *Uṇādisūtra* III, 53), yielding *dāruṇaḥ*. From the roots *vṝ* and *dṛ*, the suffix *vin* is applied (cf. *Uṇādisūtra* IV, 53), yielding:
1) *vajram* (thunderbolt), 2) *śāraṅgaḥ* (peacock), 3) *bhaye* (in the sense of fear).
[This applies to] all manuscripts, including I, X, and 166.

*darviḥ* [is derived from] *dṛṇāti-* with the suffix *tip* and shortening of the vowel, according to Uṇādi-sūtra IV, 183. *Dṛtiḥ* [is formed] by adding *alacau* after *ud-* and *dṛṇāti-*, with elision of the final syllable of the preceding word, according to Uṇādi-sūtra V, 19: *udaram*. According to Uṇādi-sūtra IV, 20: *pharpharīkādayaś ca*: *dardarīkam*. In the *pacādi* group (III, 1, 134): *daraṭ*, *darī*. In the *pṛṣodarādi* group (VI, 3, 109): *dardaraḥ* as a musical instrument, and *darduraḥ*. In the *ghaṭādi* group, the root *dṝ* meaning "fear" (I, 846) forms *darati* and *darayati*; from this [root], one forms *dārayati* (23). The root *jṝ* meaning "decay of age" (*vayohānau*): *jṛṇāti*. Past participle: *jīrṇaḥ*; noun: *jīrṇiḥ*. In the *divādi* group (IV, 22): *jīryati* (24).

The root *nṛ* (nṝ) means "to lead. It forms *nṛṇāti* and *nīrṇaḥ*. In the *ghaṭādi* group (DhP I, 847), it forms *narayati*. With the suffix *ac*, it forms *naraḥ* (III, 1, 134). According to the *Kāśikā* on IV, 1, 73, there is vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) for *nṛ* and *nara*, resulting in *nārī* (25). The root *kṝ* (kṝ) means "to injure. It forms *kṛṇāti* and *kīrṇaḥ*. In the *tudādi* group (DhP VI, 116), *kṝ* means "to scatter," forming *kirati* (26). The root *ṝ* (ṝ) means "to go. It forms *ṛṇāti* and *samīrṇaḥ*. It also forms the passive *īryate*. In the desiderative, it forms *aririṣati*, *arirīṣati*, and *īrṣiṣati* (27).

The root *gṝ* is used in the sense of "sound. [From it derive: *gṛṇāti*, *gīrṇaḥ*, *gīrṇiḥ*, *ujjagāra*, *agārīt*. By the rule *kṝgror uc ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra I.25), we have *guruḥ*. In the *tudādigaṇa*, *gṝ* is listed as meaning "swallowing" (VI.117):
*girati*. [These] twenty-seven [roots] are udātta (accented).

The root *jyā* is used in the sense of "wasting away. It is one of the nine roots that do not take the augment *iṭ*. According to Pāṇini VI.1.16 (*grahijyāvayi*), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Thus we have *jināti*; then, by Pāṇini VI.4.2, there is lengthening of the vocalized vowel, and by VII.3.80, the shortening of the *pvādi* group. Hence: *jīnaḥ*. Regarding *jīniḥ*, Durga [states this]. However, Nandī says: since the suffix *ktin* would otherwise apply, [Pāṇini] teaches *glājyāhābhyo niḥ* (III.3.95.4): thus *jyāniḥ*. Furthermore, in the *Uṇādi* section (IV.48), *niḥ* is taught after *vī*, *jyā*, and *jvari*: [thus *jyāniḥ*]. And in the rule for the suffix *ka*, the suffix *ḍa* is applied after *prasāri* and others: *brahmajyaḥ* (cf. III.2.3.1).

In the *uṇādi* [section], [the suffix] *nak* [is applied]: *jinaḥ*. Also, by [the rules] *lyapi ca* and *jyaś ca* (Pāṇini VI.1.41–42): *prajyāya* (29). *Vlī* in the sense of covering (*varaṇe*). *vlināti*. By [the rule] *artihrīvlī-* (VII.3.36), the augment *puk* is added: *vlepayati* (32). *Rī* in the senses of moving (*gati*) and harming (*eṣaṇa*). Harming (*reṣaṇa*) means injury (*hiṃsā*). *riṇāti*, *rīṇaḥ*, *repayati*. In the *divādi* [class], *nṛ* in the sense of flowing (*sravaṇe*) (IV.30): *rīyate* (30).

The root *lī* means "to adhere. From it come *lināti* and *līnaḥ*. In the *divādi* class (IV, 31), there is *līyate*; in the *curādi* class (X, 269), *lī* means "to liquefy," as in *ghṛtaṃ vilīnayati* ("he causes the ghee to melt"). The roots beginning with *lvī* and those beginning with *pvī* have been explained. 1. *vī* means "to go": *lvīnāti* (32). 2. *vrī* means "to choose" (*varaṇe*): *vrīṇāti*, *vrītaḥ*; in the *uṇādi* group, *vrīhiḥ* ("rice") [is derived from it] (33). 3. *bhrī* means "to nourish" (*bharaṇe*): *bhrīṇāti*, *bhrītaḥ* (34). [Note: All manuscripts read "so"; cf. Hemacandra’s *Uṇādisūtra* 710.]

167. *kṣi* in the sense of "to injure. *kṣiṇāti*, with the suffix *aṅ* (Pāṇini III.3.104): *kṣiyā*. In the *svādi* group (V.30), *kṣiṇoti*; in the *bhvādi* group (I.255), *kṣayati*; and in the *tudādi* group (VI.114), *kṣiyati* (35).

The root *jñā* is used in the sense of "to know" (*avabodhane*). By the rule *jñā-janor jā* (Pāṇini VI.1.5), the substitution of *jā* occurs: *jānāti*, *jānīte*. By the rule *anupasargāj jñaḥ* (I.3.76), both [parasmaipada and ātmanepada] endings are used; however, it is not so here: *avajānāsi māṃ, mūḍha?* ("O fool, do you despise me?"). By the rule *apahnave jñaḥ* (I.3.44), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used: *śatam apajānīte* ("he denies a hundred [debts]"). By the rule *saṃ-pratibhyām anādhyāne* (I.3.46), [the *taṅ* endings are used]: *saṃjānīte*, *pratijānīte*. By the rule *jñā-śru-smṛ-dṛśāṃ sanas* (I.3.57), the *taṅ* endings are used: *jijñāsate*. By the rule *nānor jñaḥ* (I.3.58): [the *taṅ* endings are used].

He desires to know his son (*putram anujijñāsati*). By the rule *jño ’vidarthasya karaṇe* (Pāṇini II.3.51), the genitive case is used: *sarpiṣo jānīte* ("he knows [the nature] of the clarified butter"). By the rule *vānyasya saṃyogādeḥ* (VI.4.68), there is optionally the substitution of *e* for the vowel: *jñeyāt* or *jñāyāt*. By the rule *māraṇatoṣaṇa* (Dhātupāṭha I.849), it is classified as *mit*: *saṃjñapayati* ("he causes to be known/pleased"). By the rule *sanīvantardha* (VII.2.49), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *jijñapayiṣati*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is not added, by the rule *āpjñapṛdhām īt* (VII.4.55), there is the substitution of *ī*: *jñīpsati*. By the rule *igupadhajñā* (III.1.135), the suffix *ka* is applied: [forming *jñaka*].

*jña-* [is formed] with the prefix *pra-* by rule III.2.6: *pathiprajñaḥ* ("one who knows the way"). Or, by rule VII.2.27 (*vā dāntaśānta...*), we have *saṃjñaptaḥ* and *saṃjñapitaḥ*. By rule III.3.106 (*ātaś copasarge*), we have *prajñā*. From the root *jñā-* [we derive]: *jñātiḥ* ("kinsman"), as in *jñātir bandhuḥ*; however, the form *jñānam jñātiḥ* does not exist, because it is superseded by the well-established usage (36). These [roots] ending in an *anudātta* vowel are thirty-six (36).

The root *bandh* means "to bind. It is marked with an anudātta accent and takes the udātta *eL* suffix. From it we derive: *badhnāti*, *badhnīta*; *abāndhīt* (by Pāṇini III.1.83: *halaḥ śnaḥ śānaj jhau*); *abhāntsīt* (by Pāṇini VIII.2.37: *ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣantasya sdhvoḥ*). From this root: *Bandhakī* (a harlot), by Uṇādi-sūtra IV.41. *Bandhūka* (the flower of the *bandhūka* tree). *Bandhuḥ* (a kinsman), by Uṇādi-sūtra I.11 (*śṝsvṛsnihi...*). *Badhiraḥ* (deaf), by Uṇādi-sūtra I.52 (*iṣitimimadi...* [with the suffix] *kirac*). *Bradhnaḥ* (the sun), by Uṇādi-sūtra III.5 (*bandher bradhibudhi ca* [with the suffix] *naḥ*).

*Bradhnaḥ* means the sun; *budhnaḥ* means the root. By [Pāṇini III.4.41], *bandhaḥ* is used in the sense of the locus with the suffix *ṇamul*: *hastabandham* bound. And by [Pāṇini III.4.42], when it is a name (*saṃjñā*): *kukkuṭībandham* bound. (37)

The root *vṛṅ* means "to choose" (*saṃbhakti*). It has an udātta accent. *Saṃbhakti* means "service" or "devotion. From this root: - *vṛṇīte*, *varitā*, *varītā* (the lengthening occurs by Pāṇini VII.2.38). - *vṛtaḥ* (past passive participle). - *vivaritā*, *vivarītā* (desiderative). - *avṛta*, *avariṣṭa*, *avarīṣṭa* (aorist). - *vuvūrṣate*, *vivariṣate*, *vivarīṣate* (desiderative middle). By the rule *jalpabhikṣa* (Pāṇini III.2.155), the suffix *ṣākan* is applied: *varākaḥ* ("miserable one"). By the rule *vṛṅa enyaḥ* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.98): *vareṇyaḥ* ("excellent," "to be chosen"). *Varvarīkā* (a woman with curly hair). By the rule *grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca* (Pāṇini III.3.58), the suffix *ap* is applied: *varaḥ* ("bridegroom," "choice").
In the *svādi-gaṇa*, the root *vṛñ* means "to choose" (V.8): *vṛṇoti*, *vṛṇute*. (38)

*Śranth* [is used] in the senses of loosening and gladdening (3). From here on, twelve [roots] follow that take the augment *iṭ* and are *parasmaipada*. [Examples: *śrathnāti*, having loosened (*śrathitvā* / *śranthitvā*). Regarding the prohibition of the *yak* and *ciṇ* suffixes, there is an addition [to the rule]: "The roots *śranth*, *granth*, and *brū*, as well as those that are *ātmanepada* and intransitive. 1. *vijñaptaḥ* was added; 2. all manuscripts read this; 3. K reads *°harṣaṇayoḥ*, C reads *°harṣayoḥ*, S reads *°praharṣayoḥ*, P reads *°pratiharṣaṇayoḥ*; 4. all manuscripts read this, though one should read *dvāviṃśatiḥ*. IX. 168.

Regarding *nam* (cf. III, 1, 89 Bh.): *mālā śrathnīte svayam eva* ("the garland unbinds by itself"); [it forms] *aśranthiṣṭa*. According to the rule *śranthigranthidanbhisvanjīnāṃ* (cf. I, 2, 6 Kāś.), the *liṭ* suffix is treated as having the *kit* designation, and the substitution of *e* for *a* is also prescribed: [thus] *śrethuḥ*. In the *curādi* class, there are the roots *śrantha* and *grantha* in the sense of "binding" (*saṃdarbhe*) with the addition of *ṇic*: *śranthayati* / *śranthati*, *granthayati* / *granthati*. In the *bhvādi* class, there are *śrathi* in the sense of "looseness" (*śaithilye*) and *grathi* in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*) (I, 35–36): *śranthate*, *granthate* (39).

*Manth* means "to churn. One churns (*manthāti*). In the *bhvādi* class (I. 47), it is *manthati*; likewise, *math* in the sense of churning (I. 901): *mathati*. (40) *Granth* means "to compose" (*saṃdarbha*). Composition is binding. One binds (*grathnāti*); the act of binding is *granthanam*. It should be illustrated in the same way as *śrathnāti*. (41) *Kunth* means "to crush" (*śleṣaṇa*). One crushes (*kuthnāti*). Having crushed (*kunthitvā*, *kuthitvā*). *Kutha* is an elephant's saddle-cloth; *kuthā* (feminine). Durga says, "One crushes (*kuthīti*). (42)

The root *mṛd* means "to crush. It forms *mṛdnāti* (he crushes) and *mṛdyate* (it is crushed). According to Pāṇini V.4.39, the suffix *kan* is applied after *mṛt* and *mṛdas*, yielding *mṛttikā* (clay). By Pāṇini I.2.7, the suffix *ktvā* is *kit* after *mṛḍ* and *mṛd*, resulting in *mṛditvā* (having crushed).

The root *mṛḍ* means "to soothe" (*sukhane*). It forms *mṛḍnāti*; *mṛḍitvā*. In the *tudādigaṇa* (VI.38), it is *mṛḍati*. From *mṛḍ*, we have *mṛḍaḥ* (a soother) and *mṛḍīkam* (gold). The root *gudh* means "to be angry" (*roṣe*). It forms *gudhnāti*. From *gudh*, by Uṇādi V.2, the suffix *ūma* is added, yielding *godhūmaḥ* (wheat). In the *bhidādigaṇa* (III.3.104), *godhā* (an iguana) is formed; here, *tal* is the suffix. In the *divādigaṇa* (IV.13), *gudh* means "to envelop" (*pariveṣṭane*), forming *gudhyati*. (45)

The root *kuṣ* means "to draw out" (*niṣkarṣa*). Drawing out is the act of extracting. In the sense of the object acting as the agent (*karmakartṛ*), the rule *kuṣirajorḥ prācāṃ śyan parasmaipadaṃ ca* (Pāṇini III.1.90) applies: *kuṣyati pādaḥ svayam eva* ("the foot draws itself out"). With the prefix *nir-*, by the rule *niraḥ kuṣaḥ* (Pāṇini VII.2.46), the augment *iṭ* is optionally added: *niṣkoṣitā* or *niṣkoṣṭā*; *nirakoṣīt* or *nirakukṣat*. By the rule *iṇ niṣṭhāyām* (Pāṇini VII.2.47), the form *niṣkuṣitaḥ* is obtained. According to *mṛḍamṛda...* (Pāṇini I.2.7), the suffix *ktvā* is marked with the *kit* designation: *kuṣitvā*. By the rule *hanikuṣi...* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.2), the suffix *kthan* is applied [to form *kuṣṭha*].

*Kuṣṭha-* [is derived from] *uṣi-kuṣi-* (Uṇ. II.4), with the suffix *-than*: *koṣṭha* means the belly; by virtue of the rule on "abundance" (*bāhulaka*, III.3.1), *prakoṣṭha* means the forearm. From *uci-kuṣi-kuṣi-* [comes] with the suffix *-kitan*: *kuṣita*. From *pluṣi-śuṣi-kuṣi-* [comes] with the suffix *-ksi* (cf. Uṇ. III.155): *kukṣi*. From *kuṭhi-kuṣi-* [comes] with the suffix *-kāku* (cf. Uṇ. III.77): *kuṣāku*. (46)

The root *kṣubh* means "to shake" (*saṃcalane*). In *kṣubhnāti*, there is an absence of the substitution of *ṇ* due to the rule *kṣubhnādi* (Pāṇini VIII.4.39). According to *kṣubdhasvānta* (VII.2.18), if *kṣubdha* refers to a churning-stick (*mantha*), it is derived from this [root]; otherwise, it is derived from *kṣubhita*. [In the perfect tense] it becomes *akṣobhīt*. In the *divādi* class (IV.129), it is *kṣubhyati*; in the past tense, *akṣubhat*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.787), it is *kṣobhate*. (47) The roots *ṇabha* and *tubha* mean "to injure" (*hiṃsāyām*). [In the present tense] *praṇabhnāti*; in the *divādi* class (IV.130), *nabhyati*; in the *dyutādi* class (I.788), *nabhate*. [From *tubha*: *tubhnāti*, *tubhyati*, *tobhate*. (48, 49) [Note 1: Like *śranthi*; Note 2: cf. Hemacandra’s Uṇādisūtra 212.]

169. The root *kīś* means "to afflict" (*vibādhane*). It forms *kīśnāti*; the future forms are *kleṣṭā* and *kleśitā*. According to Pāṇini VI.1.50, the suffix *veṭ* (the augment *iṭ* is optional) applies after the root *kliś* before the *ktvā* suffix and the *niṣṭhā* suffixes: *kīṣṭvā* or *kīśitvā*, *kliṣṭaḥ* or *kliśitaḥ*. In the *divādi* class (cf. III.4.69), it forms *kliśyati*; the nouns *kleśaḥ* and *kīnāśaḥ* [are derived from this root]. (50)

The root *aś* means "to eat. [Examples: *aśnāti*, *aśitā*. Regarding the rule *upeyivān anāśvān anūcānaś ca* (Pāṇini III.2.109), the form *anāśvān* is correct; by *āśitaḥ kartā* (VI.1.207), the agent (*kartṛ*) is udātta-accented on the first syllable. With the suffix *ghañ* (III.3.121): *samāśā gomatā jitāḥ* ("the quarters were conquered by the possessor of cattle"). By *iṣyaśibhyāṃ takan* (Uṇādi III.148): *aṣṭakā*. By *aśipaṇāyyo ruk ukau ca* (cf. Uṇādi IV.137): *aśriḥ*. In the *svādi-gaṇa*, *aśū* means "to pervade" (V.18): *aśnute*. In that same context, there are fifty-one [derivatives] involving the sense of grasping (*grahaṇa*).

The root *udhrasa* means to glean (*uñcha*). [From it derive] *dhrasnāti*, *dhrastvā*, and *dhrasitvā*. In the *curādi* group (X, 202), there is *dhrāsayati*. The root *iṣ* in the sense of repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*)—repetition meaning frequency—[gives] *iṣṇāti*. [Derivatives: *eṣitvā*, *preṣitaḥ*. In the *divādi* group (IV, 19), *iṣ* in the sense of motion [gives] *anviṣyati*. In the *tudādi* group (VI, 59), *iṣ* in the sense of desire [gives] *icchati*. [Derivatives: *iṣṭvā* and *eṣitvā*. Regarding the rule *tīṣasaha* (cf. VII, 2, 48), this very [root] is what is intended: *iṣṭaḥ*. Because of the prohibition in the rule *ato yasya vibhāṣā* (VII, 2, 15), the [substitution of *ī* for *i*] does not apply here: *preṣitaḥ*. (53)
In the sense of "separation," *viṣ* means "to separate"; [the noun] *viṣam*. In the *hvādi* class (*hvādi-gaṇa*), *viṣḷ* is used in the sense of "pervasion" (*vyāpti*): *veveṣṭi*, *aviṣat* (54).

*Pruṣa* and *pluṣa* are used in the senses of "smearing with oil," "sprinkling," and "filling. [The present tense forms are] *pruṣṇāti*; [the past participle] *pruṣitaḥ*; [the noun] *vipruṭ*. [The root] *pī-uṣṇāti*. In the *bhvādi* class (*bhvādi-gaṇa*) [roots 735, 736]: *proṣati*, *pī-oṣati*. In the *divādi* class (*divādi-gaṇa*), *pluṣa* is used in the sense of "burning" (*dāha*): *pluṣyati* (55, 56). *Puṣa* is used in the sense of "nourishing" (*puṣṭi*). [The forms are] *puṣṇāti*, *poṣitā*. In the *divādi* class (*divādi-gaṇa*) [root 73]: *puṣyati*, *poṣṭā*, *puṣkaram*, *puṣkalam*. In the *bhvādi* class (*bhvādi-gaṇa*) [root 732]: *poṣati* (57).

The root *muṣ* means "to steal. From it: *muṣṇāti* ("he steals"); having stolen, *muṣitvā* (by Pāṇini I.2.8); *mumuṣiṣati* ("he wishes to steal"). The past passive participle is *muṣitaḥ*. By the rule *muṣer dīrghaś ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra II.42), the suffix *kikan* is added: *mūṣikaḥ* ("mouse") and *mūṣikā* ("female mouse"). By the rule *sṛvṛbhūśuṣimuṣibhyaḥ kit* (Uṇādi-sūtra III.41), the suffix *ka* is added: *muṣkaḥ*, meaning "testicle" and "scrotum. The root *khav* means "the manifestation of a being"; that is, occurring after birth. *Khavnāti* ("he manifests"). According to the rule *chvoḥ śūḍ* (Pāṇini VI.4.19), the form *khaunāti* is used by the refined (*sabhyāḥ*). The future is *khavitā*; the past participle is *khauḥ*. According to Durga, the suffix *khac* is also applied.

And *heṭha* [is used] in the sense of destruction. *Heṭhati*. In the *bhvādi* class, *heṭha* means "to oppress" (*vibādhāyām*) [DhP I.285]: *heṭhate*. (60) These are the roots with an acute accent that have an acute-accented *īṭ*. 60.

The root *graha* is used in the sense of "taking" (*upādāna*). It is marked with both the acute (*udātta*) and circumflex (*svarita*) accents. "Taking" (*upādāna*) means "appropriating. There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule *grahijyāvayi* (Pāṇini VI.1.16): *gṛhṇāti*, *gṛhṇīte*. By the rule *graho 'liṭi dīrghaḥ* (VII.2.37), there is lengthening in the future: *grahītā*. Lengthening is not desired for the augment *iṭ* when it follows the suffix *ciṇvat*: *tvayā grāhiṣyate*. In the aorist, *agrahīt*, there is no vowel strengthening (*vṛddhi*) by the rule *hrmvyantakṣaṇa* (VII.2.5). By the rule *rudavidamuṣagrahisvapipracchaḥ saṃśca* (I.2.8), the suffix *ktvā* is marked with the *kit* designation: *gṛhītvā*. [In the desiderative] *jighṛkṣati*. (Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.2.8; 6.1.16; 7.2.37, 37.3; 7.2.5; 10.170).

The suffix *ṇini* is applied after [roots] such as *grah* (Pāṇini III.1.134): *grāhī*. By the rule *vibhāṣā graho* (III.1.143), the suffix *ṇa* is optionally applied: *grāhaḥ* and *grahaḥ*. However, when combined with *geha*, the suffix *ka* is applied (III.1.144): *gṛham*. In the section on *ac*-suffixes, by the rule *śakti-tomara-lāṅgala-* (cf. III.2.9.1), the suffix *ac* is applied: *śaktigrahaḥ*. Furthermore, in the sense of "that which is to be held," by the rule *sūtre ca dhāryarthe* (III.2.9.2), there is *sūtragrahaḥ*. Also, by the rule *phalegrahir ātmaṃbhariś ca* (III.2.26), and by *padāsvairibāhyā-* (III.1.119), the suffix *kyap* is applied.

The word *pragṛhya* [is derived with] the suffix *ka*; *gṛhyaka* means "a bird"; *gṛhītāmagṛhyā senā* ("an army whose horses have been seized"); *arjunagṛhyā devāḥ* ("the gods who have Arjuna as their protector"). By the rule *grahavṛdṛniścigamaśca* (Pāṇini III.3.58), the suffix *ap* is applied: *nigrahaḥ*. By the rule *udi grahaḥ* (III.3.35), the suffix *ghañ* is applied: *udgrāhaḥ*. By the rule *sami muṣṭau* (III.3.36): *saṃgrāhaḥ* in the sense of a wrestler's grip. By the rule *ave graho varṣapratibandhe vā* (III.3.51): *avagrahaḥ* or *avagrāhaḥ*. *Avagrahaḥ* [also refers to] the forehead of an elephant (cf. Amarakośa II.8.38). By the rule *pre vaṇijām* (III.3.52): [the suffix *ghañ* is applied].

The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *grah* following the word *tulā*, as well as in the sense of "seizing" (*pragraha*) and "reins" (*raśmi*). (Pāṇini III, 3, 53): *pragrāhaḥ*, *pragrahaḥ*. Furthermore, the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *grah* following the words *ava* and *ni* when expressing "abuse" (*ākrośa*). (Pāṇini III, 3, 45).

(3.45): *avagrāhaḥ* occurs in the sense of "seizure" (*haraṇe*), as in: "May there be a seizure for you, O low-born one! (*vṛṣala*); *nigrāhaḥ* occurs in the sense of "desire to obtain" (*prelipsāyām*) (Pāṇini III.3.46): "The twice-born man goes about with a ladle-seizure (*sruvapragrāheṇa*) seeking alms"; *parau yajñe* (III.3.47): "He performs the northern enclosure (*uttaraparigrāham*"); *akṣeṣu glahaḥ* (III.3.70). Because of the prohibition of roots beginning with *grah-* [from taking the suffix *iṭ*] in the rule *titutra-* (VII.2.9) by the addition *grahāder niṣedhāt* (VII.2.9.1), we have *nigṛhītiḥ*. By the rule *nāmny ādiśigrahoḥ* (III.4.58), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied: *nāmagrāham vakti* ("he speaks mentioning the name"). By the rule *graher aniḥ* (Uṇādi V.67), we have *grahaṇiḥ*, meaning dysentery (*pravāhikā*). (61)
In the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, a commentary on roots (*dhātuvṛtti*) conceived by Bhaṭṭa Kṣīrasvāmin, the *kryādigaṇa* is completed.

Om! This group of nine classes has been explained by resorting to the *kuśa* and *kāśa* grasses [as a mere support]; now the *curādigaṇa* is begun, wherein even great chariot-warriors have been defeated. Due to the loss of traditional transmission regarding both the text and its meaning, and because of the delusion of even the great, we do not know what we have omitted here or what we have added.

*cura* (to steal): the suffix *ṇic* is applied in its own sense (*svārthe*) according to Pāṇini III.1.25, *curādibhyo ṇic*. In the *kryādigaṇa*, the root *grah* is marked with the *svarita* accent; likewise, *lakṣi* and *ceṣṭ* belong to the *curādigaṇa*.

Thus, because the root *lakṣ* is remembered as having a svarita accent (*svaritet*), the ātmanepada affix *taṅ* does not occur when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, according to Pāṇini I.3.74 (*ṇicaś ca*). However, Candra has recorded it here as being both parasmaipada and ātmanepada, and he allows for the optional presence of the causative suffix *ṇic*. From the causative form *corayati*, the suffix *ām* is added according to Pāṇini III.1.35 (*pratyayāntāt*).

He committed theft (*corayāṃcakāra*), he stole (*acūcurat*), and he incited someone who was stealing (*corayantam prayuktavān*). Even from the causative form (*ṇyantāt*), when another causative suffix (*ṇic*) is added, the result is *acūcurad* alone. Because of the rule "There is an extension [of the prohibition] regarding the elision of *kvip*, the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhātva*), the *caṅ* reduplication, the subsequent *ṇi*, and the substitution of *ku*" (*kvi-lug-upadhātva-caṅ-paranirhrāsa-ku-tveṣūpasaṃkhyānam*; Pāṇini I.1.58.2), the status of being a "substitute" (*sthānivattva*) is prohibited. Consequently, since the *ṇi* has been elided in the causative (*ṇau ṇilope*), there is no absence of the condition of being "one whose penultimate vowel is elided" (*aglopitva*). Thus, by the rule "In the case of a *caṅ* reduplication following a *ṇi*, there is no shortening of the penultimate vowel for roots ending in *ā*, those marked with *ś*, or those marked with *ṛ*" (*ṇau caṅy upadhāyā hrasvo na āśāsvṛditām*; Pāṇini VII.4.1; VII.4.2), the prohibition of shortening does not apply. The word *coraṭ* is derived from the root *cura* (belonging to the *pacādi* group, III.1.134). *Corī* is formed because it belongs to the *prajñādi* group (V.4.38).

1 All manuscripts. 2 P: *iti śrīKṣīrataraṅgiṇyāṃ dhātuvṛttau kryādir gaṇaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ* (thus ends the *kryādi* class in the *Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī*, the commentary on roots). 3 P: *vāgama*. 4 PC: *°dadmahe*. 171. *X*: "A thief (*cauraḥ*): by virtue of being listed among *chattra* and others (Pāṇini IV, 4, 62), there is optionally the suffix *ṇa*; even when *ṇa* is applied, because it is treated as if *aṇ* had been applied, we have *caurī* (a female thief) and *tāpasī* (an ascetic woman). From the *bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III, 3, 104), we have *curā* (theft); from the rule *ṇyāsaśrantho yuc* (III, 3, 107), we have *coraṇā* (the act of stealing). By the rule *er aj* (III, 3, 56)—which, according to [the principle] *aṇyantānām* (see I, 187), allows for the re-introduction of the suffix *ghañ* (III, 3, 18–19)—we have *coraḥ* (a thief). (1)

In the sense of "recollection" (*smṛti*), [the root] *cit* [is used]; one "thinks" (*cintayati*). From the rule *cintipūji* (Pāṇini III.3.105), the suffix *aṅ* is applied, resulting in *cintā*. By the inclusion of the indicatory letter *it*, it is made known that the roots beginning with *cur* (the *curādi* group) are not invariably *ṇic*-transitive (*anitya-ṇyantāḥ*); otherwise, because of the status of the substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*) for the *ṇic* suffix, the rule *aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti* (Pāṇini VI.4.24) would not apply to the *ṇic*-form, and thus roots such as *cint* would have been taught with the augment *num* already attached. Furthermore, the non-invariability [of the *curādi* roots] is restricted to specific instances based on observed usage (*lakṣya*), as in:
"Having heard the words of the lord of the earth, the Puṣyamānavas shouted aloud" (cf. Pāṇini VII.2.23 Bh.).

*Yantri* [is used] in the sense of contraction. It constrains; hence *yantraṇā*. (3) *Sphuḍi* is used in the sense of joking. One says *sphuṇḍayati*. Durga says: "It is *sphuṭī*" [meaning *sphuṭayati*]; some say *sphuḍi* is used in the sense of striking. (4) *Lakṣa* is used in the senses of seeing and marking. Marking is a sign. Because of the traditional rule that "*lakṣi*" and "*ceṣṭa*" belong to the *curādi* group, it is marked with the *svarita* accent: one uses *lakṣayate* or *lakṣayati*. From the root *lakṣ*, [the forms] *lakṣaṇā*, *lakṣaṇam*, and *Lakṣmīḥ* are derived by the rule "*muṭ ca*" (Uṇādi III.160). Regarding *śama* and *lakṣa* in the sense of observation (X.156–157), the reading up to *ākusma* (X.135) is for the sake of the *ātmanepada*: one uses *lakṣayate*. (5)

The root *kudri* is used in the sense of speaking untruths (*anṛtabhāṣaṇe*). It forms *kundrayati*. In the *Pārāyaṇa*, it belongs to the *gādi* group: *gundrā* is *bhadramustā*. Some say it ends in *ṛt* (*ṛdit*). The root *laḍa* is used in the sense of fondling (*upasevāyām*). It forms *lāḍayati* and *upalālayati* [meaning] "he fondles his son. It is called *lālanā*. According to the rule *nāṅye mito 'hetau ca* (X.87), there is no *mit*-designation here. However, in the *Bhvādi* class, *laḍa* is listed as "play" (*vilāse*) at I.381; because it has multiple meanings, in the sense of "tongue-twisting" (*jihvonmanthana*), the root *laḍi* is designated as *mit* (at I.852): thus it forms *laḍayati*. The root *midi* is used in the sense of affection (*snehane*). It forms *mindayati*; *mindaḥ* refers to a leper (*kuṣṭhī*). Kauśika says it is *mideti*: thus it forms *medayati*.

*olaḍi* in the sense of "throwing up" (*utkṣepe*): *olaṇḍayati* "he throws up a load"; *olaṇḍitaḥ*. Likewise, because of the traditional rule (*smaraṇāt*) that the root is *laṇḍi*, there is no substitution of *o* for *ava*. Others, however, say that because the root is not invariably *ṇic*-caused (*anitya-ṇyantatvāt*), they assign the indicatory letter *o* (*anubandham*) for the sake of the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* in the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā-natvārtham*) [according to Pāṇini VI.1.45]: *aṇḍnaḥ*. But Durga [the author of the Kāśikā] cited *laṇḍinaḥ* in the sense of the past passive participle (*kte*); and that is worse than evil (*pāpāt pāpīyaḥ*), because the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* would apply immediately [to the suffix]; otherwise, as in the case of *vinnā* and so on, the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* would occur in forms such as *vidita*. The followers of Candra also mention *landi*: *avalandayati uṣṭram* ("he causes the camel to throw up").

How much should we be angry, and how much should we be pleased, with those who define the definition (*lakṣaṇa*) in this manner while following the object of definition (*lakṣya*) according to the maxim of the blind man and the hen?
(9) vā 1 so all the manuscripts 2 KC *lakṣirekaś* 3 P *utkṣepaṇe* 4 KC *iva*

X 172 *jala* in the sense of covering. It forms *jālayati*, *jālakaḥ*, and *jālam*. Nandī [states] that *la* [is used]: *lājayati*, *lājāḥ*. The followers of Candra do not accept both of these, since they are established from the roots *jala* in the sense of striking (I, 886) and *laja* / *lāji* (I, 257). In the section beginning with *jval* (I, 886), where *jala* means "to strike": *jalati*, *jālam*, *jalam* (10).

*pīḍāgahane*. *Gahana* means affliction (*bādhā*). It afflicts (*pīḍayati*). Although the suffix *ktin* would have been expected, since the suffix *yuc* is applicable, it becomes *pīḍā* by virtue of belonging to the *bhidādi* group (Pāṇini III.3.104). According to Pāṇini VII.4.3 (*bhrājabhāsabhāṣadīpa-* etc.), the forms are *apīpīḍat* and *apīpiḍat*. Durga states that *pīḍa* means immersion (*avagāhana*); hence *tilapīḍakaḥ* ("oil-presser").

The root *naṭ* [is used] in the sense of "falling down" (*avasyandana*). Falling down means slipping. According to [Pāṇini 3.1.56], *nāṭ*, *krāth*, and *piṣ* [take the affix *ṇic*]: he causes the thief to fall down (*unnāṭayati*); hence *nāṭaka*. In the *bhvādi* class and the *ghaṭādi* class, *naṭ* is listed as "bending" (*natī*; Dhātupāṭha 1.818): *naṭayati* "he bends a branch"; *naṭ* is also listed as "dancing" (*nṛtī*; Dhātupāṭha 1.332): *naṭati*, *nāṭayati*. Nandi says that from *naḍ* [come]: *naḍaḥ*, *nāḍī*, *praṇālaḥ*, *praṇālī*. (12)

Now, regarding *ā-śrath* in the sense of "to gladden": in the verse beginning with *ā dhṛṣād vā* (X, 264), its formation is established by the rule *śrath hiṃsāyām* (X, 280). Because it is listed here [in this specific section], there is a change in form: *ā-śrathayate*. *Nandī* says that [the root] is *krath*: by the rule *krāthapiṣām* (H, 3, 56), one says *utkrāthayati* (13) in the sense of "killing" (*caurya*). *badh* in the sense of "restraint": *bādhayati*, *abībadhat*. In the *Bhvādi* class, *bādhṛ* is used in the sense of "obstructing" (I, 5): *bādhate*, *ababādhat*. The followers of Candra say it is *bandh*: *bandhayati*, *bandhati*. In the *Kryādi* class (IX, 37), it is *badhnāti* (14).

The root *pṛ* is used in the sense of filling (*pūraṇe*). It forms *pārayati* (causative) and *pāryate* (passive). By the rule *anupasargāl limpavinda* (Pāṇini III.1.138), the suffix *śa* is applied, yielding *pārayaḥ*. In the *hvādi* class (III.4), it is *piparti*; in the *kryādi* class (III.9.19), it is *pṛṇāti*. Durga states that the form is simply *pṛ*. The root *ūrj* is used in the senses of strength (*bala*) and living (*prāṇana*). Living means existing. It forms *ūrjayati*. From *ūrjana*, the suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule *bhrājabhāsa* (III.2.177), resulting in *ūrk*. Furthermore, by the rule *ūrjasvin* (V.2.114), there is a formal exception (*nipātana*) which allows for the presence of the suffix *asun* even though it is not otherwise prescribed. Thus, *ūrjasvin* is also established.

*Varṇa* means "description. *Varṇayati* (18). Some say it means "to take sides" (*pakṣa-parigraha*). *Pakṣayati* (17). *Cūrṇa* means "impelling. Impelling is "crushing. *Cūrṇayati*. Candra says *cūrṇa* means "grinding" (18). *Partha* means "throwing down. *Parthayati*. Some say *pṛtha* (20). *Sāmba* means "connection. *Sāmbayati*; [the derivative] *Sāmbaḥ*. Candra says [the root is] *śamba*: *śambalam* (21). *Bhakṣa* means "eating. *Bhakṣayati*. [The suffix] *ṇa* is applied after roots ending in *śili*, *kāmi*, *bhakṣi*, and *ācari*.
(IH‚ 2‚ 1‚ 7): "Meat-eaters" (*māṃsabhakṣāḥ*); from the root *bhakṣ* with the suffix *ghañ* (I 1I ‚ 3‚ 18. 19): *bhakṣaḥ* (22) 1 KC *saṃpeṣaṇa* 173.

The root *kuṭṭ* is used in the senses of cutting and reviling. *Kuṭṭayati*. By the rule *jaI pabhikṣakuṭṭa* (III. 2. 155), the suffix *ṣākan* is applied: *kuṭṭākaḥ*, "sugarcane-cutter" (*ikṣukuṭṭākaḥ*). (23) *Cuṭṭ* is used in the sense of becoming small. *Cuṭṭayati*. Some say it is *puṭṭ*; both were read by Durga, but Candra did not read even one of them. (24) *Suṭṭ* is used in the sense of disrespect. *Suṭṭayati*. Candra and Durga consider *suṭṭ* and others to be *ṣopadeśa* (roots with an initial *ṣ*): *suṣuttayiṣati*. And Durga also [mentions] *aṭṭ*: *aṭṭayati*. *Aṭṭaḥ* means a platform; *attaṃ* means prepared food. (26. 25)

*Luṇṭha* means to steal. From *luṇṭhayati*, [the suffix] *āka* is added according to the rule *jalpabhikṣa* (Pāṇini III.2.155), resulting in *luṇṭhākaḥ*. Some maintain that the root is *luṇṭ* because of the observation of forms such as *luṭi* in the *bhvādi* class (Dhātupāṭha I.350). *Śaṭha* and *śvaṭha* mean lack of refinement and movement. From them come *śāṭhayati* and *śvāṭhayati*. In the *bhvādi* class, *śaṭha* is listed under deceit (I.363); from this [root], *śaṭhaḥ* is derived. The followers of Durga (*Daurgāḥ*) state that the root is *śvaṭhī*: hence *śvaṇṭhayati*. (27–29)

*Tuja*, *pij*, and *luja* [are used] in the sense of violence (*hiṃsā*) and taking by force (*balādāna*). "Niketa" means a dwelling (*āvasatha*). *Tujyati* [gives] *tuñja*. *Piñjayati*, *luñjayati*. These are listed here (X, 215, 217, 218) either for the sake of including them as transitive verbs—since the rule "from *ā* and *svad*" applies to transitive roots—or for the sake of distinguishing their meanings; or for the sake of distinguishing their forms: *tuñjayate*. In the *Bhvādi* class, however, it is *tuñjati* (I, 264). *Piji*: *piñjalaḥ* (30, 31). *Pisa* in the sense of going (*gati*): *pesayati*. In the *Bhvādi* class (I, 751), it is *pesati* (32).

*Sāntva* is used in the sense of employing conciliation (*sāma*). One *sāntvayati*. According to Candra, *sāma* means "to conciliate" (*sāntveti*); [the denominative] *sāmayati*. *Sāntva* is derived from the *uṇādi* suffixes as *nāman* and *sāman* (cf. *Uṇ.* IV, 150 and 152). (33) *Śvalka* and *valka* mean "to speak" (*paribhāṣaṇe*). One *śvalkayati*; one *valkayati*. *Valkala*, *valka* means "tree bark. (34, 35) *Sniṭa* means "to moisten" (*snehane*). One *sneṭayati*. Some say it is *smiṭa*. (37)
The root *sphiṭ* is used in the sense of disrespect. It forms *spheṭayati*; a *spheṭaka* is one who causes dispersal; *saṃspheṭa* is a tumultuous battle.

(36) The root *śliṣ* is used in the sense of clinging or joining. It forms *śleṣayati*. In the *bhvādi* class (I, 734), it is *śleṣati*; in the *divādi* class (IV, 77), it is *śliṣyati*. (38) The root *path* is used in the sense of going. It forms *paripanthayati*. The prefix *pari-* denotes an enemy. (39)

*pic* in the sense of "beating": *piccayati*. *Picuḥ* means cotton and down; [the derivative] *picavyaḥ*. (40) *Chad* in the sense of "covering": *chādayati* [he covers] the face; *chadir* in the sense of "strengthening" (DhP I, 851) with the suffix *mit*: *chadayati*; or, according to "optionally up to *dhṛṣ*" (*ā dhṛṣād vā*), *chada* in the sense of "concealing" (cf. X, 290): *chādayati*, *chadati*. Or rather, this reading is for the sake of showing a difference in form: *chādayate*. By the rule "or in *dānta-śānta-*" (VII, 2, 27), we have *cchannaḥ* and *chāditaḥ*. By the rule "*chader ghe 'dvyupasargasya*" (VI, 4, 96), there is shortening: *pracchadaḥ*.

1. *Śulka* [is derived from] *śulkayati* and *addati śulkam*. 9. Regarding *uraśchadaḥ*: by rule III.3.118, "In the masculine, when used as a name (*saṃjñā*), the suffix *gha* is generally applied," [we have *uraśchadaḥ*]. It is not used here in *saṃpracchādaḥ*. By rule VI.4.97, "In the presence of *isman*, *tran*, and *kvip*, there is shortening," we have *chadis* (with *is*); by Uṇādi-sūtra II.109, "after *arcis* and *śuci*... [we have *is*], resulting in *chadma*, *chattram*, and *gṛhacchatra*. (41)

The root *śraṇ* means "to give. From it, one forms *śrāṇayati*. Regarding the term *viśrāṇanam*, although the suffix *yuc* would have been expected, by virtue of the letter *ca* in the rule *cintipūji* (Pāṇini III.3.105), the suffix *aṅ* is desired; thus we have *śrāṇā*, which is that [food] given to a mendicant. Because it belongs to the *ghaṭādi* group, the causative form is *śraṇayati* (42). The root *taḍ* means "to strike. From it, one forms *tāḍayati*. By the rule *taḍer ṇiluk ca* (Uṇādi I.100), we have *taḍit* (lightning); by the rule *alīkādau* (Uṇādi IV.25), *tintiḍīkam* (tamarind);
and by the rule *pinākādayaś ca* (Uṇādi IV.15), we have *taḍākaḥ* (a pond) and *Tāḍakā*. Some say the root is *taṭ*: "O father, strike Tāṭakā! [From this comes] *taṭākaḥ* (43).

*Khaḍ* and *khaḍi* mean "to split. [From *khaḍi*: ] *khāḍayati*, *khaṇḍayati*. Some say *kaḍi*: *kaṇḍayati*. (44) *Guḍi* means "to protect": *guṇḍayati*. Some say *kuḍi*; from this very root, *kuḍi* in the sense of "burning" (I, 289) and *kuḍi* in the sense of "deficiency" (I, 345) are established, yet Candra did not include this one. (45) *Guṭhi* means "to envelop": *guṇṭhayati*; *guṇṭhanā*, *guṇṭhitam*. (46) *Khuḍi* means "to break": *khuṇḍayati*; *khuṇḍitaḥ*. (47) *Vaḍi* means "to divide": *vaṇḍayati*; *vaṇḍaḥ*. Some say it ends in *-ṭ*.

*vaṇṭayati*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.351), *vaṇṭati* (48). *caḍi* means "in anger": *caṇḍayati*. *caṇḍaḥ*, *Caṇḍā*, *Caṇḍī*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.298), *caṇḍate*; *caṇḍālaḥ* (48a). *maḍi* means "adornment": *maṇḍayati*. *maṇḍanā*, *maṇḍanam*, *maṇḍa* [also] means *eraṇḍaḥ*. In the *bhvādi* class (I.291), *maṇḍate*. Candragomin did not accept these [roots], but that is incorrect; for since roots such as *kuḍi*, *kaḍi*, *caḍi*, *vaḍi*, *maḍi*, and *bhaḍi* are not invariably transitive (*anitya-ṇyantatva*), the correct verbal suffix (*nyāyya-vikaraṇa*) is already established, so how could there be an *ātmanepada* ending? (49)

*bhaḍi* [is used] in the sense of auspiciousness (*kalyāṇe*). *bhaṇḍayati*; *bhaṇḍanā*. In the *bhvādi* class, *bhaḍi* is listed as "to revile" (*paribhāṣaṇe*, I.292): *bhaṇḍate*, *bhaṇḍaḥ* (50). *charda* [is used] in the sense of vomiting (*vamane*). *chardayati*. By the rule *arciśuci* (Uṇ. II.109), the suffix *is* is applied: *chardiḥ*. It is also [listed] as ending in *i* (51). *pusta* and *busta* [are used] in the senses of respect (*ādarā*) and disrespect (*anādarayoḥ*) respectively. *pustayati*; *pustakaḥ*; *pustaṃ* is the work of a scribe. *bustayati*; *bustiḥ* is a small cake (*śaṣkulī*). According to Candra (Candra-Dh. X.35), *pusta* means "salutation" (*vandana*) (52).
In the *Cūḍā-saṃcodana*. "Incitement" (*saṃcodana*) means urging (*preraṇa*). It incites; thus it is "incitement" (*codanā*), that which is to be urged (*codya*). (53) 1. S. I, 767 2. P etaṃ 3.
K busta 175.

*ṇakka* and *dhakka* mean destruction (54–55). *Cakka* and *cukka* mean affliction. One says *cakkayati*; *cakkalakam*. One says *cukkayati*; *cukkam*. And Kauśika says *cikketi*: *cikkasaṃ* is barley flour (*yavapiṣṭa*), *cikkaṇaṃ* is unctuous (*sasneha*) (56).
*Kṣala* means the act of cleansing. One says *kṣālayati* (57).

In the sense of "establishing" (*pratiṣṭhā*), [the root] *tal* forms *tālayati* and *uttālayati*. By [Pāṇini] Sūtra VII.4.13, *tālaḥ*, *tālikā*, and *tālī* are formed. Because it is not invariably *ṇij*-ant, one also has *talati* and *talam*. The root *tul* is used in the sense of "weighing" (*unmāna*). It forms *tolayati*. From the rule *cintipūji-* (III.3.105), because of the letter *ca*, the word *tulā* is formed. In the alternative where there is no *ṇic*, the suffix *ṇic* is added to the word *tula* ending in *kānta* (by III.1.135 and X.392). The root *dul* is used in the sense of "shaking up" (*utkṣepa*). It forms *dolayati*. [The nouns] *dolā*, *dolitaḥ*, and *āndolitaḥ* are formed. One also forms *āndolayati*, *preṅkholayati*, and *vījayati*; these are derived from common usage (*lokāt*).

*Pul* in the sense of rising (*samucchrāya*): *polayati*, in the *bhvādi* class (I, 894) and in the *tudādi* class; *pul* in the sense of greatness: *polati*, *pulati*. Since the causative form is already established from this very root in the sense of "to swell" (*prākṛta-artha*), Candra did not include it [separately] (61). *Bul* in the sense of sinking (*nimajjana*): *bolayati*; *bolitam*, *bolaḥ*, *bolanam* (62). *Mūl* in the sense of growing (*rohaṇa*): *mūlayati*; *mūlam*, *mūliḥ*. Nandī says: *muleti* (meaning *mūlayati*) (63); *molayati*.

*Kala* is used in the sense of throwing (*kṣepa*) in the *pila* group: *gāḥ kālayati* (he drives the cows); *kālaḥ*. In the sense of counting (*saṃkhyāna*) at the beginning of the *kathā* group (X, 319): *saṃkalayati*, *kalaḥ*; and in the *bhvādi* group (I, 526): *kalate*.
